With AcademyLMS we can now use an LMS, which offers very extensive functions and will certainly build up a large community. 
  
The quiz area is of less interest to us, as we use WatuPro, a WP plugin, which can also be used to manage large question databases - a topic that LMSs themselves cannot cover and is relevant to us. So that you can still do proper tests for the certificate in a closed group ("choose 10 random questions for this test from the pool of 1000 questions"). 

The functions around GroupLeaders, WhiteLabel and Migrate from other LMS / SCORM are highly interesting for us and with the larger conversion of existing courses we therefore wait a few weeks.

comments.title: A deal worth getting.   (with room for improvement)
comments.comment:
I'm torn with this deal...

On one hand I really like the concept and the easy way you get decent results.
I do think that there's room for improvement, for example a bigger field for the prompt would be useful, because you just get a couple of lines, and it is difficult to see or edit what you typed.
(you get better and more customized results by being more specific with your request)

I tested with English and Spanish requests, and I got good results with both, but I think a better request (prompt) field and more customization options would greatly improve the results and the user experience.

On the other hand, I'm not so sure about the deal.
I think the price is right, and as i mentioned you get good results but even getting Tier 2 you just get the basic course lengths (Basic, short and moderate), and get excluded from "Comprehensive" and "In Depth"
I get it, this is a LTD but at least with the second Tier you should have access to the "Comprehensive" length that's even offered in the free trial.
Then you have the "Company-wide" issue, that is not too clear, so as I understand it is only distributable within your company websites, and I guess that's fine but not clear.

And finally their logo in the menu is huge!
I get it, the logo removal is not included in the deal, but at least make it less intrusive with a smaller png or a simple text link.

To wrap this up, I think it is a good product, and the material you'll get is worth the investment, so I do recommend getting it, and in my opinion you should go for Tier 2.

But I really wish the founder considers adding the "comprehensive" option for Tier 2 and modifying the field for the "Learning Objectives"

comments.title: I Love it!! Especially after I learned how to edit and customize everything
comments.comment:
When I first purchased this, I created a course which was easy, but than after I explored all the options to create pictures and all the editing, I absolutely LOVE THIS!!! It is totally AWESOME and easy to use, edit, and customize which will take the auto-generated course and put it on steroids.

You can upload PDF documents or paste in text have a course created for you.

Visit this site to learn about all the functionality of Open eLMS: https://openelms.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OE/pages/299073539/How-to+articles

You before publishing the course, you can go through each slide and replace the pictures with those in the list --OR-- better yet, there's a button you can click on to have the AI generate a picture using several different style: Realistic, Illustrative, Cartoon, Fantasy, Cyberpunk, and many others.  You can generate a different picture for each style or multiple pictures from the same style and choose the one you like best.

After you course is created, you can customize almost everything just by clicking the pencil icon to customize. You can add in MP4 videos, YouTube videos, Vimeo videos. You can add multiple videos to the same slide and resize them to your liking. You can add images and animations. You can click the gear icon to access more editing options: Interface and Functionality. Under Functionality, you can choose different narrators - the voice that reads the script.
When editing, the left hand pane will list all the elements on the slide. Click on each element, then on the right hand side, there is an Edit button to customize. Most things can be edited just  by double-clicking on it, except for the background. To edit the background, you must select the background selection in the left, then click the edit button on the right. 

You can change the presenter and the presentation style and where the presenter will be in screen. (The presenter is not the same as the narrator).

On each screen, you can edit the text the narrator will read and you can format the text with different colors and highlights, bullet points, numbered lists - just like with Microsoft Word or Google docs. 

The background image can be change via a Library, Envato, or your own uploads. Just click the plus symbol to upload your pictures.  All pictures you custom created previously before publishing are available in the Library in addition to many many others. You can use the search function to bring up pictures you want.

Customize Quiz Questions and Question types:
At the end if the course, if you chose to have questions created, you can customize the questions and add more questions.
Question types: multiple choice, True/False, Multiple Response, Fill-in-the-Blank, Word Bank, Matching Drag-and-Drop, Sequence Drag-and-Drop

You is also an AI assistant to answer questions.

comments.title: Buy this deal if you want a paid, limited, unlimited free trial
comments.comment:
I struggled to rate this product. Not because the software itself is bad (more on that below), but because the deal structure is confusing and, frankly, misleading. My review is mainly about the deal terms, not the product itself. I lost a lot of time due to the team’s habit of using “website” and “course” as if they’re interchangeable.

MY CORE ISSUE
The “number of course websites” you get is really just the number of *published courses*, NOT the number of brands or domains you can use. It gets murkier because the ONLY clear limitation at the top of the deal listing is:

Number of codes = number of course “websites” = number of custom domains.

Every other feature is either listed as unlimited or doesn’t mention any limits, which makes it look like you can create as many courses as you want—just like most AppSumo lifetime deals. Even their pricing page (txhq.org/ochpricing) says unlimited courses are included on the basic plan.

MY EXPERIENCE
I considered stacking codes for multiple brands, clients, or projects. But first, I tried building out a single course to get a feel for the platform. After spending over two hours setting everything up, I tried to click “Create New Course.” I immediately got this error:

“Your maximum of 1 courses is reached. To create another course, please purchase a new code in AppSumo.”

When people bring this up, the founders quickly reply with, “Don’t worry! You can upgrade to unlimited for just $59/month. What a steal!”

It honestly feels like you’re being played. Where’s the deal? This is basically paying for a trial with a small discount to their existing Pro plan. Check their pricing page: unless you absolutely need features in Unlimited, you’re not getting extra value from the lifetime deal. If you need only basic features, get Basic. If you need Pro, get Pro. Otherwise, because of the LTD’s upfront fee, you probably won’t ever get a real discount.

One founder said unlimited video hosting forever isn’t sustainable (which is fair). But their basic tier includes unlimited storage, and it’s cheaper than their “upgrade” option, which is apparently the only path for AppSumo users. Plus, I don’t want to upload videos to their platform—embedding is enough for me, which makes that argument moot.

---

ON THE SOFTWARE ITSELF
The product is fine. I’ve been looking for an Open edX alternative and am willing to pay extra to offload technical work. When I saw this on AppSumo, I thought it might be the answer and bought a code to test it out.

- Setting up a course was straightforward.
- Features were easy to find—no endless digging.
- Stripe integration was smoother than with most SaaS tools.
- The built-in AI generator for content is a nice touch. While not necessary in every tool, it actually works. The downside: AI-generated content often didn’t paste cleanly into course fields and usually needed reformatting elsewhere.
- Course landing pages look clean and are audience-friendly. The main course interface is good too.
- I had a caching issue when setting up the CNAME, but support was quick and helpful.

---

BOTTOM LINE
As a course creation tool, this holds up with the competition.

As a lifetime deal, it’s confusing. Communication needs to be clearer about what’s actually included, and the deal structure should be reconsidered. Investors would probably love the founders’ approach: it boosts user numbers and, from what I can see, they aren’t cutting profits and are price services like more mature competitors—a win-win for them.

If you have zero technical experience (rare on AppSumo) and need every Unlimited Plan feature — maybe you’re an agency or established course creator — this deal *might* make sense. Otherwise, I’d pass and just treat this tool as another option in a crowded market.

---

A NOTE FOR THE FOUNDERS
Possible ways to fix this deal:
- Let users apply the discount to any of your three plans, not just Unlimited.
- Allow unlimited courses up to a reasonable storage limit. Keep unlimited storage for a single course per code for anyone who hits their storage cap.
- Just map codes directly to storage limits, if that’s the real concern around LTD costs.
- Cut AI usage from the LTD or limit it to personal keys if that’s part of your cost concerns.

---
Edit for purposes of reply. Trying not to touch original review here.

Thanks for the response, Vasco. I'm keeping an eye on the update re subscription options. I'm looking for an excuse to not refund here. Updated from 2 to 3 tacos on 2025-06-21 because I appreciate the responsiveness to concerns, and it does suck that the language issue of courses != websites seems out of your hands and may not be your fault.

---
Edit 2: The deal is now solid. They have given an LTD-level discount to all tiers. I think the deal is a 5-taco deal. The hiccups have been largely about botched communication related to the deal. I think if you state the deal terms plainly, this is now 5-tacos.

The team at Forento is very responsive. I had a simple question, but they answered it within 24 hours (probably sooner than that!). I like the option to preview my content as well. Accepting payments is done solely through Stripe which is fine by me, but if that's an issue, I'm not sure if they will be adding more in the future. I bought 3 codes, so that limits what I get. No memberships, bundles, community, or website. I'm not sure if I'll need those in the future so I'm contemplating adding more codes.

Overall, this is a fantastic product and I'm so glad I'm finally able to create and publish my courses, products, and services. FYI, the getting started dashboard is great! Love seeing what else I can do that I wasn't aware of.

Update:

I knocked down a star. Mainly because simple things aren't working for me. I have 4 Tiers, so I added on the website and the membership. But a simple thing like having more image options for products or using the text editor without hassling with the text being all white has been a thorn in my backside. I wish the developers would take the time to update these simple things - when I ask, they give me a workaround instead of telling me its added to any future updates. I had issues with the DNS mapping with my own domain name so purchased one through the site instead. Everything I've been doing is a work around and it would be nice to not have to do that. For instance, instead of having product images being more than just one thumbnail, I'm having to create new pages for every product so I can do that. This seems counterproductive and a huge waste of my time. I would probably ask for a return but at this point I invested so many hours into it - it's unlikely. I do still appreciate the platform on many other levels but I wish they would work on a simple text editor, making the interface more user friendly, and allowing more images and options for the downloadables sections.

comments.title: Almost perfect
comments.comment:
After playing around with Forento for about a week-or-so now, I believe it is safe to say that this platform was thoughtfully created.

Pros:
+ It quite possibly has everything you may need out of a platform from the front-end website builder to the course builder.
+ A big plus point that the team replies very fast when you reach out to them for any questions.
+ I was very glad to find out that I could upload my own fonts to keep with my branding. Same goes for being able to use your brand colors.
+ The website builder is very customizable that leaves a lot of leg room for your creativity.

Cons:
- Only Stripe and PayPal can be used right out gate. The fix for this is to get an add-on that allows you to collect payment using other payment methods, but then you will need another integration tool (Zapier) to automate the workflow. It seems a little too much. If you could just make available more payment method integrations, this could easily be fixed, I think, since (from what I can tell from previous reviews) it's not paying Forento the commission that's the problem but the availability of other payment integrations.
- Perhaps my biggest complaint is that you cannot change the currency for your courses / products / sessions / etc. until and unless you have integrated your Stripe or PayPal account. I think this should be one of the easy, intuitive parts of the platform which, unfortunately, is not. I fail to understand the need to integrate Stripe / PayPal prior just so I can list the price of my course / services in our local currency especially if it is only for cosmetics. (1) Not everyone trades in USD; (2) Not everyone has access to Stripe or PayPal; (3) Not everyone has interest in using either Stripe or PayPal.

Overall, would still definitely recommend the platform especially if you are not particular about the payment methods or changing your currency.

comments.title: A Must-Buy, Fresh Concept, But Latency, Recording, and a Few Other Issues
comments.comment:
I absolutely love GoBrunch 😊 My usecase is a fun meeting space for my community's monthly meetups, and I used it for two recorded courses, but that didn't go well (will explain more below). The concept is great, it's easy to use, the permissions features are granular, and branding options and customization are amazing. The concept itself is really fresh and fun, and makes me feel like I'm actually meeting with my community members, rather than get "Zoom fatigue" from another video meet with big boxes. ❤️

There are a few big issues for me though:
- Latency and freezing audio and video are an issue in sessions. Myself and attendees get dropped from rooms sometimes

- Using a locked room is not a fun experience. I love the knocking sound and notification, but if you miss the device dialogue box that pops up in your system tray (PC) to let an attendee in a room, it's gone forever until they try again, for some reason. I seriously cannot find an "admit" button in the actual GoBrunch meeting room itself; it just shows a message someone is trying to get in in the chat. Really annoying. I switched it to public or use an access code as a workaround. They need to add a clear, *on screen* button that admits people to the room if using the approval workflow, not just the system alert

- For scheduled GoBrunch rooms, you can't edit details about a meeting if it's too close to start time, or already started, so I only use the perpetual meeting room, just in case

- Recording quality and ease of use is terrible; the dialogue box that pops in Chrome for permissions won't got away, and since it's embedded in the Chrome UI, it warps the aspect ratio of the recording, so it makes my head look like a hotdog 😂 If you do record, there's isn't a clean, easy way to keep your aspect ratio and present things like slides or share your screen. It will mess up the recording beyond saving, again, because it warps the aspect ratio and squishes everything. So, I can't use this for classes or recording like I'd planned and tried. I have to redo the live classes with attendees that I've already recorded in another video meeting solution, because GoBrunch's recordings are unusable

- Trying to use the screenshare function in Chrome will mess up your session, so don't plan on using the screenshare function with GoBrunch. It will put in a permissions dialogue box that will persist until you close the tab or window, even if you stop screensharing. It's really annoying, and removes visible space/warps the aspect ratio of the GoBrunch room

They are a MVP for sure, but I hope they fix these issues! Again, concept, ease of use for the most part, and customization are fantastic. Fresh concept I haven't seen anywhere else. But my user experience has has some challenges.

comments.title: All in all great, but I miss 1 feature

comments.title: I absolutely love it but there's room for improvement
comments.comment:
I have been using GoBrunch for a couple of months now to teach online both groups and one on one. Before that I was using Zoom and GoBrunch does seem to better suit my needs, But I still haven't cancelled my Zoom subscription.

Here's what I like about GoBrunch:

- The space is way more customizable than Zoom, and you can really create a unique atmosphere. 

- I can create a private space for each student with a custom link, and the student can access it whenever he or she wants to.  

- It's great for community building.

Here's why I am still holding on to my Zoom subscription:

- Zoom is still more stable. I have been experiencing video and audio breakups while zoom was working fine on the same connection.

- There are still some some bugs and glitches. For instance, sometimes my chat disappears - especially when changing from dynamic mode to presentation mode. Also, after a few times of switching between shared tabs, it crashed and I had to reconnect.

- In Zoom I can see my students. When I share my screen and working on the screen I am sharing. I realize that as a web-based platform GoBrunch can't display anything outside the browsed page, so I am not complaining. Just something to take into account.

- Also easier to work with a document camera with Zoom, because the camera size is limited in GoBrunch and can't be full screen.

Here are also a couple of suggestions for improvement:

1. Make the door icon change when locking and unlocking a space to indicate the state. 

2. I don't know if it's possible but when someone speak and their mic is off, it would be nice to give them a notice like zoom does.

3. In the chat, after you reach the end of the input text box, you can see what you're typing. This is even more annoying on presentation mode because you can't expand the chat box and make it wider. 

4. The Board plugin is cumbersome, overly complicated, and the size aspect is very confusing. I would prefer to have something simple and built-in the page for the occasional doodle I need to do. I don't need boxes, flowcharts and all that.

Although I would like the editing tools be a bit sleeker it works well with no lag! Ran our first class last week and it worked flawlessly.

comments.title: Great tool. My clients love it.
comments.comment:
This is a really great tool and I have just upgraded from tier to tier 3 which says it all really. My clients love this as a Zoom alternative.

There is definitely room for improvement though.
1. It can be glitchy. Sometimes sub rooms just stop working and you can't get in or out of them and you have delete and add them again which is frustrating.
2. Simple things like being able to centre text in the background editor
3. I would love, love, love to be able to have a notice bar at the top of the room that can be edited without it affecting anything else in the room. For example if you have a notice saying when the next session is and you are also sharing a screen (Pomodoro timer in my case). If you want to edit the notice then you have to go into the room editing, change what you've written, save and exit the room and then share the screen again. It doesn't sound like a big deal but it's frustrating and as the host you are disappearing while you update the notice. And because the text editing options are limited then this can take a while as if you want the notice to be longer then you have to make the text smaller/box bigger and this can be glitchy. This is really the one main thing that bugs me that I'd love them to address. The option to have a notice bar at the top of the room that you can just edit without it affecting anything else would be amazing.  I did send it in a suggestion but never heard back.

All that said, I do think it's great.

comments.title: It's Good But Has Room For Growth
comments.comment:
To be honest, this app confused me beyond belief. I think I have a love hate relationship with it. I am not sure if i love the rooms or hate the rooms as i am so used to holding classes that have everyone on screen. It's a cute thing to see them in a sort of bubble but there's also an element of distance created from it. I like to see who i am talking to on a big camera screen where anyone can be seen clearly on a HD view. Nevertheless, its rather like the story of Christopher Columbus when he told everyone the world was indeed round. He was jeered at and poked and made fun of, and low and behold, the dude was right. 

I kinda feel a little like this. GO Brunch is the Columbus of the world trying to convince all the flat world believers they are a bunch of nutters and need to wake up. Who knows maybe we will come to an agreement over Brunch!

comments.title: Good product but still room for improvement
comments.comment:
Personally I am still testing and everything works quite well. The environment is nice and aesthetically surprising. The multi-language support is surprising.
Also GoBrunch offers solutions for many different use cases. The creation of workgroups is another great advantage.
There are very interesting options like video sharing and general interactive elements.

In general everything works very well but I still find some problems or flaws or things that can be improved.
When creating rooms it is still not easy or intuitive to link rooms or create waiting rooms and I have to find a way to do that. Everything would be easier by including specific buttons to create those options. An example is when creating a meeting, where you don't see options for additional rooms and that would be useful.
Another problem is that some options are incomplete, for example, webinars should include options to remind attendees (by email) because it is very common that in a webinar many less people attend than registered because they "forget" exactly the day or time of the event. Obviously a specific webinar software offers all that and much more, but GoBrunch should include at least basic functions or at least integration with Pabbly to use other platforms for that.
There are also little things that are missing that would improve the aesthetics and usability, for example, when there are several people in a meeting and one of them is speaking, I think his camera circle should be slightly enlarged while he is speaking, that would improve the identification of who is speaking because sometimes everything is a bit confusing.
I would also like to suggest that you can share in an iframe a Custom HTML because there are many services such as survey or contest apps or forms (e.g. paperform) that offer an HTML embed code but that can't be used here and it would be great to do that (a big improvement).
And the last problem that I have already mentioned is that there is no integration with Pabbly and that limits some things and prevents to include the attendees of a meeting to an email marketing list of our usual platform or other tracking platforms.

comments.title: A Different Vehicle for Online Everything
comments.comment:
I purchased Tier 2 of GoBrunch because I wanted to test it against the Butter video conferencing product also sold on AppSumo before my return window ran out. One of the biggest cons about Butter is their strangely repressive policy on recordings, whereas GoBrunch has plenty of video storage for recording on each of their plans, and the ability to download recordings when you need to free up space.

I also found where Butter was kind of stingy with the amount of participants, GoBrunch is the opposite, allowing for numerous participants even in their Tier 1 Plan. And where Butter seemed to be focused on meetings, GoBrunch seems to include all sorts of flexibility for meetings, events, webinars, classrooms, and more.

GoBrunch is very different from Zoom. I liken it's style to AirMeet, but much simpler and very visual. Just a brief run through of the product gave me all sorts of ideas of what I might use it for. And unlike other AirMeet alternatives, GoBrunch provides it's own video conferencing capability where you don't have to link up to another third party video conferencing tool like Zoom or MS Teams.

The only reason I gave it 4 Tacos was because it doesn't seem to have it's own whiteboard, quizzes and polls, and relies on other third party "pay to use" products like Miro and Mentimeter. That said, GoBrunch is at the start of its life, otherwise why would it be on AppSumo? I sincerely hope that GoBrunch will continue to add functions and capabilities, especially those inherent in the product.

comments.title: Pretty good on desktop, clunky on mobile
comments.comment:
Our usecase is to use this internally for meetings, and client facing meetings. It's essential for us that any user can get into the meeting and participate with the least amount of friction. GoBrunch fullfills most of that on desktop. Less so on mobile devices.

PROS
This is a fun video meeting platform. The different virtual rooms do set the tone for the meetings. For meeting leaders, it's easy to create and start meetings. There are several different meeting categories, which for us, made it easy to find the right meeting model. 

It works in a web browser without downloading any apps, or plugins. Using it on a Mac does require some fiddling in settings.

It does recording, and saves the public chat. We also like that there are private chats.

CONS
Biggest one for us - the interface on a mobile device is clunky. The meeting room does not scale well on a small screen. The meeting controls cover the bottom part of the meeting room. 

The chat window is extremely clunky to use on a mobile. 

WISHLIST
Make the use on mobile more friendly. We have many users that join meetings from their (parked) cars, or coffee shops. Having a streamlined experience on mobile is very important for them to participate in the meeting.

All in all, GoBrunch might replace our other virtual meeting tools - if the mobile experience would be less clunky.

comments.title: Best for virtual rooms with many attendees
comments.comment:
I had the pleasure of attending one of Richard’s onboarding sessions the other day. The demonstration was brilliant and addressed the questions I had encountered in my early trials and tribulations with the platform. 

Now, to be frank, GoBrunch isn’t perfect. But the platform has tremendous potential, and Richard is not only listening to customer feedback but genuinely striving to improve GoBrunch. I had some follow-up questions about CNAME as I couldn’t figure out whether to go for a single space or multiple spaces, and Richard explained the pros and cons patiently through email. 

So, I shall also provide the pros and cons of the platform, as I see them:

Pros:

Easy to set up and use with a simple and intuitive interface.

Offers a variety of spaces that suit various needs, e.g. co-working space, meetings, events, classroom, etc.

Provides decent audio and video quality for a smooth and immersive experience.

Supports both live and recorded sessions, with the option to download recordings for offline viewing.

Offers exceptional and personalized customer support to address any issues or concerns.

Cons:

Limited customization options for white label and branding.

CNAME links to a space or multiple spaces. This is confusing, or at least it was for me. In the end, I settled for a simple space and configured it as a lobby/waiting room that leads to other rooms.

Lack of integration with other tools and software.

I’ve experienced occasional glitches and technical difficulties, such as audio or video lag, which can frustrate me during a live session.

The user interface is very basic and visually unappealing. Settings are limited.

Inability to password-protect a room or space! All you need to enter a room is the URL, which makes it somewhat difficult to use for a professional business setting. Even though the admin can kick out unwanted guests once they take a seat, it’s awkward to have a client join another client’s session that overruns its time. I’d prefer a password-protected room or the ability for the admin to approve who can enter the room to avoid ‘unwanted guests.’

Overall, GoBrunch is a solid option for anyone looking for a decent user-friendly virtual classroom platform. It offers a range of features and tools to support online learning and collaboration, but it may not be the best fit for one-to-one business meetings, particularly if you require advanced customization or integrations. Nonetheless, GoBrunch is worth considering for its reliability and affordability, especially if you’re on a tight budget.

comments.title: Lots of Promise

The reason I deducted a taco is because of the lack of an app. If it had that, it would be unbeatable as an integrated videoconferencing/social interaction platform. It could destroy things like Zoom and Teams, along with even things like Slack, with a really holistic interactive experience. Can you imagine being able to summon team members through an app for a quick “pop-up” meeting. 

As a professor it also has the potential to be a broader-based market disrupter if it were tightly integrated with popular LMS’ such as Canvas. If it had a “Meet Now” option, for instance, where a student could spin up a group meeting or meet virtually with a professor, it would likely sell extremely well in the higher education market. So keep going Richard! You can see the hard work that has gone into the product and I’m hoping to see more great enhancements!

comments.title: Extremely promising, but not ready yet for serious marketeers IMHO
comments.comment:
Hi!

I'd love to give 5 tacos, and I will when this necessary feedback is implemented before my refund period of 60-days ends. I see & feel the love and commitment you have put with your team into this lovely software, that is why I upgraded to Tier 2! I'm happy to edit/upgrade my review when this happens, and/or when it's confirmed to be implemented anytime soon.

For a serious internet marketeer (and there are many here on Appsumo) who wants to collect emails, the GoBrunch webinar registration needs an upgrade.

Why? 

Because we'll lose 30 to 50% or more of our potential webinar attendees during the signup process!

Why is that?

It is a known fact that unnecessary OBLIGITARY input fields will result in people abandoning any registration/sales/signup process. A lot of marketing research and statistical data from professional split-testing experiments, confirms this.

Besides asking the name & email, you make it OBLIGATORY for anyone who signs up to:

(1) => fill in the name of the school/company. WHY? Many people don't even have a school/company, they simply want to learn! Making this field obligatory will make many people abandon the registration for sure. 

(2) => choose a password. WHY? Forcing potential customers to choose a password will turn down so many potential clients! Not even one of the major webinar software companies out there, used by professional internet marketeers, forces a potential prospect to give a password during registration. 

Please make the webinar registration process customizable, so everyone can adapt it to their needs. 

Give us the option to disable:

- the obligatory 'company/school' input field
- the obligatory 'password creation' input field

This would make many entrepreneurs happy, and not only on Appsumo.

For now, I'm forced to create my own webinar signup pages, to be able to collect emails in an easy way without any unnecessary steps. And I'll have to send them a direct webinar link via my own email software. This will make it more complicated on my end, but at least I can get started. 

Thank you, and I only took the time to give this detailed feedback because I feel GoBrunch has A LOT of potential, and I hope you will take my feedback seriously.

comments.title: Works well, active dev team!
comments.comment:
My use of GoBrunch is for hosting live chats with various members of my own development team. It allows me to invite strangers to sit in a room that feels like a comfortable business lounge versus inviting them to a platform like Google Meets. There is a clear distinction between people on the stage and people who are listening in the audience. I think if I did this via Google Meets, fewer people would show up because it would feel as though they are more involved with the call than they really are, or that they are comfortable being. So that is the use case for me.

Initial setup did take some onboarding, but thankfully, this team has a lot of content around helping you craft the perfect space for what you need it to be. The setup wizard for each room could probably be more polished, but it works as is once you've spent some time clicking through all the buttons to learn how each can affect the space you're trying to build. It's not exactly Photoshop-level complexity, so I believe an hour or two of messing around with the settings while trying to create your space would do the trick.

I spent some time looking over their content, which showcases other creators and the unique and interesting ways they are utilizing this platform to form the space that they want. By doing so, it gives me a little bit of an idea and context on how I can grow my own if I choose to go that route. Some of the community members seem to really go all in to a level that I am not comfortable spending my time. So, I believe my use of this software is pretty basic, but it serves the use case that I need it for, and I do not regret buying into this project.

I highly recommend it for individuals that work with online crowds or anyone trying to build a community with a tool that adds a sense of presence to the entire experience without making the participants feel pressured or uncomfortable while being at an event because you can design your spaces in a way that makes it appropriate for each social interaction.

comments.title: Fun alternative to Zoom squares

I love that I can change the backgrounds and that every face (or avatar) is visible. I also like the way meeting rooms can be kept open and the links reused. It makes sharing meeting info a lot easier to prep in advance! Add in unlimited recording space and no meeting time limits, and getting GoBrunch is a decision that I would make again and again.

comments.title: I think it's great (except for the logo which you can thankfully disable in most places)
comments.comment:
Great: 
- Easy to set up. It took perhaps 5 minutes for a basic orientation, and I'm ready for my first meeting on this platform. 
- Fun meeting room layouts. Those definitely elevate the meeting. 
- Very affordable alternative to Zoom and other meeting platforms. I can probably cancel my other subscription. 
- No download necessary on phone. This is huge, especially if you sometimes meet with people who are less tech-savvy and get confused if they first have to download an app. 

Only con so far: 
I cringe every time I see the logo (I guess it's supposed to be a fried egg?). 

A food-related logo coupled with the name Go Brunch makes it seem like this is a restaurant or foodie platform, not a meeting platform. This feels a bit weird when using it for professional meetings. 

The logo also makes it harder for me to share this meeting platform with people who are vegans or animal advocates (even though they'd probably love this platform). 

The logo shows up every time people connect to a meeting room and is the first thing they see, so this is a bigger deal than it might seem like, both for professionalism and inclusivity. 
[EDIT: this can be removed in most places, see the helpful response I received to my review.]

I think a more neutral logo would be more inclusive and also more reflective of what the app is actually about (better online meetings, not brunching at a restaurant). 

So: 4 (or 4.5 stars) as it is, 5 stars if it had a more neutral logo. [EDIT: upgraded my review to 5 stars since the logo can be disabled in many places.]

I hope that's constructive criticism as I really like the idea behind this app as well as its current execution.

comments.title: It makes virtual work feel human, our team of just under 10 people LOVE IT!
comments.comment:
As a keynote speaker, author, and founder with a remote team; GoBrunch is our virtual HQ because it brings the room back into the room. 
My team feels like they BELONG, which to me is impactful. It increase engagement and productivity by a good 30%. 

I find it to be:
Immersive, branded spaces—rooms, seating, circle cams, and media shape the vibe, my logo shows up twice if I want to.
Frictionless for guests—no downloads, simple controls, I sometimes invite other speakers to learn our operations.
Breakouts done right—prebuilt rooms, assign facilitators, run parallel sessions, I am not creative with layouts, so I LOVE that there are preset layouts (many actually).
Higher engagement, less fatigue—people stay present, I ask my team to be online the whole time in case someone needs something, and no one gets "tired" of being online, we truly enjoy it.

How I use it
Daily co-working with the whole team, open 24/7, and a "training room" for new team members. 
I downloaded the website on my mobile as an app, so I easily join from my android (I don't like iPhone, even though I have both)

Bottom line: If you lead teams, teach, coach, or build community, GoBrunch turns “another meeting” into an experience—flexible, fun, and aligned with my values of authenticity, service, and results. 

My wish would be that we could livestream to some social media platforms, but not everyone wants to show the world their internal operations, so it's cool.

One of the top 3 software I have ever gotten for my daily ops, in my consulting/speaking business. 

It's worth every penny.

@OVinspires

comments.title: A must have tool for all make.com automation guys!
comments.comment:
This app excels at generating PDFs and images from various sources, such as markup or HTML, and now also supports creating PDFs from widely used office formats (e.g., Google Docs or Sheets).  

With its API-driven functionality, it’s a must-have tool for anyone automating processes via Make.com. One standout feature is the precise control over the final appearance of the PDF. For my use case, the ability to automate meta information (for SEO) was crucial—something not achievable using Google Drive’s standard Google Doc-to-PDF conversion.  

Additionally, the app offers advanced features like template creation, which allows you to bypass Google Docs entirely. This is especially beneficial when integrating SVG images into documents, a task Google Docs cannot handle.  

I briefly encountered an issue with the API, but the live support team helped me quickly and was very responsive and explained me how to use the tool correctly.  

One small critique: I’d appreciate more tutorial videos to ease the learning curve. And, please, include spoken explanations in the videos—mute tutorials are totally frustrating. 

A piece of advice: It’s not always easy to transition from an LTD model to acquiring paying customers. I recommend reaching out to some of the active YouTubers who create Make.com tutorials and offering them your tool as ambassadors. This approach could significantly boost your visibility within this niche audience, filled with users who would genuinely benefit from your tool!

Happy selling!

comments.title: Make your Claude Code and Codex limits go further
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Claude Code and Codex can burn through a surprising amount of your usage allowance reading long logs, command output, JSON, and files that don't always need to be sent in full. Headroom compresses that material locally before the coding agent receives it, while keeping the original available if the agent needs it.

During our testing, Headroom ran quietly through roughly six hours of Claude Code work in the background. The dashboard showed the tokens saved and the estimated dollar savings. For someone using a subscription, the benefit is getting more coding time out of the plan they're already paying for. API users can also reduce their token costs.

The project learnings feature is another reason I find Headroom interesting. If your coding agent tries a command, gets an error, and eventually finds the correct way to do something, Headroom can save that information in the project's instruction files. The next session can then use what was learned instead of repeating the same mistakes.

No learnings appeared during the original beta test, despite several hours of use. The team says they've since improved how reliably those learnings are captured. They've also expanded the documentation and onboarding to explain the benefits beyond token savings and why the optional add-ons aren't enabled by default.

The compression engine itself is open source, so what you're paying for here is the desktop app that takes care of the setup and maintenance. You get automatic updates, a dashboard for tracking savings and usage, project learnings, and a way to enable additional tools without installing and configuring everything yourself.

One compatibility note: the earlier version I checked failed to install on an Intel Mac. The current documentation lists Intel support. I haven't retested that particular setup with the newer installer and have it running now on my Intel Mac and already see savings reported.

Overall, Headroom pays for itself if you spend a lot of time in Claude Code or Codex (who doesn't) and regularly run into usage limits. I like that it works in the background without asking you to change how you code. The compression is the immediate benefit, and the project learnings could make it even more valuable as you continue working on the same codebase.

comments.title: Community, courses and real-time chat in one place
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What I like about EzyCommunity is that it doesn't make the community feel like an extra feature attached to a course platform. The community itself is at the center, with a feed for posts and discussions alongside real-time chat that feels more like Slack or Discord.

From there, you can add courses, events, paid channels, memberships and gamification without sending members through a collection of different tools. I can see that being especially useful for someone running a coaching program, membership or paid community where the course content is only one part of why people joined.

I liked the chat experience during testing. Members can move between community discussions, channels and direct conversations, while points, badges and leaderboards give them another reason to participate. For me this is one of the big differentiators of the platform because getting people to participate reularly is one of the hardest things of running an online community. 

Courses are inside the same environment, so someone can go from a lesson to a conversation with the rest of the community without leaving the platform.

Members can also use EzyCommunity through its iOS and Android apps, which is useful for a community where you want people checking in regularly rather than only when they are sitting at a computer. A fully branded app under your own name is available separately.

You can monetize different parts of the community too. Channels and courses can be restricted or paid, and EzyCommunity takes 0% of your sales, outside of the normal payment processor fees. This becomes more valuable as a paid community grows. And most other platforms take a % commission so this is a good value proposition from EzyCommunity.

There were still some unfinished areas when I first tested it. Course certificates were marked as coming soon at the time, but the team completed them and I verified that they had been added.

Email marketing is the one area I would still check before buying if it is important to you. During my original test, the Marketing section was not yet available even though email marketing was advertised as included. The team said it was close to completion. The current pricing still lists monthly marketing email allowances, while another part of the current website continues to describe email campaigns as coming soon, so I would confirm exactly what is available today.

Overall, I think EzyCommunity works particularly well when the course, community and conversation need to feel like one product rather than three separate services stitched together. For a membership where people are there as much for each other as they are for the content, that combination makes all the difference.

comments.title: Best Scraper I've Used, Support is Great, Too!
comments.comment:
I purchased Local Scraper a few months ago (February) and hadn't really put too much time into using it. At first, I was offput by having to purchase my own proxy (the other scraper I used prior had this built in, or I didn't need my own), but this was naive on my part.

I reached out to Grant to ask a few questions, and he was VERY quick to respond and very helpful in his responses to my questions, including setting up a proxy.

Fast forward to two weeks ago...

I finally purchased a proxy subscription and put this scraper to the test and WOW! I'm extremely pleased with its ability to grab data from Google Maps and Yellow Pages. For my own personal use, I'm likely going to mostly use the Google Maps Full and Email Finder features of the application since it gives me the widest range of results.

One thing I noticed in my testing with Google is to use Zip Codes vs City name. What I do is run my list of keywords against a zip code and that gives me more results. 

For added context, I'm using Chicago to run my tests and have a list of all standard zip codes and a list of about 70 keywords. I run all the keywords against each zip code. Then I run some python scripts I wrote to merge all the CSV files into a single Excel file that also removes duplicate and empty data so I have exactly what I need. Last, I upload the Excel file into an Airtable setup that acts as a flimsy and simple CRM that specifically focuses on the data from this program.

The only thing I had an issue with is the fact that I can't run a list of keywords against a list of zip codes. I was told each list needed to be the same length. It's not the end of the world by any means, and my keyword lists are going to be a little exhaustive, so breaking them up might not be a bad idea.

Overall, I LOVE this program and will renew again next year. I've already gotten my ROI and then some and would give this 15 tacos if I could!

Does what it promises and more!

Scrape G maps, scrape websites for emails, combine csv, deletes duplicates, awesome little software. I keep it running on virtualbox on mac. Mac version was buggy, but windows works perfectly 👌

Recommended!

comments.title: Strong Base, Fast Support, With Some Features in Progress
comments.comment:
I’ve been using Skillplate for 2 days, testing out its course builder, website/landing page tools and general creator ecosystem. Overall it’s impressive, especially for the price and promise, but it comes with the understanding that some features are still maturing. 

Pros
→ Support ticket replies and live-chat responses are incredibly fast, real people-to-people follow-up gives me confidence and offering online workshop for walk-trough.
→ It genuinely simplifies the tool-stack, website + landing pages + checkout + course modules + email marketing all in one place.
→ The UI is clean and onboarding is smooth, you can get a product live in less time than expected.
→ Unlimited counts (courses, bundles, admin accounts) give freedom to scale without worrying about extra fees.
→ The lifetime deal via AppSumo makes this a compelling value if you’re willing to engage with a young platform.

Cons
→ The “AI course creator” descriptor is a bit optimistic, in practice you get title suggestions for modules/chapters, but not fully ready-to-launch content. I found many suggestions far from bullet-proof and ended up rebuilding substantial parts myself.
→ Some UX details still glitch, the custom domain you connect may not display correctly in global settings.
→ The ability to embed custom code (e.g. for flip-book widgets) into the web and landing page builder is missing for now, though the team has promised it’s coming soon.
→ It takes some time to understand how the UX-flow ties together, from course creation, to product setup, to landing page linking. The pieces work, but the connection between them isn’t always obvious at first glance.
→ Advanced content-security needs (screenshot protection, granular admin roles, heavy DRM) are not yet robust, so if that’s a core need for your business you’ll want a workaround or to track the roadmap closely. Let's vote for this one🚀

Verdict
If you’re a creator or small team looking for a one-stop platform that moves quickly and you’re comfortable with “good now, better soon” dynamics, Skillplate hits a strong sweet spot. Its combination of features, support responsiveness and price make it very appealing.

If you’re running a larger business with complex needs (deep custom code embeds, enterprise-grade content security, fully finished feature-set), treat this as a high-potential platform with some caveats. Plan for some effort, keep a migration-mindset alive, and lean into their roadmap updates.

Thanks Dimitar, and best of luck with your SaaS journey. I’m excited to see what you build next, keeping things clean and user-friendly while adding more functionality.

We did not identify an immediate compliance blocker, and the product also showed meaningful demand signals, including roughly 36K monthly traffic, 522 Product Hunt upvotes with a #2 Product of the Day finish, and 1,000+ Chrome Web Store installs with a 5.0 rating.

The main caveat is that this is a crowded and relatively replicable category,  but based on the version available during our testing period, MiroMiro delivered a useful workflow and the Partner responded well to the issues we raised.

comments.title: Powerful tool with greater potential for further growth!
comments.comment:
I found Twidget to be quite intuitive, though it is still in its early stage of development. It is rich with useful and even powerful features that allow you to build complex logic custom APIs.

Twidget enables users to build complex, custom logic directly within its API endpoint builder—going far beyond standard functionality. For example, it can handle tasks like uploading a file, storing it in an internal file system, creating a corresponding record in an internal database with all relevant file data, generating a JSON object with any desired structure containing the file's metadata and a link to the file, and sending it back as a response—all within a single API endpoint call.

What sets Twidget apart is the convenience of its no-code graphical interface, making these advanced operations accessible even to non-developers. Additionally, the platform includes a wide range of data type handlers, converters, loops, and logical expressions such as if, if-else, and else statements. Even more impressively, these can be combined into user-defined custom functions, which can then be reused across different API endpoints for greater flexibility and efficiency. Another standout feature they offer is scheduled events, allowing you to automate API calls whenever a predefined trigger condition is met. While it doesn’t include SQL commands as a feature, it more than makes up for it with capabilities that competitors simply don’t offer.

Storage is a big bonus. comments.title: Interactive Shell Review: Great Value for Quick Testing, but Needs Better Documentation
comments.comment:
I’ve been using Interactive Shell for a while now, mainly to study and follow online courses in JavaScript, Python, and similar topics—and I genuinely like it a lot.

For the price, it delivers a lot of value. It’s honestly hard to find an environment that gives you both a testing setup and a terminal for this cost, especially as a lifetime deal. If your goal is to quickly spin up an environment to run code, experiment, and learn, it does that very well.

That said, there are some areas where the product could improve—especially around documentation and clarity.

It takes time to understand how things actually work. For example, files from the “Drive” can be seen in the terminal, but you can’t modify or open them through the online desktop. At the same time, you can’t save files into /mnt, which creates confusion.

Because of that, you start running into questions like: if I can use Git, but I can’t write to /mnt, where should I work from? If database support is listed, how am I supposed to use it in practice? Should I create SQL scripts, or use Python or PHP to interact with a database? When I open an HTML file, it seems to bundle CSS and JS together—are these actually separate files? If I want to add images, where do they go? The /mnt directory shows everything mixed together without a clear folder structure—is that expected? Is there even proper support for assets like images?

Another example: how exactly am I supposed to use the Monaco editor with Drive files? Is that possible or not? These are small but important details that aren’t clearly explained, and the user ends up “hitting a wall” multiple times trying to figure out things that would normally be trivial.

The system works—but sometimes in ways that feel a bit patched together. Once you understand its quirks, you can make good use of it, but getting there isn’t always straightforward.

So here’s the bottom line: if your goal is to have a fast, simple environment for testing—running single-file scripts in Python, PHP, or HTML with inline CSS/JS—you’ll probably love it. It’s very convenient and always available.

However, if you expect a more complete development environment with flexibility, structure, and scalability, you may feel limited or even frustrated.

I believe the team could significantly improve the experience by adding better documentation, tutorials, and practical examples showing how the system actually works—especially how the desktop, terminal, and drive interact with each other. That would make a huge difference and help users fully understand what the platform is designed for.

Five tacos!

In the past, I tried importing a folder exported from Brizy Cloud so that I could tinker with the code, but while uploads appeared to work, the files rendered blank and couldn’t communicate with one another. This made it difficult to work with fully functional exported sites or multi-file projects.

That said, I want to update my original rating based on long-term use and—more importantly—the responsiveness of the development team.

I previously suggested that the platform add support for the Exercism CLI, since Exercism allows users to submit and work through coding exercises locally and is widely used for learning programming. I felt this tool would be a perfect fit for the educational use cases this platform already enables.

The developer listened directly to that feedback and implemented Exercism CLI support in a month or less.

That level of responsiveness genuinely matters. Many tools promise to “listen to users,” but few actually ship features that directly reflect user suggestions—especially on such a short timeline.

Because of this, I’m updating my review to 5 stars. I’m a bit addicted to the tool (especially when using it inside a minimalistic browser like Zen Browser), and I still believe this product is a steal, particularly considering that it delivers Replit-like functionality as a lifetime deal instead of a subscription.

I sincerely hope the product continues to improve, and based on my experience so far, I’m confident the team is actively moving it in the right direction.

- The UI/UX feels like the old days.  
- The Pro Shell packages are quite limited, they should encompass all common languages and packages.  
- The IDE design could be improved, consider using open-source options like Code Server (https://github.com/coder/code-server).  
- Should be able to set /mnt as default location.
- Support for creating files and folders from Pro Shell is needed, as I currently cannot initialize a virtual environment using the command python3 -m venv venv.

- The session durations are too short, requiring frequent logins.  
- There needs to be tagging, searching, and filtering features, as there will be many files in the future.  
- Implement public sharing with password protection.  
- Include an option to upload files and folders.  

By the way, great job to the team! I give you 5 tacos and hope these suggestions lead to innovative changes and enhancements for Shell.

comments.title: Turn GitHub repos into docs that stay synced
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

GitDoc is an essential tool in every developer's toolkit out because it does the one thing every developer says they will do later: write proper documentation.

I tested it by connecting GitDoc to a GitHub repo for a web app I built a couple of years ago. What impressed me is that it read the actual source files, not only the repo name, filenames, or README, and generated documentation that was substantively correct. I was able to publish the docs, and the result looked polished enough to share.

The bigger value is that GitDoc connects the parts of documentation that are usually split across different tools. It can generate docs from a repo, API spec, files, URLs, or prompts, then let you edit visually or in MDX, publish to a branded domain, and keep the documentation synced as the project changes which is a key differentiator in my opinion.

The AI side is also more interesting than a basic doc generator. GitDoc includes Ask AI search for visitors, plus API and MCP access, so tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or other AI workflows can query or work with the docs directly. This is extremely useful because more people now ask AI tools for answers instead of digging through documentation page by page.

I also like that GitDoc is using its own LLMs rather than relying entirely on the usual third party AI providers. The team said Gemini is only used as backup or for high availability, which should give them more control over cost, availability, and how the product develops.

One thing I would still clarify is BYOK access. The team said BYOK is already supported through MCP and that every app function can be used through your own key that way. 

Overall, GitDoc is an easy recommend if you build projects and push code to GitHub. It gives you a fast way to go from repo to published documentation, while also making those docs easier for users and AI tools to query.

comments.title: Still evaluating this tool, however...
comments.comment:
UPDATE 26/05/2026
I’ve updated this to 4 stars, as I spent the weekend working on it. With the help of Claude and the documentation, I found a workflow that has now resolved one of the scraping issues (Amazon).

The Notte workflow:
Use the CLI to explore interactively ← learn how the site works
Set up authentication if needed ← create a profile
Test interactions ← see what selectors/steps are needed
Export workflow code ← get a starting point
Adapt for functions ← use what we learned and the Function API

I’ve left off one star as I’m still testing. Also, when you create a function via the internal AI process, you can’t see the code in the deployed function. If it doesn’t work, you’re stuck and can’t edit it. If you manually create the functions, you can update them as needed.

PREVIOUS REVIEW

I've tried it on a couple of examples, and I've also implemented the API and CLI in a cloud computer called ZoComputer. And I've also tried using the interface directly in Notte. Unfortunately, in my test, it wasn't able to extract full information from eBay. However, I was able to get it to do it sort of one at a time through the CLI, but when going through the interface, it just didn't seem to want to do it properly. I was able to use BrowserAct to scrape eBay listings, so I'm not sure. 

I also wanted to scrape some reviews from iHerb, and admittedly it does have anti-bot measures, but yeah, it failed at that as well. However, I've used another tool called Chat4Data, which is an extension for the web browser, and it's able to scrape all the reviews, no problem. Admittedly, BrowserAct does have this problem as well, so it's not just one tool. But I can only evaluate tools that I've got against each other and rate them as appropriate. Also, looking at the billing, it's burnt $8 of LLM and I didn't get any data, so, alright, for testing maybe, but at the end of the day, that's a lot to burn and not get any proper result. 

I've also used Perplexity's Comet. While it's not scraping data and saving it, it can actually go through, say, all the iHerb reviews, and it can actually pick out all the positive and negative reviews, and I can ask it to isolate certain reviews and it will go and search. So, even though I'm not directly scraping data to download it, it is able to go and view that data and extract the data in terms of a summary, etc. 

So I will keep testing this tool, but for now I have to give it a middle‑of‑the‑road rating because I'm not quite sure—at least with the AppSumo deal—what benefit it has, since it seems unable to scrape certain sites.

comments.title: Great product
comments.comment:
I've spent thousands of dollars and hundreds (maybe thousands) of hours on web scraping and automations. Even on AppSumo I spent at least a thousand on RTILA alone but the truth is I always end up going back to N8N + something like SERP. Why? 

Because even if you know HTML, CSS, XHTML, JS, DOM, and all the other dev letter soup, you inevitably hit the dreaded selector nightmare. Ever heard of a fragile selector? Ever looked at Linkedins CSS? Iykyk. 

But now we have Ai, so yk, it should be easy, just tell ChatGPT or Claude to scrape HN or EDGAR or whatever you want to scrape no problem. Except of course hallucinations, virtually no logs and oh yeah no replays. 

I'm new to Notte but I like it. Here's a few reasons why. 
One, the UI is clean. That might not sound like a big deal but once you do your first 12 hour build session, you'll understand. 
Two, there's code if you want, no code if you don't. 
Three, session replays, like actual recorded videos of sessions, not just "ran at 8:03 pm on wed jan 4th. 

Then there is Anything API. Let's say you want data from FRED (or anywhere, this is just an example) that isn't exactly available in the API list, like an approximated fed shadow rate. I asked Gemini to write a prompt, then I pasted it into Anything API and got this out.

"shadow_rate_fed_funds — Notte Function Ready
What it does: Produces a continuous, investment-grade monetary policy stance series from 2008 to today. It mirrors the official FEDFUNDS rate when policy is normal, and switches to a 3-factor Gaussian term-structure model when the Fed hits the effective lower bound — using the yield curve slope (DGS10 − DGS2) and Fed balance sheet size (WALCL) to estimate the latent shadow rate."

That's a real endpoint with real logic, that I can now just use in my automations. Pretty sweet.
Not to mention basic captchas, fallback logic and personas for account creations. Also pretty sweet.

And if you need a trust signal, Notte has two. 
1) SOC 2 certification and 2) Backed by YC, yk the VC firm that backed Stripe and OpenAI.

Do not miss this deal, it's worth it, trust.
And to Andrea and Lucas, I like your product guys, it's cool. Keep it up!

comments.title: Found real issues I had missed
comments.comment:
I ran a scan on my site through MCP from my AI assistant: start it, poll the status, read the report. The report sorts findings by severity. Medium were a DMARC policy still on “none” and a missing X-Frame-Options header. Low ones included missing DNSSEC, COOP and CORP headers, and HSTS without includeSubDomains and preload. It also flagged a missing og:image on two pages, no structured data on my article index, no llms.txt, no terms of use and no accessibility statement.

Each finding names the affected URL, so I could check it against my source before changing anything. I’m fixing them now and will post the rescan result here. DNSSEC has to wait for me.

comments.title: Security checks with fixes your AI coding tool can use
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

One of the problems with vibe coding is that you can get an app working long before you know whether it is safe to put in front of users.

Vibe App Scanner gives you a way to check the app you have deployed by entering its URL. It runs more than 150 checks, including exposed API keys, authentication issues, database permissions, and other security problems that can easily go unnoticed when you're focused on getting the app working.

What I particularly like is how it handles the findings. Each issue comes with an explanation, supporting evidence, and suggested fixes you can give to your AI coding tool. You can take those instructions back to Lovable, Cursor, Claude Code, or your developer, make the changes, and scan again to check the results.

For someone developing software with AI, I can see this becoming part of the development process. You make changes to your app, deploy them, run a scan, and address anything new that comes up. It also supports MCP, so you can connect it to your AI coding tools without having to manually copy everything between applications.

In my test, the scanning and suggested fixes worked well. I initially flagged a couple of things that would make the product more useful, particularly PDF reports for sharing findings with clients and a REST API for connecting scans and reports to other tools. The team added both, and I confirmed they were available in my retest.

I would still want a proper security review for an application handling sensitive data, but Vibe App Scanner gives founders and developers a way to catch common issues during development and after deployment.

Overall, I like the direction of this product, particularly for people using AI to develop software who may not have a security background. The ability to scan a deployed app, get specific instructions for addressing the findings, and check the results after making changes is what makes Vibe App Scanner worth considering.

Let's be clear: Formly is good. I was able to create complex forms with variables, a points system, etc. This gives me great satisfaction and has impressed those around me (and my customers). I had to contact their support team, and their response was quick and clear. Very good!

They have a very interesting roadmap, and I can't wait for certain features to arrive (such as being able to put the first and last name fields on a single slide... having to make two slides for that is frankly very annoying).

However, Formly is not without a few bugs: text that disappears on its own, a text cursor that automatically goes to the end of the sentence when I want to correct a word at the beginning... in short, a bit annoying but not insurmountable.

Ultimately, Formly's biggest flaw is its interface: it seems a bit outdated to me, and it lacks some customisation options to make the forms really attractive. As it stands, they are functional. They're not ugly either, they're perfectly presentable... but they're not exactly ‘wow’ either. On the other hand, for connections and logical links, there is no simple graphical interface: everything is done with drop-down lists... and I promise you, you'd better be very well organised to find your way around! To give you an idea, I made a diagram in Freeform on my iPad before I started, because it's impossible to see clearly using only Formly's tools. What's more, if you include a points system, I'm warning you, it's going to be difficult to see clearly where you are. All these flaws cost it its fifth taco.

That said, Formly delivers on its promise. The app works, and I was able to do exactly what I had in mind, so let's not spoil our enjoyment. What's more (and once again), their roadmap announces some very interesting features that I can't wait to see!

For this price, compared to Typeform... frankly, it's worth it. I think that for some things (especially customisation), Formly is not in the same league... but then again, they may not have the same resources, and for the price paid here on AppSumo, it's ultimately a great deal! I recommend it, and I'm following its progress!

comments.title: A Promising App, But Still a Way to Go
comments.comment:
Formly has a lot great features, logical points and  scoring is the reason i chose it and for that its great so far. But a lot of catching up to do compared to more polished platforms like Typeform. It’s functional but far from being enjoyable or easy to use in its current form. I'm hoping the issues I have below can be resolved to turn this into 5 tacos.

Pros:
>> Affordable: It’s the only budget-friendly option for creating point-based quizzes, which makes it a viable choice for those needing this specific feature.
>> Easy to set up and publish: Following Typeform's UX, creating forms is pretty straight forward 

Cons and Areas for Improvement:
> Keyboard Navigation Issues: The 'Enter' key doesn’t work in Firefox to progress through the survey. This should be an easy fix but hasn’t been addressed yet.

> Desktop Formatting: The desktop version of the survey lacks proper formatting. Text spans across the screen, making it difficult to read, and the answer options are too wide, which detracts from the professionalism and readability of the survey.

> Custom Colors: While there’s an option to use custom colors, it relies on the system color picker (on macOS, for example). This tool doesn’t support hex codes (easily?) and is difficult to navigate in a browser. Additionally, it doesn't save custom color palettes, which makes branding tedious.

> Branding Limitations: There's not enough customization for incorporating a logo. The logo appears only at the top, in one size, and for some reason, it looks faded, which weakens brand presentation.

> Survey Navigation: The presence of the "OK" button after every question is frustrating. It would improve the user experience if respondents could automatically advance to the next question after making a selection, similar to how Typeform works.

> Lack of Analytics: The app doesn’t provide basic statistics like completion rates or time spent on each survey. These metrics are crucial for assessing survey performance.

> Results Screen: The results page is problematic — text is cut off, making it impossible to read which questions correspond to certain answers. This makes reviewing responses a headache.

>Inadequate Filtering: There's no ability to filter results based on specific questions, which is essential when using logic branches or segmenting respondents.

> Missing Insights: Unlike competitors, the app doesn’t offer a simple summary of responses, such as percentage breakdowns or other valuable insights. This is a missed opportunity for data analysis.

> Google Sheets Integration: I encountered issues when trying to connect and create a new Google Sheet for response collection. This integration could be smoother.

comments.title: Effortless Forms
comments.comment:
Formly is full of potential. It's not perfect, but it's a solid choice for the price. And with a bit more refinement, it could become the go-to form/survey builder for my business.

The Highlights:
1.	Creating Forms is a Breeze: Making my first form was pretty easy, using the provided examples. It was convenient since it was the one I needed, so I made duplicates of theirs to test.
2.	Client-Friendly Forms: The forms are so user-friendly; form-filling was a walk in the park even for my nontechy clients.
3.	Display Options Galore: Show the whole form or just one question at a time. Formly gives you that choice.
4.	Google Sheets Integration: Automatic syncing with Google Sheets is like my assistant minus the coffee breaks.
5.	File Uploads & Instant Quotes: Clients can upload files and if you use the quote option, they get an instant cost breakdown at the end of the form. Formly had me saying... "Yaaaaaaas, I'm that efficient!"
6.	Visuals: The option to use images on the form that can be magnified for closer viewing was fantastic for my needs! So smart and efficient! 
7.	Custom Redirects: Redirecting clients after completion is like being a digital traffic cop. I LOVE THIS FEATURE! 
8.	Tech Support: A special shoutout to Ash from tech support - the unsung hero in the digital shadows, making sure everything runs smoothly. 
9. Cname - being able to use my own brand's subdomain for the form was epic! It worked right away and was not hard to set- up(I do have some tech knowledge so that probably helped).

Every Rose Has Its Thorns…. So, The Not-So-Great:
1.	One File, One Question: The one-file-per-question limit feels a bit like juggling with one ball.…. Not so convenient.
2.	Customization: Room for Improvement: I know they have it on their roadmap. 
3.	A Few Glitches & UI Quirks: Some elements in Formly are still finding their feet. Hence the need for tech support… but their tech support ROCKS!
4.	PDF Output Needs Polishing: The PDF output looks a bit like a masterpiece drawn on a used napkin. It could use some dolling up since I sent it to clients to remind them of the choices they made on the quote forms.
5.	Stripe-Only Payments: While Formly's integration with Stripe is smooth, it's like being at an ice cream shop that only serves one flavor! The dream? A quote form with payment options as diverse as our tastes.

Formly has great potential: it is like a rough gem - not flawless, but with some polishing and updates, it could become our go-to tool for forms and quizzes.

1. If you want to have a document attached to the form, you have to include a PDF response and it has a link to the attachment inside the PDF.  Odd.  That seems a bit clunky, why not just have the file either attach to the response or have the link available directly in the response just like every other field?  That makes this tool less useful in many cases.

2. I'd like to be able to style the forms a little better.  I would love to be able to move fields next to each other so longer forms can avoid the "scroll".

3. The UI is a bit old school.  Functional though.  So not major.

Hope they address these soon.

comments.title: Simple app to create forms. Offline not working now.
comments.comment:
App works, but sometimes the admin backend is slow. Not the best user interface, looks outdated, but it’s really simple to create forms. GoZen forms was more complicated for me. Also, being able to send a PDF to the respondent with the answers is a great feature.

Regarding offline forms (was the main attractive feature for me), it’s not working. They mention they’ve updated web app and not mobile app for Android and iOS accordingly, so they recommend using web forms and not the mobile app and, therefore, no offline forms are available. They also said It might take some time before these features gets updated in the Apps to have them working offline. Be aware of this.

comments.title: Interesting tool
comments.comment:
Hello,
I just played with the tool. It looks interesting. It's workable for my needs, but I feel I need more than only 2 form templates to start with, to have many categories and templates, something like in Typeform or GoZen tools. 
The team is very responsive. Well appreciated!

comments.title: Good - could be Great

It is a good app, but would be great if one did not have to toggle between creating the form and rearranging, duplicating, or deleting a question. Good app that has the potential to be great.

comments.title: Good Value, but missing some basic features
