- Google integration worked the first time and every time so far
- Team completed my upgrade quickly within an hour of purchase 

CONS
- UI is very rudimentary and not very intuitive
- Not seeing a simple "drag and drop to reorder questions

I give this 4 of 5 tacos because of the unlimited form submission offer. With continual enhancements and strong team support this can be a 5 taco deal

comments.title: Great product and customer service!
comments.comment:
I bought this product because the lifetime deal was super attractive. I have been using TypeForm for my online consultation forms and questionnaire's for new leads, but I was frustrated by their limitations on the free plan and didn't want to pay a monthly subscription. The lifetime deal for Formly was fantastic value for money! 

I've set up a consultation form now and embedded it on my website and found it super easy to format. I did have some issues with the embed code, but found that an iFrame code worked better for me. Ashish from the support team helped with providing custom code for me to fix the issues I was seeing on the front-end of my site. 

A few things that would make me give Formly a 5-taco rating, instead of 4 are the following:

1. The ability to make changes to published forms without having to clear the history of responses. I did save these as PDFs on my computer when submitted by the respondent via the email notification, but it would be handy if this wasn't a necessity. 

2. TypeForm has the ability for respondents to use the tab or enter keys on their computer to move on to the next question, whereas Formly lacks this feature. This does make the whole user experience a bit disjointed, as users filling out the form via a laptop or desktop computer need to move their hands away from the keyboard to the mousepad or external mouse to shift the cursor to the 'next' button. This does interrupt the flow when entering information into the form fields.

3. More design options would be great, including custom HEX colours for branding. 

4. As a marketer, the ability to track these form submissions via conversion tracking for platforms such as Google Ads or Facebook Ads would be amazing! Currently, my work-around is embedding the forms on my own website's landing pages and redirecting to a thank-you page, and having the conversion tracking on my own domain. While this does work, it'd be a great additional feature.

Over and above that, it's a fantastic product and this lifetime deal is not something to miss out on, as it's great value for money! While the back-end interface is definitely not as 'pretty' as competitors like TypeForm, the end result is what you're after.

comments.title: Amazing Product!
comments.comment: I would give this product a 6 if I could.  Every time I look at it everything gets better. I know there is some free options like google forms this is in another league from that and should not be mentioned in the same conversation.  This is worth your time and money to look into it.  Truly Amazing!

comments.title: This app delivers on its promise
comments.comment:
I bought this app a while ago and finally got around to using it, and I was very impressed. It does exactly what it promises to do. It makes it easy to create forms. It makes it easy to add sophisticated logic, to create all types of conditional branching. The forms themselves look clean and well-designed. It's easy to hook up my own company branding.

One feature (that's new) that was particularly impressive – it collects partial responses. I had almost 60 full responses to my first form (a poll), and almost 25 partial responses that gave me very valuable information that would have otherwise been lost.

There are a lot of additional features that I haven't used yet, but they look quite powerful (e.g. score calculation, sending PDF results to participants, and more). 

Highly recommend this app. It's so well done, I even find myself looking for excuses to make a form – because the app makes it so easy and fun!

comments.title: Helped Turn an Idea Into a Speaking Opportunity
comments.comment: With a little help getting started, I used Formly to create an assessment that was simple, professional, and useful. Even better, that assessment ended up opening the door to a speaking opportunity. Pretty good return on a form.

comments.title: Does the job, support seals the deal
comments.comment: I've been using Formly for a while now for different forms in my business, and overall I'm happy with it. The tool itself does what it needs to do, but what really stands out is the customer support. I accidentally deleted a form and they were able to just restore it, quick and hassle free. That's the kind of support that makes you trust a tool.

comments.title: Great product with lots of potential
comments.comment:
I had purchased Formly back in 2022 and had trouble using it. Since it was only a Tier 1 AppSumo offering and I couldn't refund due to negligence on my part, I chalked it up as a learning experience. I saw it once again last year and noticed many improvements so this time I  made a Tier 3 purchase. I played around with it but didn't put it to the test until one of my client's WeForms market registration form failed and we couldn't get it fixed. 

So I decided to finally get serious with Formly and recreated the form for my client. With support help from the Formly folks I now had a form completed and ready to try out. Connecting it to Stripe just basically required me adding the client's Stripe email address to the form. Instantly, the form was working flawlessly. Using one of their templates allowed me to mimic the design of my client's website. The receipt generated and sent to the user is well laid out and clearly indicates the user's choice of markets they wished to attend along with the booth size, cost of each booth and the total. 

So here are a couple of suggestions to the Formly folks from my recent experience using their product. 
1. I got stuck when trying to connect the pricing to the booth size and location. I couldn't figure out what I had done wrong. I immediately went to their "Help" section where a list of Hep articles gave me a choice of subjects to choose from. After reading through them, nothing was helpful.
2. When the "Help" section didn't actually help, I looked for any "support@" email address in my account. Couldn't find any email contact form or "chat box" at all.
3. That led me to YouTube to see if they had any videos I could watch. My search for "Formly Forms" produced a list of videos, but they were either competitors or AppSumo marketers creating their own videos. Scrolling down the page I finally found one that Formly created just two months ago. It was a well done 13 second video highlighting "Hidden Fields", but didn't show how to add a hidden field. Again, showing how easily they added field that would be a better sales approach. That was all I could find. Still stuck with my problem.
4. Went to CHATGPT and asked it if Formly had a support email address. It displayed it right away and I was now able to write for some help. They responded immediately with an explanation of what to do. I tried it but still had trouble. I wrote back for more clarity and they encouraged me to try once more and make note of the "@" symbol placement. That's when I discovered that I had not hit my space bar to provide one space between the text and the field calculator. Once I did that, everything started working. One strike with my space bar on my keyboard was all I needed to finish my work.

This is my experience with Formly Forms. Now that I have a better understanding how everything works, I'm up and running ready to replace all my current forms Formly Forms. Good folks with a great product. Some videos like the one you just made and an easier way to communicate would be the icing on a nice cake!

comments.title: No brainer- super simple and the calculator forms are great!
comments.comment:
Definitely like it! It helps me do more than collect information. I can segment leads, ask better questions, connect everything to google sheets, and send people to the right next step automatically. I was tyring to do the same stuff with Google Forms and Sheets and this is 1000x more professional, easier to apply  logic to, and I like the grapsh you can add in teh thank you pages. I've used the webhook a few times for connections but i lie having it all feed to the google form and then deciphering users through that personally. I will also recommend that having it embed on my website has been really seamless as well for different offers. I don'tlove the way the structure is for the colors/ uploading of pictures for the forms but its minor and i try and keep them more for the form itself and using it for leads and client feedback. 
great product and i've done about 20 forms so far.

comments.title: Really, I love this!
comments.comment:
It's MUCH better than Google Translate and cheaper than Tally. I use it both for student tests and for company recruitment. The UI is still mediocre in places (e.g., previewing longer answers in the workbook—you have to download a PDF to read longer responses), but the developers are trying. A new version is now available, so it's great!

I highly recommend it—for both personal use (e.g., creating a survey for friends) and business use (recruitment, registration forms, tests, surveys, feedback).

comments.title: Amazing non Tech product and support
comments.comment: I have been using Formly for couple of months now. As a person who is totally 90% non-software savvy the Ai process in Formly works extremely well. The support is fast and always solves your problem. Amazing product!

comments.title: Should be in everyone's toolbox
comments.comment: I think Formly should be in everyone's toolbox. It's pretty cheap. They've passed the test of time on AppSumo. Sure, I wish that I could add additional fields to the forms and not just have one at a time. I wish there was some additional customization in there. Maybe they'll get there one day. But I've used this thing for even doing stuff like date polls for events at the boat club and things that it probably wasn't even intended for. It's great that you can either store it to Google Sheets or something else, or you can just save it right within Formly itself. So works for me. Doesn't cost much. Support, not always as fast as I'd like in every ash. But they get back to you. I think their intentions are in the right place. And I think it's a product that everybody should have.

comments.title: Great Tool for Agency
comments.comment: The interface feels simple, clean, and easy to understand, even if you are not very technical. I really like that it gives enough flexibility to build different types of forms for clients, lead generation, feedback, and general business use.

comments.title: One of the best deals on AppSumo, full stop.
comments.comment:
I ran into an issue where Formly's AI builder wasn't setting up the logic as requested and the support team stepped in, looked at it, fixed the underlying AI functions, and had everything working on the first try. All with a smile. 

My personal wish would be more control over colors, shapes, fonts, spacing and how forms render on mobile. But given the feature set already delivered, there's no honest way to rate this anything less than 5 tacos. Keep up the good work, Formly!

comments.title: I've been really impressed
comments.comment:
I'd been looking for an alternative to QuestionScout, Typeform, and many others that have recurring monthly costs and I've been really happy with Formly so far. 

I was able to have a 1:1 onboarding call with one of the team members to get a full walkthrough of the current features and hear what's in store on the roadmap as well. It was extremely helpful as I began implementing surveys myself as I'd been able to see what's possible in the onboarding. I wasn't just able to migrate versions of my current surveys and quizzes but take them to the next level.

I've now been using it for a month and a half - the tool has been working reliably and the layout is very easy to use, even with the logic. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a great tool for forms, surveys, and quizzes.

comments.title: A support that met my needs perfectly
comments.comment:
I requested a meeting to receive advice on building my quiz, which is a bit more complex than the templates.

I received excellent support from Sha (I believe, if I remember correctly), and he answered my questions and offered solutions.
I am very satisfied with the support I received and the product!

comments.title: Great Service
comments.comment: Ash was great in walking through the software and did a fantastic job explaining all of the features!

comments.title: Very good
comments.comment:
I purchased Formly at Tier 2, Lifetime, so I could use it on several sites without the branding or having to worry about number of submissions or number of forms since I would use the form to offer promotions and ask for information for different purposes. At first I found things to be confusing, since there aren't that many YouTube tutorial videos and the taxonomy is a little clunky to me. After testing one form for several hours I figured out how to create very visually appealing forms. A day or two later I scheduled a free Zoom call with one the developers. He was extremely polite and informative and explained everything to me: how to use reCaptcha correctly, how to use other features to further block spam such as email verification, why my attempts at using conditional logic before weren't working, how to set up the email notification properly, and so forth. 

So, after taking some time to get used to the taxonomy, I give it a big thumb's up. Web developers can use the form not just as a contact form but as a way to use conditional logic, routing, and grading responses to screen out clients with low budgets and high expectations; you could use it to have client profiles or surveys, and do it all elegantly.

comments.title: Clean UI, Strong Core Features & Outstanding Support
comments.comment:
I have been using Formly for assessment-based surveys, and overall, it’s a very solid platform. The UI is excellent...clean, modern, and very intuitive. There’s no steep learning curve to get started. The results dashboard is impressive, especially the graphical breakdowns. The charts and visual summaries look professional and are great for quick analysis.

That said, there are a few limitations, particularly for more complex corporate use cases. If you require extensive calculations or highly complicated scoring logic, the setup can become cumbersome. Also, while category scores can be shown graphically, subcategory averages are limited to text format. A visual breakdown at the subcategory level would significantly enhance reporting.

The platform generates a PDF that includes all survey questions and the end-screen results, but customization options are limited. For my use case, this makes the PDF less practical. However, to be fair, limited PDF customization is common across many survey platforms.

Where Formly truly stands out is customer service. I had a query, and we quickly jumped on a call to clarify everything. The support team is responsive, helpful, and genuinely invested in user success.

Despite the shortcomings, I’m still giving it 5/5 because the core product is strong, the UX is excellent, and the team behind it is top-notch. With future enhancements, this app has the potential to become even more powerful. Highly recommended.

comments.title: Formly Keeps Every Form Lovely
comments.comment:
Formly has a very clean and easy-to-use UI. Creating forms feels smooth and everything is well organised, so it saves a lot of time. The logic and automation features are very powerful and helped us collect and filter the right data without manual effort.

What really impressed me was the support — the team even joined a Zoom call to help us set things up and clarify our doubts. That level of support makes a big difference. Highly recommended.

comments.title: FORMLY - A FORMULA FOR ALL OF YOUR FORMS, QUIZZES, EVALUATIONS, ASSESSMENTS (AND MORE)!
comments.comment:
I had an excellent experience with Formly. Ash, the representative who guided my demo, was knowledgeable, patient, and fully present throughout our conversation. He answered every question directly, never rushed the process, and created a very pleasant, professional atmosphere.

Formly itself is an impressive platform. I recommend the product without hesitation. It is likely the last form‑producing software I will ever need to purchase. The range of options is outstanding — forms, quizzes, assessments, and more — all customizable to be fun, formal, or funky depending on your needs or whims.

In the future, I would be thrilled if they added permission control for multiple users. If that becomes available, I would upgrade immediately. Overall, Formly delivers power, flexibility, and ease of use. A fantastic tool with fantastic support.

Blessings,
LadyB~

public_name: Bit Form – WordPress Form Builder Plugin

comments.title: Close to Perfect
comments.comment:
This is really a great tool and close to perfect. But there is one super annoying thing for us in the USA, country codes. 

The phone number field should allow you to disable all country codes with a single click, or not have country codes in the pattern. 

I don't want to have to setup a number field with a custom Regex. I want to be able to have like XXX-XXX-XXXX   

Additionally the phone number box should not let you type more than the numbers allowed in your mask pattern. 

I think small things like this, will make it more mass appeal for those in the states.

comments.title: Very good with some caveats
comments.comment: This product is very good for what it is, a full featured WordPress forms plugin with lots of integrations and low latency/bloat on your pages. I want to give it 5 stars but I have a few small grievances about it that bring it down to a 4. The API documentation is not that great. So it looks like the tool is limited, but in actuality, it's a full fledged API. I almost returned it until I happened upon one of the videos where I was able to reason that I could use this other API endpoint for what I wanted. It wasn't in the video, but it led me to it. I have some minor issues with the formatting and styling of things and I have issues with the inability to assign custom field names to the field, but overall I'm satisfied with the purchase. I wish the ability to specify column widths was easier, instead of having to drag everything onto the page and then reducing the size to the appropriate width. It's mildly infuriating that you don't know the full width of the form to know how to break it into even columns. Lots of little things like that that make it just a touch more annoying to use. It's definitely not as polished as some of the bigger named forms plugins for WordPress, but what you get for the money, especially if you're willing to do a little work more than make up for it.

comments.title: Loving it!
comments.comment: I just bought this product and I'm loving it so far, I will give more updates later!

comments.title: Easy to use - but doesn't work
comments.comment:
The ease of use was excellent for the product, however, I ran into a number of problems with the install including: 
IP blocking - when using the plugin my entire site stopped working with all my websites 
Save Button - It simply doesn't work, unable to save the forms that I'm building 
I'm using WP 6.8.2 - I have reached out to the developer, and hopefully they can come up with a fix as it is one of the better plugins I've used.

**Thanks to the brilliant response from the team, they have managed to fix what was going on and now the plugin is working as it should. Well done team!**

comments.title: Way too many bugs unfortunately
comments.comment:
I tried this plugin out for 4 hours and was really impressed by the simplicity and functionality, but there are way too many bugs. I installed it on a website, migrated that to a new one and got some fatal error. I solved that by removing all forms and redoing the forms.

Then another bug occured: entries are saved and counted even after it's been removed.

Then another bug: when doing a multi-step form and pressing 'enter' on the keyboard on the first step, the form is submitted instead of going to step #2.

Also some of the logic is set on each form and some of the logic is global, which is fine, but for example the redirects we should be able to choose a global redirect to a thank you form, instead of having to go to the specific form and choose there. It creates too much extra work when having multiple forms. 

And above all other bugs, the most annoying thing is that 10-20% of the form submits are being sent to my mailbox, even though I set up SMTP, use the same top domain as sender.

I would love if this plugin actually worked because it looked great at the beginning, but 4 hours in and I've encountered 10 bugs already.

Edit: Changed my rating from 1 to 4 because of the reply from the creator. Probably worth another shot at some point.

comments.title: Everything other Forms gave us, without the yearly bill, plus support that actually answers
comments.comment:
I picked Bit Form up on the previous AppSumo deal, so this is not a first impression. It has been running the enquiry flow of our website for months, and since the deal is back I thought the honest long version might be more useful than another five star line.

We run a small education and therapy centre in Zagreb. Our website is the main way people reach us, so the forms are not decoration. They are the business. We came from WPForms. It worked, but every renewal cost more for capabilities we had long stopped considering advanced, and that was the reason we started looking.

The forms themselves were never the point. Anyone can put a name and an email field on a page. What we needed was the logic behind them.

Our forms decide what to show depending on what the person selects. They send a different confirmation depending on which programme someone signs up for. They notify the right person on our side, separately and with different wording from what the visitor receives. They carry a hidden field so we know which page an enquiry came from, which turned out to matter far more than we expected. None of that required a separate paid add on per capability, which is precisely what we were escaping.

Four things turned out better than expected.

Conditional logic is genuinely conditional. Fields, sections and entire email templates respond to what the user selected, not merely field visibility.

Autoresponders and admin notifications are separate templates, and each carries its own conditions. One form, several outcomes, no duplicated forms to keep in sync.

Dynamic options. Our course dropdown is populated live from the events we publish on the site. We change a date in one place and every form reflects it at once. There is no list to maintain by hand and nothing goes stale, which for a centre that reschedules courses is worth the price on its own.

The builder is quick and stays out of your way. Duplicating a form and adapting it is a matter of minutes.

Support deserves its own paragraph. I opened a ticket about a narrow limitation: filtering an imported post list by taxonomy term. The answer came quickly, from someone who had clearly read the question, tested it, and sent working code instead of a link to a generic article. When it turned out the capability did not exist yet, they said so plainly and logged it for a future release rather than talking around it. Fast, technical and honest at the same time is rarer than it should be.

So no, it is not perfect. That taxonomy filter is still on my wish list. But everything our enquiry flow actually stands on works, works reliably, and no longer arrives with an invoice every year.

What I value most, after months of it, is that Bit Form was clearly built by people who use forms themselves. The capabilities are the ones you actually reach for, the defaults are sensible, and the team answers like engineers who care whether your site works. It has quietly become one of the few plugins on our site that I never have to think about, and for a tool that carries every enquiry we receive, that is the highest compliment I can pay it. Thank you to the Bit Apps team for building it properly and for standing behind it.

comments.title: Absolutely the best. The dark horse of WordPress form plugins, and go check-out Bit-Flows its INSANE!
comments.comment:
I'm absolutely in LOVE with everything that Bitapps.pro has been building. 

I've since bought maxed-out plans for all of their WordPress Plugins, which includes Bit-Form here. I've been working in WordPress for 20 years now and Bit-Form BY FAR is my absolute favorite. 

I honestly own almost all other major form plugins and I've worked with each of them for years, so I'm saying from experience that Bit-Form is currently the best-fit for me, and you'll likely love it as well. 

The BitApps Team (the devs behind Bit-Form) are always fast to respond to any questions whether its sales-related or technical support, and they're friendly and provide expert-level and highly-professional responses. 

The plugins get frequent feature-updates and patches, and I had zero issues moving into WordPress 7.0 on day 1. 

BitApps also develops Bit-Integrations and Bit-Flows, two plugins of which I could not go without now. 

Ever wonder how to easily and almost instantly link-together what would normally be incompatible plugins and webhook information that is moving around your Wordpress site, AND ALSO include Zapier-like or n8n-like integration, all within your own WordPress website without even slowing your site down? Enter Bit-Flows. 

This Bit-Form plugin seamlessly integrates and sends data into several other WordPress and 3rd party tools, but Bit-Form ALSO can connect natively to another plugin known as Bit-Integrations which then connects with a ton of other critical SaaS platforms and other WordPress 3rd-Party plugins with one app at a time or one action-at-atime typically...

HOWEVER with the Bit-Flows plugin, you can literally take one action on your website, including a Bit-Form submission, and then trigger as many actions and integrations that you could possibly imagine within your own WordPress website, or with other external 3rd-party SaaS platforms and providers..its literally a Zapier or Pabbly for your own self-hosted website! 

The customization within Bit-Form is guaranteed to help you create beautiful forms that easily match your website's design, its intuitive to learn how to use the form-builder with just spending a little time playing around with it. 

When you factor-in all of the WordPress plugins and 3rd-party services that Bit-Forms natively integrates with, AND factor-in the other BitApps plugins like Bit-Flows which offers the most insane WordPress integration and automation, and even the very cool BitAssist plugin which is a native Ai chatbot on your site...you can't go wrong. 

I can't even begin to think about building another Wordpress site without Bit-Form or without Bit-Flows, and I'm not joking. 

I recommend Bit-Form 110% to anyone and everyone with a WordPress site. You cannot go wrong with this purchase, and I wish the BitApps Team the absolute best...I need you folks to stick around forever and to flourish and build even more incredible WordPress apps. 

The only feature-request I have for Bit-Form would be to please add a pop-up form feature. However, in the meantime I got the plugin named PopupKit, and I have all of its fields mapped to my Bit-Flows plugin perfectly in order to have a nice newsletter-signup pop-up form on my website and sending the data to my Noptin Newsletter plugin.

Thanks again for the world-class WordPress plugins! A++++!

comments.title: Simple, and it works!
comments.comment:
I work with Elementor, and for basic forms I usually rely on the Elementor Form widget. For more advanced and slightly more complex use cases, however, I prefer BitForm. I’m simply a big fan of drag-and-drop systems and strongly dislike outdated solutions like Contact Form 7.
With a bit of research and thanks to the clear tutorials on their website and YouTube, I was up and running quickly. The fact that they offer a Mollie integration is a big plus. Surprisingly, many other form builders don’t support this. Their support team is also quite responsive and helpful. (But they can respond a little quicker if you ask me)

Hopefully, in the future, they’ll find a way to import contacts from other forms into a BitForm database. Both my clients and I may want to switch from one form builder to another if it turns out to be a better fit. That would be an amazing feature.

I truly hope they continue improving BitForms, and I’m already looking forward to other complementary BitApps, such as BitIntegrations!

comments.title: the best plugin in a long-long time
comments.comment:
As someone who has been in the web development business for a long time, I can say that Bit Form is a breath of fresh air. It is incredibly fast, lightweight, and the UI is so intuitive that it makes complex form-building a breeze.

I’m currently using the Pro version on my latest project, umjetneograde.com, and the integration with Divi 5 is flawless. What sets it apart is the speed — it doesn't bloat the site like most other form builders. The conditional logic and built-in integrations work perfectly, saving me hours of manual work and additional third-party connectors.

If you are looking for a professional, stable, and high-performance form builder that actually respects your server resources, this is it. Best plugin in a long-long time!

comments.title: MetaSurvey: a fresh, interactive take on surveys
comments.comment:
Full review here:
https://youtu.be/q-eZ-NMTmdM

I took an initial look at MetaSurvey, a survey builder available on AppSumo. Its standout feature is the swipe-style survey experience: respondents move through questions one at a time, a bit like using a dating app. It gives surveys a more interactive feel than a conventional form and could be a good fit when you want to make answering quick and engaging.

I explored several question formats and tried creating a survey with the AI generator. My first prompt produced a survey in German, so I had to refine the instructions and specify that I wanted English. After that, it created a useful survey about lifetime deals. The AI can be a helpful way to get started, but I’d check the output and be specific about the language and content you need.

I also connected the survey to Google Sheets to see how responses are collected, and looked at the customisation and sharing options. The product includes ways to share or embed a survey, create a QR code, randomise questions and use conditional logic. Those options give you room to adapt a survey to different audiences and workflows.

My first impression is that MetaSurvey is straightforward to explore and offers a distinctive presentation style. The swipe format is its clearest point of difference, while AI generation and Google Sheets integration can help with creating a survey and working with responses.

This was an initial hands-on look rather than an in-depth or long-term review, so I can’t speak to how it performs at scale or how reliable every feature is in regular use. I’d recommend trying the builder with a real example, checking the AI-generated questions carefully, and making sure the survey and response workflow suit your needs before committing.

Overall, MetaSurvey looks like an interesting option if you want surveys to feel more interactive than a standard form. The AI gave me a language hiccup at first, but a clearer prompt improved the result. Worth exploring if the swipe-style experience appeals to you; just treat this as an early impression rather than a full product verdict.

comments.title: Very nice app but I am having trouble obtaining consent to the privacy policy of my surveys.
comments.comment:
I have tried out a  survey and find it very easy to put in the questions and really like the layout, style and user experience for those filling in the questionnaire. 

In order to request personal data and remain GDPR compliant, I must obtain consent to the privacy policy. To do this, it is important that participants in my survey are able to view it beforehand. Unfortunately, I have not yet found a way to display these privacy terms before the yes/no consent question. There is no way to link the document in the question, e.g., as a PDF file, or to insert a link that would open a page with the terms and conditions before the respondent answers. 

For me, the possible applications of MetaSurvey therefore remain very limited to completely anonymous data for the time being.

This significantly reduces the value of the product for me. I hope that there will soon be an update with a solution to this problem or a working guide for a workaround.

comments.title: Very Good...So Close to Being Great
comments.comment:
I actually purchased this tool and stacked 3 Tacos...then returned it. Then purchased it again. This is how desperate I am for a good, simple, effective survey tool that I could use with audiences when I speak. 

The interface is good and the surveys looks great on a mobile device. The Pabbly integration works fine and I have my survey setup to 

This tool has the potential to be AMAZING, but there are some really critical, simple things that are currently missing. 

1. NO FIRST/LAST NAME: There is no option for a FIRST NAME and LAST NAME question. You have to set these up as two separate questions, which feels cumbersome to users. 

2. CAN'T CHANGE QUESTION NAMES: DO NOT start from a template if you plan to do any integrations. The names of the questions are hard-coded when the survey is created and you can't change the names which makes integrating through Pabbly or anywhere else confusing. Just start from scratch and name your questions correctly. You can change the question for the user but it doesn't change behind the scenes.

3. NO HIDDEN QUESTIONS or DEFAULTS: I really need to be able to have a hidden question with a default value so I can pull that through my integration. That's not an option.

4. MULTICHOICE QUESTIONS ARE REQUIRED: If you do a pick list, at least one value has to be selected. My preference would be to have the question as optional, but instead, I have to add a "no thanks" choice, which is a shame.

I'm going to keep going with this platform and hope that they make the tiny tweaks needed to make this tool a real competitor! Thanks for offering a very good tool. :)

comments.title: Excellent survey tool
comments.comment:
5 Tasty Tacos!!
I purchased this with doing a few simple surveys in mind.

My daughter is starting a Garden Consulting business and asked if I could create a fact finding survey. I took a look at what another person did, and MetaSurvey allowed me to take things 10 steps forward!

I ended up with 35 questions, which may sound like a lot, but the swipe right/left, multiple choice and conditional logic make the survey custom to each user.

For example. If I ask a question about a raised garden beds, they can say no to a huge setup, skipping 5 photos. The conditional logic lands them on the next group of photos to say yes/no to. Nice! She knows exactly what the customer likes, and the budget!

MetaSurvey creates a real quality survey. You have several choices on how to display it. I chose a small button at the top of he page that engages a popup. At the end of her survey, I send the person to book a 15 minute call.

Cons: I was a little disappointed that I had to pay $15 a month for Google sheets integration. That was offset by the fact that they DO provide Webhooks. It took me about 10 minutes to setup the google sheet with webhooks and take the survey! Boom, I'm a happy camper now.

If you are a teacher looking to do a quick quiz, set up a formula on the last cell of your sheet to grade and assign a number and a letter grade! 

Note: the time format the survey is sent over is in ISO 8601 (e.g., 2024-04-02T18:24:27.000Z). If the time the survey taken is important, google "ISO-8601 String to Date in Google Sheets cell" and you will get a starting point for a long calculation to convert it.

comments.title: A Phenomenal SaaS - Ideal for Creating Quiz Funnels - My top purchase for where it is now, and for where it's heading
comments.comment:
***The Pros****
Very rarely am I compelled to leave this level of feedback.  KiwiForms has become my number one purchase on AppSumo. This is due to its versatility, functionality and the productivity and professionalism of the team behind it.

I’m a top tier purchaser, and have invested in some AppSumo lifetime powerhouses.  I’ve recently completed stress testing KiwiForms, and it is extremely intuitive, with a very extensive feature set.  I’ve found team Kiwi, especially receptive to my feature suggestions, and the issues I’ve had with system glitches were swiftly ironed out.  This product started strong but it’s now an absolute beast, and the direction its development team are heading, makes this one of my greatest investments on AppSumo.

My preference, is to construct my branching logic forms manually.  That said, even without it's AI functionality, I’d still say tier 3 is priced extremely competitively as a lifetime product.  However, with its AI features, such as its MCP server, I can utilise ChatGBT via Codex and dramatically lessen my workload when doing less bespoke projects.

It has so many potential uses, but as a quiz funnel it is phenomenal. The following are just three of the many features that make KiwiForms absolutely powerful for my use case:

Black listing
* Able to black list respondents by their form outcome.

Email verification
* Respondents are prevented from going any further in a form until they verify their email.

Stripe Payments
* Adding a payment field to your forms, so form respondents can make a payment.

***The Cons****
The only real drawback is that you can only map a total of 5 subdomains.  After speaking with their leadership team, this current restriction is understandable.  In my opinion, not offering unlimited domain mapping, is a drawback for agencies wanting to offer a tailored bespoke service to their clients.

***The workaround ****
That said, a great work around is purchasing a unique generic domain and then using their 'custom link' feature, where you can put your clients' business names as the slug (e.g. just4.you/client’s business name).  You can then give your clients an exclusive service without using up your domains.  You can also use their ‘embed form in webpage’ feature, to help towards offering a premium service to your clients.

Also, when possible, it would be great to have a pay-as-you-go domain mapping model, to support our clients, where we pay per month for each extra domain, only when needed.  That way, we can provide a service for some clients who want bespoke forms presented on their chosen domains.

***The conclusion****
This is an extremely versatile and valuable piece of technology, that allows you to create intricate forms with advanced branching logic, easily.  It has superb ergonomics and a very self-explanatory user-interface.  This makes it apparent that their team has put a lot of time and effort into providing a great user-experience.  Which makes it easier for us to create forms that also give respondents a great user experience.

Bespoke quiz funnels are the future, and to have an instrument like this that creates the bones of these intelligent forms, so seamlessly, is a must.  My advice is to go unlimited with tier 3, and get KiwiForms whilst you can.  I’m pretty certain that you’d never get it for this price again, and I'd be surprised to see it show up as a lifetime deal once this offer ends.

To get an idea of how powerful this piece of software is, go to their 'Help center' (https://kiwiform.com/help), and manually browse or use their search function.

The first thing that stood out was the overall usability. The interface is clean, intuitive and visually appealing. Anyone familiar with Typeform will feel at home almost immediately, making the learning curve quite short.

With that in mind, there are two particular elements of my interaction with KiwiForm so far that I feel deserve particular mention:

1. Typeform import is phenomenal.
Importing an existing Typeform into KiwiForm takes just seconds - and I literally mean one or two seconds, not even five or ten! Being able to initiate this migration by simply pasting a Typeform URL and then sitting back as a near-perfect functional replication of the form is created is actually very cool. Moreover, given I literally have hundreds of Typeform forms, and many of these are ones I would like to bring into KiwiForm, it's reducing the time it takes to do this. (Although I must say, having a bulk import mechanism would be great too!)

2. Customer support is exceptional.
OK - now I guess we all know that no software platform gets everything right, so for me, the measure of a great solution is one in which the support team are highly responsive. The good news is that in this regard, my experience with KiwiForm's support channel has already been genuinely impressive. While migrating some of my more complex forms, I discovered that matrix-style questions were not importing correctly, so I reported this issue through KiwiForm's support channel, and then went about my day, expecting to receive an overnight message. At best. You can imagine my surprise then, when within half an hour the team had responded, identified the cause, advised that a fix would be available within 24 hours, and then delivered exactly as promised. They even followed up to let me know the update had been deployed. That level of responsiveness is rare. Even Apple struggles to work that quickly! In any case, while I appreciate that it may become more difficult for KiwiForm to maintain this level of responsiveness as their company grows, it demonstrates that the team genuinely cares about their product and their customers.

Of course, like any relatively new platform, there are still a few things I'd love to see improved. For example, I'd like more flexibility in resizing logos and images, particularly when they're imported from Typeform. I also noticed that every imported form generated its own template, even though around 90% of my Typeforms shared the same template. It means I have a little housekeeping to do, but it's hardly a deal-breaker. In fact, I've found it quicker in many cases to simply create a new template in KiwiForm and then apply this.

Overall, my experience has been fabulous. If the platform continues to perform as it has during my first week, I'll be cancelling my Typeform subscription within the next couple of months without hesitation.

For me, this is an easy 5 tacos. Congratulations to the KiwiForm team - you've built an impressive product, and I can't wait to see where you take it next

comments.title: A working extension after 84 iterations: where PlugThis helps, and where Codex matters
comments.comment:
Can PlugThis build a complex Chrome extension? In my experience, yes. Can it independently identify and fix every issue? Not yet.
I use the Tier 4 lifetime license to develop Page Intelligence: page-text extraction, screenshot and region OCR, processing extracted content including tables, summarization, rewriting, and translation. The extension’s AI features run locally through Chrome’s built-in AI capabilities.
Reaching the current working version took 84 iterations. These included adding features, refining behavior, and fixing bugs—not 84 attempts to fix one problem. Simpler extensions should require considerably less work, although this is one project’s experience, not a general benchmark.
What works well
PlugThis produces a complete extension package: project structure, manifest, scripts, interface, and design. That saves considerable effort compared with assembling separate pieces yourself. It provides browser installation, downloadable source archives, and GitHub export.
One-click project duplication is particularly useful: I can preserve a working version and experiment with a copy. Settings also let me upload my own Extension Icon instead of keeping the platform-generated one.
With sufficiently precise instructions, PlugThis can implement targeted fixes in a relatively complex project. We successfully developed capture and OCR, text processing, and consistent control over the language of generated results.
Where it falls short
The built-in Preview could not test my core AI functionality. It displayed:
“Chrome Built-in AI cannot be tested in PlugThis Preview. Load the exported extension in Chrome for real testing.”
Consequently, testing required exporting the project, updating the installed extension, and checking it in Chrome. This limitation applies to my built-in-AI scenario; it does not mean Preview is useless for every extension.
Compound requests were sometimes implemented only partially, despite completion messages. Smaller, coherent tasks worked better: make a change, inspect the exported code, test it, then continue.
Some bugs required external code analysis. For example, changing the result language did not update the callback used for region capture, so it kept using the previous setting. Codex identified the cause and prepared a precise correction request; PlugThis implemented the fix. We then verified the exported code and actual browser behavior.
GitHub export failed in my case. There is also no reverse synchronization in the workflow available to me: repository changes cannot automatically flow back into the PlugThis project. Downloaded code can be developed independently, but continuing inside PlugThis requires manually transferring external changes.
Version management is another inconvenience: new iterations increment the version in the manifest, but the version displayed in project Settings does not stay synchronized and needs manual editing.
Could I use Codex without PlugThis?
Yes. Codex can help create the extension structure, write code, build it, and debug it without PlugThis. Real Chrome testing is still necessary. PlugThis is therefore a convenience and workflow choice, not a technical requirement.
Its value to me is the extension-focused environment: project generation, interface design, installation packaging, and iterative development in one place.
The two-tool approach also offers a potential cost advantage. I use Codex for diagnosis, review, and precise implementation instructions, while delegating code changes to PlugThis within my prepaid lifetime-plan allowances. This can conserve comparatively expensive Codex tokens or usage allowances, depending on the plan. I have not measured the savings, and repeated reviews and transfers still consume resources.
This division of work made complex development more manageable, but neither tool guarantees correctness. If you are comfortable managing code, builds, and Git directly, working solely with Codex may be simpler. If you prefer an integrated extension-building environment, PlugThis provides meaningful value.
My rating: 4 out of 5
PlugThis helped me produce a working extension with substantial functionality. I deduct one point for incomplete execution of some requests, the need for external debugging, GitHub workflow limitations, and version-management friction.
It is a useful development tool, but my experience calls for active testing and technical oversight—not just describing an idea and assuming the finished code is correct.

comments.title: De la frustración inicial a una herramienta que recomiendo al 100%

Adquirí PlugThis con el objetivo de optimizar mis flujos de trabajo mediante la creación de extensiones personalizadas para el navegador. Sin embargo, mi primera experiencia fue bastante frustrante. Intenté desarrollar una extensión para automatizar tareas en un portal gubernamental de Mexico (un entorno con inicio de sesión y validaciones complejas). Tras 9 o 10 intentos fallidos, el código se complicó y no lograba funcionar. Al ver que con Claude lo había conseguido en solo 3 indicaciones, me sentí decepcionado y consideré seriamente solicitar un reembolso.

Decidí escribir al soporte explicando mi situación y mis limitaciones con el idioma inglés. La respuesta que recibí de Udaya marcó una diferencia total y cambió por completo mi perspectiva sobre el producto:

Diagnóstico técnico transparente y preciso: En lugar de evasivas genéricas, Udaya analizó personalmente los registros de mis compilaciones y me explicó con exactitud qué había fallado: al estar la página protegida tras un login, la IA estaba "trabajando a ciegas", deduciendo erróneamente que los elementos estaban dentro de un iframe, lo que encadenó varios intentos innecesarios para corregir esa suposición.

Instrucciones claras y prácticas: Me guio paso a paso para inspeccionar el DOM, extraer el outerHTML del contenedor real y limpiar el código de la lógica de frames residual, permitiendo que la IA trabajara sobre la estructura exacta de la página en lugar de adivinar.

Honestidad comercial y respaldo total: No solo me ofreció tramitar el reembolso sin discusiones si no lográbamos que funcionara, sino que me reintegró créditos en dos ocasiones distintas para compensar todas las generaciones gastadas en el camino equivocado.

Siguiendo las indicaciones y proporcionando el HTML directo del portal, la extensión quedó perfectamente funcional. El sistema aprovechó las configuraciones previas que ya estaban bien resueltas y eliminó las dependencias innecesarias de inmediato.

Conclusión
PlugThis AI no es simplemente un generador de extensiones; es un entorno potente que, cuando se alimenta con el contexto adecuado (especialmente en páginas privadas o dinámicas), entrega resultados robustos y limpios.

Hoy en día recomiendo ampliamente PlugThis AI por dos razones fundamentales:

Su potencial técnico: Una vez entendida la dinámica de suministrar la estructura real de páginas privadas, ahorra muchísimo tiempo de desarrollo.

La calidad humana y el soporte de Udaya: En un mercado saturado de herramientas con atención automatizada, encontrar un fundador o soporte técnico que revise tus logs, te explique el origen del error, te reembolse los créditos y te acompañe hasta ver la solución andando, es un valor incalculable.

Gracias Udaya

Sin duda, una inversión que vale la pena.

comments.title: MetaSurvey: a fresh, interactive take on surveys
comments.comment:
Full review here:
https://youtu.be/q-eZ-NMTmdM

I took an initial look at MetaSurvey, a survey builder available on AppSumo. Its standout feature is the swipe-style survey experience: respondents move through questions one at a time, a bit like using a dating app. It gives surveys a more interactive feel than a conventional form and could be a good fit when you want to make answering quick and engaging.

I explored several question formats and tried creating a survey with the AI generator. My first prompt produced a survey in German, so I had to refine the instructions and specify that I wanted English. After that, it created a useful survey about lifetime deals. The AI can be a helpful way to get started, but I’d check the output and be specific about the language and content you need.

I also connected the survey to Google Sheets to see how responses are collected, and looked at the customisation and sharing options. The product includes ways to share or embed a survey, create a QR code, randomise questions and use conditional logic. Those options give you room to adapt a survey to different audiences and workflows.

My first impression is that MetaSurvey is straightforward to explore and offers a distinctive presentation style. The swipe format is its clearest point of difference, while AI generation and Google Sheets integration can help with creating a survey and working with responses.

This was an initial hands-on look rather than an in-depth or long-term review, so I can’t speak to how it performs at scale or how reliable every feature is in regular use. I’d recommend trying the builder with a real example, checking the AI-generated questions carefully, and making sure the survey and response workflow suit your needs before committing.

Overall, MetaSurvey looks like an interesting option if you want surveys to feel more interactive than a standard form. The AI gave me a language hiccup at first, but a clearer prompt improved the result. Worth exploring if the swipe-style experience appeals to you; just treat this as an early impression rather than a full product verdict.

comments.title: Very nice app but I am having trouble obtaining consent to the privacy policy of my surveys.
comments.comment:
I have tried out a  survey and find it very easy to put in the questions and really like the layout, style and user experience for those filling in the questionnaire. 

In order to request personal data and remain GDPR compliant, I must obtain consent to the privacy policy. To do this, it is important that participants in my survey are able to view it beforehand. Unfortunately, I have not yet found a way to display these privacy terms before the yes/no consent question. There is no way to link the document in the question, e.g., as a PDF file, or to insert a link that would open a page with the terms and conditions before the respondent answers. 

For me, the possible applications of MetaSurvey therefore remain very limited to completely anonymous data for the time being.

This significantly reduces the value of the product for me. I hope that there will soon be an update with a solution to this problem or a working guide for a workaround.

comments.title: Very Good...So Close to Being Great
comments.comment:
I actually purchased this tool and stacked 3 Tacos...then returned it. Then purchased it again. This is how desperate I am for a good, simple, effective survey tool that I could use with audiences when I speak. 

The interface is good and the surveys looks great on a mobile device. The Pabbly integration works fine and I have my survey setup to 

This tool has the potential to be AMAZING, but there are some really critical, simple things that are currently missing. 

1. NO FIRST/LAST NAME: There is no option for a FIRST NAME and LAST NAME question. You have to set these up as two separate questions, which feels cumbersome to users. 

2. CAN'T CHANGE QUESTION NAMES: DO NOT start from a template if you plan to do any integrations. The names of the questions are hard-coded when the survey is created and you can't change the names which makes integrating through Pabbly or anywhere else confusing. Just start from scratch and name your questions correctly. You can change the question for the user but it doesn't change behind the scenes.

3. NO HIDDEN QUESTIONS or DEFAULTS: I really need to be able to have a hidden question with a default value so I can pull that through my integration. That's not an option.

4. MULTICHOICE QUESTIONS ARE REQUIRED: If you do a pick list, at least one value has to be selected. My preference would be to have the question as optional, but instead, I have to add a "no thanks" choice, which is a shame.

I'm going to keep going with this platform and hope that they make the tiny tweaks needed to make this tool a real competitor! Thanks for offering a very good tool. :)

comments.title: Excellent survey tool
comments.comment:
5 Tasty Tacos!!
I purchased this with doing a few simple surveys in mind.

My daughter is starting a Garden Consulting business and asked if I could create a fact finding survey. I took a look at what another person did, and MetaSurvey allowed me to take things 10 steps forward!

I ended up with 35 questions, which may sound like a lot, but the swipe right/left, multiple choice and conditional logic make the survey custom to each user.

For example. If I ask a question about a raised garden beds, they can say no to a huge setup, skipping 5 photos. The conditional logic lands them on the next group of photos to say yes/no to. Nice! She knows exactly what the customer likes, and the budget!

MetaSurvey creates a real quality survey. You have several choices on how to display it. I chose a small button at the top of he page that engages a popup. At the end of her survey, I send the person to book a 15 minute call.

Cons: I was a little disappointed that I had to pay $15 a month for Google sheets integration. That was offset by the fact that they DO provide Webhooks. It took me about 10 minutes to setup the google sheet with webhooks and take the survey! Boom, I'm a happy camper now.

If you are a teacher looking to do a quick quiz, set up a formula on the last cell of your sheet to grade and assign a number and a letter grade! 

Note: the time format the survey is sent over is in ISO 8601 (e.g., 2024-04-02T18:24:27.000Z). If the time the survey taken is important, google "ISO-8601 String to Date in Google Sheets cell" and you will get a starting point for a long calculation to convert it.

This is an update to the original review below. I had direct dialogue with Amogh, the developer and sent over my log file and several of my concerns were addressed and QUICKLY (which matters massively with this type of software).

I am now updating my review from 3 stars to 4 stars because the credit system has been adjusted and I can confirm, credit burn is much slower (I am hoping it will be refined evern further - Amogh has assured all users this is the case) and the software is good and very quick.

Another small thing would be a terminal inside of Friday - it's just one less app I need to open but this in no way effects my usage of the software.

Again, I just want to reiterate, I really, really like this software and think it's on its way to 5 stars. 

I will update again as more changes happen.

**************************************************************************************

I like the software, first and foremost. It’s lacking some refinement, though, and I’m hoping this improves and, in time, it will replace Devin and Cursor in my stack.

A few things I think could be improved massively:

Credits get burned through, and I mean QUICK. Ask a question or two and the credits start decreasing before any work has even really begun.

Terminal commands and functions like a full Pytest run (that can be run from Windows PowerShell) also use credits, and I’m not sure why. This doesn’t use any model reasoning, etc., and as stated, I can run these for free from my own PowerShell.

I used almost all 250 credits in six hours, doing no more than I usually would in Codex/Cursor. For comparison, I only pay for the lowest tiers per month and never run out (so circa £40 per month). With how quickly Friday’s credits burn, I’ll also be spending on credits for OpenRouter. At some point, I’ll have to look at the overall cost and see which makes more financial sense. On a plus note, the actual Friday coder is excellent.

Every now and again, we’ll get halfway through working on a prompt for Friday to suddenly report, “This AI agent is available, please try again,” and every time I’ve had to restart. And yep, you guessed it, the redo uses even more credits.

There’s no ability to copy or paste without keyboard shortcuts. I use Grok/ChatGPT/Claude as the orchestrator and then Friday/Devin/Cursor to implement, so having to constantly scroll up and down to copy things is a pain.

comments.title: A desktop AI builder for turning ideas into apps
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

I took Friday Code for a deep dive and was genuinely impressed. It's a robust desktop AI builder that turns plain language prompts into websites, web apps, backends, and small tools you can actually deploy. What I like about it is that it gives you more than a chat window for code. You can describe what you want to build, work through the project inside the desktop app, refine it through conversation, and export the full codebase if you want to keep building elsewhere.

In my early test, I used Friday Code to build and deploy a to do app and a landing page. It did not get everything right on the first try, but it responded well to follow up instructions and improved the output over a few rounds until I got what I wanted. That is what I expected from this type of application. After a few rounds, I got a better feel for how to guide it, what level of detail to give it, and how to get to the expected result faster. The best way to use Friday Code is to see it as a faster way from idea to working version, with room to keep improving the output through iteration. The important part is that it gives you the tools to do that without starting from a blank codebase or having to manage the whole process manually.

Friday Code also supports templates, local project storage, and different AI model options. The OpenRouter support is especially useful because you can use your own OpenRouter API key, which gives you more control if you already have a preferred AI setup.

There were a few launch readiness glitches in the first build I tested, especially around Intel Mac compatibility and the Windows install experience. The team has been addressing these ahead of launch (the Intel build and a couple of experimental features have been cleaned up). I retested again with the new launch build, and those concerns are no longer an issue. App generation worked well, the early issues were resolved, and the product now feels much closer to what buyers should expect at launch. It also keeps getting better.

Overall, Friday Code is worth considering if you want a desktop AI builder for quickly testing ideas, building tools, and getting projects deployed without starting from a blank codebase. It sits somewhere between a no code builder and a terminal based AI coding tool like Claude Code. You still need to guide the AI through a few rounds, but you do not have to live in the terminal, manage a local dev setup, or think like a developer from the first prompt. It's a solid solution for helping non technical users turn ideas into working apps in a more guided desktop environment.

comments.title: An Accessible Desktop Agent for Building, Automating, and Managing Without the Heavy Lift
comments.comment:
Friday Code is a desktop AI agent (Mac and Windows) that turns plain-language requests into working full-stack applications, automations, research, and environment-management tasks. It integrates with GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, Slack, and others, focusing on end-to-end product work rather than isolated code generation. Inspired by Tony Stark’s AI assistant, it aims to be a single workspace for shipping ideas without a full team or complex tool stack.

I tested it with both default and local options. Initially, Friday Code was reluctant to name its model, insisting it was simply “Friday Code.” It later acknowledged using OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 as the primary model. While no longer the absolute newest frontier model, GPT-5.4 remains strong for professional knowledge work, coding, tool use, and agentic tasks.

The more interesting design is the orchestrator setup: you keep talking to the main model, and Friday uses other models as tools when helpful. You can link a more expensive model for harder work or route tasks through Ollama (local or cloud) to stretch credits. This differs from many agents that hand the entire session to whatever model you select.

I also run other agents (OpenCode, Hermes, OpenMuse) that require my own tokens, and I maintain a monthly Ollama subscription while running several models locally on a laptop with an RTX 5090. Friday Code’s ability to act as an orchestrator while still involving Ollama made it feel complementary rather than purely overlapping. Several friends pay around $200/month for foundational model subscriptions; some months they exhaust credits, others they don’t. Against that backdrop, the lifetime-deal structure is attractive.

I purchased Tier 2 (roughly $430 one-time for 250 monthly credits). Doubling credits costs another $500, and extra credits can always be bought later. That flexibility, plus Ollama routing, made Tier 2 right for my usage. On the company’s site a comparable 250-credit subscription is listed around $25/month, so the one-time price looks reasonable if usage stays within bounds.

Pros

Low barrier to entry. Describe what you want in ordinary language; Friday handles planning, multi-step execution, integrations, and refinement. Approachable for anyone wanting to experiment with AI for web pages, simple programs, or managing parts of their environment without mastering prompt engineering or tool chains.
Orchestrator design. Interact with one consistent agent while it calls other models (including via Ollama) as tools. Reduces constant context-switching common in pure BYOK setups.
Credit and model flexibility. Stick with default GPT-5.4, escalate to a stronger model, or use Ollama to extend credits. Extra credits can be purchased without changing plans.
Lifetime-deal economics. One-time payment avoids open-ended monthly bills. For variable usage this can be more predictable than subscriptions that sometimes leave credits unused and sometimes run out.
Practical full-stack output. Generates working applications with backends and deployment options rather than only code snippets; you can export the code.
Good on-ramp for light or exploratory use. Useful for a landing page, small web app, automation, or testing an idea without stitching together separate tools.
Cons

Credit consumption. Complex tasks involve many internal steps, so credits can go quickly. Budgeting is necessary; heavier daily use may require top-ups or a higher tier. Some early AppSumo users noted this, though efficiency has improved.
Default model cost trade-off. GPT-5.4 prioritizes capability. Cheaper open models (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) are available via Ollama, but the core experience leans on the more expensive proprietary model.
Tier limitations. Lowest tier is more restricted. Broader language support, mobile apps, custom agents, and higher limits start at higher tiers.
Young product. Early users reported bugs or rough edges the team has been addressing. Long-term maturity is still being proven relative to more established tools.
Desktop-centric. Runs as a local desktop application rather than a pure browser experience.
Who It’s For

Friday Code suits people who want to dip their toes into using AI to create web pages, programs, or manage parts of their environment without heavy technical or financial commitment. You don’t need deep expertise in agents or local models. Plain-language interaction, an orchestrator that can call other models, exportable output, and a lifetime-deal credit system keep the risk low for exploratory or moderate use.

(Note: I’m the author of several books on AI, including the latest, “You Are Using AI Wrong, but it isn’t your fault,” available on Amazon.)

comments.title: Took my time on this one...
comments.comment:
So I have now used Friday to make a chrome extension, an app, and a couple websites over that last couple of weeks.

This thing is good. It is hovering on an interesting line between Lovable's ease of use and Openclaw's agentic power and it really feels nice to use.
It solves Openclaws worst aspect, which is a complicated setup. 

Now it isn't quite as powerful as either of those apps for what they do, but if you are wanting a hybrid that can do both jobs realistically about 90%+ as good, Friday is your software.

The founder is 10/10 as far as "in the zone" dealing with issues and people while juggling 2 projects. I am very impressed with Amogh, I am not sure I could do anywhere near as good of a job handling things.

Now lets get into the "bad". Friday Go which is the base model and is not very good. I am assuming this is the cheap model's fault more than the prompting itself and just like all AI models I think this will improve with time. Even "bad/cheap" models are getting better crazy fast. I did move away from this model quite quickly and might not have given it a fair shake on more simple tasks.

The agent made automations work but I had some issues with them deleting themselves after a few runs. I didn't test a lot so this may have been random and caused by the automation being broken so the agent decided to remove it but I was never able to find out what happened to it. Happened twice but the task became un achievable after a couple runs due to an expiring auth token so I am assuming the agent caught on and removed the automation but I was never able to confirm.

Aside from those 2 things it works pretty well. I see a lot of mentions of credits being used quickly and I am barely making a dent. Seems on par with the competitors from what I can tell and I have not been using the cheaper models.

I think most people complaining of credits being used too fast just are not familiar with AI coding, it is a heavy token activity. There really is no way around that without seriously affecting quality. 
Thats exactly how you end up with Greta where it can make a pretty website but not much more because the Agent isn't given enough context to work on projects of any amount of size.

It is slow but again this is normal with AI coding, the agents are calling many different tools, and essentially completing an entire list of todos prior to coming back to you with the results. 
I have had Claude Code going for well over 30mins on a task a few times now.
Again, this is less of a Friday problem and more of an impatience issue.
If you give an employee the same task it could take them hours, days, maybe even weeks to complete what these agents do in minutes.

~BYOK was added if you run out of credits or want to use a specific model.
~Custom MCPs allow you to connect just about anything to your agents now.
~Integrated Appsumo favorites like NoCodeBackend make adding a database a breeze for pretty much all Appsumo users. No more having to juggle 2 free Supabase projects that you keep having to freeze and unfreeze so they don't get deleted.
~Its got Agent skills so you can call a skill for tasks that need repeated often and you don't want to start by explaining the job every single time.
~Its got memory built in so the Agents all know what you have been working on and important details and preferences.
~They recently added the ability to run local models for all you super computer people that want to save money that way.
~Little widget on the screen that tells you when the agent finishes and you can even prompt with your voice straight from there as well.

I could keep going because Friday is that extensive but we will stop here.

Now the only true bad news here is that I can not recommend T1 because its just a Greta replacement and you will be disappointed. It also does not have BYOK and you are locked into Friday Go which is just ok.

T2 gets much better by unlocking most of what you need to replace your lovable, bolt, or replit subscriptions. The main things your missing here will be the Automations which is what makes having AI Agents super useful imo because you can literally farm out daily tasks without even asking. You also are missing a couple key integrations in this tier.

My recommendation is T3+ for anyone seriously wanting to test Friday out and actually be able to replace some of those subscriptions you are wasting money on.

I personally have T4 and I think its overkill for anyone but daily users and automation nuts.

Giving this one a 5 out of 5 tacos and by far, this is the best AI agent/coding software that has hit Appsumo and its not close.
They even outdid their own platform Bind. 

Ease of use: 9/10
People new to coding with AI might still feel intimidated but its pretty easy to figure out.

Quality: 9/10 
Had a couple issues early on.

Install: 10/10
Simple and quick

Integrations: 10/10
Custom MCPs make this an easy 10

Value: 10/10
Worth every penny

UI: 10/10
Knocked it out of the park

comments.title: Adaptive forms are the real differentiator — useful for discovery, not just data collection
comments.comment:
We use Dashform for project discovery and guided follow-up rather than as another generic form builder.
The feature that made us keep it is the separation between a normal logic-based intake and an AI-assisted follow-up funnel. A fixed form is great when you already know every question you need to ask. In discovery work, however, the useful next question often depends on what the person just told you. Dashform gives us a practical way to test that adaptive layer without replacing the deterministic intake underneath it.
We ran a synthetic discovery proof across multiple scenarios and retained a production Logic Funnel plus a production AI follow-up Funnel afterward. That was important for us: the product had to prove that it could add decision-useful clarification, not simply make a form feel more conversational.
I also like the direction around MCP, webhooks, integrations, analytics, and agent-assisted form creation. Direct create/readback from ChatGPT has been useful, and the product is much more interesting to us because the form can participate in a broader workflow rather than remain an isolated survey.
The main area I want improved is least-privilege integration. During our testing, the MCP/OAuth path exposed rough edges around scope/resource interoperability before the direct ChatGPT path became usable. For an automation-oriented product, the ideal experience would be very explicit read-only vs. write scopes, no unnecessary offline access, and documentation that always matches the live authorization behavior.
I would also love more explainability around adaptive questioning: for each generated follow-up, expose why the system decided the question was worth asking, what missing/ambiguous fact it is trying to resolve, and the stopping reason. That would make the AI funnel easier to audit and safer to use in structured business discovery.
Overall, Dashform has earned a real role in our stack because it solves a different problem from Tally or Google Forms. We still prefer deterministic forms when fixed branching is enough, but when we genuinely need guided clarification, Dashform gives us a useful adaptive layer instead of forcing a human to manually conduct every follow-up conversation.

comments.title: So much more than a basic quiz builder
comments.comment:
I came to Dashform with a fairly complex assessment in mind. I didn’t want to simply tally a score or put people into generic personality types. I wanted different answers to work together to create a genuinely personalized result across several sections.

I pushed the platform pretty hard, and what impressed me most was how Jake and the team responded when we reached the edges of the existing functionality. They listened to what I was trying to accomplish and actually expanded features to support the more complex backend logic my quiz required.

My 12-question quiz is now live and embedded directly into my website, producing individualized results that would have been difficult to create with other platforms I explored.

The AI-assisted builder makes sophisticated forms possible without needing to be a developer, and the support has been outstanding. Dashform is still evolving, but the team clearly listens to its users and actively improves the product.

If you’re looking for more than a basic form or cookie-cutter quiz, I warmly recommend Dashform. I’m very happy I grabbed the lifetime deal.

comments.title: More Than a Form Builder, It’s a Workflow Front Door
comments.comment:
I bought Dashform with a pretty clear vision of how I wanted to use it, and after testing it in real workflows, that vision has been validated.

The moment it clicked for me was when the branching started working the way I expected. Once I understood how Dashform handles branches, groups, and conditions, the product became much more intuitive. More importantly, I stopped seeing it as just a form builder.

For me, Dashform is a workflow front door.

I’ve already used it to build a business systems assessment for my consulting work and a Shift Change Culture Audit for convenience-store managers. The same form can send people to completely different outcomes and next steps based on their answers. That opens up a lot of possibilities for consulting, training, education, community groups, operational audits, course follow-up, and more.

The AI-generated starting point was useful and appreciated, but the real value shows up after the form is built. Lead scoring, response analytics, branching, different endings, and the ability to identify patterns in replies can help determine what services, training, or tools people actually need.

That service-intelligence piece is especially important to me. Instead of guessing what to build next, I can use actual responses to identify recurring problems and opportunities.

I also see strong potential in Dashform’s agent/MCP direction. I have not fully tested that piece yet, so I won’t pretend I have, but the idea that AI agents could discover, understand, and interact with these workflows is a major differentiator.

There was a learning curve, and I initially misunderstood parts of the branching logic. I also ran into a routing issue that the founder investigated and addressed. What stood out to me was that he did not rush out a polished response. He investigated, fixed the issue, and then responded.

The flexibility is what earns the 5 tacos for me. I can see using the same underlying system across consulting, training, C-Store Center, education, and community projects without needing a different platform for each use case.

I came into this already expecting to upgrade to Tier 3. Testing Dashform did not change my mind. It validated the vision and instinct I had when I first saw it.

I’ve seen a lot of software described as “more than a form builder.” In this case, I think that description actually fits.

And if you think you see a use case for Dashform, don’t leave it sitting in your cart too long. My wallet practically opened itself once I saw what I could build with it.

5 tacos.
