comments.title: Purchased, upgraded, downgraded
comments.comment:
I am a long-standing user of VPNUnlimited, and fairly happy with their lifetime plan, but every VPN got its downside, and for VPNUnlimited it is that after a few days of continuous use the connection seems to be throttled. I'm not sure if it's due to the fact that I'm in Hong Kong, and the government may use deep packet inspection to investigate the type of connection. 

I decided to give goose a chance, since it offers open VPN over port 443, the latter may help to reduce the chance of being throttled.

Starting off with the Tier 1 USD 29 plan, the connection seemed stable and I decided to upgrade to the Tier 3 cyber alarm plan. However, the latter was really not helpful to me. After a few days of use, I have two alarms for a messenger app and it reported to have inspected 1.6 GB of data - much less than the actual use. All my data - including DNS requests - were sent over Goose. 

IMHO, I believe there should be more alerts (my firewall blocked more than what Goose reported). I'm not sure if Goose is using DNS to check in website visits? As I'm using unbound (routed over VPN) and this may obscure traffic.

I've now downgraded to the Tier 2 plan, and I think I will stay with this, at least, as long as Goose is stable.

And yet I am still missing something.
1. If I do a single scan (live scan) for a customer, I will see after the scan whether anything has been found.
There is an option to save it as a csv file. If you don't do that right away, you've lost it.
I would like to at least see that I gave this query. Possibly with a date and the data is temporarily stored.
So that when I speak to the customer, I can view, save and display the data even after a few days.

2. The date format is now MM/DD/YYYY. I would like to set this in DD/MM/YYYY. Each country / region has its own preferences.

3. I scan my own company's domain name, email address and telephone number daily.
As long as nothing is found, nothing will be shown. That's very nice ;-)
However, the screen remains blank. “Is something going on?” I ask myself. Can it also be displayed differently?
E.g. show the scans of the past week and a dash - if nothing was found?

4. I would also like to see an option to add an organization and scan it once a week (or another period).
That costs less credits, but you do keep an eye on one organization.

comments.title: Build your own app, they said. It'll be easy, they said.

Well dang, they were right!

I have wanted an app that was simple but had the features I wanted. I tried Fuzen to build the app and was very happy with the results.

The Ai got stuck getting a feature to work right, but a ticket to support and they had things running in less than 24 hours.
I was sent an email offering an online meeting if I still had trouble or questions. I had hit another issue with my app so I set a meeting. The meeting was quite helpful in learning more about Fuzen and when they found out how long and the amount of credits used trying to get my current issue solved, they jumped right on it. The next day my app was again running and they had replenished some of my credits.

I have run into an issue with Ai in general and Fuzen does it too. If you are running a test on you app that generates a report or results and there is no data to work with Ai's will create data from the "cosmos" and then generate your answer. I have had this happen with multiple Ai models, even after telling the model Not to create fake data. I think in general Ai is taught to deliver a positive answer, stating there is no answer is negative so the Ai creates data to give a positive answer.

I would say to give Fuzen a try if your looking to build an app of your own, it's simple to use and you get the app features you want with none of the add on bloat.

I am looking forward to building a couple other apps I have been thinking about with Fuzen.

Security

comments.title: Insurance for your WP Installs
comments.comment:
How much is your time worth to you, because if you value it then you'll want to buy WP Reset. We can go over all the features that not only help you maintain your WP sanity by offering great recovery and rollback options, but also deployment options when setting up a new WP instance.

Snapshots to help rollback mistakes -- why isn't this part of WP to begin with?
Emergency Recovery when the site is unresponsive -- I didn't know tech had its own defibrillator!
Automatic backup to offsite cloud storage -- Smart
Collections to help deploy a pre-configured WP instance w/ extensions -- Time dilation in your favor. Turn Hours, or even DAYS, into mere minutes all within a few clicks.

There are a few bugs, like when somehow BING (or a port number) gets a localhost license which can take away from some of the automated benefits. Also, it would be nice to allow sites to be redefined on the cloud admin side of things so when the IP # changes or domain name changes that backups stay relevant instead of reuploading them to the cloud.

In the end it still is a simple solution with some of the most powerful features. Love it!

comments.title: Prevention is better than cure.
comments.comment:
There could be so much residue from hosting a website that just deleting everything doesn't mean you have a clean site. WP Reset takes care of all that for you, giving you confidence you are starting again with that fresh out the packet feeling.  I mostly use the "Snapshot" feature, where it saves its current state. It is not a backup replacement, but gets me out of a pickle every time.

More importantly, it gives me the confidence to push on or experiment, not worrying about something breaking. In by doing so, it allows me to learn more. In fact the only time I get into a pickle now is forgetting to install the WP Reset plugin. :)

I create licence keys and use them like folders, where you can separate a "key" for clients, tutorials and local websites. This is to prevent any deletion of client sites and as I get closer to my quota, it makes it easier which sites to delete to make more websites.

I am looking forward to exploring more features like creating "collections". I don't mind installing things manually at the moment, but once you have a system and workflow in place, you can use "collections" to store your workflow of themes and plugins, so it can be automatically installed. I think Paul from WPTuts review of WP Reset said it best when he said;

"WP Reset is one of those tools that you simply don't realize you need until you see it in action, and then you wonder how the hell you actually live without it."

comments.title: A must-have LTD for any website owner, agency, or ecommerce business! A+++ Super-easy to setup and start using it. An amazing CYA to protect your website and business from legal headaches as well!
comments.comment:
I’m extremely happy I found WebAbility.io on AppSumo. Good accessibility SaaS tools are surprisingly hard to find, especially ones that are affordable, easy to install, and built for people who do not have a full accessibility team or a huge compliance budget.

The setup was quick and straightforward. You can add it to sites on platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, Wix, and Webflow, or ANY kind of website since you can just drop the snippet right before your </body> tag, and then scan your website for accessibility issues. The widget offers useful visitor controls and accessibility profiles, including screen-reader support, keyboard-navigation improvements, text-to-speech functionality, contrast and visual adjustments, focus support, and options that help people with visual, cognitive, hearing, and motor-access needs.

I also appreciate that it does more than just place a widget on the site. It helps identify issues across content, navigation, forms, and media; automates certain safer fixes where possible; flags items that need human review; and provides an accessibility statement. It is designed to support work toward standards and requirements such as ADA, WCAG 2.1/2.2, Section 508, AODA, EN 301 549, and IS 5568. Of course, no tool should be treated as a guaranteed legal shield or replacement for a proper accessibility review, but this is a very practical layer of support and a strong starting point.

Support has been excellent. Every time I have reached out with a question, the team has been fast, responsive, and helpful in getting things resolved. That matters a lot with a product connected to accessibility and compliance.

This topic is much more important than many website owners realize. There are attorneys and automated systems actively looking for websites that appear to lack accessibility support, and businesses of every size can face complaints, demand letters, or legal costs. Search Google or Reddit for recent accessibility-related legal issues and you will quickly see why this deserves attention. With AI making automated website analysis easier, that risk may only increase.

More importantly, accessibility is not only about reducing risk, it is about making your website usable and welcoming for real people with disabilities. That should be the main reason to take it seriously.

In my view, this is becoming as essential as a cookie banner: something businesses should put in place early instead of waiting until there is a problem. Between the easy installation, scans, automated assistance, custom accessibility statement, useful widget controls, responsive support, and LTD pricing, the value is hard to beat.

Honestly, nearly every AppSumo buyer who owns, manages, builds, or maintains websites should consider owning this tool. 

Thanks SO MUCH to the WebAbility.io Team for making such a fantastic disability tool so easy to deploy on all my websites and to get my fully compliant very quickly!!

comments.title: Must Have and The Near Future is Going to be Awesome
comments.comment:
Updated June 2026

I still own WebAbility and I'm still keeping it.

My original review was based on first impressions and excitement about where the product was headed. After spending more time with it, my view is a bit more nuanced.

The core reason I bought WebAbility hasn't changed. Accessibility feels a lot like SEO did years ago. There are simply too many potential issues for most website owners to manage manually, and automation will likely play an increasingly important role.

What I like:
• Easy setup, especially on WordPress.
• Accessibility statement generation.
• Useful audit reports.
• Helpful accessibility scanning and issue visibility.
• Strong value for the lifetime deal price.
• I can see how automated remediation could become very valuable over time.

What I would still like to see improved:
• Bulk exports of accessibility issues.
• More scalable review workflows for larger websites.
• Better handling of template-level issues that appear across many pages.
• Continued product development and feature refinement.

Overall, I still believe the product delivers value for the small business and solopreneur audience it is built for, which is why I continue to keep it in my stack.

I published a much deeper review covering my experience, screenshots, audit reports, what I liked, and what I would improve:

https://marketingwithdave.com/webability-review/

comments.title: Great support
comments.comment:
With most cookie plugins ditching their free plans and requiring annual renewals, I decided to buy a lifetime plan for Consently. I installed it on a few websites without any issues at all.

Seriously, especially with WordPress, the process is very simple. Add the plugin to the site, add the site to Consently, create an API key, add the API key to WordPress, set up the banner, and run the scan. Then review the cookies it found, add them as needed, and confirm that the categories are correct.

But then I ran into a problem with one particular installation where the site had hundreds of pages and hosting resources were limited. The scan kept completing with warnings, saying the crawler couldn’t access the pages even though it could read the sitemap and see that those pages existed.

I worked with both the hosting company and Consently, running support tickets with each and sharing their replies back and forth until we finally got to the bottom of it. We whitelisted Consently’s crawlers, adjusted the caching and CDN settings, and gave the cached pages time to build up before running the scan again. This time, the crawl completed successfully.

Both the hosting company and Consently provided awesome support and stuck with me until the issue was completely sorted out. I highly recommend Consently for handling the cookie consent requirements that websites have to deal with in so many countries.

comments.title: Replaced a broken "accept-only" banner in an afternoon — and it actually blocks scripts
comments.comment:
I run a small local business directory hosted on a third-party platform (GoHighLevel-based), and the built-in cookie banner it shipped with had one button: Accept. No reject, no preferences, nothing that would survive a look from a European regulator. I needed a real CMP I could drop into a site I don't fully control, and Consently did that.

What it got right for me:

Script blocking that works. The chat widget loader on my site was setting session identifiers before anyone had clicked anything. I added the domain to Consently's blocked-scripts list and it stayed blocked until consent — verified in DevTools, not just trusted.
Scan and categorise. The scanner found what the site was setting, I sorted it into categories, done. The Stripe fraud-prevention cookie showed up too, which I'd have missed otherwise.
A preferences link I can put anywhere. The showConsentPreferences() global let me add a plain "Cookies" link to the site footer, so visitors can change their mind without a floating icon cluttering the page.
Subdomain sharing. One consent covers the main site and the info subdomain. Small thing, saves a second banner.
Sensible GDPR defaults. Accept / Reject / Manage, equal weight, no dark patterns to undo.
Two things worth knowing before you buy: it ships with the US "Do Not Sell" template switched on alongside GDPR, so US visitors got a button-less notice until I turned CCPA off — easy, but not obvious. And it's not the tool if you need IAB TCF for ad-tech vendors; I don't, so the Basic mode was the right fit.

For a lifetime deal on something that does one job properly, I'm glad I picked it up. It's now on a live site with real customers, which is more than I can say for a few other AppSumo buys.

comments.title: Focused secure sharing without forcing us into a full client portal
comments.comment:
We use InPrivy for a narrow job: securely sharing information when a full client portal or collaboration platform would be unnecessary.
That focus is what we like about it. Sometimes the right experience is not “create an account, join a workspace, learn a portal.” It is simply “here is the protected information you need, through a controlled sharing surface.” InPrivy fits that use case well.
We also value the ability to use our own branded custom domain for the sharing experience. That makes a focused secure-share tool feel like part of our normal client-facing workflow instead of sending someone to an unrelated third-party URL.
We are intentionally not trying to make InPrivy our document-management system or client-operations platform. We already have broader tools for those jobs. Its value is that it stays comparatively simple and gives us a purpose-built option when secure sharing is the actual requirement.
The biggest improvement for our use would be deeper automation and audit integration: an API/webhook path to create and expire shares, retrieve current state, and read view/access events would make it much easier to use InPrivy inside a governed workflow while keeping the provider as the secure execution layer.
For the focused job it solves, InPrivy has been a useful addition to our stack. I would rather have a small tool that does this job cleanly than force every occasional secure exchange into a much heavier portal.

comments.title: Secure links that stay private
comments.comment:
InPrivy helps you send passwords and other private stuff safely. Instead of putting secrets in email or chat where they can be saved or seen by others, it makes a special link. The link can only be opened once and then it stops working. You can also turn the link off yourself at any time.

Features

- One-time link that stops working after it is opened
- Turn off (revoke) a link any time before it is opened
- Set a time limit or how many times the link can be viewed
- Keeps the secret safe while the link is active
- Shows if and when the link was opened
- Simple and easy to use

Pros

- Keeps secrets safe after the link is closed
- Very easy to make and share links
- Lets you control how long the secret is available
- Helps avoid email scanning and hacked accounts
- Good for sharing one-time passwords or keys

Cons

- The person you send it to must open the special link (small extra step)
- If someone opens the link by mistake, the secret is gone right away

I am really happy with InPrivy. It makes sharing passwords quick and safe. The one-time links and the ability to turn them off give me peace of mind. 

Highly recommended for anyone who wants an easy, secure way to share secrets.

comments.title: Simple, Fast, and Seriously Useful
comments.comment:
I’ve been testing Inprivy and I’m honestly impressed. It nails the two things that matter most: simplicity and speed.

What I love:

- Simple and powerful: The UI is clean, intuitive, and just gets out of the way. You don’t need a manual to start sharing sensitive info.
- Secret Pages look great: Plenty of customization options for the design, so your pages can match your brand or use case.
- Blazing fast: Pages load instantly. No waiting, no friction.
- No bandwidth limits: Share confidently without worrying about throttling or caps.

Where it could get even better:

- “No Expiration” option: Right now, you have to select a far-future date (e.g., 100 years) for long-lived secrets. A simple “No ending” toggle would be perfect.
- Edit secrets after creation: It would be a big win to be able to update a secret’s content—add/remove files or tweak limits—without having to create a new secret each time.

Bottom line:
Inprivy is an absolute win for anyone who needs to share sensitive information quickly and securely without dealing with complicated workflows. It’s fast, polished, and easy to use. Add a “No Expiration” option and post-creation editing, and it’s a 10/5. As it stands, it’s already a strong recommend.

1. Support
Many people claim the support is good, but my experience was quite different. I didn't receive any email replies from the support team, even after reaching out to Appsumo for help. It's important to have fast and accurate support in this business, and I noticed that many others are disappointed with the lack of responses. I hope this issue gets more attention.

2. URL Authorization
As someone who can use these addons on unlimited sites, I noticed a feature that allows me to activate the plugin based on a specific URL I enter in the dashboard. However, I found out that this URL activation only applies to automatic updates and doesn't lock the widgets. This means that once the pro plugin is installed, all the pro elements become available, regardless of whether a license number is entered or the website URL is registered. This can be a problem because anyone who installs the pro plugin can use it on any website and access all the pro elements without needing to register. My suggestion is that if a URL is not activated or removed from the authorization list on the dashboard, the pro elements should remain locked and inaccessible.

3. Web Bugs
I noticed some issues with your website. Myself and other users often encounter unrelated websites opening when we type your web URL, like this one: https://tuto.ateliers-achats.fr/Wnu61Q9o. Additionally, I found some irregularities in the Google search results, such as links with Chinese writing. It's important to check and fix these problems.

While these addons offer a wide range of functionality, there are a few areas that require improvement, as I wrote above. I give you 5 tacos because your product is really good, and I believe that you will continue to improve the quality of this product and service as well.

comments.title: A New Standard in Digital Asset In-depth Security That Inspires Trust
comments.comment:
Having utilized several password managers, including LastPass, 1Password, Pcloud Pass, and Locker.io, I find TransferChain Pass truly stands apart. Its core architecture, built on end-to-end zero-knowledge encryption combined with a unique distributed storage model—where encrypted data is sliced and distributed—gives me unparalleled confidence that my digital assets are thoroughly protected.
The zero-knowledge protocol is the foundation, ensuring that not even the TransferChain team can access my vault. However, the feature that truly differentiates it is the "slice and distribute" model. Knowing that my encrypted data isn't just sitting in one place, but is instead fragmented and spread across a secure network, effectively eliminates the risk of a single-point-of-failure breach. This innovative approach demonstrates a deep understanding of modern security threats.

I also want to commend the support & technical team Mr. Ozan & Ms. Esra. When I encountered an issue during account activation, they proactively initiated a one-on-one video call and resolved the matter with impressive speed and efficiency. I truly appreciate their hands-on approach and rapid resolution.

comments.title: Cool tool with a few issues
comments.comment:
Great tool overall. I would also say it’s the best among the other password tools featured on AppSumo. I just hope the team can fix a few issues, I have listed below:

1. 2FA authentication through google or other authentication when login in or email codes for better security
2. When adding a password, I wish there was an option to include an image. For example, I could add a QR code for 2FA. Some apps I use require 2FA, so the only way a member/employee can access them is by scanning a QR code using a 2FA app. Having the option to add an image would let me share the QR code in the password folder for the member to access so I dont have to manually send them by email.
3. From a UX perspective, you can't open password folders by clicking on them directly. Instead, you have to click the three dots next to the folder to open it. This is unusual they have this limitation. I recommend allowing users to open folders by clicking on the folder itself, rather than on the side, to make it more user-friendly.
4. After creating a password folder, you cannot change or update its name; it seems you can only delete it. I suggest adding an option to edit the folder name, as users may need to update the name instead of deleting the entire folder and starting over.
5. Not easy adding and sharing logins with members, I agree with the previous person who made a review. I hope they can improve this and make it more simpler and optimized. For example I like how LastPass makes it easy to onboard new members/users, get notified when added to folders or passwords etc.

-------------------------------------------------
Update Reply:

Thank you for your reply. I'm glad to hear that most of the recommended points 1-4 will be discussed with your team or introduced in new updates.

For point 5: Email notifications when a folder is shared with a user I believe is important. For passwords, it would be helpful to have a toggle for notifications, so users/owners can choose or set which alerts they receive or don’t receive. This allows customization, as some users may want notifications for password shares while others may not.  

For the onboarding flow, it would be nice if, when a user receives an invite to sign up, they get a mini tour of how Transfer Chain works after logging in. This could be a pop-up tour for new users or a short video, helping them understand the basics, such as where folders are located, the dos and don’ts aswell as how to install browser extension and how to use it.

comments.title: SchedulePress adds great publishing features to Wordpress

I really do like the calendar. I only used the manual scheduling option. It gives you a good perspective on your publishing activities. After you have saved your post it appears in the calendar tab and you can move it around on the calendar easily. 

When you move the post into the past it is immediately published, no need to press any buttons! When you move it to the future it is automatically scheduled on 12.00 that day. So it's quite easy to adapt your publishing schedule after you have finished writing multiple posts, without going into every post separately. You can also republish or unpublish WordPress posts at any time you want, which isn't possible in Wordpress, as far as I know.

The plugin even is able to prevent "Missed Schedule"-errors, due to wp-cron errors. I did not experience those yet, but I can image that it makes publishing more reliable.

Support is responsive. I had a licensing bug issue because of the rebranding to SchedulePress. The ticket was answered quickly and I could continue working with SchedulePress. A few weeks later the bug was fixed and I was neatly informed. Great developer!

comments.title: A Good Option For WordPress Hosting, Plus Some Nice Bonuses 😊
comments.comment:
Basically I have some small WordPress sites that I had on separate hosting over at HostKoala, which was about $25/year - but which has been TERRIBLE as far as giving me near-constant downtine alerts via my Better Stack monitor. I've been looking around for a good deal on hosting and found this one on AppSumo.

I got this Hostinger deal and moved all 10 small/low-traffic sites over pretty easily. You can migrate your sites of course, but I did mine manually and so far, everything is working very well.

I did have a few pretty minor hiccups with the domain assignment  with just a few (was still showing the temporary WP installation Hostinger domain), but going through the domain assignment again fixed it.

Currently I am not using any of the AI/agent features provided, but they're in the sidebar and easily found. Also there's some how-to information on the website if you look around.

Hostinger uses a custom dashboard, which to be honest takes some getting used to. I'm not complaining - just be aware that it won't have the look & feel of things like cPanel or DirectAdmin. That being said, that's fine, because it's very modern and so far it works great.

-- File manager: I had ot use the File Manager for some of my WP installations when my WP plugin's import failed for my backup image. You can access the file manager for each website installation under the Tools menu drop-down. It works great, so that's a relief!
- SSH & FTP are available and all the info is in your dashboard.

Web apps: So, with this plan you can also run your own web apps. The basic plan lists these options as being supported:

• Supported frontend frameworks: Angular, Astro, Gatsby, Next.js, Nitro, Nuxt, Parcel, React, React Router, Svelte, SvelteKit, Vite, Vue.js
• Supported backend frameworks: Astro, Express, Fastify, Hono, NestJS, Next.js, Nitro, Nuxt, React Router, SvelteKit
• Supported Node.js versions: 24.x, 22.x, 20.x and 18.x
• Supported package managers: npm (default), yarn and pnpm

Currently I'm working on my first entry-level ReactJS etc. applications, so I look forward to using this as well. I'm using a cheap hosting account elsewhere, but there are issues with using some generic web hosts for React / Next JS projects as built-in image compression fails. I look forward to resolving this via using Hostinger (I'm trying to avoid having to pay for Netlify or Vercel, etc.)

Unfortunately, no Python web app support so those will have to be hosted elsewhere. 🥲

Overall, I'm very happy with the hosting and got a great deal. I have had a single Better Stack downtime notification yet, unlike my old host. 😅 The API agent features look useful if you're planning on building something based on those.

It's well worth checking out! :)

(Note: there are a few USA server locations to choose from, in case you're wondering. I picked Arizona.)

EDIT: I forgot to mention there's also Git integration option if you'd like to connect your GitHub account & use project repos which is nice!
EDIT #2: This plan does include backups.😊

The AI page builder is interesting. I've had it turn out some nice-looking pages, but it seems to only build landing pages. Which, if you just want a landing page, is perfect.

comments.title: Super website builder.
comments.comment:
I used to host my site on WordPress. For sure, WordPress can give you all the bells and whistles you need to build anything from your first to your 500th website. But the cost starts to ratchet up once you factor in additional plugins and hosting. 

So, I decided to try the Grigora lifetime deal a while back. It's a pretty intuitive website builder, and it includes newsletter capabilities, though I'm still using VBOUT for this because I don't think Grigora can generate nurture sequences yet. Hopefully that's in the pipeline, because I find VBOUT really unintuitive and clunky, even with Claude helping me. 

Grigora also has an MCP connector that lets me use Claude to create and add webpages and posts. So I can use the built-in AI to help generate webpages, or I can use my Claude subscription, which I tend to do because it can generate posts by referring to my Karpathy-style wiki on my hard drive. 

Recently, Grigora added new SEO and GEO analysis to help identify issues; it is in beta but already helpful. 

The AI features are useful. You can easily link pages, and it can also help generate alt image text. Grigora AI can also generate blog posts (though I haven't used it for that), and it has an AI image generator, which I also haven't tried in a while because I use Nano Banana with my Gemini Workspace account. That's less convenient, but it helps me maintain brand consistency. The AI tools can also generate FAQs or turn a video into a blog post for you. 

The team is very responsive to feedback and super helpful when you contact them about issues with your sites. They're also frequently building new features and improving the user interface.

It was a great deal when I bought it, and it still is.

I just wish the Grigora team would use their AI to help work on their own copy and training, because I think it could help with identifying benefits rather than features and improve their marketing. Right now, it's a super little gem but it's more of a secret than it ought to be.

comments.title: Amazing Trajectory of Features & Engaged Team
comments.comment:
2026-10 UPDATE: Here is an overview video I did to share some of the features:
https://youtu.be/mWMmCeYIvyQ

We purchase Grigora at Tier 5 the last time they came to AppSumo. I am so glad we did! They continue to update the platform. It only costs $5/month to add an email. If we exceed the 100 websites/custom domains - it costs $5 per month.

Pros
1. The website builder is straightforward, but feature rich, especially since the updates last month and the updates released just today to simplify the container and columns to a single type that is easier to manage. The animation functionality allows for scroll, entrance, hover, and infinite animations. The integration of CMS to be able to use blog posts as content on the website is wonderful.
2. The blog is amazing. It guides you through optimizing your URL, title, description, and content for SEO. It has AI assisted features like linking related, existing content; adding FAQs, and more. It also has collaboration features so you can work with others on content, including the ability to leave comments.
3. The email is easy to use and clean.
4. Includes basic SEO analysis tools
5. You can now upload html files and make them available as a static page - wonderful for basic web apps generated on Gemini and other tools (great for helpful lead magnets). 
6. The credits are generous. If you run out of credits, you can purchase an additional 25,000 credits a month for $5/month. This makes it easier for agencies to plan for new clients.
7. Support is responsive. I have receive responses from the team within a few hours, sometimes a few minutes.
8. The new AI generated pages feature is powerful. It is like being able to vibe code a webpage and then manually edit it so you do not have to make minor changes through a chat!

Because of the features and our experience building out our own content, we are making Grigora our nonprofit's centerpiece for a new workforce development program where we are going to offer training to youth and young adults to be able to offer digital agency services with the opportunity to support our soon-to-be nonprofit, mission-driven digital agency.

Cons
1. As with all tools, there is a learning curve. At this point, we have used every feature, except the directory. That is next on our to do list.
2. Analytics are not as robust as they could be. We have our sites connected to VisitorTracking.com and Rybbit - to better understand the customer journey and conversions. 
3. Based on SiteGuru analyses: Trailing slashes may cause duplicate content - when we check our site analytics on all tools, we see page visits for pages with and without trailing slashes
4. They added a video to blog function, but it requires you to upload a video - unlike Video-to-Blog where you can enter a YouTube video. The output is still a work in progress, but if this feature is like others, I anticipate they will continue to improve it.
5. The blog AI features are great, but they have no memory/cache. For example if I use the internal linking feature and something happens and it closes, if I open it again, anything that was generated is gone. If you do not add the originally generated content, you have to spend more credits regenerating (and you will not get the same output as the first time).
6. Every AI function requires credit usage, which is fine. However, if you use all of the AI features, you can burn through 
7. Improve documentation - as the very welcomed updates to the system are implemented, it renders existing documentation obsolete or confusing. More videos would also be appreciated, but please none of those AI autogenerated tutorials.

Here is my personal site I used Grigora  to create - it is still a work in progress, but it should give you some ideas of functionality: https://drmartin.io

Get it while you can...as they say about AI - this is the worst the system is going to be, it will only get better. I am looking forward to continuing to grow with the Grigora team.

As it worked so well for me I decided to quickly check if the things in the negative reviews were actually true. 1MB code file limit (non code files 50mb) exist but honestly that should just be your warning you likely doing something wrong. You can fit angular, react, and vue in a single file and still have it be like 500kb. Favicons for the web, and app icons for iOS / Android work just fine, manifest files work correctly. There are tons of templates so can't speak to how well those are all coded, but nothing about the editor.do would prevent a mobile app or PWA. My little test site looks fantastic on my phone. Files are served with correct MIME types and reasonable caches, if you don't see an immediate update it's just your browsers local cache which is the nature of the internet your browser and your code not really an editor.do problem. Ctrl+f5 is your friend. IMHO this fits perfectly in a niche, I have dozens of options for stackblitz like tools with virtualized build systems etc.. in a world of dev, staging, prod repos, CI, runners and actions, quite refreshing to go back to the old days and just quickly make edits in "production".

comments.title: Kind of great, but still a work in progress
comments.comment:
THE BASIC CONCEPT IS GREAT

o Give it a Google sheet, whose cells refer to a collection of images, Google Docs, etc. 
o Choose a website template.
o And it will pull together the referenced resources and create an attractive, useful, 1-page website based upon the chosen template.

STRENGHTS AND WEAKNESSES OF THIS APPROACH

The strength of this approach is that you can quickly and easily create and update attractive, functional 1-page websites.  The weakness is that someone else has made all the design and layout decisions for you, and very litte customization thereof is possible.

They say that you can fully control styles with custom CSS, and they give you a big text box where you can paste whatever CSS you want, but they don't document their CSS classes and selectors, so in effect very little custom stying is possible.

THE TEMPLATES ARE UNEVEN

Of the 29 templates, some are very useful.  For example the Documentation template will compile a list of Google Docs into an online "book", where each Google Doc is a chapter.  And the Blog template looks pretty useful.

On the other hand, some are not really useful, such as the eCommerce template, which doesn't handle sales tax, and applies the same, fixed shipping charge to all purchases.

And there are some that are in-between, such as the Table template, which produces a very attractive table layout, but only of four columns.

And the Landing Page template is totally useless.  It basically gives you your own copy of the Sheetany home page, but doesn't let you create your own content.

GETTING STARTED IS HARDER THAN IT SHOULD BE

The basic process of creating a 1-page website from a template is fast and easy — once you learn all the tricks.  But they don't have a simple explanation of all these tricks, so it took a lot of frustrating experimentation, and some back and forth with support, to be able to figure it out.

THE DOCUMENTATION IS LACKING

Of the 29 templates, there are only explanations in the online documentation for 14 of them, of which six are actual explanations, and the rest just contain copies of the explanation for the Waitlist template, so are effectively meaningless.

ONE SPECIAL PAGE, PLUS MULTIPLE GOOGLE-DOC PAGES?

An architectural oddity is that after using a template to create a 1-page website, you can add additional pages to the website by specifying one or more Google Docs, each of which will become an additional page in the website.  So you end up with one "fancy" homepage, maybe a blog, and an arbitrary number of additional "plain" pages that are generated from Google Docs.

CLOSING COMMENTS

There is a lot more that could be said, but the above gives the big picture.

In my opinion, for those  who want to be able to create clean, attractive, functional 1-page websites, such as a documentation site, or a blog, but don't know how to design, code and test them, and if Sheetany has a working template that fulfills their needs, then Sheetany is an excellent product, and the lifetime deal is an incredible value.  I bought tier-3.

comments.title: Keep Pushing
comments.comment:
I have been using Sheetany since its launch, and overall, I am quite pleased with the platform. It offers a simple and user-friendly interface, which makes it accessible for users who want to quickly create websites without a steep learning curve. This ease of use is definitely one of its strongest points.

However, there are some limitations that hold it back from being truly outstanding. For instance, the platform currently lacks certain basic features, such as the ability to apply multiple filters or more advanced customization options. While I understand that Sheetany is designed to be straightforward, this simplicity sometimes restricts users who want to differentiate their sites and add a unique look and feel.

A notable drawback is the inability to change default template text, such as the "About Us" section or the labeling of buttons—for example, the "Submit" button in the directory is hardcoded to say "Tools" in its content, making it nearly unusable for directories focusing on other types of content than tools. This significantly limits flexibility and customization, which is essential for creating a site that truly fits your needs.

Despite these shortcomings, I continue to use Sheetany because it meets my primary requirements, and I appreciate its intuitive design. I am hopeful that future updates will add more functionality while preserving the excellent usability that initially attracted me to the platform.

In summary, I would rate Sheetany 4 out of 5 stars. It’s a solid product with room for improvement, especially regarding customization and flexibility.

If in the future these problems are solved, i will be back and edit the review.

If SpreadSimple is the established powerhouse of spreadsheet-based sites, then Sheetany is the eager newcomer — clean design, low price, and a few rough edges.

Feature-wise, Sheetany still trails behind. You can only search titles (not full text), and in most templates, filtering is limited to a single filter at a time. Want to combine filters? Usually not possible. Support is minimal: there’s no portal, just an email address — and out of two messages, I got one reply.

But here’s the thing: Sheetany’s templates are stunning. The minimalist design is crisp, modern, and frankly more elegant than anything SpreadSimple currently offers. If a template fits your needs, it’s a joy to use — fast, intuitive, and visually impressive straight out of the box. And with a roadmap full of upcoming features, it’s clear the team is moving fast.

Not as powerful as SpreadSimple — yet — but a beautifully promising alternative.

UPDATE: 1th July 2025: Initially, I gave 4 tacos, but the developer has been so proactive and already addressed all the points I mentioned. I can’t give anything less than 5 tacos now!

comments.title: A good security addition to our agency stack and a quick reality check on licensing
comments.comment:
WP Login Lockdown is a good addition to our agency tech stack. The centralised dashboard makes managing multiple client installations painless, the interface is clean, and the Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) works wel. In an environment where brute-force login attempts and automated credential stuffing are constant threats, having frictionless, reliable 2FA deployed across client sites is an absolute no-brainer.

It is surprising to see highly upvoted reviews criticising this product due to licensing limitations and support response times. Those criticisms stem from a fundamental misunderstanding of both commercial software licensing and standard agency operations.

How Agency & White-Label Licences Actually Work
There is a distinct legal difference between an agency white-label licence and Master Resell Rights (MRR):

The Agency Model: An agency licence permits you to rebrand the plugin and install it across client sites as part of a comprehensive service offering, such as website design, secure hosting, or ongoing maintenance and care plans. The client pays for your managed service and security oversight; the white-labelling simply ensures a clean, bespoke experience without third-party vendor clutter.

The Resale Fallacy: No software company sells a lifetime licence that allows a purchaser to turn around and resell individual licence keys, setup standalone purchase links, or distribute raw downloads to the public. You cannot buy a stock photograph and sell it on your own stock library; you integrate it into a client project. Expecting distribution rights to run an independent software resale business off the back of an agency tier is completely detached from industry reality.

A Realistic Look at Support Turnaround
Complaining that technical support responded in "a few hours" is equally misguided. In the software industry, standard developer Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for non-emergency tickets typically sit between 24 and 48 hours. Receiving a direct, effective resolution within several hours is well above industry standard, it is an agile, responsive development team that deserves applause, not docked stars.

The plugin delivers precisely what it advertises: robust login security, rock-solid 2FA, intuitive remote dashboard management, and fair, transparent licensing terms that protect both the developer and the agencies building value on top of it. Highly recommended for any serious web professional.

comments.title: Build the WordPress site, then manage it after launch
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

There are plenty of AI tools that can make a website, and plenty of tools that can manage WordPress sites after they have been made. SiteSkite tries to cover both sides.

On Tier 2 and above, AI Site Studio can take a description of the site you want and generate a real, editable WordPress site in its own sandbox. You can explore different directions, refine the site through conversation, and then publish or export it to your own WordPress host. Because the result stays in WordPress, you are not moving the client onto a proprietary website builder just to use the AI generation.

After launch, the same platform handles the work that comes with maintaining WordPress sites: backups, plugin and theme updates, uptime monitoring, security checks, staging, rollbacks and client reports. For an agency or freelancer, I can see the appeal of using the same system to create the first version of a client site and then continuing to use it for the maintenance contract afterwards.

The sandbox side is useful even if you are not using the AI builder. You can create a fresh environment or clone an existing site from a backup, test plugins or updates away from production, and only push changes once you are comfortable with them.

SiteSkite also supports MCP, so you can connect tools such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor and use them to work with your connected WordPress sites and SiteSkite operations. During my original test, the Cursor setup asked me to copy my active browser login cookie into the configuration, which I wasn't comfortable with. The team replaced that method, and I rechecked the change.

I also ran into an issue with AI Site Studio during my first test. It spent 1,625 credits and more than 11 minutes generating a site before checking whether I had an available sandbox slot. The generation finished, but it couldn't publish. The team added the capacity check before generation, and I verified that the change is working well.

Backups were the one area where my experience was less straightforward. A full backup of my test site repeatedly stopped at 13%, even after I updated and disabled the other plugins and tried again in incognito mode. The partner was eventually able to back up the same site and traced the problem to restrictions or caching at the 20i host that I was using for my test site. So this turned out to have been specific to that hosting environment, but I was never able to get that particular full backup to complete myself. I would test backups early on the hosting providers you use most.

You can also store backups in your own cloud storage instead of relying entirely on SiteSkite's included storage, which is useful if you already have your own backup setup or want more control over where those files are kept.

For me, the main advantage is the full WordPress workflow. You can create or clone a site, test it away from production, publish it, and then continue managing, monitoring, backing up and reporting on that same site afterwards. For agencies in particular, that can replace several separate tools used at different stages of a client's website.

comments.title: I am genuinely impressed -every Taco well deserved
comments.comment:
I bought Support Board a few weeks ago and have been busy setting it up. I was completely new to chatbots and had to learn everything from scratch. Before Support Board, I purchased another chatbot here on AP and had tried yet another one before that, but neither met my expectations.

It took me some time to understand a lot of things—not only related to Support Board but also general concepts like how to prompt a bot correctly, how different functions work, and where to find them. There are definitely areas that can be improved, and I’ll get into that, but first things first:

The support has been outstanding.
I want to highlight the great support I received from Federico. His help and patience were exceptional. At some point, I even felt bad for asking so many questions, but he still responded thoroughly every time. Their website support bot is also incredibly helpful; I spent a lot of time chatting with it while setting up some more advanced configurations.

The possibilities you get with Support Board are impressive.
The sheer amount of features is on another level, with Shopify integration being just one of them. SB is not your typical basic chatbot—it’s built to handle many business cases. I still can’t believe how much value you get for such a low investment. I’ve compared it with other tools and even chatted with other business owners about it; they were genuinely impressed, especially after hearing about the price and capabilities.

Is it perfect? No—there are hiccups. But overall, this tool is amazing. You get an OpenAI-powered chatbot with many visual and technical customization options. You can connect multiple WhatsApps, integrate various platforms, create and separate inhouse departments, and even access a built-in CRM. There’s an API for WhatsApp bulk messaging—which was NOT easy to set up, but once it works, it’s a game-changer. I'm wondering why this gets so little attention, it is a GREAT GREAT feature you easily pay good money for if using another subscription tool. You get human takeover, and OMG: SMART REPLIES (something I had been searching for without even knowing the name, I cant stress how much I love this feature), which give real-time suggestions to human agents based on your training material —even new hires will be able to perform well with that in support. There’s also a unified inbox for all communication channels, snippets, flows, automations, agent notifications, user notifications, fallback messages via SMS/email, and so much more that I can’t even list everything.

At the beginning, I got mixed results, but that had more to do with my own prompts and training material. After restructuring and improving my content, the bot performance improved significantly. I wish I had been able to test it on a broader scale; I’m about to launch a new Meta Ads campaign where SB will play a major role in retargeting a campaign as the first responder via WhatsApp, really looking forward to it and that will REALLY be the stress test. Even with limited testing, the results were already pretty decent, and the Shopify integration worked very well.

Again, it’s not perfect—no tool is. Many business owners I know spend up to $150/month on bots (without Meta messaging costs) and still don’t get perfect results. So expectations need to stay realistic.

A few things I would love to see improved or added:

-The API works, but I struggled to retrieve the phone field form the user contacts. In one automation case i managed to get them, but in another i just couldn't find a way.
-A simple, native auto-reply function that doesn’t require OpenAI or Dialogflow.
-A native iOS app (the PWA works, but a more robust app would be great).
-The UI is somewhat basic and feels outdated—but honestly, I prefer a simple UI that works over a flashy one full of bugs.
-The menu can be confusing at first, though manageable once you learn your way around.
-Automations are available but either lack certain functions or I couldn’t figure out how to configure them properly.

Overall: this tool is AMAZING. I genuinely don’t understand why more people aren’t talking about it. It deserves way more attention than it gets. Maybe I am over enthusiastic and I really hope I will not change my mind when I try it out on a major scale, but for now, I am happy about this purchase.

So my final conclusion: 5/5 Tacos — and GRAB IT WHILE YOU CAN!!!

comments.title: Makes Inbox Management Fun

I am horrible about managing and organizing my inboxes. I have one personal and one business email and decided to give AI Emaily a shot with Tier 1 mostly for email organization not for any AI email drafts. In about 24 hours I made significant progress in getting things organized and am really impressed with the UI/UX. It's the only email tool I have used that actually makes email management and organization surprisingly fun. I plan on keeping this and possibly upgrading but I do think there is some room for improvement. 

1. Custom Tabs: Would like to be able to create my own custom tabs and delete default tabs that are irrelevant to me (VIP)

2. Label Tier Flexibility: Currently you can only create a Parent Label, A child tier and a sub-child tier. I would like the flexibility to create further level tiers below the sub-child tier level.

3. AI credit analytics and customization: I would like to see more robust credit usage analytics by AI category and the ability to turn off AI features that might not be adding enough value to justify the credit burn. Just a quick look at my AI credit usage and I can tell you that Thread Summaries seem to be a significant credit usage category for me but adding limited value. I would like the ability to turn off Thread Summaries (as an example) in order to save my AI credits for AI features I value more. Adding the ability to customize AI credit features is a win/win for AI Emaily and your clients.

4. Ability to add custom API non-email messaging channels: I would like the ability to turn this into a true multi-channel unified inbox by adding the ability to integrate custom API messaging channels. (Textlink API SMS, WhatApp and others)

5. AI Credits burn very fast: I am not even using the AI to draft emails and I have already used over half my monthly credits in 48 hours of use. I acknowledge that setting up and running new rules are likely a big contribution to this and that is why the one-time credits are provided.

6. Missing an AppSumo Tier: You need to add a new tier for Solopreneurs between the current tier 2/3. The tier should be for one seat, one inbox but with all the features of tier 3. It just doesn't seem fair for a solopreneur to over pay for extra seats and inboxes that aren't needed.

7. Lack of AI credit flexibility on AppSumo Tier 3/4: I really don't like that AI credits are capped per user. For tier three as an example just give 3600 AI credits that are distributed among the 6 seats which averages 600 credits per user. That way there is a way for a smaller organization or solopreneur to get more value out of the tier credits and also allows employees with greater usage needs to go over while employees with less AI credit usage needs will average it out.

Overall an impressive start with some small areas of improvement and a promising roadmap.

comments.title: Cold pitches out of the way, replies ready to review
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

My email is scattered across five different inboxes, so I sometimes miss important messages simply because I haven't checked the right account. Having all five in one place would make it much more  manageable. Then there are the cold pitches that aren't technically spam. They're emails from people I've never spoken to, asking for a quick call or trying to sell me something, and they arrive right alongside messages I actually need to answer.

AI Emaily is designed to recognize those pitches and move them out of the way. It looks at the sender, the content, and whether you have an existing relationship. The emails can be filed separately rather than deleted, so you can recover a message or allowlist someone if it gets the classification wrong.

The reply feature is also very useful. You can give AI Emaily your writing preferences, business information, and individual client profiles. It uses that information and the conversation history to prepare replies. I would much rather review a draft that already has the relevant details than explain the same things to an AI assistant every time I open an email.

In Copilot mode, you review and approve the replies yourself. There is also an Autopilot mode for people who want to automate certain actions using rules they control.

The core features worked as expected during testing. I initially couldn't find where to configure the webhooks, but the team has since made those settings available under Billing & Developer. The product also supports MCP, BYOK, and an API, which gives users more options for connecting their email to other applications and AI assistants (not just Google Workspace and Outlook accounts).

Overall, AI Emaily is worth considering if you manage several inboxes, receive a lot of unsolicited outreach, or spend too much time writing similar replies. I particularly like the combination of bringing multiple accounts together, filtering cold pitches, and preparing replies using your own client information. For someone like me, I can see it helping me stay on top of things and manage my email in a way that makes perfect sense.

- Easy to deploy and customize: The widget interface is easy to configure (position, animations, display behavior), supports over 30 messaging and live-chat platforms in a single widget, allowing us to deliver a unified solution to clients without installing multiple plugins.
- Optimized for e-commerce and services: Good WooCommerce integration, plus contact form, FAQ, and Knowledge Base help reduce tickets, boost sales, and improve customer experience.
- Fast support and quick deployment: Customer support responds quickly, enabling our agency to roll out across many projects with minimal technical issues.
- Many monetization ideas.
Bit Assist Pro delivers clear value for an agency — both technically and as a revenue-generating tool through service packages for clients. After consideration, I purchased Bit Assist Pro and give it 5 stars. Highly recommended for shops and service sites.

comments.title: Solid omnichannel platform with huge potential—needs deeper CRM customization, contact sync, and thread controls
comments.comment:
We have been using AnyChat integrated with our custom CRM for several months to manage client communications across WhatsApp (QR), Instagram, and Facebook Messenger from a centralized dashboard.

The core system delivers well on basic messaging aggregation and webhook architecture. However, to become an indispensable, top-tier solution for sales teams, there are a few key feature gaps and workflow friction points that need to be addressed:

1. Better Thread Management (Stop Auto-Archiving Bot Chats!):
When the automated bot interacts or replies to a lead, the conversation often gets archived or displaced from the main active inbox. Bot-handled threads must stay explicitly visible in a dedicated status tab (e.g., "Bot Active" or "Pending Review") until a human agent manually marks the lead as resolved or archived.

2. Contact Identity & Google Contacts / Gmail Sync:
There is a strong need for direct integration with Google Contacts / Gmail API to resolve raw phone numbers or social handles (@username) against our team's contact address book. Syncing contact names automatically would make the inbox experience significantly more personalized and organized.

3. Native Support for @usernames (Phoneless Messaging):
As WhatsApp and social platforms shift towards username handles without exposing traditional phone numbers, AnyChat should seamlessly support starting chats, sending attachments, and linking leads using handles alone, without hard-requiring a numeric phone number.

4. Deeper CRM Customization & Automated Follow-Up Engine:
We would love to see more native customization for CRM workflows:

Automated Sequences: Triggering scheduled follow-ups (e.g., sending an automatic re-engagement message 24–48 hours after a quote is sent if the customer hasn't replied).

Flexible Auto-Replies & Snippets: A more customizable auto-responder system supporting rich media (PDFs, images, and quick-reply templates) tailored to specific lead stages.

5. Transparent Monthly Reports on System Stability & Product Improvements:
As AnyChat continues to mature, it would be extremely valuable for agency owners and team leads to receive a monthly report or digest. Having a structured breakdown covering platform uptime/stability metrics, newly deployed feature improvements, and upcoming roadmap items would help us keep our clients informed and demonstrate the ongoing value of the system.

Verdict:
AnyChat is a robust product with a great foundation. If the roadmap includes Google Contacts integration, better thread preservation for bot interactions, deeper automated follow-up tools, and regular improvement reports, it will easily become the ultimate gold standard for omnichannel client management.

I've been using AppSumo for over 8 years and have purchased more than 20 products. Surprisingly, this is actually my first review on the platform.

Before purchasing AnyChat, I spent several days testing it thoroughly, and I have to say I was genuinely impressed.

### What I Like

* The documentation is quite clear. There is definitely a learning curve because there are many features and integrations to configure, but I was able to get most things working within a day or two. I don't think it's too difficult, even for people with limited technical experience.

* The interface is better than some reviews suggest. Personally, I had no major issues with it and found it fairly easy to navigate.

* I encountered a few minor issues with the widget, but nothing critical. Most of the time I tried to solve them myself, and if needed I can always contact support.

* I made an effort to test almost every feature, even those I may not personally need. I also tested multiple languages, and overall the results were very good.

### What I'm Still Waiting For

**1. Appointment Booking**

This is probably the biggest feature request from my perspective.

AnyChat already does an excellent job answering questions, but if it could directly access calendars, manage bookings, and schedule appointments automatically, it would become much easier for me to sell to clients.

At the moment, my workaround is to detect booking-related keywords and send those requests to email, but a native booking system would be a huge improvement.

**2. Translation Features**

Many of my clients interact with foreign customers every day. Sometimes the biggest challenge isn't answering questions—it's writing the answer in the correct language.

I have seen other chatbot platforms offer translation features, but they require users to access the admin panel and, honestly, the translations are often poor.

A well-designed translation system inside AnyChat would solve a real business problem for many users.

### Final Thoughts

I originally wanted to give this product an 8/10 because there is always room for improvement.

However, I'm giving it a **10/10** because I can clearly see the effort and dedication behind the product. The platform has improved significantly, the team continues to develop it, and it has become one of my favorite AppSumo purchases.

Keep up the great work.

**P.S.** If a UX Designer compliments your product, that's probably a sign you're doing something right. 🙂

If the team continues improving stability, onboarding/tutorials, and automation templates, this could become one of the strongest communication platforms on AppSumo.

Overall:

- Excellent value for agencies
- Powerful white-label opportunity
- Massive feature set
- Multi-channel support done well
- Active development team
- Strong customization
- Great LTD value

Definitely one of the more impressive AppSumo purchases I’ve made recently.

comments.title: It's new, it's shiny, it still needs work -- but it's got a ton of potential!
comments.comment:
I was debating the 5-llama rating on this, truth be told. Five stars, for me, would normally be a fully finished and ready-to-go product. This isn't quite there yet; it works, the bones are there, they just need to be fully fleshed out first.

The thing is, and what made me keep the 5-burrito rating on it, is the pure ambition and complexity of what they're working on here.

If you're looking at this, I'm assuming you've used agents to do parts of things in your work life. You've probably got one running in the background right now (Claude, how's that plugin going anyways?). What's missing, though, is the brain that's holding all the bits and pieces together. 

I know, ideally, I'm supposed to be that brain in my world. The problem is, between the 'tism, the ADHD, and the wildness of my 20s, the brain doesn't do so hot when it comes to retaining context. Heck, I'm not even good at sharing context -- my totally disjointed stories are proof of that (just ask my wife). 

So what do we do when the flesh-brain doesn't work too well? 

Up til now, I've segmented off parts of it to hand off to robot brains. They used to be very bad robot brains, because robot brains couldn't point out things like "maybe the toaster isn't a good bath bomb," but now they're smart enough to be like "maybe something in a soothing lavender instead?"

Where was I going with this

Oh right, anyways, Agently is setting out to be that robot brain in the centre of things -- the one that knows what's going on so your fleshy brain doesn't need to. The one you can turn to and be like "Hey Jarvis, I hit my head and don't remember who I am, what do I need to do next?" and it'll list off the five top emails you need to reply to, what meetings you have, and your local hospital's average emergency wait time so you can hopefully get that concussion checked before those meetings.

So, for overall product *readiness*? 3/5 guacamoles. 
But, for project ambition and *where it's going*? 7/5 puppies wearing sombreros. 

Overall score: 5/5 freshly baked apple pies.

As a SaaS startup owner, managing user feedback was becoming a chaotic mess. We were drowning in feature requests scattered across emails, Slack threads, and support tickets. FeatureShift has been the perfect tool to bring order to that chaos.

What makes it brilliant:

• Unbelievably Easy to Set Up and Use: We had our public roadmap portal live and embedded in our app in under an hour. The interface is so intuitive that our entire team—from developers to support—adopted it without any training. This simplicity is its superpower.

• Transparency Builds Trust: The public roadmap has transformed our relationship with our users. Instead of their suggestions vanishing into a black hole, they can now see, vote, and comment on ideas. We've noticed a significant drop in frustrated support queries and an increase in constructive, collaborative feedback.

• Focuses on What Matters: It cuts through the noise. The voting system automatically surfaces the features our users genuinely care about, making prioritisation data-driven and easier to justify. It's stopped the "squeaky wheel" from getting all the grease.

• Excellent Value for Money: Compared to clunky, enterprise-grade tools that cost a fortune, FeatureShift offers exactly what a growing product team needs at a sensible price. It's a lean, focused tool that delivers immense value without unnecessary complexity.

A Minor Consideration:

If you're a massive enterprise requiring deep, custom integration with Jira on a field-by-field level or complex permission schemes, you might find it a bit lightweight. However, for most small-to-medium-sized businesses and product teams, its feature set is spot-on.

FeatureShift has become an indispensable part of our product development cycle. It has made us more organised, our process more transparent, and our users feel heard. For any UK product team looking to professionalise their feedback loop without overcomplicating things, I cannot recommend it highly enough.

comments.title: A solid offering for product reviews (updated)
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I’m a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give. 

Update to my original beta test score:
The issues and concerns I discovered during my testing (see Cons) seem to have all been appropriately addressed since my original testing. I now believe ProductBridge to be a valuable platform for anyone needing to track feedback and keep users updated with changes. I have changed my 3 taco score based on initial testing prior to the Appsumo launch to 5 tacos. Welcome to Appsumo ProductBridge!

After a thorough beta testing session of ProductBridge, I am giving this tool a solid 3 out of 5 tacos. ProductBridge is a versatile client portal and feedback management software that allows you to collect, analyze, and act on user feedback to improve your product or service offerings. The platform centers around three core modules: Feedback, Roadmap, and Changelog. These features are incredibly beneficial for finding out what users want in a product, tracking bug submissions, and keeping customers updated on improvements and new features.

What truly differentiates ProductBridge from many other platforms in this category is its AI agent. The AI automatically collects feedback for you by pulling data from public review sources like Trustpilot and the App Store, monitoring support channels such as Intercom and Zendesk, and listening to team channels like Slack and Discord. This means you don't have to manually gather feedback. Furthermore, the AI works very well when tasked with creating posts and determining the proper next course of action after reviewing the provided feedback.

However, the product is not without its flaws. The onboarding experience lacks sufficient resources, leaving new users without adequate guidance on how to effectively utilize the platform and its workflows. Additionally, the UI's monochromatic gray background with black text lacks vibrancy. Despite these hiccups and a few bugs, the tool is definitely ready for an AppSumo launch. With a few fixes, more integrations, and expanded user limits, this could easily be a 4- or 5-taco deal.

Pros:
Modular Flexibility and Automation: ProductBridge provides significant value through its modular approach, allowing you to enable specific tools like Feedback, Roadmap, and Changelog based on your specific communication needs.  
Easy Setup and Navigation: The platform stands out for being easy to set up and use overall, enabling users to get started with minimal effort. The layout is intuitively designed, providing a clear structure that makes it easy to locate and interact with features across the different modules.  
Versatile Portal Deployment: ProductBridge provides multiple deployment options for making its customer portal accessible. You can easily choose from a popup, sidebar integration, iframe embedding, or direct link sharing, which ensures compatibility across various use cases and user preferences.

Cons: (please note that these cons have all been addressed since initial beta testing, but have been left here for reference)
Restrictive Team Limits: The 15-member maximum per organization for tiers 3 and 4 may be significant limitation for some, especially for organizations with larger teams. 
File Upload Issues: A frustrating bug prevents the uploading of larger documents to the knowledge base. Users are only able to upload small file sizes, forcing them to break documents down into smaller sizes to bypass the restriction. (Please note that this limitation and others may have been corrected since my beta testing).

comments.title: This is really groundbreaking...

Spokk is great so far and the founder has been extremely responsive. Just starting to get set up with it and ran into a few kinks. To date, Samesh has helped resolve all of them. 

Truly hope this helps us get more reviews. Just sent out our first requests today; we'll see who responds. (Love that a QR code is generated to use instead of the review link if we want, too.)

In practice, it seems like the concept needs a bit of explanation before we sent clients, since it's SO new. Literally NO ONE ELSE is using this that I've seen. So I explained that "a review would be generated from their initial ratings, which they can edit, paste into Google (our location choice), or answer a few short Qs to get a more customized review to paste." Felt like just sending them to the rating page without that preface would've been bad practice.

With such a novel concept as an "AI generated review," we wanted to explain what to expect, so so they didn't feel like "we'd given them a review to paste into Google." If that makes sense. I also explained that we're seeking their *honest* feedback, not "5-star reviews." 

Anyhow, appreciate that the UI is clean and attractive. (And FAST. So many of the tools I've tried from Appsumo are slow as molasses!) It's lacking a few basic functions -- like deleting locations after you added them, and editing some elements you expect to be able to edit -- but writing support has gotten replies in <24 hours (often w/i minutes), so not a huge issue. (Resolutions actually, not just replies.) 

I look forward to seeing how this tool develops and grows, but honestly it's already amazing right out the box. One of my top buys from Appsumo to-date. Looking forward to continuing to test how to incorporate Spokk into our workflow, to maximize the changes we'll get more -- and more detailed -- reviews!

comments.title: Four tacos for now — and here's why
comments.comment:
This is, so far, a mixed bag that I hope gets better as they get over the huge increase in traffic and technical problems from this deal.

I bought Wordplay yesterday, and the first thing I wanted to do was test the AI module and see if it could knock out a decent long-form article with just a keyword or two as the creator claimed.

It. Was. Flawless. I selected 500 words (you can also opt for 750 and 1500) and got back 630. However, I was only charged for the 500 (nice).

I own three other AI writing tools, and have subscribed to several more, including the so-called best of breed. NONE ever spit out anything like the piece Wordplay gave, even after I worked with a tool for an hour or more, using all their prompts, tricks, and workarounds. 

All I did was give Wordplay two words, and in a few minutes I got back a finished piece with subheads I didn't generate on my own, and it made sense. I could have stood up at a podium and delivered what they gave me, and would have received a decent grade.

Okay, that's the good part of the review. 

Their site is shaky, and they say that's because of the workload they hadn't anticipated. I'll take them at their word. If true, this should improve. 

My second project didn't work. I asked for quotations on a subject. The system wrote another nice intro paragraph and then wrote: "Here are 15 motivational quotes..." The trouble is, no quotes followed. Maybe there are workarounds. Hopefully, somebody from the company will see this and respond.

Wordplay needs a chat service. My guess is this is a very small team and they don't have the people to handle that, or they just don't think it's necessary. All you can do is email and they indicated it will be up to two days before they reply. 

Other thoughts...

Wordplay limits are very tight. You only get 7500 words per month. 

I also bought Writecream yesterday, and they offer 400,000 characters per month, or about 67,000 words, for $59. In my writing, I count 6 characters as one word, so Writecream's limit is NINE TIMES higher than Wordplay.

If they presumably use the same technology to power their systems, I wonder why one is so much more than the other.

I know I can buy more codes from Wordplay at $99 each, but that's really not the issue. The limit is too low.

I also suggest Wordplay create the option to buy additional words in a given month when a project requires it...say one-time bundles of 10,000 words for $10. That way, you could even write a book and not have to think of where you are with your word count.

Four tacos for now. The output can be industry best, no doubt, but the system also needs work — and I hope they review limitations to add better value and opportunity.

I'd like to think Wordplay can be a keeper.

With other AI's I'm usually tinkering around for several days on a single article, trying to piece whole paragraphs together to get a single decent blog post to read right. WordPlay's came out (basically) finished right out of the gate. I created and edited 3 articles in a couple hours. I'd say they're 87% ready to go, VS other apps that spit out writing that's like 50-60% ready and needs lots of human input.

-I marked 193 words for removal or editing, out of 1643 total words. (To me that's VERY good. Editing was pretty quick and easy)
