comments.title: Breeze through from idea to output
comments.comment:
I have had a couple of ideas scribbled on sheets of paper and this seemed like the perfect way to expand these thoughts into full fledged novels. I have purchased the Pro plan. 

The UI is great and flows easily. There is so many different fields (in a good way) to help direct the AI to give you the output you need. From explaining the premise, choosing the genres, and feeding sample text, it is clear you are giving enough instructions to get a clear output. The model then kicks in to generate the characters, their attributes and their role. You can edit this to your liking. Then an outline is generated which can be edited as well. Finally, the chapters get generated. All of this is pretty straightforward and this is great positive for this tool. Chapter generation is also clear. You are presented with different models to choose from. One thing that could be done here is to show the model you have used for the previous chapters. This way, the user doesn't use different models when they come back to the book after a while.

Once the chapters are created, there are metadata fields that, as a newbie, I would never know to fill. You can use AI to generate a book cover and finally get to various export formats. On a whim, I was able to do all of these steps in about 90 minutes. This was amazing.

Now comes the hard part. Reviewing the output of AI and seeing if this was ready to publish. I found the output to be quite repetitive in terms of the text. I gave paragraphs from Douglas Adams' Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy as my sample text. The output used the same phrases multiple times over the course of the book. Mr. Adams has a way of exaggeration and the trick is to keep it spread out enough to be funny. I understand it is hard for AI to understand things like frequency of usage and the effect of oversaturation. Using 6-8 paragraphs is not a good marker or reference. I wish this window could be expanded so the output is better.

Overall, quite happy with my purchase. I am also glad I took the Pro plan. For a book that came to 90 odd pages as a PDF, I had burnt through 500+ credits. For serious lengths, 1000 credits are an absolute minimum. Repeating text and phrases is the reason I am not giving this 5 tacos.

comments.title: The upgrade versatility is appreciated.
comments.comment:
I bought the lowest plan knowing that someday I *might* need more features, so I appreciate being able to buy evergreen credits/recurring plans that stack alongside my AppSumo deal without having to create a totally new account or risk overwriting the original AS deal. I wish more deals functioned like that. 

That hybrid growth model reduces the friction, decision fatigue, and questions choosing which AS tier to go with based on what I need now and guessing what I might do in the future. It also makes organically supporting a company beyond the deal/as it grows in features easier than being shoved a post-deal FOMO email upgrade, out of the blue, that only gives me a limited time to act.

The biggest con (and a pro) is this: it’s not a “click and get” book software. I’ve uploaded two ideas that are lingering in the middle of onboarding because the setup questions are so comprehensive. I find myself abandoning the setup because I’ve already figured all this out in ChatGPT, so I have to dig through my conversations there to copy/paste or ask it to summarize again in the context of the AIWriteBook onboarding question.

Next, some features gated on higher tiers seem more suited for fiction writers such as NSFW, book series, character builder, audiobook, NanoReads distribution, and thus the Author Page (which shows up on a NanoReads domain). I wish it was more balanced for Non-Fiction writers. I know that non-fiction is a book type I can pick; it just feels like an after-thought. I intend on writing non-fiction, visual books that are not for kids (no recurring characters needed), which is why I appreciate being able to get the visual book feature separately once I figure out if I even need it.

I haven’t reached the book designer yet, but based on the examples on the website and as a graphic designer who has designed book covers, they all have the same style…as in you feel like if AI didn’t exist, these authors all hired the same illustrator. So the book design feature didn’t sell me on the deal. I understand the need for it among non-designers, and I’m sure output will get better.

So all in all, I’ve purchased based on the marketing, planning, editing, and KDP book support aspect of the software. I’ve found it more useful to silo all that research inside AIWriteBook instead of the numerous ChatGPT projects that I forget exist.

comments.title: Great tool with massive potential, just needs more love on the visual books section!
comments.comment:
Overall, I’m really enjoying AIWriteBook! The AI writing assistant, book structuring, and bonus publishing tools are fantastic for keeping everything in one streamlined workflow instead of jumping between multiple platforms. It saves a ton of time and offers a lot of value.

However, as someone who creates visual books, I feel like that section still needs work to become truly intuitive. Right now, the page management and graphic layout features feel a bit clunky.

Here are a few specific areas where the experience could be improved:

- Easier Page Management: Reordering pages is currently quite difficult, especially when trying to insert a new page at the very beginning of a project. A simple visual drag-and-drop page overview grid would make a world of difference.
- Better Typography & Graphic Text Placement: It’s challenging to get a proper graphic layout for text on visual pages. Adding more formatting flexibility, custom font options, and precise text-box positioning would give creators the control needed for polished internal layouts.
-Text-to-Illustration Auto-Parsing: It would be an absolute game-changer if we could upload a manuscript or text PDF, and have the software automatically parse the scenes and generate complementary illustrations around or alongside the existing text.

The foundation of AIWriteBook is solid, and the developers clearly care about building a powerful tool. With some UI polish and stronger layout controls for illustrated titles, this could easily be the ultimate all-in-one publishing suite. Definitely worth grabbing!

comments.title: Great idea, but the publishing workflow needs work
comments.comment:
I bought AIWriteBook because I wanted a straightforward way to create and publish children's books, and there is a lot I like about the idea behind the software.
I created a complete children's picture book using the platform. The book itself came together well and I was happy enough with the finished content and illustrations to actually publish it.
The problems started when I tried to turn that finished book into a real Amazon KDP paperback.
The biggest issue was getting the exported files to match the exact KDP dimensions and requirements. I tried different settings and sizes, but ultimately had to use other software and manually work through the sizing and cover problems before Amazon would accept everything.
I did eventually get the book successfully submitted to Amazon KDP, so the software can certainly help create a publishable book. But the final journey from “finished book” to “uploaded to KDP” was much more difficult and time-consuming than I expected from software aimed at book creation.
I also found the credit system frustrating. Generating and rendering a book can consume credits while you are still experimenting and correcting problems, so it can feel as though you are paying again while trying to finish something you have already started.
There are things I genuinely like. Editing some of my earlier pages did not cost additional credits, the image quality could be surprisingly good, and the basic concept of creating the story, illustrations and book in one workspace is excellent.
My main suggestion to the developers would be to concentrate heavily on the final publishing stage. If I choose an 8.25 × 6 inch KDP paperback with bleed, I want the software to produce the correct interior PDF and complete cover file for that exact specification, ready to upload to KDP without needing Canva or another program to repair or resize it.
Ideally there should be a simple final step: choose the KDP book size and print options, run a preflight check, and download the correctly sized KDP-ready interior and cover.
I like the concept and I want the software to succeed. My first book has now made it all the way to KDP review, which is why I haven't given up on it. But the publishing/export side needs to become as straightforward as the book-creation side before I would consider the whole process finished.

comments.title: A useful writing partner, not a one-click author
comments.comment:
I bought AIWriteBook through AppSumo because I wanted a practical workspace for turning book ideas and existing material into a structured draft. My experience so far is still early, so I’m reviewing the part I can honestly assess: it is much more useful as a writing partner than as a one-click book generator.

The strongest part is the guided workflow. Keeping the premise, outline, chapter goals, style, characters and references together makes it easier to move forward and see how the book fits as a whole. It can genuinely help structure a project, get past a blank page and speed up the first pass. I also like that the author remains in control: the output is something to review, edit and accept, not a replacement for the author’s judgement.

The important caveat is that “publish-ready” still needs a human behind it. I would fact-check every nonfiction claim, verify citations and links, watch for omissions or invented details, check continuity and edit the voice. I would use AIWriteBook to organise, accelerate and suggest—not as the source of truth or the final editor.

My wishlist is fairly specific: true version history and restore; lossless import/export with a clear inventory of sections, links and metadata; downloadable editorial reports with comments anchored to the exact passages; more precise, localised editing instead of broad rewrites; live-web research with per-claim sources for nonfiction; market/country/language controls for trend and keyword tools; and a clear way to export a working manuscript before publication steps. I’d also appreciate clearer credit estimates and the option to skip automatic image generation when it isn’t needed.

Overall, this is a promising and useful tool for authors who want structure and momentum without handing over authorship. I’m glad I bought it, and I expect its value to grow as I use it on real projects, but I’m keeping the human editorial pass firmly in the workflow.

comments.title: Almost all in one place
comments.comment:
A structured and fast AI book builder, but watch your credits and formatting limits.

I recently used AIWriteBook to write a children's book for elementary school kids. Overall, the software has a lot of potential, but there are a few important workflows and limitations that future buyers should keep in mind.
The Good:Fast and Structured Workflow: If you come in with a clear idea, the writing process itself is incredibly fast. I really appreciated that the platform does not let you skip steps. It forces a disciplined, step-by-step creation flow which is great for staying on track.
Excellent Sidebar Tools: Each step in the process comes with a very useful set of additional tools in the side menu. There are so many nice extra features included that I haven't even had the chance to try them all yet.

Consistent Image Generation: The generated images were surprisingly consistent across the project. However, it is a bit hard to control the exact look of everything, and I am still not fully sure if this consistency is due to smart AI tracking or if the system simply uses the exact same base style every time.

Book Series Feature: The option to build out entire book series is a fantastic touch for maintaining continuity, though having only completed my first book, I can't yet speak to how well it holds up across multiple volumes.

 Improvement:
Outline Precision is Crucial: You must be highly specific about what you want in each chapter during the early outline stage. If you aren't, the AI tends to create plot contradictions between chapters, and you will find yourself regenerating the same chapter over and over again.

 During Editing: Watch out for your credits! While the editor states it costs only about 3 credits per edit, it accumulates incredibly fast. I burned through 500 credits just doing edits.
Lack of Guided AI Editing: Although there is an AI editing tool available in the sidebar, I struggled to get it to do what I actually wanted. The manual editing process was a bit tedious. If I wanted to change something, I had to do it completely manually. You cannot highlight a specific block of text or prompt the AI directly to explain exactly what is bothering you or what needs fixing.

 for elementary school children, I found that the AI initially generated prose that was far too high-level. I had to spend a significant amount of time rewriting and simplifying the language to make it age-appropriate.

 Limitations: The formatting tools inside the chapter editor are very basic. I would love to see a more professional book layout engine. Currently, you can easily end up with annoying layout issues, like a single page at the end of a section containing only two lines, or make the chapters starting in the middle of a page rather than at the top of a page as is standard in professional publishing.

Amazon KDP Cover Constraints: While the front cover generated nicely, the system only outputs the front image. To actually publish on Amazon KDP, you need a full-wrap cover (front, back, and spine). I had to take the image into external software to manually calculate the spine width (using Amazon's calculator based on page count) and build the back cover. Having a full print-ready cover layout generator built directly into the app would be a massive upgrade.Audiobook Credits: Generating an audiobook requires far more credits than what my monthly allowance provides in tier 3, so I had to skip trying that feature entirely.
Verdict: 4/5 Tacos. It is a solid foundation that will save you days of drafting if you feed it a highly detailed outline. However, be prepared to do heavy manual editing, keep an eye on your credit usage, and use external tools if you plan to publish a physical paperback on Amazon.

AIWriteBook ist ein interessantes Tool, wenn man schnell von einer Idee zu einer kompletten Buchstruktur kommen möchte. Besonders hilfreich fand ich die Bereiche für Charaktere, Gliederung, Kapitelplanung, Metadaten und Cover. Auch die Möglichkeit, verschiedene KI-Modelle für die Kapitelerstellung auszuwählen, ist praktisch.

Mein Buchprojekt konnte ich damit tatsächlich von der ersten Idee bis zu einem vollständigen Manuskript bringen. Allerdings sollte man nicht erwarten, dass das Ergebnis ohne Kontrolle direkt veröffentlichungsfertig ist. Bei meinem Projekt war noch recht viel Nachbearbeitung nötig. Einzelne Handlungselemente waren teilweise widersprüchlich oder zu dramatisch, Details passten nicht immer zu bereits angelegten Charakteren und auch geografische Angaben mussten korrigiert werden. Gerade bei längeren Projekten sollte man deshalb die Kontinuität zwischen den Kapiteln genau prüfen.

Auch bei Metadaten wie Autorenbiografie und Danksagung wurden teilweise Angaben ergänzt, die nicht von mir stammten. Hier sollte man unbedingt alles kontrollieren und nicht ungeprüft übernehmen.

Positiv ist, dass sich Kapitel nachträglich bearbeiten lassen und der KI-Editor gezielte Änderungen ermöglicht. Nach mehreren Überarbeitungsrunden ließ sich daraus ein gutes Ergebnis entwickeln.

Beim Export für Amazon KDP gab es bei mir noch ein technisches Problem mit nicht vollständig eingebetteten Schriftarten, das ich extern korrigieren musste. Auch das Printcover wird nicht automatisch als vollständiger Umschlag mit Rückseite und Buchrücken ausgegeben, sondern benötigt noch zusätzliche Bearbeitung.

Fazit: AIWriteBook nimmt einem sehr viel Vorarbeit ab und ist besonders für Struktur, Ideenentwicklung und Rohfassungen hilfreich. Für ein professionell veröffentlichtes Buch sollte man aber Zeit für sorgfältige Prüfung, Überarbeitung und technische Nacharbeit einplanen. Wer das berücksichtigt, bekommt ein nützliches Werkzeug mit viel Potenzial.

comments.title: A Real Writing Tool
comments.comment:
Before I dive too deeply into this review, understand I consider this a good tool with a very high ceiling. There is a lot of potential here beyond just "push a button, get a book". This can be a real tool.

I've tried several AI writing tools. Each has its strengths; all have their weaknesses. AIWriteBook is no different. The issue for them isn't their approach or service. Both are sound. Their roadmap and board are actively updated and monitored. They seem to be very customer-centric. The issue they, and all other AI tools, deal with is the newness of this technology. So I leave this review with that understanding and the understanding that I have not used the tool as intended.

I already had my book written in rough form. In fact, I've uploaded two near-complete (meaning in the refinement stage) books to AIWriteBook. What I have used it for is formatting and consistency. This is where it has shone for me. I have a series of non-fiction books. Sometimes in these books I slip into rant mode, like it's a podcast. I also sometimes tell my stories for too long, like it's my next fiction book. In those situations, the app underlines the questionable text and tells me why it doesn't fit the book's tone, is redundant, or needs to be more concise. It then offers three different styles/solutions or lets you revise it yourself. If you pick a style and don't like the results, you can reject the solution. I appreciate that option.

In addition, if you have hit a wall with a chapter. The AI can help you write it or even completely rewrite it for you. This gives you control over how much or little AI input you get in your book.

The bonus tools like KDP A+ content, bio, keywords, etc., are all nice additions to the program. You can double-dip some of that with other sites like Lulu and get good results there as well. 

I haven't tested the audiobook feature yet. The audiobook world is a little afraid of AI-voiced books, and I have a pretty good clone on ElevenLabs and am getting ready to try out Vocallab. So, eventually I will get around to AIWriteBook's built-in audiobook, but I can't comment on it yet.

The option to add illustrations is a nice touch that's often overlooked. It still needs some work. If you edit the image it gives you, it has a pretty solid chance of losing whatever settings you had originally set. For example, if you ask it to change a character in a horizontal black-and-white pencil drawing from male to female, it may give you an excellent vertical photo of that female character. It didn't always fail in this regard, but it is a work in progress. I'm just glad they are giving it a go. 

Export is set up to happen after you finish the book. I understand the logic here. You want authors to fully complete the book in the ecosystem to maximize the value of the AI tools. This is also a weakness for other tools. In my use case, I write the book and then have a retired college coach and others read my manuscript. I then make changes based on those reviews. In my current workflow, that means going back to Word and making the changes. With this tool, you can go back to the chapters and edit them, but you can't upload from Word if you make changes there. That is understandable, and the workaround is copy and paste. This is really only an issue for people I am sharing a digital copy they can mark it up. For those getting a PDF or paper copy to redline, I'd have to manually enter those changes regardless. There are apps that offer a Beta reader feature where you can share a digital copy with an expiration date and receive comments. I'll have to recommend that on their page. 

The app largely treats each chapter as its own entity (at least in non-fiction mode). There isn't a 'whole book' feel to the AI process. As in, review my entire book for XY consistency or ABC redundancy. It would be even better if it could do that across a series. I am sure, as the technology grows and the app develops, there will be more tools to address concerns like this.

It feels like a product that will continue to grow and develop for its user base.

Overall, I am happy with the purchase.

I’ll admit it... I’ve bought nearly 400 deals over the years here on Appsumo and I don’t leave reviews often. And yes, true to form, I let this one sit for a bit before I finally cracked it open. But when I logged in and realized my monthly credits were about to refresh and I hadn't even used any of them, I decided I may as well use some of those credits to take it for a spin.

Test #1: I gave it an idea I wasn’t committed to, just to see what it would do. It built a full 12-chapter book. Good structure, very readable... but when you don’t give it much to work with, it fills the gaps with its own made-up examples. Lesson learned.

Test #2: I gave it one of my own proprietary frameworks, my own definitions and examples. WHOA... What a difference! In one afternoon I had a clean nine-chapter book, an Editorial Review of the whole manuscript, a cover, and a 2.5-hour audiobook that I uploaded  to a Past Appsumo Deal - Soundwise - so I can listen to it via an App on my Phone through my Bluetooth as I'm driving around in my Car.

What impressed me most:

* You pick the AI model chapter by chapter (I've tested Gemini & Claude and as you likely already know Claude it better overall for writing as represented by the 30 credits per chapter instead of 15 credits per chapter for Gemini) so I've been using Claude for each of my Chapters.

* Read the Line Edits before accepting them. Some suggestions made my plain-talk style a bit too academic for my taste... In fact, while the Editorial Review provides to usable data, I found myself pretty much skipping the Line Editor (at least for my second book) even though once I get even better at using it, maybe I will find the Line Editor more useful for me.

* The audiobook feature is impressive, but it uses a big chunk of credits, so good thing I have Tier 4 - because if you plan on using the Audiobook feature much, you'll require reasonable credits for that.  My 9 Chapter approx 22K word book cost about 2,500 credits (or around that amount).  The quality of the AudioBook Voice I selected turned out really good though.

Bottom line... If you have content, frameworks, courses, or ideas sitting around that deserve to become books, this tool will get you from “someday” to “done” faster than anything I’ve tried.

comments.title: AIWriteBook – An End-to-End AI Companion for Authors
comments.comment:
AIWriteBook positions itself as an all-in-one AI platform tailored for authors and self-publishers looking to take a book from concept to a published format. Unlike standard generic chatbots, it focuses heavily on maintaining narrative consistency, stylistic alignment, and a streamlined publishing pipeline.

Key Strengths

Personalized Style Matching: One of AIWriteBook’s standout features is its ability to learn an author's unique voice. By uploading an existing .docx manuscript or pasting a writing sample, the platform adapts its generation style to mirror the user's natural prose rather than outputting generic, recognizable AI phrasing.   

Comprehensive End-to-End Workflow: The platform covers nearly every stage of the writing journey in a single dashboard—from outlining and character building to chapter generation, book cover design, audiobook creation, and KDP (Kindle Direct Publishing) metadata preparation. This eliminates the need to stitch together multiple fragmented tools.   

Model Flexibility: Users are not locked into a single AI architecture. The platform allows creators to choose between different underlying models (such as Gemini, Claude, or Grok) depending on the tone, genre, or specific chapter requirements they are working on.   

Granular Control Over Revisions: Rather than overwriting text blindly, AIWriteBook provides clear revision checkpoints where authors can review, accept, or reject specific changes or chapter suggestions, ensuring the writer stays firmly in creative control.
   
Areas for Improvement

Learning Curve and Credit Consumption: For beginners, understanding how to configure the tool effectively can take time. Because the platform operates on a metered credit system, initial experimentation and trial-and-error can accidentally consume credits before finding the optimal workflow.

Connection Stability Risks: Users drafting on mobile browsers or unstable network connections have noted that sudden interruptions can halt generation mid-sentence while still deducting credits, requiring customer support intervention to restore them.   

Niche Ecosystem: Compared to mainstream general-purpose AI tools, AIWriteBook maintains a smaller independent user base. This means fewer third-party tutorials, community plugins, or crowd-sourced troubleshooting guides are readily available online if a user encounters an unusual roadblock.

Conclusion

AIWriteBook is a robust, time-saving ecosystem for self-publishers and authors who want to streamline their writing, formatting, and pre-publishing pipeline. While it requires a brief adjustment period to master the credit consumption and settings, its voice-matching capability and comprehensive production suite make it a compelling asset for bringing a manuscript to life.

comments.title: A Powerful AI Writer with Room for Improvement
comments.comment:
A Powerful AI Writer with Room for Improvement

Writecream stands out as a prominent AI writer, particularly renowned for its proficiency in crafting comprehensive, long-form articles. Its AI capabilities showcase impressive potential, but there are notable downsides that affect the user experience and flexibility.

The primary drawback lies in the lack of control users have over article length. Despite requesting a 2000-word article, Writecream often generates texts that exceed this limit by a significant margin, sometimes producing articles of 3500 words or more. This lack of logical adherence to user-set word counts can be frustrating, leading to excess content that may not align with the user's needs or preferences.

As an existing user, I've reached out to Writecream's owners to emphasize the necessity for greater user control. Here are a few suggestions that I believe could significantly enhance the user experience:

User-Controlled Article Length: Providing users with full control over determining the length of the generated articles would be immensely beneficial. This feature would allow users to set specific word count parameters, ensuring the AI generates content within the desired limits.

Text Quantity Customization: Allowing users to specify the number of texts generated for each request would offer more flexibility. For instance, having the option to request a single article without variations would streamline the output for users seeking focused, singular content.

Expanded Article Outline Support: Writecream's AI 
(A simple 4-step article writer) sometimes falls short in generating the desired number of sections outlined by the user. Despite outlining ten sections, the AI consistently produces only four sections. Improving this discrepancy to ensure the generation aligns with the user's outlined structure would enhance Writecream's functionality.

Outline Integration for Instant Writing: Providing a feature that allows users to insert an outline for instant writing would be highly beneficial. This integration would enable users to input their desired structure or section details directly into the AI writer, ensuring more precise content generation.

In conclusion, while Writecream exhibits impressive AI writing capabilities, the lack of user control over article length, text quantity, and adherence to outlined structures hinders its full potential. Implementing the suggested improvements could greatly enhance user satisfaction and streamline the AI writing process, making Writecream a more versatile and user-friendly platform.

The interface and positioning are also smart enough to create a strong first impression.

That said, once you spend more time with it, it starts to feel less unique than it first appears. A lot of the appeal seems to come from the branding and the way it is presented, rather than from features that truly stand out. The WordPress connection sounds great, but many other tools already offer something similar, sometimes with more flexibility and fewer restrictions.

The writing quality is not bad. For quick, machine-generated drafts, it does an acceptable job, and for some users that may already be enough. But compared with stronger tools like Writecream or NeuronWriter, it still feels a bit limited in depth and overall polish.

comments.title: Improvements needed, however still better than using chat overall...
comments.comment:
Pros: The intuitive interface is simple to use and connects to WordPress easily. The articles are of a good length. I love the editor window; it is nice, especially if you wish to DRAFT and then post or manually post later on different platforms. The dashboard has a Keyword Research link that makes SEO a snap. The FAQ toggle and chart addition were nice touches. That was unexpected.

Cons: The scheduler would be better served in a calendar-based system like the WordPress post calendar. No TAGS feature. Some word concatenations were troubling, and I would not have seen them had I not used Grammarly to check. The article also lacks a lot of proper punctuation; in fact, Grammarly made 73 corrections for missing commas alone.  Also, the plagiarism checker is not 100% accurate, as the first article scored 83 out of 100 and had a 5% plagiarism warning. That said, Grammarly is a bit on the strict side, and common phrases are not exempt from being flagged, so take that with a grain of salt. 

There is no way to prompt for particular article subjects other than Keyword shortlists and Titles. Negative Prompting and Additional prompting would be nice to move the needle in a better end-post product. I just completed a larger sample of articles trying to work out if ranking for other keywords would work. The articles suggested that my client was a veterinarian when I was trying to highlight vet care in the area. That was a failure.

OVERALL: This is a promising product with great potential as development continues. You can't beat the lifetime pricing; for me, it could be a great time saver, which is what I needed. I look forward to the next iterations as the development team moves the goal line. My guess is that if you are an affiliate marketer trying to gain SEO ranking, this tool will be of great value to you. If you are a marketer trying to help your client truly create articles that help their clients, this one needs more development time, or you can think of it as a starting place for all your client's articles. Set it and forget isn't quite there yet.

comments.title: WPautoblog: Promising Features with SEO Optimization Potential

WPautoblog shows promise as a tool for creating blog posts, but there are a few areas that could be improved to enhance its functionality and SEO readiness.

One notable issue is the length of the meta descriptions, which are often too long. Additionally, the absence of generated keywords and the delay in timely post generation are factors that hinder immediate effectiveness. Furthermore, the lack of meta information attached to images presents a missed opportunity for optimizing content.

Despite these shortcomings, WPautoblog's trajectory is promising. While it may not be entirely SEO-ready or friendly in its current state, it presents itself as a valuable plugin for blog creation.

Moving forward, integrating basic features such as optimized meta descriptions, generated keywords, prompt post generation, and meta information for images would significantly enhance its utility and appeal to users seeking robust SEO capabilities.

In conclusion, WPautoblog holds potential and remains a worthwhile tool for bloggers. With ongoing improvements, it has the opportunity to become an indispensable asset for those seeking efficient and SEO-friendly blog post creation. 4 star rating

comments.title: Fantastic product with one Huge Problem

Firstly, I can only echo what everyone else has said about Fliplink. It's fantastic and does everything it says on the tin and more.

I'm so excited about the potential to use this for my business use case that I went all in and added it as one of the core services I offer in my sales funnel; it fits perfectly as a visual representation of the books I create for my clients.

However, there's a big problem; unfortunately, it has not been solved for some time.

Today is the last day of my 60-day refund period. Usually, I would exercise my right, get my credits back, and move on. But I do believe in the vendor. And love the product so much, so I won't refund.

However, the main issue is that Malwarebytes keeps flagging the fliplink.me domain as a phishing site.

If anyone has Malwarebytes installed on their computers or mobile devices, they will receive a warning message that this is a phishing site and will be blocked from accessing the domain, more importantly, from the flipbook.

This has been going on for some time, and I understand the vendor has reported it, but it has been two months in my case. A simple search for the keyword Malwarebytes in the questions section will reveal that this issue has happened since last year.

The vendor even says three security software programs flag the fliplink.me domain, and he has reported it, but that was a long time ago.

You may think I'm over-reacting as you've not seen this problem, but that's probably because you don't have Malwarebytes installed on your PC... As of 2025, Malwarebytes has millions of freemium users and 60,000 paid enterprise customers worldwide; however, any of those could be your prospective client or an already paying customer being blocked from seeing your flipbook, and losing trust in your brand.

Where does this leave us?

I'm giving this a 4-star review for now, which I'll change to 5 once this has been fixed. 

I do hope the vendor makes this a priority, as I said before, it's a beautiful product.

comments.title: One of my best purchases on here...
comments.comment:
Hi,
I purchased fliplink.me largely based on the comments. Many of the reviews indicated that there was nothing more it could do to meet their needs (from the reviewers perspective). So, I was hopeful it was the perfect solution for me to sell my digital products. 

I've been using the product for about 6 months now and it is a fantastic product. For what it does, it does it well and is worth 5-stars.
Such as, 
-The ease-of-use, 
-the ability to charge for a flipbook, 
-to have multiple CNAMEs in the link, 
-to brand your products in other ways 
-AND to be able to replace a pdf file without having to redo the entire listing 
It is worth 5 stars for those things alone. 

Another reason for 5 stars is because it has been a good fix for other purchases that didn't work out.  Once I was in it and using it, I understood my needs better and realized other features that I need but that currently don't exist.  Having them would truly make Fliplink.me a perfect all-in-one solution for me.

So, I contacted Sumit to ask about those features. He gave me a thoughtful response in a timely manner, which is also why I think the product deserves 5 stars--great customer service.

Here is what I asked and his answers, in case you want to know about these features as well.

Q1) Is there a main page that customers see, so that they can access all of the products we have available at once?

A) "Fliplink doesn’t currently offer a built-in storefront to show all your flipbooks in one place.
However, you can embed flipbooks on your own website or landing page — either as a direct flipbook view or a clickable image that opens the flipbook in a new tab. This allows you to create your own custom catalog or collection page."

Q2) If there is not a main page that lists all of our products, is the only way that they will know that a product exists, is if they have the direct link to the flipbook?

A) "Yes, in the current setup, each flipbook has its own unique link. So unless shared directly, customers won’t know another product exists."

Q3) If number 2 is the case, does that mean that I will have to use another platform to list all the books separately with their individual links and that customers will have to follow each link to purchase a product? For example, to see that I have 50 books available and if they want to purchase 50 books, they will have to go through 50 different links to do that?

A) "Correct — for now, to list multiple books together, you would use an external platform (like your website, Notion, Linktree, or a simple landing page builder) to display all the individual flipbook links in one place(i.e with direct embed or as clickable image)."

Q4) Are there any future plans to be able to do questions 1-3 if those are not already features?

A) "At the moment, features like a built-in storefront or centralized product listing aren’t part of our immediate roadmap. That said, if it proves to be a valuable and widely requested addition, I'd be happy to explore it further. While i can’t promise a timeline, your feedback is incredibly helpful in guiding future updates."

Q5) Will there be an option to offer "bundles" of books--the ability to purchase several books at one time?

A) "While I can’t commit to an exact timeline, I’ll definitely explore the idea of allowing users to purchase or unlock multiple flipbooks at once. It’s a valuable suggestion, and we’ll surely consider it for future updates."

I hope they'll add a main page so that everything is on one site. That would be great!  In the interim, I have implemented his suggestions and they are working.

comments.title: Social media Ai & MCP
comments.comment:
- I really like the concept and I’m looking forward to seeing more intelligent features across social media. At the moment, Instagram is full of high-quality content(also a lot of useless noise), but there isn’t yet the intelligence to detect images and distribute them to the niche where we need them, because simply indexing the text in the caption isn’t enough. For example, if I follow lots of fashion accounts and only want to receive updates or posts about ‘blue trousers’, the only way to get that information is via AI that can analyse the photos in the posts. This example is actually useful for any other product where you need information that isn’t included in the caption.
- Please, even if you sell the company in the future, remember that we Earlybakers are thinking about how to improve this even further and wouldn’t want to lose our account to someone else, especially after setting up our workflow. Most of us here are small businesses, and changing key components is traumatic when they disappear or fail.

comments.title: Follow.it could become the feed reader I was looking for in the future.
comments.comment:
Follow.it could become the feed reader I was looking for in the future.

Pros:

    - One place to centralize all the information you need: news, reminders, alerts, etc.
    - Multiple ways to display the information: on the website, in an app, as push notifications, email, RSS feed, Telegram… and many more to come. This is something other news readers do not provide, or only in their enterprise tier and only via an API.
    - Quite fast replies to support requests.

Cons:

    - Some of its features feel half-baked. What I mean is, for example:
        * The dark theme has some text in the same color as the background, making it illegible.
        * Recurring reminders have limited options available: daily, weekly, monthly and yearly. I cannot set a reminder for every six months or every two weeks.
        * The "Track Currencies" feed has a list sorted by name, but the "Cryptocurrency Prices" feed does not. For example, try finding Bitcoin in the list.
        * The "Coming soon" features are integrated and mixed up with the current, real ones. This is a bit annoying. It would be better to have them removed, or at least shaded out to show them as unavailable for now.

I will update this review once I have had more time to review Follow.it in depth.

Finally, I must say that I purchased two lifetime Tier 4 licenses.

That's all for now,
Regards

UPDATE: The dark mode, was fixed

comments.title: Gamechanger
comments.comment:
Keeping up with the news used to be quite a hassle. There were countless sources, an overwhelming amount of news, and I always had to sift through everything manually to find what was actually relevant to me. In the past, this was always a huge time sink.

With follow.it, that changes fundamentally. I can add all my favorite sources, filter them according to my preferences, and only deal with the news that truly matters to me. This tool is an incredible time saver.

For English-language news, there’s an extensive database of sources that you can easily integrate and use. What I do miss a bit is a similarly large selection for German-language sources. On top of that, I would really appreciate it if the user interface were available in German as well. As far as I can tell, though, that’s already a feature in development.

If you take a little time to get familiar with it, you’ll appreciate that there are various ways to have the news delivered to you.

All in all, this tool provides a very solid foundation, and with the features that are still to come, it’s sure to become really great. For that reason, I’m giving it four out of five tacos at this point.

comments.title: Very useful to stay on top of the latest news
comments.comment:
I'm using this to get info for a site I am creating.  It's great if you need to keep track of news in your industry or you want to get the latest videos from a specific YouTube channel.

I like that you can create your own news feed and then have it delivered by email at a time when you want to see it, rather than just getting random notifications all day long.

There is also an app you can install from Google Play and that works well too.  It shows your custom news feed on your phone.

I do wish it would have an MCP connector so that I can get Claude to do a follow up on some specific news in the feed without manual intervention.   That's the only piece I feel is missing, otherwise it's a very useful tool for people who want to track various info sources.

comments.title: Another way to track news
comments.comment: So far I'm impressed about follow.it. I can let it follow an RSS feed and let it look for certain keywords. E.g. a CVE feed and only notify me if there are wordpress issues, but not when it's a wordpress plugin.

comments.title: My personal newsroom
comments.comment:
With the current overload of information on the internet and social media, I did not hesitate to check out and purchase this follow.it LTD. Although I am still exploring all the options, I already know this is a keeper. The onboarding was straightforward, and the content quality matches my expectations.

While far from completely set up to my liking for the moment - I am in the (lengthy) process of adding keywords, tags, etcetera - I am convinced this will become my made-to-measure newsroom. No more endless web-diving to find information on the topics I am interested in; it will all be presented nicely in the app, or in any channels I want it to appear in.

My main interest lies with news feeds, based on my selections, but other options like enabling alerts for several website features  - broken link checking, to name one - are a welcome surplus. And there are many.

There is still room for improvement. Organizing the topics into folders or categories, and definitely more detailed documentation. For instance, I haven't figured out how to exclude keywords. The UI mentions include or exclude, but there is no guidance on exclusions.

I am looking forward to exploring more of the planned functions on their roadmap.

comments.title: Multi-Channel and Deep Customization
comments.comment:
Most subscription management tools rely solely on email newsletters. follow.it expands options by allowing subscribers to choose how they receive updates. These are very helpful to me.
- Email digests: Instant, daily, or weekly updates
- RSS & Feed Readers

UI Learning Curve: Dashboard offers many configuration options that may feel overwhelming initially. But you can get used to it after playing around a while.

For RSS-to-email delivery service that gives complete control over how and when they receive updates, follow.it is one of the best tools available

comments.title: Great Tool for Centralizing Feeds, but API/MCP Support Is Needed
comments.comment:
The tool is very simple to set up, and the onboarding experience is excellent. It doesn’t take long to understand how everything works and start adding the feeds you want to follow.

One of the biggest strengths is the variety of different feeds and sources you can monitor. That was the main reason I purchased it. I’ve grown tired of manually checking multiple websites and sources just to see what’s new, so having everything consolidated into one place is a much better workflow. It makes it easier to stay on top of updates without constantly jumping between different sites.

The biggest limitation for me right now is the lack of an API or MCP integration. Being able to collect all of this information in one place is useful, but the next step is being able to actually use that data elsewhere. An API and/or MCP server would make it possible to connect the tool with other apps, AI workflows, internal dashboards, automations, or custom tools.

That would make the product much more flexible and turn it from primarily a feed-reading tool into something that could become part of a larger workflow.

I’m personally giving it 4 stars for now because the core product already works well, setup is easy, and the range of feeds is impressive. If API and/or MCP support is released so users can access the collected data and integrate it with other tools, I’d happily update this to 5 stars.

comments.title: Erst kurz im Einsatz, aber schon jetzt hilfreich
comments.comment: Ich nutze follow.it erst seit kurzem, aber es hilft mir jetzt schon. Ich sammle damit Quellen an einem Ort und filtere per Stichwort, was für mich relevant ist. Was mir in der App noch fehlt, ist eine Sprachauswahl, zum Beispiel Deutsch. Für den Alltag wäre das eine echte Erleichterung. Für einen Lifetime Deal bisher ein guter Kauf.

comments.title: A Capable Feed Reader With Search Still Evolving
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I’m a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Follow.it worked as designed overall, and even an account from the previous deal continued to work correctly. The main friction was discovery: some expected podcast and topic searches returned limited or no useful results, while parts of the Find Feeds UI felt crowded and could benefit from clearer sorting and filtering. 

The Partner responded actively to the feedback, expanding the podcast directory to nearly 20,000 feeds with more planned, adding a Follow action directly to search results, clarifying the mobile-app requirement for push delivery, and addressing several smaller usability issues. Folders and tags were moved higher on the roadmap, while some navigation and sorting improvements remained non-deal-breaking caveats.

So one suggestion I would make: separate the feeds in the My News section. The interface just needs to be laid out better, but I love it. It's a great idea and I'm looking for the little improvements that would make it even better.

comments.title: Follow.it Tier 2 Review
comments.comment:
Follow.it funciona como una gran herramienta para empezar el día recibiendo un resumen personalizado de fuentes de noticias directamente en la bandeja de entrada, lo que evita visitar múltiples sitios web o distracciones en feeds infinitos.

La plataforma ayuda a rastrear noticias, sitios web, blogs, canales de YouTube y otros contenidos en un solo lugar, facilitando la búsqueda de información relevante mediante filtros de palabras clave y de inteligencia artificial sin necesidad de comprobaciones manuales.

Resulta especialmente útil para creadores de contenido que buscan descubrir temas en tendencia, investigar competidores y encontrar ideas para publicaciones, artículos y vídeos.

La mayor ventaja radica en su simplicidad: la configuración es directa, añadir fuentes es sencillo y automatiza el trabajo para ahorrar tiempo, reducir la sobrecarga informativa y evitar el desplazamiento innecesario por contenido negativo.

La oferta en AppSumo ofrece una buena relación calidad-precio por un servicio útil que se integra rápidamente en la rutina diaria y ayuda a ahorrar tiempo al juntar todo el contenido nuevo en un solo lugar y en un solo mensaje diario.

Usa filtros automáticos para mostrarte solo los temas que te importan mediante palabras clave.

Es muy útil tanto para personas que quieren mantenerse informadas sin distracciones como para creadores de contenido que buscan ideas nuevas o investigan qué está pasando en su sector.

Tengo muchas ganas de ver cómo avanza éste proyecto en el futuro. Muchas gracias a todos los desarrolladores por el esfuerzo que le dedican a ésta aplicación.

comments.title: Really nails it as a solid Inoreader replacement
comments.comment:
(Note: This review focuses on the desktop browser version, where I spend most of my time.)

I've used and promoted my favorite RSS reader, Inoreader, for years, and even had a paid subscription for a while. I eventually settled on the free version, mainly because I felt that the paid features weren't worth it. After using Follow.it for a while, it really exceeded my expectations. It is both familiar yet still unique in some nice ways. 

As an RSS reader, Follow.it is very solid and capable. It's laid out logically and thoughtfully, with nuances that other RSS readers often overlook. Overall, it's very polished and modern-looking. I found every feed I had set up in Inoreader except one. Not bad! You can't add a custom feed yet, but that appears to be in development. Definitely not a deal-breaker for me.

EDIT: Yes, you CAN add custom feeds without issue. I think I fat-fingered the original URL, so I tried again, and it worked perfectly.

Beyond being an RSS reader, Follow.it includes many other features, including publishing content and pushing notifications and content to a myriad of services. And I haven't even scratched the surface of what it can do.

This lifetime deal is quite affordable in comparison to Inoreader, nicely extending features above and beyond the free tier. Don't get me wrong, the free version is amazing. This deal just amps it up.

I've tested and used countless programs and services, so I hope to really put Follow.it through its paces and provide some solid feedback. So far, highly recommended!

comments.title: A great way to stay informed without endless scrolling!
comments.comment:
Follow.it has become a great way for me to start my day. Instead of visiting multiple news websites and getting distracted by endless feeds, I now receive a clear, personalized summary of my favorite news sources directly in my inbox every morning.

The biggest advantage is its simplicity. Setting everything up is straightforward, adding news sources is easy, and once configured, Follow.it does most of the work for you. It saves time, reduces information overload, and puts an end to unnecessary doom-scrolling. A convenient overview of the news that actually matters to me.

The AppSumo deal offers value for money. For a very reasonable price, you get a genuinely useful service that can quickly become part of your daily routine.

Is Follow.it perfect? Not yet. There are definitely areas that could use further improvements and refinement. However, the foundation is solid, the concept works well, and I believe this product has potential to become even better. I'm particularly looking forward to the expansion of the Find Feeds feature with Company Feeds and Topic Feeds. These additions would make it even easier to discover and follow relevant content, taking the platform's usefulness to the next level.

Overall, a smart, affordable, and easy-to-use solution that already delivers real value. A promising product with a bright future. Highly recommended!

comments.title: Sehr hilfreiches und übersichtlich gestaltetes Tool!

comments.title: Follow.it Review: A Useful Tool for Content Research
comments.comment:
Follow.it helps you track news, websites, blogs, YouTube channels, and other content in one place. Its keyword and AI filters make it easier to find relevant information without checking every website manually. 
It is especially useful for content creators who want to discover trending topics, research competitors, and find ideas for posts, articles, and videos. 
Overall, Follow.it works best as a content discovery and monitoring tool. It helps you save time and stay updated on topics that matter to your audience. However, you still need separate tools to create videos and publish posts.

comments.title: Ein echtes Must-Have für Nischen-Monitoring & Wissensaufbau!
comments.comment:
Ich bin wirklich sehr begeistert von follow.it. Das Tool ist eine fantastische Möglichkeit, bei spezifischen Fachthemen immer auf dem neuesten Stand zu bleiben.

Besonders stark finde ich die flexible Keyword-Suche: Egal, wer auf YouTube zu einem bestimmten Stichwort ein Video auf seinem Kanal veröffentlicht, ich werde zuverlässig darüber informiert. Extrem praktisch ist dabei, dass man die Benachrichtigungsfrequenz komplett individuell anpassen kann – ob direkt in Echtzeit (just-in-time), einmal am Tag oder als wöchentliche Zusammenfassung.

Alles in allem ein genialer Helfer, um den Überblick zu behalten und mühelos neue Kanäle, Podcasts und inspirierende Wissensquellen zu entdecken. Absolute Empfehlung!

comments.title: Great for keeping a city directory fresh
comments.comment: Picked this up for my city directory and honestly it’s already earning its place. I use it to keep on top of local news without checking ten sites a day: I set up a few searches for my area plus the local papers, filtered them by keywords, and now I get one tidy digest in the morning. I also follow a handful of competitors and similar directories in a weekly roundup, which is a really easy way to see what they’re posting and spot new businesses I could list. The best part is I pull 2–3 stories from the digest every day for our social media, so I’m never stuck for something to post. The keyword and AI filters cut out a lot of the noise, setup was quick, and for a one-off price it’s great value. The only thing I’d change is that you can’t follow Instagram or Facebook pages directly, which is where a lot of local businesses actually post, so I still have to check those by hand. Apart from that, really happy with it!

comments.title: A Practical and Powerful Tool for Following What Matters
comments.comment:
I purchased follow.it because I needed a better way to keep up with news, websites, industry updates, research, and content from many different sources across several projects.

After spending time exploring the platform, I have been very impressed by how much it can do. It is far more than a basic RSS reader. It supports a wide range of sources, including websites, news, YouTube channels, feeds, and website-change monitoring. This makes it especially useful for anyone who needs to follow information from many places without checking each site manually.

One of the strongest parts of follow.it is its filtering capability. These days, access to information is not the problem—finding the information that is actually relevant is. The filters make it much easier to reduce noise and focus on topics, keywords, and updates that matter for each project. I can already see how this will save a meaningful amount of time.

The setup process was also more straightforward than I expected. Although the platform has many features, adding sources and configuring filters feels manageable. Based on the reviews and discussions from other users, it is also encouraging to see that the team appears active, responsive, and open to feedback.

I am particularly interested in the future MCP integration. While I am not judging the product based on a feature that is not yet available, I can see great potential in combining follow.it’s collection and filtering functions with AI tools for research, analysis, opportunity discovery, and content planning.

There are two improvements I would especially appreciate:

One-click translation inside the story-reading view
As a non-native English speaker, I subscribe to many international websites to stay informed and access the latest information. A built-in one-click translation option directly within each story would make follow.it much more convenient for users who follow content in foreign languages.

Text-to-speech for stories
As the number of subscribed feeds grows, it becomes difficult to read every story individually. It would be fantastic if stories could also be listened to like podcasts through a text-to-speech feature. This would make it easier to catch up while commuting, exercising, or doing other tasks.

Overall, follow.it already solves a real problem for me: staying informed without spending hours visiting and checking countless individual sources. It is useful, capable, and full of potential. I am very happy with my purchase and look forward to seeing how the platform continues to improve.

Five tacos from me! 🌮🌮🌮🌮�*

comments.title: Schon Gut aber einige Verbesserungen erforderlich
comments.comment: Bin schon recht zufrieden mit dem Produkt, Mehrsprachigkeit und MCP aber noch unbedingt erforderlich.

comments.title: Solid Product
comments.comment:
I'm enjoying using follow.it so far and particularly like that there is a good mobile app. Having a single location to subscribe to content from multiple publications, including YouTube channels and podcasts is great. Also being able to filter content per platform by things such as tags, keywords or AI. There are a lot of interesting API feeds also.

I was glad to see from searching the reviews and questions that a folder/workspace feature is already planned too, as a way to have separate sets of feeds for different purposes.

I also like that this product seems to have been around for a long time, which is a good indicator for longevity. Overall, I am happy with follow.it and believe that I'll be making good use of it for years to come.

comments.title: Great product with a lot of useful features
comments.comment: This is a product with features you didn't know you needed until you saw them—like link and backlink monitoring. Some of them are still a bit basic, but I'm sure that Nick and the rest of the team will continue to improve them. Can't wait for the monetization feature!

comments.title: Useful research radar with keyword filters and a daily digest
comments.comment:
I have just started using follow.it to build a research and news radar for our equine health education business. We set up ten feeds covering equine science, specialist publications, four targeted PubMed searches, and updates from tools we use for our website.

The combination of RSS subscriptions, keyword filters, and a daily email digest is particularly useful for this workflow. We could filter broader sources by relevant topics and bring scientific research and technical updates into one place.

One detail to watch during setup: follow.it notes that daylight saving time is not adjusted automatically, so the digest delivery time may shift by an hour.

These are early impressions based on the setup. I have not used it long enough to judge long-term delivery reliability, but it looks promising for keeping track of several specialised sources.

comments.title: A great way to follow your favorite content — especially with the iPhone app!
comments.comment:
A great way to follow your favorite content — especially with the iPhone app!

I’m really happy with follow.it, and the combination with the iPhone app is a particular highlight for me. Being able to follow content and conveniently catch up on my phone makes the service much more useful in everyday life.

What makes follow.it appealing is the flexibility. You can follow websites and RSS feeds, filter updates by keywords, tags, or authors, and choose how you want to receive them. Having options such as individual email notifications, daily or weekly digests, Telegram, and RSS means you can fit updates around your own preferences.

The filtering options are especially useful for sources that publish frequently: you can narrow things down to the topics that actually interest you instead of receiving every single update.

There’s also a useful publishing side. Website owners and bloggers can automatically notify subscribers about new posts and let readers choose how they receive updates. That gives the tool potential beyond simply following content yourself.

For me, though, the standout is still the combination of follow.it and the iPhone app. If you enjoy keeping up with your favorite sources and want more control over how updates reach you, this is well worth a look. Definitely a recommendation from me!

comments.title: Love it so far!!
comments.comment:
A promising way to organise trading research, learning and everyday interests

I bought Tier 2, and although I haven’t had time to test everything properly yet, follow.it has several features that fit what I’m looking for.

One of my main interest is trading and investing. Between crypto prices, stock news, financial websites and YouTube channels, there is a lot to keep up with. I want a more organised way to follow these sources without constantly jumping between websites and opening more tabs.

The crypto and stock price feeds particularly interest me. My plan is to combine price updates with news filtered around the assets and topics I follow, including of course Bitcoin and others,  company earnings and interest rates. Keyword filtering is a big part of the appeal because I want to focus on relevant information rather than collect every headline.

I am also an IT gig, AI enthusiast and gadget lover. To keep up with all of these, it is a nightmare. So this is perfect for me as well especially with filtering.

I also like the option of following specific YouTube channels and getting updates about relevant new videos. This could be useful for market analysis, trading education and keeping up with AI developments. GitHub monitoring gives me another way to follow updates to open-source trading and technology tools.

Beyond finance, I can see several uses for my work as an educator. Following educational websites, technology blogs and industry news could help me find fresh examples and resources for lessons on AI, project management and digital marketing.

There are personal uses too: keeping up with favourite creators and podcasts, following travel websites for destination ideas, and watching for interesting software deals. Having these interests accessible through one platform is appealing, especially when I already have plenty of bookmarks and tabs to work through.

The choice of email, Telegram and daily or weekly digests gives me flexibility. I’m aiming for a daily roundup of financial news, with less frequent summaries for learning, travel and other interests.

I still need to spend more time testing the filters, delivery speed and overall workflow, but the range of feeds gives me plenty of practical uses to explore. The biggest attraction for me is having more control over what reaches me and when I read it.

Cannot wait for new features and updates! Keep it Up! Loving it so far! A LOT!

comments.title: One place for everything I follow
comments.comment: Been using follow.it for a few days now and it’s helped me aggregate most of the common Google News site articles I normally save elsewhere (Raindrop), into one convenient place. I use it to watch doc pages so I know when something new gets added, and to get a roundup when YouTube channels I follow post a video instead of dealing with the notification bell. I also set up keyword alerts for my business idea since I’m launching next year and want to catch any mentions early. You can pick how and how often each feed reaches you, so the important stuff comes through right away and the rest lands in a digest. Only thing I wish it had is subreddit following. Nick quickly help me set up one and informed me they're working towards making this feature more accessible and streamlined later. I got stuck on a couple of setup things, emailed the founder, and he answered fast and actually helped. If you keep checking the same sites and channels every day, it’s a good deal.

comments.title: A promising tool
comments.comment: Writeseed is a promising tool. Unlimited GPT Image 2 generation at tier 6 is potentially an unbeatable deal for most people; the image output quality is great, as expected. However, its resolution options are not suitable for my workflow. ChatGPT free offers higher-resolution output at 1254 x 1254 or 1024 x 1536px, while Writeseed appears limited to 1024 x 1024 or 720 x 1280. That may be perfectly adequate for many users, and in many cases the smaller image sizes could even be beneficial for site speed, but it is a limitation for my needs. I will reconsider purchasing again once the resolution is increased, although I would understand the cost sustainability concerns. Wishing the team continued success.

However the wording is very good and the pricing as well.
Some dont really work but I believe Hendrik is tryong

comments.title: Works well and the limits are well....unlimited
comments.comment:
Even if i'm not a big fan of the "all in one" app, i decided to test writeseed further and i'm happy for what it does. The Wp Autoblog deliver and connects decently well and with some good articles, clearly can't expect this to compete with AI strong Blog writers, but it's not bad at all. The image generation is basic and can't select models, just 3 styles and a negative prompting, and that's it. It's still very good for basic quick image creation. 
I will still recommend, even if it seems not to be super-developed lately, and when i reached to them about a potential WP bug with their connector, they replied and then ghosted.....not super.
I'd buy and use for what it does now, but won't put a lot of expectations in the future development, so buy for immediate use, not as an investment. That's at least my honest opinion!

comments.title: Good but it needs an iOS app
comments.comment: It is a reasonable platform that does the same job that other AI writers do. However, it lacks an iOS application and that makes its usability limited in comparison with other providers. comments.title: Expand StoryChief's MCP Integration for Full ChatGPT Control
comments.comment:
I recently purchased StoryChief through AppSumo and successfully tested publishing through ChatGPT using MCP. Great start!

After reviewing StoryChief's existing capabilities, I'd like to request the following prioritized MCP roadmap:

Priority 1 — Full Publishing Access
Expose connected channels, publishing controls, scheduling, rescheduling, editing, deletion, and publication verification through MCP.

Priority 2 — Complete Analytics Access
Give ChatGPT direct access to StoryChief's existing Insights dashboards, including analytics for all supported social platforms.

Priority 3 — Intelligent Scheduling
Expose recommended posting times, audience activity, and historical performance data so ChatGPT can optimize schedules.

Priority 4 — Complete Content Workflow Access
Extend MCP controls to the editorial calendar, campaigns, approvals, newsletters, and cross-platform content management.

Priority 5 — Advanced AI Automation
Expose performance monitoring, publishing errors, evergreen recycling, and automated reporting through MCP.

My request: Please prioritize making StoryChief's existing capabilities accessible through MCP rather than requiring users to operate them manually in the dashboard.

The ultimate goal is full end-to-end StoryChief management through ChatGPT.

And since StoryChief already offers these capabilities within its platform and has an established MCP integration, I would imagine exposing them to ChatGPT should be relatively straightforward. Could your development team confirm whether this is feasible and provide an estimated timeline for implementing these MCP enhancements? I'd like to upgrade tiers before the deal ends. Thank you. =)

comments.title: One piece of content, published everywhere from one place
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

I actually bought StoryChief when it first appeared on AppSumo back in 2018 and used it for a while, so I already knew the basic idea behind the product. What is different now is how much more of the content process it covers. This updated version fits much more naturally into the way I publish content today.

You can start by looking at website performance, Google Search Console data and competitor research to decide what is worth creating or updating. StoryChief can also run weekly content audits to find older articles that are losing traffic and suggest what needs attention.

Once you have something worth publishing, you can take that main piece of content and repurpose it for your website, social channels, email and other destinations. StoryChief supports publishing across more than 30 channels, so you are not treating every version of the same idea as a completely separate piece of work.

This solves a problem I run into with content all the time. The article ends up in WordPress, the social posts are somewhere else, the newsletter is in another tool, and then the performance data is somewhere else again. StoryChief brings the planning, writing, approvals, publishing and reporting into the same workflow.

The AI side also goes beyond generating a first draft. It can use your company knowledge and brand voice, help optimize content for SEO and AI search, and repurpose approved content into other formats. You can also connect ChatGPT or Claude through MCP and create or manage StoryChief content from the AI assistant you already use. According to the current Q&A, a regular Claude Pro account works for this without needing separate Anthropic API billing.

I also like the Broadcasts feature. Approved content can be shared through email, Slack or Microsoft Teams, which gives companies another way to get more reach from content they have already created.

If you already have a library of WordPress content, that doesn't have to stay outside StoryChief either. Existing articles can be imported through its WordPress plugin, and there is also an API if you need a more customized setup across multiple sites.

One thing worth understanding about the AppSumo tiers is that the main platform features are available across them. What changes most is how many workspaces, users, articles, social channels and AI credits you get. The AI Visibility feature starts at Tier 3, and AI image and video generation is a separate add-on rather than part of the recurring LTD credits.

Having bought StoryChief during its first AppSumo run, this version feels like a much more complete product than the one I originally purchased. It now fits very nicely into my current publishing workflow because it can help me decide what to create, produce it, repurpose it, publish it across my channels, see how it performs, and then identify what needs to be updated next. That's what makes me excited to start using StoryChief more seriously again.

For me the main point is to be able to push easily to different channels using scheduling and without having to set the canonical URL. That's what I use it for. It's a good starter if you set a campaign for a client with, say, Blogger/FB/Linkedin/Medium etc. So for that reason only it's worth stacking a few codes. The other elements such as Ambassadors seems to me pretty useless : if you have only a few contacts, a direct email will perform better, if you have a long list you probably already manage it with another tool (if you don't, well, learn).
The SEO tool is extremely basic. None of these features are bad - it's just that they seem tailored for newbies. 

So if you are a newbie or you have your own website for your business, get this deal, it will help you. If you have an agency, you can get several deals because it's will automate posting in a way which is easier&quicker than other tools (and much less expensive with that deal). comments.title: A solid platform you should pick up!
comments.comment:
Let me start by saying, this is the most complete blogging-platform I have seen, and it has a great potential. If I have chosen to give tacos based on potential or value for money, this might have been a 5-taco review. 

However, I feel several things are missing, if the tool already now should have worked as a ‘complete blogging platform’ – that might btw. be a very unfair ambition at the moment.

I miss more editor features to improve content creations. It could be templates, the ability to save text snippets for later use, and an option to move areas of text/paragraphs up or down in your articles. Also, it is not clear to me, if the tool integrates with different grammar tools?

Speaking of integrations, I think the team behind the product needs to decide if the tool should do ‘all blogging stuff’ from A-Z. If so – this is if not impossible, then very ambitious. Another way around is to work as a framework/open platform, with several more integrations available than currently offered.
Example of integrations I would love to see: 

-	Aweber (for e-mail marketing)

-	NoteJoy, Airstory, Fleeq, and StepShot Guides, for content creation

-	Stock-photo databases, graphic SW (Stencil, Design Bold, Canva, Visme, and RelayThat etc.) for the more graphic related parts

-	VooPlayer for videos

-	I’m sure integration with several influencer platforms would be great (e.g. Public Fast – a past AS-deal)

-	Missing Ltr, and maybe Social Media Management systems to ensure continuous engagement through different kind reformulated ‘drip posting’ over time.

-	Webtext tool for SEO

-	A way to keep blog-pictures within your control, and with ease – maybe Pcloud could be used?


Also, I would like to see more social networks available, and if possible advanced syndication options.

Let me repeat the tool has a great potential, and help structure the whole blogging process, but to ensure the tool don’t become an ‘average tool in the middle’, I would advice the team to consider where and when they want to put most energy – built-in features to become a ‘stand-alone tool’ and/or integrations to become a blogging-platform/framework. 

Congrats with a very solid foundation. I recommend people to pick up the tool!

comments.title: A must-have for content teams. Instant Value
comments.comment:
I’ve been playing with this for a few weeks now and I’m completely in love with it. You don't have to worry about shelfware with this one. This is a very polished app that you can start using right away. It’s already saved me a ton of time in the content creation/distribution process and I’m just getting started with it. I’ve begun rolling this out with one company I work with that has a 10 person content team where all writers are responsible for different campaigns and blog content. They currently use a common process of Dropbox Paper to write everything together, then copy/paste to WordPress and do the SEO and then separately post to Medium. They also post to all the social media channels from a separate schedule and also add to a MailChimp newsletter. This app literally fit almost perfectly into their process already and replaced a big chunk of it while making it 20 times easier. It also provides more insight into which campaigns are getting the most traction. I’m glad SC rolled out the sideloading of images into WP this week, so far it's working great.  

My favorite parts of StoryChief are:
- How easy it is to post to Medium. I was previously using MissingLettr for this, but StoryChief allows you to have a lot more control. Ex. We have a Medium publication and want to post to that publication as the specific author of the article, you can do that with SC very easily. It’s great. 
- Getting the views and analytics on an article or campaign level is great. It’s the first time I’m seeing views/reads across all platforms including social media. 
- The team I rolled it out to so far absolutely loves the content calendar and being able to sync it with their Google Calendar  
- ACF integration 

Some things I’d love to see added are:
- Adding comments for the Article Title (I’ve been told they’re working on this)
- Some sort of basic task or to-do lists functionality. So you can assign tasks outside of content to individuals. For things like assigning the featured image to your design team, it would be nice to ping thing.  
- It would be nice if the scheduled time indicated less than a day in advance. I had a post scheduled for a few hours from now and it still said will be posted “a day from now”
- It would be nice if you could add an author that doesn’t have a StoryChief account. If the post was ghost written to be published on a site as an author, but they won’t actually be involved in the writing or editing or posting. (Ex. CEO) 

I definitely stacked a few of these, can’t wait to see how SC grows in the future.
