comments.title: From 0 to Published in Record Time!
comments.comment:
I decided to take a look at Story Chief today because I wasn't quite getting how it was different from something like MissingLettr or SocialBee, both of which I love, when it comes to distributing content. 

My first impression having published my first this morning is I like it and can already see how and where it differs, which I'll get onto in a moment.  You can see my first creation here: https://marilyn-devonish.storychief.io/can-you-really-see-your-future-in-the-now-and-create-it

It took about 30 minutes to create. 

The story editor is very slick and super easy to use when it comes to inserting pictures and videos, as one would expect in this day and age.  One of the features I wasn't expecting and love is the ability to add a CTA form within the post using just my email address; no MailChimp or Zapier integrations required. 

Where it differs from MissingLettr because I've seen this come up in discussion threads is that ML is drip feeding your Blog over a period of 365 days.  From what I've seen so far, although hitting the same platforms, it's a manual publishing process with SC should you want to same content to go out several times, however I've only been using the platform for an hour so there is much more to be discovered. 

One of the key initial differences between Story Chief and SocialBee is the fact I can publish across multiple channels at the same time with SC and write different intro text for each whereas with SB it uses the same soundbite/intro content across all platforms unless you schedule them separately.  

Another useful piece of functionality is the SEO information both in terms of improving what you are writing, and an easy way to track the stories progress after publication.  I also like that on the published piece it tells readers how many minutes it will take the read for those out there who are not PhotoReaders! 

The WordPress plugin and connecting my social media sites was easy, and from what I can see you can also add a custom domain.   

Very early days however so far I very much like what I see. 

Marilyn Devonish

comments.title: The path to the ultimate content syndication
comments.comment:
Until now whoever dabbled in "SEO content syndication" that brings any meaningful results, knows how hard it is to build each piece of the puzzle, and then keep everything working flawlessly. 
It's a mega task and no wonder so many "Fiverr" deals are just for that - to build an "IFTTT Content Wheel"; and they still do a crap job most of the time.
Typically for a proper content syndication, you are looking to push your s**** to:
- Social Media (FB/TW)
- Web2.0 (WP.com/Blogspot)
- Bookmarking (Pocket/Pinboard)
- Doc storage (G-Drive/Evernote)
- Aggregators (Paper.li/Feedburner)
- others
Just to give you an idea - I'm looking at 8 properties linked to StoryChief, 27 on IFTTT and 5 on Zapier. This is just one account. 
The main challenge I found is to feed proper versions of RSS to your different properties. Also, a standard IFTTT/Zapier(free)-setup won't provide the rel="canonical" injection to avoid duplicate content risk.
To set it all up, and to work out all the kinks with your custom website theme takes tremendous effort and focus. But wait...
NONE of it is a problem with StoryChief. It is an ULTIMATE content syndication tool.
But by no means they have everything nailed. Here's a little breakdown of what I like and what needs more attention:
PROs:
- 1-click integrations
- easy interface: you log in, you drop the story, you post, you rank
- briefs for your writers - this is a superb feature I'll be using
- SEO widget - I think it is white-labelled Yoast - just exactly what I need
- also, you can edit the content and it gets fixed across the other blogs
- and, you get blog.storychief.io DR40-subdomain for your content!
- the system is fast, reliable and the customer service is super-responsive and has gone extra-mile for me on multiple occasions
 
Not-There-Yets:
- the content on sub-blogs (Medium/Blogger) does NOT link back to the primary source (my main blog)! The workaround is to put a manual annotation to each new post on SC and then manually remove it from your main blog - this HAS to be on top of the list to fix - what a bummer...
- Tumblr and Weebly are missing!
- SC does not respect my custom WP template and pushes content to a default WP text box - manual intervention is needed and the whole automation shebang misses its target
- The "Matchmaking Beta" is "alpha" IMO - I've requested a writer and nobody responded for a few days - no way to see the progression stage or anything. The response was after my escalation and the quote I received for 750w article was... Let's just say I could have easily produced 10 quality 1000w articles for that price. Guess I'll have my VA's learning SC dashboard for now.
- Dozens of integrations are missing and I doubt they'll ever replace the IFTTT/Zapier need entirely - but the list of essential channel types has to be expanded

All in all, StoryChief Team is a clever and resourceful bunch and I have faith in them.
I was only able to afford 5 deals stacking this time... what a bummer... :P
25 tacos.

comments.title: For best results, you need to make it work for you.
comments.comment:
Inkfluence AI can be a helpful tool or a disappointing one, depending on how you use it. Many of the negative reviews seem to come from users who have taken the app builder’s claims too literally. For example, the Influence AI page on AppSumo states, “Generate complete books and eBooks from a single prompt, with structured chapters, covers, and branded layouts.” This promotion suggests you can create an entire e-book by providing just one simple prompt. While this may be the app builder’s selling point, it should not be interpreted literally.

I subscribe to several apps for writing both fiction and non-fiction e-books. Each has its strengths, but the reality is that no writing app—Inkfluence AI included—can produce a polished, professional-quality book from a single prompt. If you try, the result will almost certainly be unsatisfactory.

To get the best outcome, you need to actively guide the app rather than expecting it to do all the work. You cannot simply hand over the entire book creation process—outlining, chapter generation, and writing—to the app and expect a polished book. Instead, you must develop the book concept yourself, create a detailed outline, decide on the number of chapters, and come up with chapter titles before feeding this structured information into the app.

Giving only a one- or two-line prompt in hopes of generating a complete e-book will likely produce unprofessional results. I’ve tested this myself, and the quality fell short of expectations. This is because even the most advanced large language model (LLM)- based apps start to “hallucinate,” generating inaccurate or irrelevant content when pushed with repeated corrections or vague instructions. Writing apps that rely on LLM technology share these limitations.

What I’ve found to work better is preparing a comprehensive outline, including chapter titles and summaries for each chapter, before using the app to flesh out the content. While this might sound like a lot of upfront work, it’s actually quite manageable, especially with tools like ChatGPT or Google Gemini.

Influence AI is no exception—it performs much better when approached with this strategy. I have used this method myself, and the results were very satisfying.

Inkfluenceai can give you higher-quality writing when you apply this strategy. This applies not only to non-fiction but also to fiction.

comments.title: i like inkfluence ai, and this is the review that can change your platform's life if you take the advice.
comments.comment:
Inkfluence is a 5 star product for me when it comes to creating e-books quickly. I also like that it can create books in multiple formats, including Word and PDF, which is one of the main reasons I bought it.

I would like to request a possible future feature for Inkfluence: an AI storyboard writing tool and a movie manuscript tool. This would give you a unique advantage over other e-book platforms if you add this feature.

Since Inkfluence is already good at helping people create stories and books, I think it could also help users turn those stories into detailed written storyboards for short films, long films, music videos, or book adaptations. Other companies have storyboard generators but where i believe they have it wrong is they don't begin with the full story. So i got to thinking this is where inkfluence could fix a unique problem by making a written storyboard into sections.

I am not suggesting that Inkfluence generate images or videos. I am suggesting that it create the detailed written information people need before using AI video tools such as Seedance 2.0.

Here is the idea i am proposing that inkfluence ai builds into their platform as a feature:

The feature could break a story into 15 second storyboard sections, since many AI video clips are created in short increments. For every 15 second section, Inkfluence could write a complete prompt style description that explains exactly what should appear in that scene.

For example, each section could include:

- Detailed character descriptions, including appearance, age range, hairstyle, clothing, personality, emotion, and important visual details that must remain consistent.
- Detailed location descriptions, including the setting, time of day, weather, lighting, background details, props, atmosphere, and overall visual style.
- What happens in the scene, including character movement, actions, reactions, and important story moments.
- Dialogue or narration for that specific 15 second scene.
- Camera and cinematic details, such as shot type, angle, movement, focus, mood, and pacing.
- A ready to copy prompt description users can paste into an AI video generator.

Before creating the storyboard, Inkfluence could give users four different ways to build the project:

- AI guided option - Inkfluence suggests character descriptions, locations, wardrobe, visual style, and story settings, then asks the user to approve or revise those details before writing the storyboard.
- User provided option - The user enters their own character descriptions, locations, story rules, dialogue, visual style, and other details before the storyboard is written.
- Collaborative option - The user provides a basic idea, and Inkfluence helps improve it by suggesting stronger character descriptions, more detailed locations, better scene ideas, visual consistency, dialogue, and story flow before writing the final storyboard.
- Book upload option - The user uploads a book they created with Inkfluence and uses it as the foundation for the storyboard. Inkfluence could pull out the characters, locations, plot points, dialogue, and key events, then organize them into a structured 15 second scene by scene storyboard. The user could review and approve character descriptions, location details, visual style, and story changes before the final storyboard is written.

This would help users keep their characters, locations, wardrobe, story details, and visual style consistent across every 15 second scene.

I think this would be a very unique feature because it would allow someone to create a book with Inkfluence, then turn that same book into a complete written storyboard and prompt package for AI video creation. It would give creators another major reason to buy Inkfluence, especially people who want to bring their books and stories to life as films without needing Inkfluence itself to generate the actual video.

comments.title: 🌮🌮🌮🌮 4.5 Tacos: A powerful drafting engine (if you actually know what to expect)
comments.comment:
I’m giving this 4.5 tacos because it does exactly what an AI book creator should do: give you a massive, structured head start.

I’ve seen some grumbling elsewhere about plagiarism checkers throwing flags, but anyone in publishing knows those tools often panic over standard industry jargon. The content generated here is clearly fresh. Also, the idea that an AI should deliberately introduce grammar mistakes just to "trick" AI detectors is baffling to me. I want clean, well-formatted text that I can edit and humanize myself—and Inkfluence delivers that, right down to automatically cleaning up the formatting on export.

As for the cover designer, the search bar and category filters work perfectly fine if you take a second to look around the interface, the AI cover mode is more credit stingy but very high quality, and the stock images are more than enough to get a solid mockup going.

I’m holding back the half taco simply because the output still requires a heavy human editorial pass before publishing—but honestly, it always should. Great tool, highly recommend for getting past the blank page!

comments.title: 5 Stars: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A Hidden Gem for Non-Fiction Authors, Educators, and Systems/Framework Thinkers
comments.comment:
I hope even more love and development are poured into this project over time. It only launched last November, yet it has already built an impressive user base.

What I understood going into this SaaS is that it is an awesome end-to-end ebook generation first-draft tool, and not a magical "25-second finished product".   In this way, it is good for turning single-line prompts OR SUPER-MASSIVE INFO DUMPS (with an ungodly word count) into a structured, formatted book with an extremely fast output score. Kudos for that!

I also expected it to be particularly effective for non-fiction projects, and it exceeded my expectations in that area. One awesome surprise was its own intention to generate visual frameworks such as Comparison Matrices or are they called Meaning/Semantic/Concept Grids and/or Definition Matrices (ie: Lexical Comparison Matrices? Ontology Matrices? or some kind of Meaning Coordinate Systems). I have never seen that before quite like that in Ai outputs. 

I was genuinely surprised by that feature, and you can delete them or edit them on the inside with just one click if you want.  It's that easy. Creating those kinds of frameworks manually can take hours with research, or organization, and then formatting, yet the software produced useful first-pass versions almost instantly. For anyone working with educational, analytical, philosophical, or FUTURISTIC (SciFi-like) non-fiction content, that capability alone is a significant time saver and impressive to have such a comparison chart. I don't remember asking for them but I got quite a few of them. 

Sure, you can use this for creating courses and lead magnets, although I currently use other AI tools for those tasks. That said, those alternatives can become quite expensive over time, and Inkfluence offers enough functionality that I can see myself relying on it more often, especially when I want an all-in-one solution without juggling multiple subscriptions.

Power-users  may note that the audiobook features need some refinement, and they are not like 11Labs, but they work well, even for making children's books and ESL books. Again, it is not Elleven Labs, but the key takeaway is its All-in-One Workflow that can push everything out to GumROAD and other platforms, which I have to learn more about. 

It outlines, writes, designs covers (but do a second take for an extra credit and it turns out FAR BETTER the second time around), and it formats (PDF, EPUB, DOCX) in an easy, SUPER CONVENIENT workflow and speed, be it your own testimony, story, study guide, workbook, or a business lead magnet.

It's SUPER User-Friendly, better than Apple in the 90s, great for beginners, but for professionals it's more like a great drafting tool. Again, it is not a 25-second master creation tool with a perfect ending all at once, so don't expect such, and you will be just as delighted as I have been. 

In comparison:
-Amazon KDP can easily cut a 100-hour project down to 20–30 hours.
-ChatGPT is only good for Outlining, Brainstorming, Framework creation
-Cluade is better for Long document and Book-length projects but it costs more.
-SudoWrite is better for Fiction and Character development
-Atticus⁠ is great for KDP formatting, EPUB creation, and Print book formatting
- Vellum is another "competitor", highly regarded by successful authors for formatting and publishing capabilities, but requires a Mac. Unlike Inkfluence, it does not generate books, outlines, chapters, covers, or comparison matrices with AI, nor does it integrate directly with AI models.
-Inkfluence is my one-stop SaaS for turning ideas into finished products, from brainstorming and outlining to writing, cover design, formatting, and final edits. It handles most of the publishing workflow and most any type of output I need.

My main areas for improvement would be:
1. The addition of both Japanese and English text-to-speech voices. Even basic voice options would be valuable for reviewing content, language learning materials, and accessibility.

2. Another feature I’d love to see is B5 paper size support. In many parts of the world—especially Japan—B5 remains one of the most practical formats for books, workbooks, study guides, and educational materials. Honestly, every printer should come with just two paper trays: one for A4 and one for B5. As long as we’re still living in the pulp-and-paper era, B5 deserves to be a standard option, not an afterthought.

3. A visual print-layout mode that displays page boundaries (and maybe margins and bleed areas later), but for now, page-break markers in the editing mode for said/selected print paper size directly within the editing workspace are a dire necessity. Being able to see exactly where content will fall on the printed page would greatly improve the quality of PDF and KDP-ready outputs and reduce formatting guesswork. This one is an urgent need, and is probably being worked on already, right? Hopefully, it will be completed or perfected within this year. TY

comments.title: Treat It Like a Ghostwriter, Not a Finished Author — and It Crushes Especially at Tier 3
comments.comment:
Inkfluence AI delivers on the core promise: one prompt, a full draft (chapters, cover, formatted exports) in seconds. I tested it live generating a novella from scratch, and the speed and output volume are real — PDF/EPUB/DOCX export, Gumroad integration, and the public showcase page are genuinely useful for getting a book to market fast.
Where I'd set expectations: treat it like a ghostwriter, not a finished author. I ran my raw Inkfluence draft against an edited version through five different LLMs blind, and every single one picked the edited version as stronger — better pacing, voice, and payoff. The drafts are a great starting point, not a publish-ready manuscript.
If you're realistic about that — fast, capable first drafts that need a real editorial pass — this is a strong addition to a publishing stack. Tier 3 in particular (audiobook generation, unlimited drafts) makes it a solid engine for volume.

comments.title: A month of content planned around your brand
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What caught my attention about Vocable is how it approaches content planning. I can get ChatGPT to write a LinkedIn post or an article whenever I want. Planning a month of content that fits my brand, covers the right subjects, and gives people a reason to keep reading takes more work.

Vocable starts by learning about your business. It can scan your website and existing social content, analyze your writing patterns, and use your brand guidelines to develop a profile that informs the content it generates. From there, you can create a 30-day campaign around a topic or business goal and organize the posts in a calendar or Kanban view.

I particularly like the idea of having that brand information available throughout the writing process. You can work on individual drafts in the editor, revise sections, keep earlier versions, and check whether the finished content still matches your brand guidelines. That last part is especially relevant when you are producing content for several channels or managing more than one brand.

The MCP connector is another interesting addition. It gives Claude access to Vocable’s content planning and publishing tools, so people who already work inside AI assistants can use them with their Vocable projects.

Vocable is primarily a written content tool, so you will still need something else for graphics and videos. I would also treat the generated campaign as a plan to work from. You still need to bring your own experience, examples, opinions, and final edits to the content.

Overall, I like the direction Vocable has taken. For founders, consultants, agencies, and small businesses that regularly publish articles, newsletters, and social posts, having the brand information, content calendar, drafts, editing, and publishing in one place is appealing. I would consider it especially if you already know what you want to talk about but need help turning those ideas into a consistent publishing schedule.

comments.title: A serious branding tool if you bring your own judgment
comments.comment:
We ran Branding 5 end-to-end for our own marketing agency: intake questions, inspiration links, ICP, competitor analysis, brand values, and the full archetype flow. Honest breakdown below.

What we liked:

- The wizard structure is genuinely good. The intake questions, ICP builder, and values step walk you through defining a brand in a sensible order, and the character limits allow real answers, not snippets.
- Inputs carry forward faithfully. The description, audience, and USP we wrote early showed up verbatim in the final review, and the AI summary read our positioning back almost word for word. Consistency between what you type and what it concludes is the core promise, and it delivers.
- The refinement feedback loop actually listens. When we told it our tone should be calm and warm rather than combative, the next pass fixed exactly that.
- The website analyzer impressed us most. It read our site and concluded, quoting evidence from our actual copy, that we already execute our intended tone. That matched our own internal assessment, which is rare for an automated read.
- The competitor research is real, not invented. It blends live SERP overlap data with AI reasoning, filters out aggregators, and lets you edit everything. The final landscape summary gave us a positioning statement we will actually use, and the insights section produced two product ideas we are keeping.
- The trait sliders re-rank the archetype shortlist based on your weightings, and our final result landed exactly where our messaging points.

What we had issues with:

- The archetype suggestions misread us completely. The AI reasoned from our company name (it literally cited "Blitz" implying bold action) instead of the detailed questionnaire we had just completed, and proposed Hero, Magician, and Outlaw. Worse, all four suggestions arrived pre-selected; clicking Next without looking bakes the wrong personality into your report.
- The ICP generator invents statistics. A precise gender split, an income range, a decision timeline, all presented like research findings. None of it came from us or from any data. The qualitative persona underneath was solid, but fake precision is a real flaw in a tool whose reports may be shown to clients.
- The "Help me with AI" buttons on text fields push generic agency-speak. Every time we used our own copy instead, the downstream output was better.
- One radar chart contradicted its own written analysis, scoring a competitor high on a dimension its own bullet points called weak.

What was insightful:

- The three suggested brand directions were thought-provoking and composable rather than competing options.
- The per-competitor insight blocks (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) were specific enough to inform real positioning work, not filler.

Who this is for:

Agencies and founders who already know their positioning, or are willing to review every AI suggestion before accepting it. Treat it as a structured workshop with a helpful, occasionally overconfident assistant, and you get real value. Click through on autopilot, and you will inherit its mistakes as your brand.

Verdict:

The engine underneath is better than the defaults it serves. Bring your own judgment, and Branding 5 earns its place in the workflow.

comments.title: Updated Review-Strong Product, Early Friction, Outstanding End Result
comments.comment:
UPDATED REVIEW:
I want to provide an updated and more complete review.

To be fair, support did reach out, however their replies from the support email were blocked and caught in our spam folders on our end. So I definitely appreciate the more than acceptable response time.

That said, while attempting to complete our first fully finished report, we did run into a couple of additional technical hiccups and error messages. Fortunately, those issues seemed to resolve themselves fairly quickly. No platform is perfect, and we’re not expecting 100% perfection, but given the earlier experience right from the jump, it did make the process feel a bit more frustrating than it otherwise would have been.

Now, here’s the part that truly matters.

The end product is unparalleled compared to any other one-source branding or brand-analysis tool we’ve come across. The depth, clarity, and actionability of the final report is simply beautiful. It delivers exactly what we were hoping for: a comprehensive, client-ready brand intelligence report that provides real insights.

Despite the early friction, the platform ultimately does what it promises, and the value of the final deliverable far outweighs the initial bumps. We look forward to continued use of the platform and the added value it will provide to our clients moving forward.

Strong product. Big potential. Worth the investment.

Break-End of Updated Review, if they decide to come back to the market place do not hesitate to add this tool to your arsenal! 

This is not a review I expected to be writing, especially as a first-time user and someone who immediately upgraded to the top-tier plan after doing my due diligence and relying heavily on reviews from fellow Sumoling users.

From the very first attempt to run a report, the platform repeatedly failed at the competitor analysis step, throwing constant “AI analysis error” messages no matter what inputs or adjustments I made. Different competitors, different browsers, multiple attempts, same result every time. Completely blocked from completing a core function of the product,  and even ONE of the 20 reports I'm due each month

Naturally, I contacted support.

I submitted a detailed request through the on-site support widget, including a screenshot clearly showing the error. I waited over 24 hours, not even an acknowledgment that the message was received. No auto-reply. No ticket number. Nothing.

Assuming the widget may have failed (ironic, given the situation), I followed up by emailing their support address directly. Once again, crickets.

At this point, the experience feels D.O.A. (Dead on Arrival). The platform failed at a critical step during first use, and support has been completely unresponsive. That’s unacceptable, particularly for a paid, top-tier SaaS product that positions itself as a professional brand intelligence tool.

I truly do not want to request a refund, but if I do not hear back by close of business, that will be my next course of action. A working product is one thing—but silence from support when something breaks immediately is a deal-breaker.

Extremely disappointed.

comments.title: A price that makes sense
comments.comment:
The product is developing / maturing well enough to speak for itself in non-LTD terms.

That is to say, these results already speak "quality" rather than promise it somewhere out there. If the leadership continues this trajectory, then I don't doubt they will own the niche. To me, this AppSumo deal seems like MarketMuse (acquired by SiteImprove) years ago. It was already a more mature offering, and priced higher than peers in the AS suite of offers. That deal obviously panned out exceptionally well for LTDers. I think this will too - again, if leadership maintains an eye for excellence in outputs, development and stability of critical features, and stay ahead and vocal about being beyond the "anyone can do this with Claude+Design" The token issue matters to many, but even more important is securing consistency with a process that produces value the consultant and the client both need to trust. I bought Tier 3 last round and upgraded to Tier 4. I think they might have shut down the LTD element. 

Does it require involvement/effort? Yes, but that is simply the consulting work of asking clients to answer questions they didn't know they weren't asking themselves to surface answers required to get where they want to be.

To stress-test the quality, I piloted with a lead marketing colleague for their business. We finished after a thorough, 90-minute discovery/intake dialogue session (perhaps longer or accelerated by preparing some of the answers in advance, if you've not done this work before or the client isn't familiar with the concepts). Don't be mistaken, it's a serious inquiry activity. Upon finishing, I passed along reports to them, which they said would fundamentally reshape their approach, especially confirming a considered path they had shelved in hesitation and now were confident was the better way forward.

Bottom line: if you already do this kind of work, you will recoup your investment the first time you use it with a paying client. If you don't yet, perhaps because it's a service offering you haven't figured out how to have the time to fold into your offers, then you will see it become something immediately saleable.

comments.title: Strong creator-marketing foundation with room to become a complete partnership platform
comments.comment:
I purchased Jem Social at License Tier 2 because I wanted a more organized way to find creators and manage campaigns without relying on spreadsheets, scattered DMs, separate contracts, and disconnected payment systems.

What I like most is that Jem brings several important parts of creator marketing into one workflow. Users can search by platform, niche, location, follower count, engagement, activity, language, and other criteria. Creators can also be found through the AI Assistant, AI Shortlist, URL-based matching, or added from outside the platform.

The Opportunity Board is another feature I appreciate. Instead of depending entirely on cold outreach, a business can publish a detailed campaign brief and allow interested creators to apply. This gives campaign owners an opportunity to evaluate people who have already expressed interest in the work.

Jem also includes Gmail-connected outreach, direct conversations, offer negotiation, contracts, escrow payments, collaboration pipelines, production tracking, revisions, approvals, creator rebooking, and analytics. These features address a genuine buyer need by reducing the number of separate systems required to manage a creator campaign.

The analytics capabilities are especially useful. Campaigns can be organized around sales, conversions, leads, website traffic, engagement, app installs, or brand awareness. Jem can generate creator-specific tracking links that direct audiences to a selected landing page, helping businesses evaluate performance beyond views and follower counts.

I also found the documentation well organized. It walks users through brand setup, creator discovery, outreach, campaign briefs, bookings, production, and analytics. This is valuable for businesses that understand the potential of creator marketing but need a clear operational process.

There are some areas I would like to see improved. During my testing, the Influencer Finder returned “No influencers found” and displayed an “External API call failed with status: 400” error. Since creator discovery is one of Jem’s primary features, the search needs to be reliable and explain clearly when an external request fails.

My dashboard also shows 20 monthly Creator Bookings, while the AppSumo listing advertised 50. I would like that discrepancy corrected or explained.

Creator activity and responsiveness should be easier to evaluate. Last-active dates, average response times, invitation-response rates, read receipts, completed-campaign history, missed deadlines, and a verified-active badge would help users avoid spending credits and time contacting inactive profiles.

The Opportunity Board would benefit from stronger applicant screening as well. Campaign owners should be able to add required questions and filter applicants by niche, audience location, engagement, availability, relevant experience, and whether they meet the campaign requirements.

The largest opportunity I see is for Jem to expand into ongoing creator product partnerships. Many creators have trusted audiences and valuable expertise but no ebook, course, guide, workbook, template package, coaching offer, membership, or other digital product to sell. Marketers and product-development partners could help those creators identify audience needs, develop suitable products, and launch them through the creator’s platform.

Jem already has much of the infrastructure needed for this model: discovery, communication, agreements, deliverables, tracking links, analytics, and payments. Adding product-ownership terms, intellectual-property agreements, milestones, affiliate commissions, hybrid compensation, recurring revenue-share tracking, and automated commission payouts could extend Jem beyond one-time UGC campaigns.

What would motivate me to purchase the highest level is not only a larger booking allowance. I would want more Finder Credits and AI Searches proportional to that allowance, reliable active-creator verification, advanced screening, team and client workspaces, higher Autopilot limits, API or webhook access, advanced attribution reports, and support for continuing creator partnerships and revenue sharing.

Overall, Jem has a strong and thoughtfully organized foundation. It already addresses several real problems in creator discovery and campaign management. Correcting the Finder and account-limit issues would strengthen my confidence, while expanding into long-term creator partnerships would make the platform considerably more valuable and provide a compelling reason to upgrade.

comments.title: Influencer marketing without hiring an agency
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Jem Social is built for brands that want to find, contact, and manage creator relationships without hiring an influencer marketing agency.

What I like about the product is that it makes influencer discovery feel more accessible. A lot of influencer marketing tools seem built for large brands with large budgets, or they push you toward a managed service. Jem Social feels more useful for smaller brands, ecommerce companies, agencies, and founders who want to run creator outreach themselves and keep the process organized.

The value is in having creator discovery, outreach, campaign management, and relationship tracking in one place. Instead of manually searching social platforms, keeping creator lists in spreadsheets, and trying to remember who replied where, Jem Social gives you a more structured way to build and manage influencer campaigns.

I also like the positioning. It does not need to compete with expensive enterprise influencer platforms, instead, it focuses on helping underserved buyers get into influencer marketing with a more intuitive and affordable workflow.

On the first review, most of my notes were around polish and trust. There were leftover template pages, missing legal and help pages, creator database size numbers were inconsistent on different pages, and case study details that needed clearer attribution. The team has since addressed those, which is good to see and shows fast responsiveness.

I found the ‘Invite’ option in settings still did not work in my retest. Clicking it did not open anything. That does not affect the main creator discovery use case, but it is something I would still like to see fixed, especially for users who plan to bring others into the account.

Overall, Jem Social is worth considering if you want a more approachable way to discover creators, manage outreach, and run influencer campaigns. Its best fit is a brand or agency that wants to make influencer marketing more organized, measurable, and manageable in house.

comments.title: Strong Productivity, Limited Research Features !
comments.comment:
I want to use this app in my daily work as a teacher who prepares lessons, summarizes content, and writes notes and feedback for students. Even though I already own two advanced tools, Fluent and Elephas, I decided to purchase this app because its core concept is very strong for educational productivity: it brings AI directly into the applications I am already using, instead of forcing me to switch between different windows and copy–paste text manually.

From my perspective, this app focuses on fast in‑place work inside any text field with simple commands and multi-step workflows, while:

- Elephas is stronger for source‑based academic research, building knowledge bases from the user’s files, and offering broader local processing and privacy options.

- Fluent functions more like a wide platform for models and local integrations, with access to many models, document and image workflows, and deeper file‑based memory.

Compared with them, this app stands out because:

1- It is easier and faster to use for everyday writing inside existing applications.

2-  It is very convenient for transforming, simplifying, and rewriting text while you are typing.

3-  It fits teachers and students who mainly need direct assistance inside Word, email, and learning platforms.

Still, I see it more as a “writing and productivity assistant” than a “complete academic platform”. There are three key areas I recommend the developer to focus on:

Clearer and more robust support for Arabic and right‑to‑left writing, including mixed Arabic–English paragraphs, correct handling of punctuation and lists, and improved Arabic voice dictation and OCR.

Stronger research‑oriented features based on the user’s files, such as chatting with PDF and Word documents with visible page‑level citations and a built‑in citation generator for APA, MLA, and Chicago styles.

Dedicated tools for teachers and students, including templates for lesson plans, learning objectives, rubrics, and feedback forms, together with clearer privacy options for educational institutions.

Overall, I currently rate the app 4 out of 5. The concept is excellent and the development pace is encouraging, but full Arabic support, long‑term stability, and source‑based academic research features still need further development before it can become a core tool in university and school environments.

comments.title: Powerful, flexible, and a founder who actually answers - with some rough edges
comments.comment:
I’ve been setting up and testing KeyShift for a few weeks on Windows 11 (v1.7.2), plus the new Android app (v1.0.1), and I upgraded to Tier 3 because I plan to use it heavily on a second computer. Here’s the honest picture.

What I like:

Custom actions and a custom AI prompt. I built about 30 actions in Spanish for my businesses (fix writing, reply to clients, format for WhatsApp, cost calculators) and each one is a shortcut away. This is the real value.
“Review before inserting” lets me check the result before it replaces my text.
Credits are transparent and cheap in practice. Short actions cost about 1 credit, just as the founder describes.
Bring-your-own-key and local model support, so sensitive text can stay on my machine.
Workflows work well, and the founder confirmed they’re in Tier 2 without a price increase.
Support is excellent. I reported a bug, and the founder investigated and replied within a day, with a clear test to run. Updates ship every few weeks.
My custom actions sync to the Android keyboard.

What needs work:

Some secondary windows (feedback, new action, prompt context) open behind the main window and don’t come to the front when clicked.
The window opens small on every launch.
Localization is incomplete in Spanish: the tray menu, trigger descriptions, “Check” button in About, “Quick Actions”, and the “1 of 4” tour counter are still in English.
On one occasion the Markdown action cut its output mid-name when the text came from Windows Notepad, while the same text worked from a browser. I’ve reported it with my tests.
The Android app is fully in English with no interface language option. Its feedback box doesn’t scroll to follow the cursor while typing, and the keyboard lacks autocorrect and accelerated delete.
Built-in modes can’t be edited or removed, and I’d love to choose which mode the double-space trigger runs.

Verdict: a genuinely useful tool with a responsive founder. Most issues are polish, not missing core features, and I expect it to keep improving.

comments.title: Nice Pismo Alternative that runs with local LLMs for max privacy. Available for Mac and Win.
comments.comment:
I am only using Keyshift for a short time. The primary reason for me to invest in this software was the ability to run it with local models, which is particularly useful since Tier 1 meets my needs, especially given that I already have Pismo and/ or Triplo, similar softwares, integrated into my stack.

Btw. for speed and ease of use, plus AI multistep workflows, I definitely recommend Tier 2 and up!

--
Low Hardware Specs, maximum Privacy (with Local LLM/ Ollama)

Given my testing environment, which includes an M1 MacBook with only 8GB of RAM, I am limited to a smaller selection of models, on this setup. Currently, I am testing with the llama3.2:3b model, and to my surprise, it has performed well in rephrasing and optimizing text, such as emails or this review. However, translation results were not satisfactory, but I expect significant improvements once I upgrade to hardware with 16GB of RAM or more, and have better models to choose from. (Just tested on a 16gb MacMin M4 with gemma4:e2b-mlx and ministral-3:8b, works even better...)

In addition the app needs two permissions on MacOS to fully function:

1. Accessibility permission
- Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.  
- Find KeyShift and turn the switch on.  
- If asked, enter your Mac password to confirm.

2. Input Monitoring permission
- In Privacy & Security, go to Input Monitoring.  
- Find KeyShift and turn the switch on.  
- macOS may ask you to quit and reopen the app; click Quit & Reopen.

---
For other users I would like to share "How to Connect KeyShift AI to Ollama" on Mac

Ollama runs an OpenAI-compatible API locally out of the box. Follow these steps to link them:

1.) Make sure Ollama is installed and running. (Choose a non-thinking model).

1.) Open KeyShift AI Settings.Navigate to AI Provider → select Custom (or BYOK).

2.) Enter the default Ollama local endpoint URL: http://localhost:11434/v1

3.) Input the Model Name exactly as it is designated in Ollama (e.g., llama3.2:3b).

4.) Set the API key field to anything placeholder (like ollama), as local offline instances do not check authentication tokens

5.) Press "test connection" and all should be setup

6.) Final Tip: Keep in mind that by default, Ollama automatically unloads an inactive model from your RAM after exactly 5 minutes of inactivity. This can be changed manually. 

---

I’ve got both the tier one (for local LLMs on the more powerful machines) and tier two licenses (especially for the AI workflows). Buying a software twice is unusual for me, but Keyshift is something so solid and useful that I wanted it to run on every mac we use as a daily driver.

Endri, thanks for making something this useful.

comments.title: From brainstorming an idea to a coherent book draft
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Writing a few pages with AI is easy. Keeping an entire book consistent from the first chapter to the last is a different problem.

Aivolut Books can start even earlier than that. If you don't have the book idea figured out yet, you can give it some direction and have it brainstorm several concepts for you. You can also bring your own idea instead. I generated several book ideas, chose one I liked, and turned it into a full brief with a title, subtitle, premise, target reader and chapter outline.

From there, it generated a coherent multi-chapter nonfiction draft of several thousand words. What I like is that the book is treated as one project rather than a series of unrelated prompts. Aivolut keeps the brief, outline, writing style and source material together and uses that plan to guide the chapters as the manuscript is written. Which means less time reminding the AI what the book is supposed to be about every few chapters.

There is quite a bit around the writing itself too. I generated a cover that matched the book and could choose from different styles. It also produced the Amazon description and keywords without using additional credits. Once the manuscript is ready, you can export it as DOCX, EPUB or PDF and continue editing or prepare it for publishing.

Digital products are live too, so the platform can also be used for things like workbooks, guides, checklists and lead magnets. BYOK is available on tiers 3 and 4, which is useful for something as AI-heavy as generating and revising entire books.

During my original test, children's picture books and audiobooks were still marked as coming soon. Those features are now available on the Pro tier, along with manuscript import, translation and deeper research.

Additionally, during my first test, the saved ideas count updated but the actual list did not refresh until I reloaded the page. The team said they are addressing that issue.

Overall, I like that Aivolut Books doesn't assume I already have everything figured out. I can start by brainstorming book ideas, choose one worth pursuing, turn it into a structured brief and outline, and then generate the manuscript while keeping the whole book connected. This is much more useful than opening a general AI tool and trying to piece together a book one prompt and one chapter at a time. For self-publishers who want a guided path to a KDP-ready draft, it delivers.

comments.title: Promising European email marketing tool with fair pricing
comments.comment:
We bought InTouch because we were looking for an email marketing solution for three of our brands. Even though it was a Launchpad deal, we chose tier 3 so we could really try it out.
So far, the experience has been very positive. The interface looks great, everything feels clear, and I especially like the automation journey. It is still in beta, but it already makes building an email flow feel very visual and intuitive.

We chose InTouch for two main reasons:
First, we are planning to move to Italy next year, so it feels good to support an Italian business. It is also a European company, and we are trying to move more of our overseas subscriptions to European alternatives.
Second, I really like that their pricing is based on the number of emails sent rather than the number of subscribers. For us, that feels like a much fairer proposition. I am not an avid newsletter writer, and I have always found it frustrating to pay based on subscriber numbers when actual usage depends on how many emails you send.

Of course, there are still a few things that could be improved; it’s a new product, so that’s to be expected. The onboarding process, for example, currently uses a PDF form, which feels a bit clunky. That said, I could also smile about it, and the support team was quick to help us out. 
They addressed all our questions and minor issues promptly. I do hope the template builder gets a makeover at some point. It feels a little outdated, but it does work.

Overall, InTouch feels like a promising platform with a clear interface, a fair pricing model, and a responsive, helpful support team. We feel confident enough to purchase two more Tier 3 licenses for our other businesses.

comments.title: Good basic email service, but needs a few improvements
comments.comment:
Like: The user interface is reasonably easy to use and understand (though the videos need updating as it has changed slightly since they were made). The automation builder was straight forward and I really liked how the emails could be cloned and made into templates. The email builder itself was also easy to use if you just want to create simple emails. It's great that SendFox is also able to directly integrate with Book Funnel and Story Origin.

Dislike: No text wrapping in email builder. This gives less flexibility in design layout and while there are workarounds, they don't look good for both desktop and mobile. I also wish there was an 'or' feature in the automations, especially for triggers, so new subscribers could enter a flow by being added into this group OR this group OR this group. Having said that, I'm not sure it is a regular feature in any ESP, but it would be great. Forcing double opt in is also a little problematic, as subscribers may have already completed double opt-in before they hit Send Fox. This creates extra friction and annoyance for subscribers, and means I need to manually follow up or manually cull them so they don't weigh my list down. Once inside, I also discovered that someone unsubscribed cannot resubscribe later if they want to. That could be a problem.

Overall though, it is a very affordable and easy to use platform and I am mostly satisfied so far.

comments.title: Product No Longer Functions the Way It Did

UPDATE! 6-16-2026
Support Came Through For Us

I want to update my previous review with what happened after I posted it.

After reaching out to SendFox support about the HTML editor issue, their Customer Experience Manager Luka followed up personally, acknowledged the problem, and restored HTML editing access to our account. We tested it immediately and our full custom HTML template rendered perfectly.

The initial experience was frustrating, especially as a brand new customer who purchased just days before the change. But the way our issue was handled, with honesty, a personal follow-up, and a real resolution, reflects well on their support team.

I can only speak to our own experience, but for us they made it right. 
That counts for a lot. FIVE well earned tacos!

Original Review:
We purchased SendFox through AppSumo for our non-profit Raiders booster club and used it successfully to send our monthly newsletter and occasional announcements to our members.

The HTML editor was a key feature we relied on to create branded, professional-looking emails. It worked well and allowed us to maintain a consistent look and feel that represented our club properly.

Recently the interface changed completely. The HTML editor no longer functions the way it did. When we paste our custom HTML code, the styling does not render correctly. Background colors are stripped, text content disappears, and the layout breaks. What used to work now does not work.

We have contacted SendFox support and are waiting to hear back. But as it stands, a feature that worked when we purchased the product no longer works. For a club that depends on clean, professional email communications to stay connected with its members, this is a significant problem.

We hope SendFox resolves this soon. Until then, we cannot recommend the product in its current state.

comments.title: I am in the middle ground here

I am mid on this product and on the fence about a refund.

1. I really do not like the onboarding process. The OTP on setup works very poorly. On my Mac, it didn't just go to spam, it went into like hidden spam that I had to specifically look for. The other onboarding emails did not do this. Something about that system is flawed. I requested a new code 5 times before I found 1 and had to request a new one because it was still the wrong one.

2. There is not an ability to download each grouping separate. You can download all, all the 'safe' ones, you can download the really bad ones, but there is a grouping in the middle that includes 'risky' emails that gets lumped in with spammy ones, ones with filled inboxes, disposable ones, with "catch all" and I can not download separately. I want to delete all the 'disposable' ones in my list without getting 'catch alls'. This matters to me, now I have to download all and separate manually and delete the ones I don't need. Other similar ones I have paid for in the past as one off needs for agency clients didn't have this limitation.

3. The deal itself is really solid if you need to clean email as far as numbers and limits go on a monthly basis - if it works....

4. Not loving the reliability of markings. Emails that are marked as 'spam trap' and 'disposable' are shown as active people in my Kartra account opening and getting emails and with custom domains they are using in their business. They just don't appear to be as consistent as running through NeverBounce and KickBounce

comments.title: Great for pre send list cleaning
comments.comment:
I bought Reoon to do one thing: clean email lists before outreach (and avoid stupid bounces). So far, it delivers. You upload a CSV, run the check, and export the results (valid, invalid, disposable, role based, catch all). It is quick, the flow is simple, and it does not try to be clever in a way that gets in your way.

I have not used it at massive scale yet, but in the batches I tested it matched what I expected and helped me keep my CRM cleaner (which is the whole point for me). It is the kind of tool you use, get the answer, and move on.

If I had to ask for improvements, I would start with a more polished dashboard and better guidance for borderline statuses (especially catch all and unknown), plus more native integrations. Overall, very good value if you just want reliable list hygiene without extra drama.

comments.title: Glad I Pulled The Trigger
comments.comment:
I got ClickMoat after digging as deep as I could into the 21 different options on the market. When spam clicks and bots that run rampant on Google and Meta ruin your day, week, month and campaigns, you need to act on it. 

Appsumo, as usual, is my go to marketplace to see if an up and coming SaaS product can fit the bill for our needs. This account says it is only from April 2024 but I have been using Appsumo since 2013, this is an account for one of our businesses. I am fine keeping our Tech Stack on all the monthly subscriptions but no lie, when you find an emerging developer that gets it right long term, the benefits are phenomenal. 

I have been using ClickMoat for almost a month now, on a small and learning campaign in Google Ads, that we have been using for Testing Purposes. 

Here is our experience with it to date: 

Support for the issues you will read in the review has been fantastic, the founder Nirav, is on top of things and actively helps get his team to do what Everyone that is on Appsumo comes to do: work their product into a staple in their vertical. Which from my interactions with ClickMoat, shows me they are genuinely focused at doing exactly that. If you are on Appsumo and think you will pay 1-3 months subscription fees for a lifetime deal and then you give zero feedback that helps the developer work out the kinks, you have no idea what you're doing and need to educate yourself why this all exists. Help them out. 

Onboarding - this process was not overly complicated but it was disjointed, which caused some confusion for me. This is where I had to first reach out for support, which I didn't know how to do (due to the Appsumo process in place, this looks to be different than what monthly subscribers go though). I came back here to find who to contact and reached out to Nirav, who got me what I needed very fast. They took my feedback on how to smooth that process out, which I hope they tweaked.

Functionality - We have noticed a definite improvement in the number of what we always suspected were fraudulent clicks. Google Ads own report showed 49.3% fraudulent clicks on their report. When you talk to any rep, they act like you didn't say anything, every time. Then you have to submit a "never-never" form and prove your case to them (like guys, your OWN form shows this, it isn't a number we got out of thin air). The patterns where this would happen have been pretty much eliminated. They only places we still have an issue are always the new keywords Google Ads constantly puts into the campaign each day (doesn't matter if you use Broad "Phrase" or [Exact] match, they still do this now. Yay for "improvements" by Google. Move the goalposts once again to suck more money for themselves while making the user experience worse for almost everyone else. Whole Separate topic). 

Clicks Saved - ClickMoat tells us that in almost a month we have 15 clicks saved. They estimate this at 42 cents per click but our work is one of the, if not THE, most expensive CPCs in Googles world, where the auction can range from $2 to almost $50 per click. This depends on if you are advertising for Clicks or Conversions of course but the principle is the same. Googles mission is to blow through your budget and spend double that on a daily basis, like a drunk patron mindlessly hitting the slot machine button, spending money without regard. So ClickMoat has likely saved us quite a lot more than what they estimate.

General Value for the price - At Appsumo prices? Insane Value. At the monthly price the other 20 players in this space charge? We see the value on this side and think that if they keep improving the way they have directly communicated to us, that they will be top of the market.

Support teams - They have been extremely responsive. Is it 24/7? No they keep their own office hours, which is to be expected, they have families and lives like the rest of us. However the support has been based on the type of need. If it is systems related, it is handled fast. If it is general, it is done during their business hours. Personally I am not a fan of Slack at all, it just makes the whole experience seem even more disjointed but that could just be me. The result is that you do still get what you need. 

TL;DR: This is a product that has helped us greatly. There are bugs and processes that need to be worked on and developed out but that is exactly why they are here. The responsiveness and grateful messages from the real user feedback, as well as the improvements we have seen, with the ones coming, make us think that we will have a winner on our hands for long term, when they are done. Glad we bought this deal.

comments.title: It’s good but..

So I have had the time to play around mystrika for a few months and here is my honest review.

1. The UI is disgustingly trash. This is just my opinion but I hate how it looks and feels compared to instantly or smartlead. I feel like I’m using a software from the early 2000’s. Update this please for the love of god it’s so ugly

2. Email warmups are not the greatest to setup for new users. It’s pretty bad and hard to see if it’s turned off or on. You have to take all the settings applied and delete them rather than a switch. Please change that also. 

3. Save campaigns without importing contacts. I have had this happen more then once where I write everything out for about 30-45 min and don’t put in a contact and it will delete everything. I just want to do copywriting and I don’t get why I have to import a contact to save. I just put my personal email and take it out later but it’s annoying.

4. Add a drop down for syntax. I hate typing out {{ fname }} just let it be a drop down and click. Also have an area where it will atomically detect a field instead of only asking us company name, email, full name. I want to add more sometimes. 

5. Add a button to run a campaign instead of the 3 dots.

6. I believe Instantly and smartlead do better then mystrika, but the pricing is WAY better for mystrika. I would say purchase if you don’t have the money to spend currently. 

Overall I do like the software, but it has its issues. I will keep using it because I believe in it. I pray to the mystrika gods they revert their whole UI tho because it is beyond garbage. I never complain about UI but this one is just not it man. Hopefully they come out with an updated cleaner look that is very easy to use very very soon. All the things above I hope they add to compete again instantly and smartlead strongly. I wanted to discuss the negative sides rather than positives since there is plenty of positive reviews. But I would say go ahead and try this app

I have to delete them one by one, and each deletion for each lead isn't fast at all. It takes like 5-10 seconds for 1 lead to be deleted. (Imagine if like 50 leads were finished per day... I have to delete them one by one.. It's frustrating a little and time consuming.)
Especially that you have a limit of total leads in all campaigns (1 code has a 5000 leads limit), keeping those "finished" and "bounced" leads are anyway useless to keep. So, i wish we could be able to delete them easily and in bulk. And anyway Mystrika says that leads are reusable in the features (refered as stackable and in the offer refered as reusable i think, next to the number of leads). So, if you delete a lead, you can reuse this lead (if i had 1000/5000 leads and deleted 200, it will show 800/5000 and not stay 1000/5000).
So please, add this feature. Thanks a lot for this software anyway. It's insane.

comments.title: I have now tried   Mystrika Clickreach Hexospark
comments.comment:
I am in search of an alternative to LemList. At 100$ per month for one sending address, I have been looking at exploring alternatives. I have contacts that are of low importance, so I am fortunate to have some ability to play around with trying alternatives. 

I have now tried 

Mystrika
Clickreach
Hexospark.

Across the board, key features that are missing from all products

#1 No option to bcc each sent email. I want to be able to bcc the email to my salesforce sync email.

#2 Lemlist has a native way to sync with salesforce’s api, so it can pull the contacts natively. This is critical since it is how I manage who opts out. If I send an email in salesforce and the contact opts out, it pulls the record from the salesforce report, and thus pulls it from lemlist campaign automatically. For all 3 platforms, if someone opts out outside of the platform, I have to manually either pull the record or upload it to the universal blacklist. This is really confusing to coordinate. My current workaround that I will attempt is to hard delete the contacts from each platform respectively at the end of each campaign and then re-upload fresh from the exported SF report when I go to do a new campaign. 

XXXXXXXX Mysrtika - 4 out of 5 stars XXXXXXXX

This platform by far has been the most useful between Mystrika, Clickreach, and Hexospark as it has the option for email warmup. 

I also like that it has a unibox and it allows for email rotation. 
The design/UIX is a little old school, but it gets the job done. 

I’ve removed one star since it also has a bug like Clickreach, where it is sending the email in duplicate randomly. However, it is not duplicating it from the same sending email address, so for now I have decided to let it run its play


**|| I wrote the following to mystrika for support; ||**
Was able to successfully get a campaign up and running. Just encountered a fun bug. It seems to have sent the same email to the same end user twice, but across two different sending accounts… Fortunately the end user has an OOO set up, so your unibox feature actually caught the issue in action! I am worried that it might be occurring though more, so I'm going to pause the campaign for now. 

**|| I got the following response from support; ||**
“Though the Mystrika system is completely distributed, with multiple checks in place to avoid this from happening.
There is a small chance that this is possible.
The chance of this happening should be less than 0.1%.
Also, note, this issue can only happen on the first contact email, and can never happen on the follow up email.
We are continuously improving our algorithm, and hopefully we should be able to bring the chance of this happening much lower in future.”

comments.title: An ad agent that can go from analysis to action
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

A lot of AI marketing tools can look at your ad data and tell you what they think you should do. Soku is designed to continue past the recommendation and actually make the change.

You can connect Google Ads, Meta and TikTok, along with sources such as GA4, Shopify and Search Console so Soku has the conversion and revenue context behind the ad performance. It can then find things like wasted spend, ROAS drops, CPA spikes or campaigns that need attention.

You also don't have to hand over full control on day one. Read access is the default, so you can start by letting Soku audit the accounts and make recommendations. From there, you can enable actions that require approval and eventually let routine changes run automatically within the rules you set.

Soku can do things such as pause ads, move budget, add negative keywords and launch new ads rather than simply producing another report telling you to do those things yourself. Actions that could increase spend can still be held for approval, and the activity log shows what changed and the numbers behind the decision.

The automation side should also save a lot of checking. You can schedule daily and weekly briefs and set alerts for things like ROAS drops, CPA spikes and unusual spending, so you don't have to keep three advertising dashboards open waiting to notice something has gone wrong.

There are creative tools in the same platform too. You can take an existing ad and resize, localize, caption or modify it, or turn a product image into another ad variation without starting over.

During my testing, I also found the API and MCP connection available, along with BYOK under Integrations. I didn't run into anything that warranted an action item for the partner. Native webhooks would still be a useful addition for completed automations, approvals and credit thresholds, but that was more of a suggestion and a wishlist item from me.

One thing to understand with the AppSumo deal is how credits work. They are used for AI work such as analysis, creative generation and agent actions, reset each month and don't roll over. Additional one-time credit packs are available and those do not expire.

Overall, I think Soku's advantage is that it closes the loop between noticing a problem in an ad account and doing something about it. You can keep yourself involved in the decisions you want to approve while letting Soku handle more of the repetitive monitoring and execution.

comments.title: Very nice - just one thing missing...
comments.comment:
This is a very nice tool.  But I really hope you understand that being able to pass data through the shortlink does matter.  

If this was just a shortlink tool, that would be one thing... but this does a lot more, i.e. pixel capture...  So we would like to be able to use it with our CRM... or with our affiliates.  

That means creating shortlinks like myshort.co/landing - and when we use that link in an email spawned by our crm, it will append data (as all CRMs do) - i.e. myshort.co/landing?id=043a44 (dynamic depending on the lead the email is going to).  Well, that added id is pretty important, as it identifies a connection back to the crm for that user.  That parameter should be able to "pass through" to the destination URL.  

The same thing for affiliates.  If we have 50 affiliates and we want to use Switchy, right now we would have to create a link in Switchy for EACH affiliate...  so if we have 10 different destination links to use in our various funnels, multiply that x 50 so we can add in the affiliate codes for each affiliate we share those links with. :-(((  Instead, we need to be able to create 10 links... and allow the affiliates to add ?aff=101, etc. to the link, so that their affiliate code can pass through to the destination.

So far this doesn't appear to be a priority - yet is such a fundamental need for anyone who is doing any form of advanced marketing - so for that I have to drop a star.  

If you don't need this, then consider this a 5 star review.  But we do need it, and a lot of the groups we work with do as well. 

I would love to put that 5th star back on, because otherwise it's a very good tool and deserving of it.  

Thanks

comments.title: Still using this 6 years later — hard to beat for the price
comments.comment:
I bought Switchy six years ago and have been using it across campaigns ever since. When I saw it back on AppSumo at the same price, that alone tells you something — tools that hold their value over that kind of timeline are not common.

What Switchy actually gives you is control over what happens after someone clicks. Custom domains, UTMs, retargeting pixels, and redirect logic mean you can control how links behave based on the channel, the audience, or the campaign stage. For anyone running traffic across multiple platforms, that flexibility has compounding value over time.

Where it is more limited is analytics. It functions as a monitoring layer — you can see what is happening at the link level — but it is not a full reporting solution. If you are expecting deep segmentation or campaign-level attribution, you will want to supplement it elsewhere.

The product feels more maintained than actively developed.

The core functionality is solid and does what it says, but do not buy it expecting a roadmap of new features. Buy it because what it does today is genuinely useful and the one-time pricing makes that a reasonable long-term bet.

If you care about tracking, retargeting, and control more than feature expansion, Switchy still holds up.

Full review: https://marketingwithdave.com/switchy-review/

Switchy vs Linko comparison: https://marketingwithdave.com/switchy-vs-linko-link-management-software-comparison/

comments.title: Overall great value for the price, but here's the problem:
comments.comment:
Consider this as a "swiss knife" for sales:
many supported features here that will serve you truly for that cause.

But do each one of them excel above the competitors? 
See, this is the common problem with "swiss-knife" products.
Usually, the value is overwhelming - you get all these stuff for a fraction of the price.
But when you look closer, you start noticing some setbacks, and begin to understand that "hey, maybe i got all of these here... but for function X / Y / Z, I'd better off using this other tool", and somehow you end up stripping the product from it's value because you'd prefer using other tools that are slightly better for specific functions. 

I'm not saying that this is the case here - I'm just saying this has happened to me with other "swiss-knife" tools, and I haven't tested SalesBlink enough to bring a real solid recommandation.
But from my short experience - the prospecting tools (companies, people) are far inferior to other platforms.
AS IS, this cannot replace Linkedin Sales Navigator / Zoominfo / Uplead for making a laser-focused outreach list, as you can't narrow down the search with many filters.
Only company size and main industry are available in companies search, and for people search - it's just based on domains and emails, so you can't really search for titles ex. "CEO" etc.. and then narrow it down even further by company size etc.. 
this is what I would expect from a good prospecting tool, but seems like SalesBlink has it different.
who here build an outreach list based on domains anyway? let's say I got the entire company's email addresses by searching their domain, how do I know which one of them is the decision maker? so now I have to try and pull it from LinkedIn or Facebook? it's a weird workflow.
Also let's say I found this company via the company search, who says it's my ideal customer? can't really say it judging only by their size and general industry. This search is too wide to begin with.
Can't really say I was impressed by the database either, but this is something that other platforms are lacking as well.

Anyway, I hope they improve the whole prospecting workflow and database since I do see the potential here.

comments.title: Essential Tool That Replaced Three Monthly Subscriptions
comments.comment:
Before grabbing SalesBlink on AppSumo, my outreach stack was expensive and fragmented. I was paying recurring monthly fees for cold email automation, a separate per-mailbox warm-up tool, an AI writing assistant, and a third-party calendar scheduler. SalesBlink consolidated everything into one clean platform on a lifetime license.

The setup was seamless across my sending accounts. The automated email warm-up and smart sender rotation protect domain health without needing manual intervention. Inboxes scale safely, keeping messages out of spam filters and landing right in primary inboxes.

BlinkGPT is a huge time-saver. Instead of spending hours writing copy and pacing follow-ups, I input a quick summary of my offer and audience, and the AI generates a multi-step sequence in minutes. The drafts are punchy, conversational, and avoid generic sales fluff.

Day-to-day management is equally smooth with the Master Unibox, which aggregates replies from all sending domains into a single inbox. The integrated calendar scheduler lets leads book meetings directly from messages, automatically halting ongoing sequence touches so nobody gets redundant follow-ups.

For founders, freelancers, and agency teams wanting to scale outreach without getting hit by recurring per-seat fees, SalesBlink delivers outstanding reliability and value. Highly recommended.

comments.title: I Bought It in 2022. The New Release Just Put It on Solid Ground.
comments.comment:
I bought Screpy back in 2022 for uptime monitoring and it's quietly done its job for four years. This month's platform rebuild gave me a reason to revisit it.

What impressed me: 5,000 crawled pages per project (well above most tools at this price), 150 tracked keywords, and Google Map Ranking, which I rarely see in an SEO tool this affordable. Working through the audit tool, I counted 37 individual checks spanning technical, content, and security issues, making for a thorough audit. The standout, though, is native MCP integration with AI assistants, letting you pull Screpy data directly into your workflow.

The honest gaps: the Rank Tracker only shows the first 10 Google results, so you'll still lean on Search Console for anything past page one. AI Search Visibility is advertised but isn't available yet (the team confirmed it's on the roadmap). There's also no backlink analysis or scheduled reports.

Support was excellent throughout. I flagged a few small bugs during testing, and the founder was active in the AppSumo questions section responding directly, with fixes shipped the same day.

This rebuild puts Screpy on much stronger footing going forward, and I'm genuinely excited to see what they ship next. It's worth buying today for what it already does well.

If you'd like a deeper look at the features, screenshots, and my hands-on testing, you can read my full review: https://marketingwithdave.com/screpy-review/

comments.title: I "mostly" like it.. *lol*
comments.comment:
The platform gave me a cool tool to use with my other AppSumo purchase (https://appsumo.com/products/websiteim-website-builder/) to optimize the two new sites I built. The tool is good, but not perfect.

Two somewhat minor issues that I discovered:
1. The platform can't seem to discern that I only have ONE home page and instead the results would indicate that I have THREE home pages.
- https://mentorsandmimosas.com
- https://mentorsandmimosas.com/index.php
- https://mentorsandmimosas.com/

Hence I am getting an erroneous "Duplicated H1" warning. even IF as their support says it is "caused by pages redirecting to each other", these are not distinct pages and this isn't an error that should be occurring. They do need to address this.

2. The platform also seems to fully ignore OG tags and will flag pages for "Twitter Card Incomplete" even if an equivalent OG tag is present in the markup. Though I had equivalent OG tag on my pages, I had to create the following (duplicate) Twitter tags "twitter: description" & "twitter: title" for the software to stop flagging my pages with the "Twitter Card Incomplete" warning. and BONUS.. because it cannot discern that the home page is only 1 page and not THREE pages, I still get "Twitter Card Incomplete" warning for the "three flavors" of the homepage *lol*.

Hopefully they will address and fix both of these issues soon. 

Their support is not something I'm loving though. They respond. EVENTUALLY.. But maaaaaaaaan they sure do take their own sweet time doing it! *lol* I hope as the tool improves the customer service gets a LOT more responsive.

Otherwise this is a solid analysis tool and I am pleased with my purchase. I can't give them a full 5 tacos because of the slow customer service response, but they are a SOLID 4 tacos for me.
