comments.title: Feature-Rich and they Keep Coming!
comments.comment:
I'm a new user of Screpy. I had the chance to try it in the past, but I only jumped in on V6 which is all worth-it! 🚀

What I love most about Screpy is its simplicity, ease-of-use, and its clean and easy to understand dashboard. Compared to other similar SEO tools, this is a better choice for quick website monitoring and site audits without the complexities. A go-to solutions that gets the job done.

In the past weeks, I have been updating our websites based on Screpy's audit findings and recommendations - with some items I can't believe we've missed! After updating, we saw significant improvements on our Pagespeed Insight scores, thanks to Screpy! 

GSC integration is a time-saver as I no longer need to open a separate tab for GSC. And GSC appears to be more visually insightful on Screpy than on its own platform. Quick Wins is a very nice bonus and one of my reasons for getting this LTD.

Other features we are using are the Rank Tracker, SERP Analysis, Index Status, Core Web Vitals, and Uptime Monitor. The Content Writer is nice to have and can create useable output. But manual editing is needed to improve SEO scores.

Advanced integrations with Bing, Cloudflare, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity are available. And n8n, Zapier, and Make are in the pipeline.

It's good that the items on the menu that are not included in the LTD were removed. It created confusion and affected the clean UI/UX.

Another thing that impressed me is the frequency of updates and improvements which happens almost daily! Recently, they added new insights in Quick Wins - Cannibalization Risks, Content Decay insights, and Internal Link Opportunities which are all very helpful in SEO.

Yes, there is still room for improvement and support can be delayed at times. But for all these helpful features at a one-time cost, how can we complain?

comments.title: Screpy, a powerful ally for SEO monitoring and performance tracking.
comments.comment:

Screpy offers a wide range of essential features: technical auditing and monitoring, Pagespeed analysis, uptime tracking, syntax checking, Google Lighthouse report, meta tag analysis, SSL monitoring, as well as automated SEO tasks. These features are ideal for quickly spotting and fixing technical issues and ensuring the best possible performance of sites.

I find the tool extremely useful for tracking my sites' positions, as well as keeping an eye on my competitors, which is important in an SEO strategy. The analytics are accurate and the security alerts allow you to react quickly in case of problems. The Google Lighthouse report for each page is a real plus, as are the robots.txt and Sitemap.xml checks, which help optimize indexing.

With space for 100 teams, 250 sites, and a large volume of analysis credits, Screpy is designed to efficiently track a large portfolio of projects. Since using it, I have observed significant improvements in terms of stability and functionality. The development team seems very responsive and dedicated, which further increases my satisfaction.

For those looking for a powerful, flexible, and ever-evolving tool to manage their SEO, Screpy is an option I highly recommend. It’s a great investment that offers unbeatable value for the features offered.

comments.title: I Bought It in 2022. The New Release Just Put It on Solid Ground.
comments.comment:
I bought Screpy back in 2022 for uptime monitoring and it's quietly done its job for four years. This month's platform rebuild gave me a reason to revisit it.

What impressed me: 5,000 crawled pages per project (well above most tools at this price), 150 tracked keywords, and Google Map Ranking, which I rarely see in an SEO tool this affordable. Working through the audit tool, I counted 37 individual checks spanning technical, content, and security issues, making for a thorough audit. The standout, though, is native MCP integration with AI assistants, letting you pull Screpy data directly into your workflow.

The honest gaps: the Rank Tracker only shows the first 10 Google results, so you'll still lean on Search Console for anything past page one. AI Search Visibility is advertised but isn't available yet (the team confirmed it's on the roadmap). There's also no backlink analysis or scheduled reports.

Support was excellent throughout. I flagged a few small bugs during testing, and the founder was active in the AppSumo questions section responding directly, with fixes shipped the same day.

This rebuild puts Screpy on much stronger footing going forward, and I'm genuinely excited to see what they ship next. It's worth buying today for what it already does well.

If you'd like a deeper look at the features, screenshots, and my hands-on testing, you can read my full review: https://marketingwithdave.com/screpy-review/

comments.title: I "mostly" like it.. *lol*
comments.comment:
The platform gave me a cool tool to use with my other AppSumo purchase (https://appsumo.com/products/websiteim-website-builder/) to optimize the two new sites I built. The tool is good, but not perfect.

Two somewhat minor issues that I discovered:
1. The platform can't seem to discern that I only have ONE home page and instead the results would indicate that I have THREE home pages.
- https://mentorsandmimosas.com
- https://mentorsandmimosas.com/index.php
- https://mentorsandmimosas.com/

Hence I am getting an erroneous "Duplicated H1" warning. even IF as their support says it is "caused by pages redirecting to each other", these are not distinct pages and this isn't an error that should be occurring. They do need to address this.

2. The platform also seems to fully ignore OG tags and will flag pages for "Twitter Card Incomplete" even if an equivalent OG tag is present in the markup. Though I had equivalent OG tag on my pages, I had to create the following (duplicate) Twitter tags "twitter: description" & "twitter: title" for the software to stop flagging my pages with the "Twitter Card Incomplete" warning. and BONUS.. because it cannot discern that the home page is only 1 page and not THREE pages, I still get "Twitter Card Incomplete" warning for the "three flavors" of the homepage *lol*.

Hopefully they will address and fix both of these issues soon. 

Their support is not something I'm loving though. They respond. EVENTUALLY.. But maaaaaaaaan they sure do take their own sweet time doing it! *lol* I hope as the tool improves the customer service gets a LOT more responsive.

Otherwise this is a solid analysis tool and I am pleased with my purchase. I can't give them a full 5 tacos because of the slow customer service response, but they are a SOLID 4 tacos for me.

comments.title: Very solid start, hope they grow well
comments.comment:
I've been looking to replace Google Analytics + Google Tag Manager for a long time. It's very heavy on the website, very complicated and convoluted and (something that got more important for me over time) very intrusive with all the data Google grabs from you and your customers.

I'm using Matamo on side hustles and checked out Fathom and Plausible, but every tool is lacking in some aspects. In comparison, VisitorTracking is a very strong contender and, in my opinion, at least as good or better than the mentioned services.

What I like
- Very lightweight, not a single issue was detected while measuring performance
- Very nice, simple and intuitive UI. I like it very much.
- All important data at a glance
- Very useful User Journey Data (Scroll depth, visited pages, conversions etc.)
- Simple to Set-up Conversion Tracking, also ability to set up Funnels

As I run ads a lot for myself and clients, many things I miss are ads or business related:

- (Grouped) Statistics for organic, ads, social media, newsletter traffic (medium)
- Statistics for ads and campaigns (perhaps with help of url parameters)
- Some kind of conversion integration with popular ads services (google, bing etc.), so that I can send conversion data back to the ad platform
- Conversion values 

I also would like to see an improved dashboard for conversions with:
- Ordering/Sorting Conversions
- Ability to group conversion types or add sections for certain conversions (engagement, contact/lead, Purchases etc.)

Visitor Dashboard
- As mentioned, auto tagging of the medium (social media, ads, organic, newsletter etc.)
- As I rely on url parameter for campaigns, I often have very long Landing-Page URLs, what is kind of ugly in the visitor dashboard. It might be a good idea to present it without parameters and to show it only on demand (hover/popup) - but only if a feature regarding the medium exists. Right now, the original long url it is the only way to see where the user interacted with our campaigns.

I hope the feedback is useful. I think VisitorTracking can become a really outstanding tracking tool in the future.

comments.title: VisitorTracking: Simple and Basic Web Tracking Solution

VisitorTracking is a universal website tracker that works with any platform and provides basic information. It is not an alternative to Google Analytics but is a great software that you can easily install on any kind of website.

The installation process is straightforward, and the data is easy to understand. If you or your client don't have a dedicated person for your website, then you are the target market for this app. Additionally, you get free customer support to set up the tool. Once configured, you can simply consult the data.

There are many free and paid alternatives to Google Analytics that make sense if your website has high traffic. However, if you have fewer than 1,000 visitors per month, you won't have enough data to understand visitor behavior deeply.

Before Google Analytics became the free standard about 20 years ago, there were many paid software options to track small and large sites. VisitorTracking's one-time cost is worth the investment if you are a beginner and only interested in basic information.

I've spent 2 weeks trying to learn this tool. I find the training videos so far long and arduous. Daniel knows the process so well he is forgetting at times to not give too much. Initially, it may be good to explain "why" but after that initial mind dump, just give us the precise steps. I've attempted 3-4 times to write out the steps but keep running across another dimension that confuses me. Short and to the point videos would be highly appreciated.

They have an excellent concept and I decided to buy a 2nd code to give myself more room with the imposed limits. 

I am disappointed at the number of post I've tried to make in the Facebook group that are being rejected. One in particular, I thought would have a good discussion everyone could learn from. Just so you know, if you don't give me a reason why the post is being rejected then you leave me with the feeling that encourages me not to contribute or to participate. I've been in a couple groups who remove anything that might be construed as a negative. That's a huge mistake. You need to know what people are thinking and allow people to share. If it gets out of hand remove the post, but I doubt that is what will happen. Shut the voices down and you'll lose people. You have lost me for now.

Im excited to see where they take this tool so I made the investment. I really would like a SEO tool of choice that handles everything I need to plan and write my articles. This is the best tool I've ever seen in over 12 years of internet marketing. I especially like the AI and how well it writes. 

One last thing. I'd like to see a better wizard that walks me through the steps. Make is stupid simple to produce my first article. Maybe a wizard for the Pillar page and a separate wizard for supporting pages that are shorter. Not sure but simplicity would get me more excited. 

Make is easy in the wizard to identify and save my supporting keywords for pillar page and supporting pages. The wizard should walk me through the steps and make it easy for me to remember each step and how to troubleshoot that part of the process without having to think so hard. comments.title: Decent Writing Tool - Needs Improvement, 3.5 Tacos
comments.comment:
I've been playing around with WriterZen to see if it could replace Frase as my primary content creation tool.  Honestly, I don't think it's there yet.  (Though it's better than nothing if you weren't able to get in on Frase.)

Before I get into the negative stuff, I will say that the topic discovery tab is pretty useful.  I was able to find what looks like a pretty good keyword almost immediately, and I'm pretty picky on what I'll write about because I have very little time and have to make every article count.  Not sure what it's doing with the "ideas" because they seem to be all over the place, but the page as a whole is a winner.

The keyword research page is also very helpful and lays out most of the information you would need in a useful manner.

Here are some areas that would need to be improved before I could use it full time:
1) Plagiarism tool is hot trash.  I plugged in an article that I know the writer plagiarized major sections of (in some cases almost copy pasted), and on high it came back as 67% plagiarized because phrases like "how to do it?" and "coffee grounds are" were used in other articles somewhere on the internet.  On medium, it came back as 96% unique.  Quetext doesn't catch everything, but it catches the main sections that were ripped from other sites, even if the author changed a word here or there.
2) Once #1 is fixed, the plagiarism word count limit should be at least doubled.  My shortest articles are at least 1,000 words, and an article shouldn't have to be broken into multiple pieces to be run through a checker on a paid tool.
3) The content creator (the main piece I use in a tool like this) is off to a good start, but it doesn't put all of the information at your fingertips in the way Frase does.  In Frase, you can scroll through the articles in the serp using the "top content" tab and see all of their subheads.  If you want to take a closer look at one, you can just expand it and see a summary/excerpt of the content written under that subhead.  This lets you scroll through and see everything being recommended on the serp (for a best x for y post) without having to open and read all of the articles.  WZ tries to do this, but it feels clunky, doesn't have as much information available, and subheads often come out with HTML/JS code in them.
4) It really needs NLP so it can compete with tools like Frase and Surfer.  Having a few keywords is useful, but it lacks the depth of the other tools.  Also, having a "topic score" that measures relevance based on the NLP terms pulled from the top ranking articles would be useful as well.  This would greatly help with content optimization.
5) The keyword research tool is extremely slow.  I looked something up before I started writing this, and as of the time I'm submitting the review, the insights tab is still spinning.

Overall, I like the tool, but it does need a few things improved before it can be used as a primary tool for anything other than keyword research.

When setting it up on my website and looking for ways to integrate it into my sales and marketing lifecycle, it appears that the only way to get a lead data into Hey Oliver is for them to interact directly with a Campaign in Bubbly, the chat app provided by Hey Oliver.

The ability to launch into a Campaign or Form within the Bubbly app from a button click or link would be a great feature add.

The Zapier integration in its current state only allows Hey Oliver to send data to other third-party apps, not the other way around. I tried to set up a webhook in Zapier to have my website send lead data to Hey Oliver via and Optin form I have on my site, but the Zapier integration is only one way right now.

As I said, this is a powerful tool with lots of room to grow. But I can't see it as a complete solution to handle our lead nurturing and communication all by itself with its current feature set right now.

Hopefully, with time, it will improve to include things like launching into a Campaign or from a button click and two-way Zapier integration allowing third-party apps to send data to Hey Oliver.

comments.title: An (almost) perfect tool
comments.comment:
Labrika was the first tool of this kind I ever came across and after reading what it does, I almost instantly decided to get it and try it out.

In the weeks following the purchase, I analyzed and tried different similar services but in the end, Labrika always came up on top of all competitors.

It's just THAT good and does everything one would expect from a website analyzer and SEO service plus much more: it will analyze your website and tell you everything that is wrong with it, from the most detailed code issues to the SEO, with the content optimizer function being a real cherry on top.

So why am I leaving only a 4 instead of a 5 in this review?

Here's the thing, when you have a product that is "this" close to perfection, I feel it's a real shame not to make that last step, and my not leaving a 5 here, wants to be a "motivational push" into adding that little more to the offer to be deserving of the full 5 rating.

To me personally, the suggestions would be these:

- Content Optimizer: it would be nice to be able and use this BEFORE a blog post is actually on the website, as to optimize a post before release. This feature alone would place Labrika in the Olympus of website tools, placing it on top of other services like, for example, NeuronWriter, for many people. I'd really LOVE to be able and use the Labrika optimizer as a blog writing editor, entering the keyword and then slowly building up the post with Labrika's suggestions in there, before copying it to my website.

- Backlinks: since most of Labrika's SEO functionalities revolve around competition analysis, I believe that backlinks analysis of such competition should be a must-add inside any report. I would also add a keyword finder but I know they're already working on it so I'll leave this out for now :)

- UI: I find the Labrika UI to be a little cluttered and, on many points, unclear. Especially in the content optimizer, there are times that It tells me that there are issues... but I can't understand what issues we're talking about, I still have, for example, one blog post that Labrika keeps telling me has "1 SEO issue" that I literally have no idea what it is cause it's not explained. I can only "guess" it's related to some red highlights I see on the page but really, no clue how it should be solved. Also, all other pages and info are a little cluttered.

- Competition: Even tho Labrika makes it possible to disable analysis on some specific competition, I found it a little frustrating that such competitors are not "replaced" with the ones below in the search, finding me with maybe only 1-2 references for the most niche posts. 

This said I will end this review by stating, once again, that Labrika is an excellent tool sure to help you out in your website management and quest to the first spots of google and I really can't wait to check out the improvements that the team is sure to send our way in the future.

comments.title: So far so good
comments.comment:
I've used and still do a lot of SEO related tools over the years as Ive been providing seo services for over 20 years. So far, I am finding this tool very useful and much better than most of the other tools I am currently using. I wish I could give it 5 tacos but I am wavering between 3 or 4 tacos. 

To be fair, I gave it 4 tacos because I think the technical features of the tool/service are most excellent, a noticeable improvement over other tools like this and will be very useful in my business. Things it has like optimization KW grouping, competitors list, over optimization and such I find well thought out.

What I don't like is the reporting side of things. The "white-label" reports, well not as useful to me as I would prefer. Sure you can print them (tool doesn't actually seem to provide a simple method to do this.) But I don't find any place to add any other info such as my logo, company info or extraneous comments. 

In addition, the "over 100 reports" well, I'm still trying to figure out where they all are and how to get to them. For me, the reports side of things is equally as important, sometimes more important. The tool makes a nice report at least for the 3 reports I've seen (still looking for the other 97) with some great data but then being able to add some customization's to make it unique to your company, not there.

And lastly, you can "share" the "white-label" reports on a special url. But it is NOT a whitelabel or "generic" url. Most every "white label" tool I use that provides a shareable link uses a generic rather plain url not associated with the service, so there's that.

If this was a true white label tool with ability to further customize reports, a white label domain to use for posting urls to and/or a white label control panel to send a client to to read their white label reports. the tool would be awesome and rate 10 tacos for sure.

comments.title: A lot to take in, but well organized and easy to use
comments.comment:
I am still finding my way around Labrika, but I think it is very likely to be my #1 go to option for analysis of my site. Things are presented in an easy to navigate menu, and you can stick with the summary view or drill downing into a dizzying level of detail.

A couple of things are giving me trouble though:

1. "Test the availability of your website from locations worldwide" - Shows my site as inaccessible from every option but one. However, I have several audit packages, multiple VPNs in those countries and monitoring set up for several of them and none of those indicate any problems. The pages load fine.

2. My page is broken into subdomains. I have several of them. However, the app indicates that it's only crawling one page, my homepage, despite the pages of the subdomain being indexed by Google, listed in the sitemap and "Also search subdomain" being selected in the settings section.

Overall, except for those two problems, I like pretty much everything about Labrika better than the other apps I use. Hopefully those issues can be resolved and I can change this review to 5 tacos :)

On the flip side, plenty of tools that do get AI pricing "sustainable" end up charging steep monthly fees that price out small entrepreneurs and solopreneurs.

Labrika has found the middle ground that most companies miss: affordable, non-subscription AI credits that still keep the business sustainable on their end. That balance is rare, and it's exactly what independent creators and small business owners need.

Another underrated aspect of Labrika's pricing structure is that limits are tied to the number of pages, not the number of websites. If you're running ten or fifteen smaller sites which is common for people managing multiple niche projects, this structure works heavily in your favour. On the core SEO side, I genuinely haven't found a missing feature yet. Whatever I've needed for optimizing my websites - technical audits, on-page analysis, content optimization, Labrika has covered it.

I haven't tested the full depth of the AI suite yet, but what I have tried so far is promising, particularly for GEO needs and AI-driven audits. For anything outside that scope, I simply lean on other tools already in my stack - no single tool can do everything.

Final Verdict: Labrika has earned a central spot in my toolkit. It combines a flexible, open approach to content optimization with an AI pricing model that's actually sustainable for both the user and the company - something surprisingly few SEO tools manage to get right. If you're comparing lifetime deals and want a tool that won't feel gutted a year from now, and you also need the freedom to optimize content written anywhere, Labrika deserves serious consideration.

comments.title: Excellent Product with some Opportunities for Improvement for Agency Features
comments.comment:
This is a really solid product for QR code campaigns, I'm very happy with the purchase and I'm excited to see how they continue developing the program going forward. It's feature-rich and has a lot to offer. I purchased the enterprise plan so I can use it for my clients and I think it will be a really helpful tool. 

As a consumer tool, I would give this a solid 4.5 stars (the payment processor issue I noted below is the only reason holding it back from 5 stars on the consumer side). As an agency, I gave it 4 tacos for the reasons listed below. I'd love to see these features added that I think will bring a huge amount of value for agencies:

1. White-label dashboards - Allow agencies to brand the dashboard with a custom domain & logo (either the agency's brand or the client's brand). This makes it a lot easier to package the services and set pricing to onboard new clients. As it is now, I can't really sell this as a standalone product without devaluing the product or bundling my services in a package with the software. 
2. Workspace Storage Limitations & Stats / Granular Workspace Analytics - Allow agencies to set limits on the amount of storage that each workspace can use and see how much each workspace is using. This would allow agencies to more accurately estimate costs for storage upgrades, build flexible service plans with expanded storage capabilities, and set rates & client expectations accordingly. Workspace usage analytics would also be nice to allow agencies to see how clients are using the program, which features are being used and how often it's being used so agencies can adjust sales & marketing approach to align with client needs. 
3. Control Over Feature Sets in a Workspace - Allow agencies to choose which features will be included in a workspace. This would let agencies build service plans that have different feature sets. For example - if marketing a QR solution for restaurants, the Pet ID would not be necessary. So the dashboard can be optimized to sell to a particular audience. This would also allow agencies to create custom tiered plans that include different feature sets. Also the ability to turn off irrelevant features in the account as a whole would be nice (I'm a US agency, so the two payment options for Singapore & EU are irrelevant to me and could confuse my clients)
4. Stripe Payment Option (or other mainstream US Payment Processor) - Currently there are two payment features available in ElkQR, but neither of them work for US residents from what I read. Enabling Stripe within the QR code builder tool and the ability to turn off the other payment options (as mentioned in the previous note) would be very helpful. Although QR codes could be built as a basic link to an external payment app, as a US user, there is currently no built-in feature for payments, so I can't market that as a feature for my clients and will undoubtedly get questions about the existing payment options. The Event Promotion feature is amazing, but if it were integrated with Stripe to allow processing payments, that would be top-tier and would replace the need to use eventbrite or website payment processors. 
5. Brand Profiles and Design Templates - Creating the ability to save brand/design preferences to a workspace would be awesome. For example, saving the logo, colors fonts, and QR design templates in the brand profile which would allow a quick starting point when building new QR codes and handing a prepared workspace off to clients. I know you can duplicate a QR code, which is great, but having the design specs saved would make things really clean and easy for management. 
6. BONUS FEATURE: Agency Support Requests - Allow workspace users to send the agency a message or support request. Not really a NEED, but would be nice to have so clients can have a direct line of communication to the agency within the program for any onboarding questions or support requests. This feature would also allow agencies to easily include support as part of their service packages. Ex: Agency includes 1hr/mo of support, client can reach out to request assistance building a QR code or setting up a campaign.

comments.title: Still using it after six months, but the analytics need work
comments.comment:
I've been using SearchIQ for about six months and it remains one of the better AppSumo purchases I've made.
I originally bought it because site search data is one of the clearest signals of visitor intent. I wanted to know what people were searching for, which searches produced no results, and what content visitors were struggling to find. While some of this can be implemented in Google Analytics, it typically requires custom setup and ongoing maintenance.
SearchIQ makes that much easier. Installation is straightforward, the search experience is noticeably better than default WordPress search, and the analytics surface exactly the signals I was looking for.
The biggest benefit for me has been understanding what visitors are actually looking for in their own words. That kind of insight helps identify content gaps and opportunities that would otherwise be easy to miss.
The analytics do have real limitations though. They need longer data retention, better historical reporting, and internal traffic filtering. I flagged the last one to the team six months ago and it has not been implemented yet, which also raises questions about the pace of active development.
Strong value at $39 lifetime. The search experience is already excellent. The analytics just need to catch up. I cover all of this in more detail, including a full feature comparison and six months of hands-on findings, in my complete review at https://marketingwithdave.com/searchiq-review/

comments.title: Solid SEO tool with room to grow
comments.comment:
Nuwtonic is a genuinely impressive platform for anyone serious about staying visible in both traditional Google search and the increasingly important world of AI-generated answers. The fact that it connects directly to Google Search Console and surfaces gaps in AI citations is something I haven't seen done this cleanly in one tool. The idea of replacing Ahrefs, SEMrush, and a GEO monitoring tool with a single workspace is compelling — and Nuwtonic largely delivers on that promise.

The agentic approach is what sets it apart. Rather than just handing you a report, it prioritizes and helps you execute fixes, which saves a ton of time for marketers and agencies juggling multiple clients.

That said, I'm holding back one taco because the data input experience still needs polish. There are a few places where entering or importing your own data feels more manual and friction-heavy than it should be — things like bulk input options or smarter defaults that would make onboarding faster. For a tool that's all about automation, a smoother "get started" flow for user data would go a long way.

Overall, this is a smart buy at the AppSumo price. The core functionality is strong and the direction is exactly right — I just hope the team smooths out the input experience in upcoming updates. Highly recommended for forward-thinking SEOs and agencies.

comments.title: Most SEO tools tell you what's wrong. Nuwtonic is one of the few trying to fix it.
comments.comment:
Most SEO tools tell you what's wrong. Nuwtonic is one of the few trying to fix it.

After spending considerable time testing Nuwtonic for MarketingWithDave.com, what stood out most was the workflow. Rather than handing me another audit to work through, Nuwtonic focuses on detecting problems, prioritizing them, applying fixes, and then verifying whether those changes actually helped.

The page-level optimization is where the platform earns its reputation. I ran it against an article on Philip Kotler's eight demand states and got specific, actionable recommendations instead of "add more keywords." Some fixes route to me for review, others push straight to WordPress, and you can verify afterward whether they actually worked.

The GEO Content Writer surprised me too, producing noticeably stronger output than most AI writing tools I've tested on a subject I know well. It didn't understand my proprietary frameworks and occasionally invented first-person experiences I had to catch, but it needed far less editing than expected.

Tier 1's biggest limitation is the 15 tracked SERP keywords. That's enough to evaluate the platform, but it becomes restrictive if you intend to use Nuwtonic as your primary rank-tracking solution. The platform also relies heavily on proprietary scores that aren't always explained, and while many recommendations are excellent, others still fall back on advice that feels too generic.

If you're already familiar with your website and know which pages deserve attention, Nuwtonic's philosophy makes a lot of sense. Rather than crawling every corner of your site, it helps you improve the pages that actually matter. Combined with automated fixes, that makes it one of the more forward-thinking SEO platforms currently available on AppSumo.

comments.title: It showed me who AI recommends instead of me, then helped me to mitigate the gap
comments.comment:
For years my competitor research meant one thing: who outranks me on Google. Nuwtonic made me realize that’s only half the fight now. When I ran my first round of prompt tracking on the questions my customers actually ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini, my brand was missing from many of the answers. A couple of competitors I’d never considered a serious threat were getting cited again and again. That was a wake-up call.

The part that won me over is that Nuwtonic doesn’t stop at “you’re not visible.” It digs into why. The Citation Gaps fix targets the prompts where my brand isn’t being cited, and the GEO audit looked at my pages the way an AI engine would, pointing out things I’d never thought about: thin factual claims, no clear direct answers, weak trust signals, content that just wasn’t quotable. Meanwhile, the competitor gap view showed me the topics and keywords those rival sites were covering, and which of their pages AI engines were pulling from. Put those two side by side and the strategy writes itself.

What I didn’t expect was how fast the wins came. Instead of a huge list of reports, it pointed me to pages that were already close: posts losing clicks over time, pages missing schema or a proper FAQ block, answers that only needed tightening to become citation-ready, and competitor gaps with missing topics. I worked through those with the agents, reviewed every change before it went live, and cleared most of the list for quite a few pages.

From there, the content side felt like a natural next step rather than a separate tool. The keyword research and clustering lean toward the conversational, question-style queries people type into AI assistants, and the topical map shows exactly where my coverage has holes compared to competitors. The GEO writer then produces articles structured to be quoted: clear answers up front, solid facts, lists, tables, and both external and internal links. I’ve also been refreshing older posts with it, which is giving content I’d written off a second chance.

It’s not a lightweight tool. There’s a lot inside, and it took me a while to explore all of it and settle into the workflow. But every section connects to the next, which is exactly what my old stack of separate rank trackers, AI visibility checkers and writing tools never did.

If you’ve started wondering why AI search recommends your competitors and not you, Nuwtonic is the first tool I’ve used that answers that question and then helps you fix it. 5 stars.

comments.title: The SEO + GEO Tool That Finally Ended My Search

I've tested a lot of SEO tools over the years and quite a few GEO tools recently, and most fell short somewhere. Even the best of them was "good enough" at most. Nuwtonic is the first that does everything I need, plus a few things I didn't know I was missing until I used them.

I'll skip the feature tour, since the listing covers that. Here's what actually changed how I work.

The first thing I noticed was the support. Every question I sent got a fast, complete answer, not a canned reply. That kind of responsiveness is rare.

Then came ai visibility, which is where it clicked for me. Most GEO tools show you whether you're being cited. Nuwtonic lets you tell it which exact URL should be cited for a prompt, then shows you the gap. Once you can see the gap, fixing it is no longer guesswork. Add generous prompt limits and a visibility dashboard you can actually act on, and AI search finally feels manageable.

The workflow is built around doing, not reading. Both SEO and GEO follow the same loop: audit, analyse, and then go deeper with Advanced Optimization. It works on one URL or a batch. The SEO dashboard surfaces quick wins I can ship the same day instead of burying me in reports.

Auto-Traffic Campaigns are my favorite feature. Nuwtonic reads your data and builds goal-based campaigns like "Get More Clicks," "Improve Rankings," and "Fix Underperforming Pages," and it picks the eligible pages for you. You choose a goal, run the fix, and watch it move. I didn't know I needed this, and now I can't picture working without it.

Competitor analysis goes past "here's what they rank for." Each competitor comes with an opportunity gap and a plan, and you can carry out that plan inside the platform. The topical map does the same for content: you see the clusters, click a keyword, and start writing.

The content creator produces solid, GEO-ready articles with images and internal links built in. Brand analysis and presets keep the output sounding like you. The schema, FAQ, meta, and alt-text agents are quiet workhorses that save small chunks of time every day.

There are a few things I'd change. First, the content creator only accepts one keyword. Let me add secondary keywords and entities so articles can go deeper. If I could group keywords myself and build content from those groups, it would be another real win.

Bottom line: I came looking for a better tool and found one that does the work of several. SEO, GEO, content, and competitor analysis all live in one place now. It has a few rough edges, but this is version one, and it already outperforms everything else I've tried. Highly recommended.

Nuwtonic caught my attention because it is not focusing only on traditional Google SEO. It is trying to bring SEO and GEO/AI search optimisation together in one platform.
I particularly like the direction they are taking with AI visibility tracking, competitor gap analysis, topical maps, content optimization, AI citations, and identifying opportunities where an existing page can be improved instead of simply suggesting that you create more content.
Another major advantage for me is cost-effectiveness. Tools like Semrush and Ahrefs are excellent and well-established, but their recurring subscription costs can become quite expensive, especially for smaller businesses, independent SEO professionals, and growing agencies. Nuwtonic provides a wide range of useful SEO and newer GEO/AI-search features at a much more accessible cost.
Of course, I would not say that Nuwtonic currently replaces every feature of mature platforms like Ahrefs. However, considering the price and the combination of traditional SEO with emerging AI-search optimization features, I think it offers very good value for money.
Another thing I appreciate is that Nuwtonic is moving beyond just showing data. Most SEO tools can give you hundreds of reports and recommendations, but ultimately you still have to figure out what to do next. Nuwtonic is clearly trying to bridge that gap between analysis and execution.
As an SEO specialist who has used many tools over the years, I believe AI search visibility is going to become an increasingly important part of SEO. We still need traditional SEO, but we also need to understand how our brands and content appear across AI-powered search and answer platforms. Nuwtonic appears to understand this shift quite well.
The platform is developing quickly, so naturally there are areas where the UI and workflows can become more polished and easier to understand. With so many features, there is also a learning curve in the beginning. But I would rather see a young SEO product continuously improving and adding meaningful capabilities than another tool offering the same features we already have elsewhere.
I also appreciate that the team appears to be actively listening to users and regularly improving the product.
Overall, I see Nuwtonic as a promising and cost-effective option for SEO professionals, agencies, and business owners who want to prepare not only for traditional search but also for the growing AI-search ecosystem.

I've spent a fair amount of time testing different SEO and GEO tools, and Nuwtonic has been one of the more interesting ones I've come across.

What I appreciate most is that it doesn't feel like a collection of unrelated features. The different parts of the platform actually connect with each other.

For example, I can look at my SEO data, identify pages that are underperforming, investigate competitor gaps, look at AI-search visibility and citations, and then move into content or page optimization. The GEO functionality is probably my favorite part.

Traditional SEO tools are excellent for understanding Google rankings, keywords, backlinks and technical issues, but AI search introduces a completely different layer. A page can rank reasonably well on Google but still have very little visibility in AI-generated answers.

Nuwtonic helps with that by tracking prompts and AI visibility and showing where competitors are being mentioned or cited when your brand isn't. The citation gap analysis is particularly useful because it turns something that can otherwise feel very difficult to measure into something you can actually work on.

The SEO side is strong as well. The Google Search Console integration, SEO audits, content opportunities, topical maps, internal linking recommendations and optimization workflows make it useful beyond just GEO.

I've also compared the overall workflow with tools such as Ahrefs, Semrush and some of the newer GEO-focused platforms. Ahrefs and Semrush are still excellent when you need extremely deep keyword, backlink and competitive research. GEO-specific tools can also go deeper into certain AI visibility metrics. Where Nuwtonic stands out is the combination of both worlds and the fact that it tries to take you from analysis to execution.

Another thing I like is that the platform doesn't simply tell you "there's a problem." It often gives you a direction for what to fix or optimize, which saves a lot of time.

There are still areas I'd like to see improved. Some sections take a little time to understand, and I think the interface could become even simpler as the platform matures. But considering how quickly the SEO and AI-search landscape is changing, I'm impressed with how much functionality Nuwtonic is bringing together.

For anyone managing SEO, content or AI-search visibility, I would definitely recommend giving Nuwtonic a serious look. It's much more useful to me as an execution platform than a simple SEO reporting tool.

comments.title: Modern, fast and simply cool web analytics
comments.comment:
LitLyx is a very easy to install analytics solution from Italy. We were surprised how quickly and smoothly everything ran with a test domain. The graphical user interface is modern and almost self-explanatory. The support, also via Discord, is excellent and within a few hours (less than 3!) we had a meaningful answer. That is not a matter of course!
What initially bothered us a little was the information that only one domain is recommended per project for understandable reasons of data mixing, which confused us, but a filter should help, even if it makes sense to have one domain per project.
Even if we have by no means exhausted all the functions and possibilities, we see LitLyx as a truly good and state-of-the-art analytics alternative to other plattforms out there. LitLyx could also be installed as a self-hosted solution. We like it, but it doesn't have to be.
For us as a company, data protection is always important. The privacy policy and data policy could be a bit more comprehensive for business use, but the fact that LitLyx offers a DPA per se and without asking shows that they take GDPR seriously. For us 5 tacos and give it a try.

comments.title: Underrated
comments.comment:
This gem has been a pearl in the crown of my one man agency. So glad I invested when I did. Sure, there were a couple of kinks at the time I invested, but none of them show stoppers IMO, and almost all have been ironed out over the past year. Also the customer support team is so prompt, responsive and kind. Shouts out to Oliwia. I seriously don't understand how this isn't a 4.9 star - and I suspect if they launched here today, they'd surely be there.

To be completely clear - the MCP for me - is by far the biggest value driver. It's been an invaluable investment for me, to automate GBP review management, alert scheduling, as well as local rank performance tracking. 

I dont believe in automated AI replies for GBP reviews. LRT's MCP allows me to set up a daily workflow, where I manually review, and update all new GBP replies for all my client's GBP profiles via a Google sheet. I can tinker with the reply wording, approve, and Claude just pushes out all of the replies in one fell swoop. No more clicking into 20 different client GBP profiles.

On the GBP posting side - if you hypothetically generated 12 months worth of weekly posts for a client, you can schedule them all in one click. Uploading and scheduling that many alerts ALONE would take maybe a whole day to do manually inside of a GBP.

On the reporting side - once you've set up a client's project, you can configure a bunch of local search keywords to track on an ongoing basis. From there, you can basically consolidate local performance data alongside other web analytics in an automated monthly report. Or like, integrate it all into client dashboards. Choose your destiny.

I.e. For me, on the 15th of each month, all of my client website performance reports are automatically generated. Local search data from LRT gets pulled, analysed, and consolidated inside a report [alongside MCP gathered website analytics (Rybbit, GA4) and general SEO (from Ubersuggest's MCP)] - FOR ALL MY CLIENTS.

If you're a one person agency like me doing local SEO work, this is seriously a no brainer.

comments.title: Clean and Functional, With Room to Differentiate
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I’m a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Seline is a simple, privacy-first analytics tool with an AI chat you can ask questions in plain English, and it did what it promised: setup was quick, the core reports worked, and I could get useful answers within my first session.

On first test, we found a few small issues: a sticky date header overlapping visitor journeys, and an AI-generated funnel that added steps we didn't want. The team clarified that funnels can be edited after creation, and they're deliberately keeping the interface minimal, so there's no built-in UTM builder, and Shopify currently works through their setup guide rather than a native app.

If you want a lighter alternative to Google Analytics for a small site or team, it's well worth a try.

comments.title: Great Analytics Tool, Excellent Support, and a Killer Proxy Feature( Updated Review)

Updated Review:

Updating my review after getting the license issue sorted out. The AppSumo license activation process was a little confusing at first, but Kostya was incredibly quick to respond and resolve the issue.

The app itself is fantastic and I have been an eyeing it for quite some time! The standout for me is the proxy feature because that's the feature I only need in those analytics app, something surprisingly few analytics tools offer. With so many browsers and ad blockers blocking analytics scripts these days, being able to use your own domain is a huge plus.

Great product, beautiful design and execution and analytics. Don't miss it.

comments.title: Simple, useful, and actually gets used
comments.comment:
Seline is one of those tools that looks simple at first, but becomes more valuable once real data starts coming in.
Setup was quick, the interface is clean, and it makes it very easy to understand where visitors come from, which pages they view, and whether they actually reach the goals I care about.
The funnel feature is especially useful. I can define a conversion path in minutes and immediately start seeing what percentage of visitors complete it. Traffic sources, visitor journeys, page performance, and conversions are presented without the complexity of heavier analytics platforms.
I also like that the product stays focused. It gives me the information I need without turning analytics into another full-time job.
Two things I would love to see improved:
1. Deeper AI/referrer attribution, especially for traffic coming from ChatGPT and other AI assistants, so AI traffic can be separated and analyzed more precisely.
2. More automated insights and anomaly detection, for example notifying me when a page suddenly converts better/worse or when a new traffic source starts producing meaningful conversions.
Overall, Seline has earned a permanent place in my workflow because it is fast, understandable, and genuinely useful rather than simply having a long feature list.

comments.title: Modern, generous and built for client growth. Loving Seline!
comments.comment: As a founder I need website analytics that make sense without spending hours digging through reports, and that’s what I loved when switching to Seline. I wasn't sure what to expect but the interface is clean, easy to navigate, and a much more approachable Google Analytics alternative for me. Having real-time analytics, visitor journeys, conversion funnels, and revenue attribution together gives it depth beyond basic traffic numbers. And regarding the deal? The generous monthly limits are a big plus, especially since we can link multiple websites to the included project and share the allowance across domains. I also love that we can put a separate client project on an affordable monthly subscription outside AppSumo, which makes this deal more practical for a growing agency. It’s the combination of simplicity, useful features, and flexible pricing that makes Seline stand out for me. 5 Tacos with extra toppings! Amazing job Kostya and team. Absolutely beautiful.

comments.title: Love it - but the built in domains are useless.
comments.comment:
Almost 5 tacos, not quite! But a solid 4 and superb value...

Provided you have a spare domain or don't mind picking one up this is a fantastic link shortner that has some excellent filtering.

Is it as detailed and complex as something like ClickMagik? No - but for the one time price the feature set is superb.

I got the Tier-2 and have added three of my own custom domains and verified them (clear simple instructions are given so even a non-techie should be able to follow it).

I can't give it 5 tacos because of the issue with the built in domains (one gives a warning and the other is starting to get flagged by some security software), but that was inevitable. It only takes one idiot customer to use it to forward to a site with phishing or malware on it and the whole domain gets blacklisted.

comments.title: Gutes Social-Media-Tool mit Potenzial – die Benutzeroberfläche könnte moderner sein
comments.comment:
Insgesamt macht das Tool genau das, was es soll. Es bietet die wichtigsten Funktionen, um Social-Media-Beiträge zentral zu planen und zu veröffentlichen. Mein erster Eindruck ist positiv, auch wenn ich bei der Benutzerfreundlichkeit noch Verbesserungspotenzial sehe.

Was mir besonders gut gefällt:
Die Verbindung der Social-Media-Accounts hat wirklich hervorragend funktioniert. Die Einrichtung war unkompliziert, schnell und intuitiv. Das ist definitiv ein Pluspunkt.
Auch die eigentliche Content-Planung wirkt auf den ersten Blick übersichtlich und relativ einfach. Ich bin gerade dabei, meine Beiträge für verschiedene Plattformen einzuplanen, und bisher funktioniert das zuverlässig.

Was aus meiner Sicht verbessert werden könnte:
Mein größter Kritikpunkt ist die Benutzeroberfläche (UI/UX). Im Vergleich zu anderen Social-Media-Management-Tools wirkt das Design etwas veraltet und könnte insgesamt moderner, hochwertiger und intuitiver gestaltet sein.

Besonders drei Dinge würden meinen Workflow deutlich verbessern:
1. Live-Vorschau direkt neben dem Editor: Ich würde gerne meinen Beitrag auf der einen Seite bearbeiten und auf der anderen Seite unmittelbar sehen, wie er auf der jeweiligen Plattform aussehen wird. Das würde die Content-Erstellung wesentlich angenehmer machen.

2. Ein einheitlicher Content-Editor: Aktuell muss ich vorab auswählen, ob ich einen Text- oder Bildbeitrag erstellen möchte. Viel intuitiver wäre es, einfach einen Beitrag zu schreiben und bei Bedarf ein Bild hinzuzufügen. Das Tool sollte automatisch erkennen, um welchen Beitragstyp es sich handelt, ohne dass ich vorher eine Auswahl treffen muss.

3. Weniger Klicks und ein flüssigerer Workflow: Gerade wenn man regelmäßig mehrere Beiträge für unterschiedliche Plattformen plant, machen kleine Verbesserungen in der Bedienung einen großen Unterschied. Ein durchgängiger Editor mit weniger manuellen Schritten würde hier einiges an Zeit sparen.

Mein Fazit:
Die grundlegenden Funktionen sind vorhanden und funktionieren bisher gut. Besonders die einfache Account-Verbindung hat mich überzeugt.
Die größten Verbesserungsmöglichkeiten sehe ich eindeutig im UI/UX-Design und im Workflow bei der Beitragserstellung.

Mit einer moderneren Oberfläche, einer direkten Live-Vorschau und einem flexibleren Content-Editor könnte das Tool noch deutlich besser werden.

Für mich aktuell solide 4 von 5 Sternen. Ich bin gespannt, wie sich das Produkt weiterentwickelt.

comments.title: AdaptlyPost 1st Personal-Check
comments.comment:
AdaptlyPost im persönlichen Ersteindruck: ein Kalender für viele Netze, mit einigen kleinen Haken

AdaptlyPost ist ein Planer für Social-Media-Beiträge. 
Man schreibt einen Post, passt ihn pro Netz an und lässt ihn später raus. 
Dazu gibt es KI für Texte und Bilder und eine Schnittstelle für KI-Agenten. 
Für Solo-Leute und kleine Teams brauchbar. Kein fertiges Agentur-System und kein Bildprogramm.
Die Website nennt 11 Netze, darunter Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon und Telegram. Das Produkt ist jung, gegründet 2026, das Team sitzt in Gdańsk.

Was es löst 

Statt sich in jedes Netz einzeln einzuloggen, legt man den Beitrag einmal an. 
Der Kalender zeigt Entwurf, Geplant und Veröffentlicht. Die KI schreibt Bildunterschriften, Hashtags und kann ein Bild aus einem Satz bauen. Sinnvoll für die Woche im Voraus. 
Wer nur einen Kanal bespielt, braucht das wahrscheinlich nicht.

Was gut funktioniert

Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon und Telegram sind dabei, nicht nur die großen Netze. 
Dieselben Funktionen gibt es in jeder Preisstufe. Man kauft mehr Konten, Plätze und Credits, nicht erst die Bild-KI. Über einen API-Schlüssel kann man Claude oder Cursor anbinden. Der Agent legt Beiträge in den Kalender. Vor dem Senden sollte man selbst noch einmal prüfen. 

Taras und das Team antworten bisher schnell. Das ist in meinen Augen ein klares Plus.

Wo Verbesserungsbedarf ist

Instagram und Facebook hätten sich bei mir nur mit Creator-Konten verbunden. 
TikTok ging schnell. Oft hilft ein Refresh der Verbindung.
Jeder Post auf X verbraucht KI-Credits. Theoretisch 2 pro Beitrag. Die genaue Zahl steht nicht fest auf der Deal-Seite, also im eigenen Konto prüfen.
Für Text auf dem Bild oder einen sauberen Schnitt ist man meiner Ansicht nach weiter bei externen Programmen richtig. Die Analytik ist da, aber noch ausbaufähig, vor allem bei den neueren Netzen.

Was es kostet

Stand 4. Oktober 2026, adaptlypost.com, sieben Tage testen. 
Geplante Posts sind unbegrenzt. Credits braucht man für KI und für X.

•	Creator, 19 $ im Monat: 30 Konten, 1 Arbeitsbereich, 150 KI-Credits
•	Pro, 39 $: 60 Konten, 3 Personen, 3 Arbeitsbereiche, 400 Credits
•	Enterprise, 89 $: 100 Konten, 10 Personen, 10 Arbeitsbereiche, 1.000 Credits

Auf AppSumo aktuell: 59 $ (statt 190 $), 499 $ und 799 $. Fünf Stufen, 60 Tage Geld zurück. 
Höher stufen, solange der Deal läuft, runter nur in den ersten 60 Tagen. Stufe 4 und 5 laut Update vom 18. September 2026: 250 Konten und 3.000 Credits, bzw. 500 Konten und 5.000 Credits. 
Vor dem Kauf empfiehlt es sich den Plan-Wähler öffnen.

19 $ für 30 Konten ist günstig im Vergleich zu Buffer oder Later.

•	Preis-Leistung: 4,5 von 5
•	Gesamt: 4,2 von 5

🟢 Vorteile
- Viele Netze in einem Kalender
- KI für Text und Bild, plus API und MCP

🔴 Nachteile

comments.title: Finally a scheduler that works with AI agents, not just with humans
comments.comment:
I run content for a small education centre and publish the same story across a LinkedIn page, two personal LinkedIn profiles, Facebook, Instagram and Google Business Profile. Over the past year I tried several schedulers, before settling on SocialBu.

The reason I stayed is the MCP server. My AI assistant prepares the texts, first comments, ALT descriptions and UTM links, and then creates the drafts directly in SocialBu, one per channel, with the exact schedule time. I review, attach the image, approve. Nothing gets published without me, and I no longer copy-paste anything. Of all the tools I tested, SocialBu's MCP is the one that actually covers the real workflow: create, update, list, schedule, GBP call-to-action, metrics.

One more thing I did not expect from a scheduler: Curate and Listen are also exposed through the same MCP. My assistant can pull curated articles for our topics and read the listening streams (mentions, keywords, competitors) in the same session in which it drafts the posts, so the "what should we react to this week" step no longer means opening three tabs. It is early days for me with these two modules, but having them reachable by the agent, not only through the UI, is exactly the direction I hope the rest of the tool keeps taking.

What I would like to see next: attaching an image directly through MCP (today it needs a public URL or base64), creating a whole set of posts in one call instead of one post per call, and a configurable delay for the first comment so it does not land in the same second as the post. Also, ALT text set through the API is lost if the post is later re-saved in the UI.

Solid tool, responsive team, and the only one I found that treats an AI agent as a first-class user. Recommended.

comments.title: Much more useful than I expected, but there’s a learning curve
comments.comment:
I bought Tier 1 expecting a dashboard of which AI bots were hitting my site. What I actually got was visibility into things I'd never seen before: whether Googlebot has found an article I just published, traffic HoneyLog identifies as Fake Human despite normal-looking browser user agents, and a world of 404s I rarely see in GA4.

The report builder is the standout feature. Instead of "Googlebot visited 9 times," I can ask which URLs, which status codes, and how long each request took. That's saved me from a couple of wrong conclusions already, including one case where 12 requests to an article turned out to all be Fake Human once I filtered by bot.

Two honest gripes. Onboarding is rough: I hit an unclear "waiting for aggregation" message with no sense of how long to expect, and ended up contacting support. HoneyLog is also much better at showing you what happened than telling you what to do about it. If you're comfortable digging into the data, that's fine. If you want a tool that hands you the next steps, it's not there yet.

I'm keeping Tier 1. It's already surfacing insights I'm not getting anywhere else in my stack, and the 60-day return window gives you time to let HoneyLog prove its value on your own site before deciding.

Full hands-on review with screenshots and examples:
MarketingWithDave.com HoneyLog Review

comments.title: Much More Than an AI Bot Tracker
comments.comment:
I originally bought Honeylog to see AI crawlers and bots that normal analytics and WordPress can miss. After using it on real traffic, I realized it is much more useful than that.
The strongest part for me is the evidence. I can see verified crawlers, fake bots, suspicious “human” traffic, the exact URLs being crawled, sitemap coverage, status codes and bot behavior without relying on JavaScript analytics.
The report and raw-log tools are especially useful because they help separate real crawler activity from misleading traffic. Bot Conversions is also a very interesting direction because it starts connecting crawling activity with actual human visits.
Honeylog has become one of the tools I trust when I need to understand what is really happening on a website rather than what a normal analytics dashboard assumes is happening.
Two things I would love to see next:
1. More actionable insights — not only showing what happened, but suggesting the likely cause and the next thing to check.
2. Stronger custom views / actor classification so monitoring services, owned bots, SEO crawlers and suspicious traffic can be separated very easily.
The product has real depth and the support has been responsive. I’m very happy I kept it.

It felt like I’d been sleeping in a bed of snakes: warm, gross, and honestly terrifying once you see who’s actually visiting your site. Bots, fake users, and spammy IPs were all there!  

This made me realize I need to fix this problem ASAP.  

By the way, the setup was easier than I expected (still took a lot to wrap the concept around the head and then implement it at first but now I know what to expect going forward), and this was the first time I moved my namserver to Cloudflare.

To sum it up, HoneyLogs not only shows me which bots are visiting but also gives me a way to tackle that big question every SEO and GEO expert wonders about: how can I optimize my site’s visibility? Highly recommended, and thank you Lorenzo for all you help!

comments.title: One Year Review

After testing this software over a period of time (purchased April 2022), I am finally leaving a review. 

Here are my observations in chronological order: 

1. At first, I was very excited about the UI.  It seemed to work as advertised and continues to do so far.  

2. The download to my Windows OS was not preferable, as I change devices based on my portable needs.  However, it was a great alternative to monthly subscriptions, so it was a concession I was willing to make. 

3. The time to full implementation took me about 10 days (30-45 minute sessions).  I am not a developer, so I tend to read all the details before engaging if I am taking on new software ventures myself.  

4. My audience has sensitive needs, and I wanted to ensure my site would not be penalized.  It has not been so far. 

5. The repin and scheduling features were my main needs.  I don't mind spending a few hours/days setting it up if automation needed only minor tweaking (less than 1 hour per week) was needed to keep it going. 

6.  The unadvertised and unexpected bonus is that I was able to conduct some research to target posts.  I launched another initiative that gained immediate traction based on my findings (targeting, key phrases, etc); so for that alone, it was worth the investment. I like data science for my breakfast cereal, so this was very good for such a product. 

Overall, I wish it was available without putting my computer and social account at risk, but it is only for one brand account. I don't use it much as I could, simply because I manage most of my social accounts on the go by a portable device not suited for this download. 

If I were managing more than one brand using this software, I would look at different alternatives.  

5 tacos because it works as advertised and the developers continue to improve.

comments.title: A great deal - don't miss out.
comments.comment:
I have a digital learning product that I've been slowly building and promoting over the last couple of years. The only way I've been driving traffic is with a bit of Facebook and Google advertising alongside building an organic search and social following. Without a big budget to hand this has all been slow and steady, which is fine by me, as this is a side project I don't have loads of time for.

Even though I'm pretty sure influencer marketing would work well with my product, I really wouldn't know how to get started. So when Intellifluence came up on here, I thought I'd give it a go.

My first project was up and running within about 15 minutes - and within 30 minutes I had made contact with an interested reviewer. After a couple of messages I had my first person on board. I think what makes this such a great platform for me is that because my product is digital, but of quite high value, it's appealing to many influencers, but effectively free for me to give away.

There seems to be two parts to getting influencers - finding a good fit using the platform and inviting them to talk about your product, and Intellifluence sharing your product with it's users and them asking for an invite.

I may have got my categories wrong because I think the people the platform pitched to initially weren't quite right - and I think only one of those has accepted the pitch. Once I'd changed things a little I had more success with both manually pitching and also getting interest from users.

When it comes to finding influencers you can search across loads of different metrics like gender, country and total reach, as well as by keyword. One thing that I checked that's a little concerning is 'Last Login' - which allows you to see, I assume, when someone was last logged in. When I set this to '7 days' it came up with just over 1000 hits. I'm not 100% sure what counts as a log in, so I won't draw too many conclusions from this.

Any platform like this is going to have variability in the quality of the users, and that's definitely been my experience. I think some people are really just on there to collect as much free stuff as they can. Some of the websites that people had were really poor quality, as were some of the social profiles I came across. These may be real people - but I think their value to brands might be pretty limited.

But now on to the positive. There definitely are plenty of real, passionate users here. From my initial campaign I've got 3 active reviewers, with several more interested, but not yet signed up. I've not received any reviews yet - but I don't want to have had any yet - I want a real opinion on my product.

And this is something I wouldn't know how to start doing myself. I wouldn't be able to get in front of these people without Intellifluence. Plus Intellifluence does the management of the pitches for me, so I don't have 100 emails to look through.

Will I subscribe in a year's time? I don't know. But I will use it a lot before then.

While most platforms require signing in or creating an account, LoveBoard makes it easy and seamless to give a testimonial for your brand. No complexities and zero friction!

Video reviews is where LoveBoard takes the crown. The in-browser collection makes it easy for clients. No app or sign-in needed. Why does this matter? Studies show that video reviews are up to 27 times more engaging than text testimonials, 9.5 times better for information retention, and 1.9 times more effective at driving sales conversion!

On the platform, I love that LoveBoard is easy to learn and use with no learning curve. The UI/UX is neat and organized, including the analytics. I embedded it on two of our websites via iFrame. I tested the mason, grid, carousel, and badge embeds, and we had no issues at all.

- Smoother carousel animation
- Auto-approve reviews on/off toggle
- CNAME (sumoling favorite)
- Color options to match our website
- Pop-up widget embed type
- Import reviews from sources (CSV or URL)

The limits on this LTD are very generous, even on the lower tiers. Given its value, potential, and responsive support, I plan to upgrade to a higher tier soon!

comments.title: Promising, but held back by registration limitation and poor localisation
comments.comment:
I had high hopes for BeHuman.Online (BHO) as a viable alternative to Zoom Webinar. The platform generally looks great, but unfortunately, I came across a few limitations that means I will be requesting a refund after writing this review.

The key limitations for me are around the following areas:
1. Registration:
I need a system where attendees can simply register with an email address, double opt-in to confirm a valid emai address, and they receive their unique join link (for future attendance reporting) - that's it, as simple as this!

However, BHO currently mandates that Google Login, Email, and SMS options are ALL visible options. The biggest concern I have is that all of these methods requires the guest to create a dedicated BHO account. I do not want to force my webinar guests to sign up for a third-party platform just to attend my webinar. Additionally,
(a) My attendees are generally business that use O365. I don't want someone see the Google option and to feel using their personal GMail account is an option for them and something we'd request.
(b) I don't want SMS even listed as an option as collecting phone numbers feels unnecessarily invasive (for my needs at least) - it's either none ('anonymous') or all three options visible.

Our Website Privacy Statement likely doesn't allow for capturing (a) and/or (b) above.

When I reached out to support about the registration issue, they initially suggested using their "anonymous" and "form" features. I don't feel this option capturing registrations, but instead designed to allow guests to click the link on the day. This does not work for my webinars where I need to track attendee numbers before the event - potentially cancelling the event if numbers aren't there. When I clarified and pointed this out, support referred me back to using their standard registration feature. When I replied again, advising their standard registration doesn't work for me per the reasons stated in my original support request, asked how I can simply do email address/double opt-in/unique link - it's now over one week and I haven't heard back.

2. Localisation: I don't believe BHO currently caters well to a global audience. The registration page locks you into a US date format (as far as I could tell). Additionally, the SMS field always defaults to a US country code rather than auto-detecting the guest's location via IP address. I know of many online apps seamlessly default to a user's local country code, so I believe BHO creates a clunky experience for international guests.

It is a shame, as the interface looks promising, but these basic functional gaps and the lack of final support resolution has stopped me from fully evaluating or adopting BeHuman.Online.

EDIT (after reply from founder): 
Fantastic news! It is a real testament to the hard work you put into your business. Not only taking feedback seriously but prompt development for a resolution (I hope double opt-in option is there too to help reduce any potential spam entries). 

The last feedback, if I may, is I wish someone had just provided me a status update. I (now) completely understand the priority was fix and make a customer happy, but after a week of silence, as far I was concerned, my request was too difficult so I took the path of least resistance. Kudos to you and your team for the outcome - upping from 3 to 4 tacos. I will consider re-purchasing.

It is not hands-off. You will still review and tweak outputs, but that is also what keeps quality up.

Top 3 Pros:
1. Fast pin creation at scale. Generate batches and move much quicker than doing everything manually.
2. Template flexibility. Once you find a design that works, it is easy to duplicate and iterate.
3. Useful insights. Keyword research, trends, and the profile audit help guide what to create and improve.

Watch Outs:
1. Set realistic expectations on automation. You still need to review and select what to publish.
2. Some workflow friction. A few settings and steps could be smoother.
3. Pinterest limitations. API restrictions impact things like categories and posting control.

If Pinterest is part of your strategy, this is at least worth giving it a test drive. Just go in with the right expectations.

I provided a more detailed review here:
https://marketingwithdave.com/pin-generator-review/

Ollie, I couldn't find a way to reply to your comment so I am adding my response here.
Thank you for the reply. I really like the product and would love to keep providing feedback. Here are a few areas that I think would have the biggest impact:

1. Automation improvements
I mentioned to Candice the idea of automatically adding alt text to pins that are missing it. That feels like low-hanging fruit most users would enable without needing review.
More broadly, it would be great if automations had controls at the board or section level, with the ability to run batch updates (alt text, titles, links, etc.). A wizard-style flow with an “apply to all” option would make this very efficient.

2. URL management and reuse
During setup, selecting URLs works fine at first, but it quickly becomes difficult to track what’s already been used across a larger website.
It would help to have a persistent URL library that shows:
Which URLs have pins created
Ability to search and filter
Ability to select the next batch
Optional notes or status
This could become more of a control center for ongoing use.

3. Queue visibility
I created ~20 pins and selected about five to refine and publish. I used “add to queue,” but I haven’t been able to find this queue.
If there is a queue, it’s not obvious. If not, having a clearly visible saved/queued area would help a lot.

4. Access to previous batches
The only way I’ve found to revisit past images is through “view recent batches” in Automation, which is easy to miss.
A more visible library view of all generated or imported images, with the ability to organize (keep, delete, group), would improve the workflow. Folders or tagging could help here.

5. Image sourcing workflow
Providing a URL to pull images from can feel slow and inconsistent, especially with sources like Amazon.
It would be helpful to have a more direct way to select images, possibly via a browser extension, that could also pull in title, description, alt text, and my affiliate link in one step.

- resizing the elements is unintuitive and hard;
- one can argue that I could use the SVG file import from Canva; well, for that, you need to have a paid version of Canva and you still need to manipulate the text fields after the import;

Pinterest Scheduler for Autopins:

I have fed back a few functional points to the Founder that would make a good tool even better. For example, making a few more choices from the Chrome extension before pins are generated, like choosing the brand template and quantity to generate. Also, it would be great if we could sort drafts better and manually adjust our schedule, not just rely on automation.  

A few purchasers have commented on the credits. I fell for this initially, not realising that every AI click and download also used a credit. This is a user error; it is clearly stated, so do read the info carefully before you pump out a load of pins, and don't be overzealous at the start! Wait until you have multiple pins ready before setting your schedule, or you'll get too many of the same pumping out in one go. 

You can save designs and return to schedule them later in another month so you're not immediately using all your credits, and use your own external AI tools for titles and captions to save on a few more credits.   

Overall, it is a great innovative product that now firmly sits in my suite of tools I will use daily for running my blogging business.

I would like to congratulate you on your product. I purchased Tier 2, and so far, I’m quite pleased with what I see. The interface is very well designed, clean, intuitive, and it offers a wide variety of filters that make querying a smooth experience.

That said, I must mention an important aspect where I believe there is room for substantial improvement: the MCP server performance. While the endpoints themselves are numerous and well-constructed, I’ve encountered persistent issues related to the stability and speed of data delivery through the MCP. The errors coming from this server—connection timeouts, unexpected limits, and odd messages such as “Search capacity temporarily exhausted. Retry in 108585212 seconds”, indicate there is something off in terms of how requests are managed or processed.

My Hermes agent tries to limit and pace queries carefully, so it seems the throttling or resource management at the MCP level needs better calibration. Whether it’s a matter of request limits being too strict or something deeper affecting server integrity, this is the one area that affects the overall experience and should be addressed for smoother, more reliable operations.

Despite this, I want to emphasize that the platform itself is very good. The range of filters and functionality provided so far have met my needs well, and for now, I am happy to give a 5-star rating with the caveat that the MCP performance issue is a critical point to monitor. If improvements are made to stabilize and enhance MCP, I would have no hesitation in maintaining or even increasing my confidence in the product. Conversely, if this continues to cause problems, I might need to reconsider my rating over time.
