comments.title: Makes editing audio and video files fun!
comments.comment:
I'm really enjoying this platform. I'm mainly using Trebble to record brief audio lessons and audio files.  The resulting transcript is 100% accurate and editing is fun and for the most part intuitive.

After recording or uploading my audio...I moved onto editing the generated transcript.  Deleting inaccurate words and copy/pasting text from here to there (if needed) is very easy and on point.  I found the rendering time to produce the final audio download perfectly acceptable - in my experience, a 5-minute audio with edits takes about 3 - 5 minutes to render. 

I also tried uploading a 10 minute MP4 video with audio and this is similarly quick - and again the resulting transcript was very accurate. After editing the transcript, you can play back your edits but this does take a while to process - maybe 2 to 3 minutes.  I hope the dev can speed this up.

I also used the *magic* audio enhancement feature to clean up any background noise and smooth out my voice - it's very effective. I like the enhancement.  That said, I would still like perhaps three short sample audio file snippets (for my review) so I can pick which Magic AI enhancement sound level I prefer before committing to the final rendering process.

I'm hoping he will add more minutes to the plans for those of us that record 4 - 8 hour audiobooks - it would be great to have this software available to polish up audiobooks without running into hourly limits, but I guess that's what code stacking is for. So maybe rethink the code stacking tiers to make them more enticing and generous for Sumolings.

So, if you record podcasts, audio lessons, guided meditations and the like, then this is a no-brainer! You could even read/record blog articles or newsletters aloud and record the audio for your readers - adds a nice personal touch imo.

The customer service is responsive and solution focused by email, and it's clear that the dev really cares about this platform.  I'm def looking forward to using Trebble frequently for my audio editing needs.

comments.title: Very simple and intuitive
comments.comment:
I am a professor and leadership coach, so I need an editing app for both audio (podcast-style recordings) and video (short lecture or how-to videos). I was an early adopter of Descript because of its intuitive, text-based interface. Over time, though, Descript has added many features and requires some re-learning every time I use it (maybe once every month or two). 

Enter Trebble. Think of it as a simpler, more intuitive, cleaner version of Descript. While it has more features to explore, I've been satisfied with the basics: upload a video (mp4), remove filler words and speech anomalies, enhance voice, and remove or minimize background noise - plus, if needed, remove or add sections - then export as an mp3 for audio use. That's really what I need and what Trebble is doing well so far.

comments.title: The most Undervalued descript alternative in Appsumo
comments.comment: You can try all the fancy tools like Minvo, or countless other AppSumo products that claim to make editing easier, but the fundamentals lie in the algorithm. Does it correctly remove filler words? Does it improve the sound quality? Is the text editing smooth? And does the AI truly increase your work speed? I tried them all and had to request refunds for every one because they're mere imitations. YouTube reviewers don't genuinely use them, and you'll spend more time correcting their output. Treeble is the only exception. They seem to focus on audio podcast editing, but they're clearly moving into video. Their editor is on par with Descript. They efficiently remove filler words and noise without making the sound robotic. Even when adding background music, they achieve a great balance to keep the voice audible. These small details speak volumes about the developers, and ultimately, these details are crucial when considering the long-term value of an AppSumo LTD deal.

comments.title: Good tool for editing audio
comments.comment:
Two things I liked about this. 

First, the ability to edit the transcript, and have part of my audio deleted or moved around. But, it is only for deletions and moving around sounds. (You can't add new text because this tool does not clone your voice.) It's easier to edit words, than it is to look at waveforms in Audacity and Ocenaudio. 

Second, it also detects the silences, and represents the silences with a dot. If you don't like the silence, you can delete the dot. That trims the silence. 

A good tool. It has a lot of potential and it is in a very special niche. Its real competitors are Descript and Hindenburg. It's a very small set of competitors. The other tools which allow you to transcribe recordings don't allow you to make changes to the audio. All they do is extract the text, and maybe use AI to summarize the transcript. So, if you've read this review, you'll know that it is a very special tool. Worth stacking up if you're making podcasts and e-learning courses. 

Disclosure, I've used this tool to edit two very long audio recordings.

comments.title: Fantastic Feature Set, But Severe Rate Limiting Cripples High-Volume Use
comments.comment:
Unmixr AI is a legitimate "Swiss Army Knife" for creators, bundling high-quality TTS, STT, and AI video dubbing into one platform. The sheer value proposition, especially with the wide range of natural-sounding voices and language support, is truly impressive. The TTS functionality, in particular, is a standout feature and the user experience is very smooth.

However, I have encountered a critical, workflow-breaking issue related to API usage limits. My account was throttled and returned the following error message:
{"detail":"Request was throttled. Expected available in 49772 seconds."}
This throttling means a mandatory lockout of approximately 13.8 hours before service resumes.

While I understand the necessity of rate limiting, a half-day recovery period is catastrophic for high-volume users or projects with tight deadlines. If Unmixr aims to be a reliable production tool, the team must urgently re-evaluate the throttling mechanism to provide shorter recovery times or clearer, more robust capacity for AppSumo users. Until this is fixed, I caution any high-volume user.

So in that sense, it’s a bit disappointing for me.

However, there are positive points as well. The speech speed control is excellent, and even when I slow it down significantly, the prosody doesn’t break. In that regard, I think it’s better than ElevenLabs. Also, the number of voices available in Tier 1 is a little limited. But overall, I’m satisfied.

comments.title: Unmixr Needs to Adapt: Free Alternatives Are Now More Realistic and Feature Rich
comments.comment:
I bought Unmixr about nine months ago, and at the time I was genuinely impressed. I made several work tutorials using the Jenny and Expressive Jenny voices, and people at my job immediately noticed how much better the audio sounded compared to my older tutorials. Unmixr was also extremely fast. I could generate an hour of audio in just a few minutes, which even beat ElevenLabs for long form work. For a lifetime deal, it felt like a great value.

Unmixr was clearly stronger than tools like Revoicer and Speechelo, and while ElevenLabs still had the most natural voices overall, Unmixr was not far behind. My workflow back then was simple: use Unmixr for speed and rely on ElevenLabs only when I needed something more expressive.

But nine months later, the landscape has changed dramatically. Google Studio Text to Speech now offers around twenty voices that are completely free, unlimited, and in many cases more natural than Unmixr’s Pro voices and even better than some ElevenLabs voices. Because of this, I find myself using Google more than Unmixr, even though I own multiple lifetime deals.

I also use Clone Voice AI every day now. For the kind of work I do, it has become better than what I was doing with Unmixr. Google gives me natural voices with no limitations, and Clone Voice AI gives me unlimited voice cloning, text to speech that sounds better than Unmixr’s Pro voices which still are not included for AppSumo users, a built in voice changer which I have been requesting from Unmixr for a long time, and even music generation. Competitors are moving fast, and they are offering more powerful features at lower prices.

This is why Unmixr needs to rethink its AppSumo tiers. In the past, they refused to include the Pro voices for AppSumo customers, but at this point they really need to reconsider that decision if they want to stay competitive. With Google offering extremely realistic voices for free and other platforms offering unlimited cloning and advanced audio tools in their lifetime deals, Unmixr cannot afford to hold back its best features.

There are also several improvements Unmixr needs to add if they want to keep up. They need better voice flow and more natural pacing. They need more emotional control and detailed voice settings, not just basic sliders. They need a voice changer option, more modern and expressive premium voices, and a stronger voice cloning system that can compete with what other platforms are offering. They also need better dubbing, better pronunciation control, and a more advanced timeline editor for fine tuning audio. These additions would help Unmixr stay relevant in a market that is evolving very quickly.

Unmixr still has potential, but they need to move faster to match today’s standards. Including the Pro voices for AppSumo users, improving voice realism, offering more tools, and expanding features are essential steps now. The foundation is good, but the market has clearly moved forward, and Unmixr needs to catch up before more users switch to platforms that are already ahead. I am being generous and giving four stars because Unmixr did help with a lot of my earlier work, but I have to admit this is really a three star platform at the moment because other platforms are outpacing it, especially Google’s free text to speech.

However, i do believe that if unmixr listens to the feedback, they can redeem their platform and make it strong again but they need to act quickly because other better options exist now for free on speech to text like google studio ai.

This one is one of the better ones, and I'm tempted to get a 2nd full stack (if that's allowed - or if I can stack beyond the max stack, I'd do that). Why?

1) Most of these voices have "tells" that they're AI - but nearly all AI - even best-in-class AI - have their hiccups. But they have ways to let you modulate many of them to make them far more malleable than other platforms.

2) This lets me do hour-long podcast episodes. They call it the "Long Voice Studio (V2)" currently. A "full stack" account currently gives you 1.1M characters. One hour long script is about 65-75k characters. So I can do roughly 15 HOURS per month with a full stack. That's a great deal.

My fears?

1) They voices never improve? Many are trash, but some are solid, you DO have to play with them a bit (They let you preview for free)

2) The software dies (like Speechki, which was the BEST and which I'm dying to replace; or Uttr which became Blakify, and then subsequently died). 1.1M characters per month - if we use it - isn't free. They're banking on this base helping them launch. I hope they're successful (that's why I'm leaving them a positive review). But Appsumo's options currently are batting only 3/5 (and Play.ht seems to have depricated some things for sumos).

I've also purchased a full stack of VoiSpark, which has higher quality voices, but currently has a STAGGERINGLY SMALL 10k character limit, which is like 6-8 minutes. That migght be great for some poeple, but not me (I'm TOLD they're raising that, possibly this month (Sept. 2025) - but that is yet to be seen.).

So...

I'm hopeful. I really do want to stack more codes or - if I have to and am allowed - buy a second (or third) full stack. This combined with a platform like Subscribr (also found via Appsumo, and probably in my top 10 all time deals) is KILLER for making a podcast that has legs. If VoiSpark fixes the low character limit, I might 2x or 3x that deal, because they're that useful and will be for the foreseeable (but probably not indefinite) future.

You can get this deal in good conscience.

(So I wrote this review, but accidentally put it on VoiSpark - they're hard to keep straight!)

comments.title: The most stress-free text-to-voice tool I’ve used (with a few hardware caveats)
comments.comment:
Overall, I’ve been very pleased with Vois Studio. The single biggest win here is workflow freedom: when you’re trying to get a line read just right, you don’t have to sit there counting credits as they drain away with every minor adjustment. That alone makes it the most stress-free way to generate text-to-speech. Seriously... I can't tell you how good it feels not to feel guilty about just one more run.

Quick Highlights:
* Zero Credit Anxiety: Perfect for tweaking words, cadence, and timing without worrying about a burning meter.
* Audio Quality: Extremely solid. It’s not quite the flagship polish of ElevenLabs, but it easily beats most standard cloud tools I’ve used.
* Hardware Demands: It is a resource hog. Needs solid specs to unlock its full potential without relying solely on Lite mode.
* Voice Cloning: Worked seamlessly on my desktop, but crashed on my 16GB laptop during reading/rendering.
* Support: Fast, responsive, and actively looking into the laptop rendering issue.
* Catalog Diversity: Needs a wider selection of ethnic and regional dialects (or deeper customization tools) for complex multi-character projects like fiction.

A couple of honest observations on hardware and features:

First, it is definitely a resource hog if you want to push it to its full potential. It will run on my HP Victus laptop (16GB RAM), but only in Lite mode. The stock catalog voices work well enough on the laptop, but when I tried reading with my own cloned voice, it crashed—the cloning process itself went fine, just not the playback render. That said, support was quick to respond and is actively looking into it. When I moved the clone over to my desktop, it ran without a hitch.

Second, the audio quality is very strong compared to most cloud solutions out there. It’s not quite ElevenLabs level yet, but standard tier output is genuinely good—if the Omni upgrade is a step above this, it must be impressive.

My main wishlist item is voice and accent diversity. In my writing, I deal with characters from all over—different ethnic backgrounds and distinct regional dialects (deep Southern, New York, Midwest, Canadian, etc.). I know building out every demographic and sub-region is a massive undertaking, but to become the top-tier player in this space, Vois will either need a much broader ethnic/regional catalog or better tools for users to tweak and customize accents easily on their own. Maybe that is what Omni offers, I don't know.

It’s not quite ready to handle every single intricate character voice for a novel, but for the vast majority of everyday text-to-voice needs, it is ready to be your workhorse. Well worth grabbing.

comments.title: My last text-to-speech tool?

I've purchased several text-to-speech tools on AppSumo, including Vocallab AI, VoiSpark, Unmixr AI, and the now-defunct Utrrr. My main goal is to learn new languages, and these tools have been invaluable for improving my listening skills. The voice-cloning features are especially helpful for practicing pronunciation. However, I keep adding more tools due to concerns about their longevity and generation limits.

Vois addresses both concerns. I started with the free trial on an underpowered 8GB M1 MacBook Pro and was surprised by the results. Although generation times were slow, the generated audio matched the quality of other tools, and Vois imposes no generation limits.

I’ve since upgraded to Tier 2. Every issue I reported was fixed in version 2.4, though I never received confirmation.

The quality of the short sample voice clone is comparable to that of other tools. Its best feature is automatic multilingual support. The extensive list of languages covers all the languages I need. As with most AI text-to-speech tools, it’s best to split the text into smaller parts, especially for cloned voice generation, which Vois handles easily.

With this purchase, I hope to have made my last text-to-speech purchase on AppSumo.

comments.title: A promising, multi-purpose tool with a few rough edges
comments.comment:
I actually hit the ground running with Vois Studio, which is allowing me to share my thoughts perhaps a bit sooner than I normally would. Still, bear that in mind that I'm still learning the tool and may uncover more along the way, but I was able to get up and running quickly and actually created real content so I feel like I'm reasonably qualified to speak to it even at this early stage.

My short review: Vois is a capable tool that has a few areas that need some polish and improvement, but is business-ready if you're able to work around those rough edges (I was). If I could give a more nuanced rating, I'd probably go 4.5 tacos to reflect that "almost there" status, but for a relatively young product, I was pleasantly surprised by how good it already is. So I'm  happy to round up to 5 tacos to reflect that as well as the potential I see.


My longer review:

My specific use case is that I regularly create short podcasts for myself and my clients, so Vois' voice cloning and script features were very familiar to me. I had been leveraging a SaaS product (Wondercraft) to do this, and while it's not terribly expensive, I was paying for more than I ultimately needed, especially with their push to get me to upgrade to access their new AI tools.

While Vois does not have all the shiny, built-in AI functionality (note: they have rolled out the ability to use local AI agents through CLIs), the core capabiltiies are pretty solid. I cloned three voices within minutes, learned how to craft and annotate my script pretty easily, and it generated an almost-ready-to-use audio file on the first pass.

Further, the interface is pretty easy to figure out, though it lacks a few conveniences that I'd like to see added soon (more on that below). Still, I was able to go from download to having my first episode finished in about an hour.

Setup isn't too bad, though I ended up redoing my clones a few times. Vois is particular about the clip length (it must be under 60 seconds long), and I found that I needed a really clean recording to upload.

Here's my more detailed list of Pros (+), Cons (-), and Observations (/):

+ The ability to run an unlimited number number of generations is very nice. No need to monitor a credit allowance!
+ If you have any experience with an editor, Vois is pretty easy to figure out. It has it's own specific quirks, but the fact that I went from installation to a finished product in about an hour I think is telling
+ You can override pronunciations on a global or project-specific basis
+ There's a solid selection of pre-built voices to select from, along with the ability to clone voices (the number of clones being based on your plan)
+ There's an easy way to add some audio "personality" - a chuckle, sigh, etc. - into your recordings
+ Adding music is simple to do and, again, there's some built-in options or you can upload your own

/ Processing time was reasonable. As everything runs locally, your experience will depend on your hardware. I'm running on a 3 year old business-focused Windows machine - not a gaming rig - and Vois was acceptably fast
/ The tagging of the script is pretty easy though some keyboard shortcuts would be welcome rather than having to mouse-click everything
/ There's mention of an Ultra or Pro plan in the software but it's not currently available. However, if/when it is, there's apparently going to be an additional fee associated with it
/ If you are doing anything commercial with your recordings, you need to be on Tier 3

- Every run seemed to create at least one audio artifact - an unexplained pause, an odd pronounciation, or an unwanted word (on one point, Vois said "dot" when there was a period)
- The timeline interface is 85% great, but lacks a built-in scroll bar which was surprising
- There's no option to regenerate just one clip so Vois reprocesses everything when you have a change. To the positive, it recognizes unchanged clips and skips those, but to the negative, every time you regenerate, it resets all the timeline changes (moving around clips or shortening them all gets reset).
- Vois could benefit from more contextual recognition. Take "read" for example: "I read the book" vs. "I will read the book" both generated with a past tense pronunciation. I had to fake Vois out by switching it to "reed"


Still, I'm pleased with the purchase. It's a rare experience for me to find something on AppSumo that can fully replace an existing tool from the outset but it looks like Vois is going to be that for me. I do see room for further refinement, but where the product is at already is impressive and I see things only getting better from here.

comments.title: Why buy Vois when you have three other text to voice programs?
comments.comment:
Why buy Vois when you already own other text-to-speech tools?

I’ve purchased many TTS programs over the years, including a few on AppSumo. Most of them are useful. Very few replace the others. Vois is one of the few that actually earned a permanent place on my machine.

The biggest reason is simple: it runs on your own computer. Because generation is local, there are virtually no practical limits on how long a file can be. You are not watching a character meter, a minute cap, or a “this chapter will cost extra” warning. For audiobooks, courses, long YouTube scripts, and multi-episode podcasts, that changes how you work. You can rewrite a paragraph, regenerate it, and keep going.

The voices are quite good and expressive. This is not the flat, robotic TTS a lot of us settled for a few years ago. The AppSumo version also comes with a massive voice library, so you can actually cast a project instead of forcing one generic narrator onto everything.

Two-person / multi-speaker support is rare
This is only the second text-to-speech program I’ve found that handles two-person podcasts well. You can assign different voices to speakers in one script and generate the conversation instead of stitching separate files together. If you make interview-style shows, explainers with a host and co-host, or dialogue-heavy training content, that alone is a strong reason to own it.

Voice cloning and voice design
Clones are very good and only take a few seconds to create. They were also surprisingly free of background noise. Vois does not only clone voices — you can design them as well. The results are clear and expressive enough for real published work, not just demos.

One caveat from my first tests: cloned voices worked in test mode but produced gibberish when I tried to generate from text. After several upgrades, I’m not sure whether a patch fixed it or whether recreating the clone did. When I rebuilt the cloned voice, everything worked fine. If a clone sounds broken, recreate it from a short, clean sample before assuming the product is unusable.

What concerned me
The other issue was support. While I was fighting the clone problem, I could not find an email address or an obvious support link. The problem is resolved now, but I hope the Vois team publishes a clear support path. Local software is great until something goes wrong and you cannot find a human.

Who this is for
Vois is a comprehensive package with almost no usage limits. Because it lives on your computer, you do not have to worry that a subscription change, credit increase, or shutdown will cut you off from a tool you already paid for.

It also includes a CLI, so an AI agent can drive the system. That is useful if you already generate scripts with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Cursor and want the voice step in the same workflow.

Bottom line
If you only need the occasional 30-second voiceover, you may already have enough tools. If you produce a lot of audio — long files, multi-speaker scripts, cloned brand voices, or content you do not want uploaded to a cloud TTS service — Vois is one of the few AppSumo TTS deals that is not just “another voice pack.” It is a local studio: unlimited generation, strong voices, cloning, voice design, multi-speaker podcasts, and room to grow.

I’d buy it again. Just plan on a short learning curve with clones, and I would like to see support made easier to find.

comments.title: A local voice studio for creators who revise a lot
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Vois Studio is one of the more refreshing voice tools I tested because it runs on your own machine.

For anyone creating voiceovers regularly, that changes the way you work. You can rewrite a sentence, try another take, change a voice, fix pronunciation, adjust the pacing, and generate again without thinking about usage limits every time you touch the script. That's what I like most. Voice work usually needs revisions, and Vois gives you room to keep working until the audio sounds right.

I tested it on Windows 10 and it worked really well. The product feels more like a desktop voice studio than a simple text to speech box. You can write scripts, use multiple speakers, generate speech locally, arrange clips, add music or sound effects, master the audio, and export for different platforms.

The local setup is a big part of the appeal. Once the models are downloaded, speech generation happens on your computer, so your scripts and audio do not have to be uploaded to a cloud service just to produce a voiceover. For courses, YouTube channels, client work, audiobooks, tutorials, or unreleased content, I like having that control.

Vois also has more depth than I expected. The listing now includes 100+ voices across 23 languages, a pronunciation dictionary, inline vocal reactions, mastering tools, and export presets. The CLI is also officially released. The team explained that this is the supported path for AI agent workflows, together with Vois skills, instead of MCP. That makes sense for this type of desktop app because repeatable production steps can be handled locally while the user stays in control.

A few things buyers should know upfront. Vois supports Apple Silicon Macs and Windows x64, but not Intel Macs. Internet is still needed for setup, model downloads, activation, and periodic license validation. Also, commercial use is included in Tier 3, so check the tier details before buying if you plan to use it for client or commercial projects.

Overall, Vois Studio is an easy recommend for people who create a lot of voice content and are tired of per generation limits. Its best fit is a YouTuber, podcaster, course creator, audiobook creator, or agency user who wants a local voice studio they can keep using and refining without watching a credit meter.

comments.title: Easy to Use, Fast Creation of Graphics
comments.comment:
I'm giving 5 stars because it delivered what it promised with zero learning curve. I produced a ready-to-use, very high quality jpg in less than 5 minutes!

PROS
- Super easy to use. No training or downloads required.
- UI is clean and loads fast as I make edits.
- Produced graphics can be made public and shared in 1 click to FB, X, LinkedIn, and Pinterest.
- Very professional templates that get the point across quickly. If you work in a traditional company/industry, this will make you look like a legit ALL-STAR! 

CONS
- No/low flexibility to change the size of the assets to accommodate the text. I had to reword my info to fit.
- Add some more modern templates that will better appeal to the younger generations. Traditional industries are changing and this will become outdated if not updated eventually.

WISHLIST:
- Ability to add my company logo watermark in the app, without having to use a separate tool to add it
- Tooltips for error warnings

Overall, it's a keeper for me. Please keep up the support of this nice tool for the long-term! Thanks :)

comments.title: Product has great potential and founder seems responsive and change-ready
comments.comment:
Transparency

The founder is registred at a business center in Delaware with his other company Catextech.com. Here it is stated that the team is located in Nigeria, Africa. 
While Memogram claims to be complient with GDPR, NDPR, and CCPA regulations, it's not possible to find its business address or company registration number on the website.

Onboarding

- After redeeming my tier 3 license I was onboarded with a 7-day free plan, renewable in 99 years, yet with limited features. I reached out to support and got that fixed quickly. I think others have had the same issues onboarding.

First impressions and dashboard

- The dashboard is nice and clear. I do wish that the introductory video wasn't so prominent. It's a 2-minute video, but it takes up a lot of the screen all the time. One might consider gathering all the video guides under a menu item in the left panel.

- While testing, I experienced some inconsistency with translation. Sometimes the text wouldn't translate if I change language at random pages, returned to the dashboard and changed the language again. Example:
1. Starting on the dashboard page (default English language)
2. Changing the language to Danish. All good, text is translated.
3. Visiting the "My Events" page.
4. Changing the language back to English. All good, text is translated.
5. Navigating back to the dashboard page. All text still in English.
6. Changing the language to Danish again. Now, all text remains in English.

Event creation

- An observation: It’s not possible to create an event from the "My Events" page. It's necessary to go back to the dashboard to create a new event. I think there's room for improvement here.

- I'm a bit unsure what Event Categories are used for?
It's not possible to filter by Event Category in the list of events on the "My Events" page. If the Event Category is neither filterable, searchable, nor used in statistics, why have a dropdown list of categories where a selection is mandatory? Perhaps an input field where you can name a category yourself would be sufficient.

- The event date can’t be set to more than a couple of months ahead. E.g. There’s now only 3 months left of 2025, however, I can’t set an event date in 2026. This should be possible.

Landing page

- The Memogram logo appears for a split second when the landing pages load.

- The black overlay is very dark. It should be possible to choose the opacity or even choose a different overlay color.

Upload

- During upload the % scale doesn't move. One is just notified that X out of Y images have been uploaded.

Team members

- Is a welcome email sent when a team member is created? If so, my imaginary team member never received the email (and it's not in the spam folder)

- For agency tiers, there’s a role missing: “Client”. There’s only the team member role, and it's not white labeled. It’s a bit disappointing that we're only able to use the team member role for clients who might want to login and edit their event or download media on a PC. They are met by Memogram branding and “How did you hear about us”.

- Observation: Why show the create event button when a team member is logged in, if team members don’t have access to create events?

Editing events

- It’s not possible to close the modal layer (Congratulation) unless one click “View all events”. The layer should close when one clicks outside of it or on an X in the top right corner.

About the campaign's progress and execution in general

- I think many have been confused by the terms for purchasing tier 3, which turned out not to require prior purchase of tier 1 or 2.

- On July 29th I asked if the prices would increase at some point, e.g. in connection with the launch of tier 3 (See Questions). Your answer was: "price increase is imminent. We strongly advise you purchase while prices are still low". And so I did (FOMO), but the prices never increased :-(

comments.title: Excellent Collection, but limited 3D Animated Icons
comments.comment:
Flat Icons has become an indispensable asset in my design toolkit, offering an extensive array of meticulously crafted vector icons that cater to a myriad of design projects. The sheer diversity of categories ensures that there's an icon for every occasion, while the availability of various formats such as SVG, EPS, and PDF allows for seamless integration and customization within my workflows.
One of the most remarkable aspects of Flat Icons is the commitment to expanding and updating the collection, particularly for those who have invested in lifetime access. This dynamic approach ensures that my designs remain fresh and relevant, with new icons constantly at my fingertips.
However, I do feel that the inclusion of a more comprehensive selection of 3D animated icons within the base package would elevate the product even further, adding an extra layer of depth and interactivity to my projects. Additionally, while the overall quality of the icons is exceptional, I have encountered instances where certain icons feel somewhat familiar or dated, having been used extensively in other designs.
I have also noticed that some users have experienced difficulties in locating editable icons for color customization, suggesting that there may be room for improvement in terms of functionality and clarity. Furthermore, the website's smartphone interface could benefit from some refinement to enhance the user experience, although I have found the app itself to be quite intuitive and user-friendly.
Lastly, streamlining the file naming conventions could greatly facilitate the search process, allowing users to quickly pinpoint the exact icons they need for their projects.
Despite these minor areas for improvement, Flat Icons remains an invaluable resource for designers and developers alike. The extensive collection, coupled with the reasonable pricing, makes it an attractive option for those seeking high-quality icons. With some tweaks to the user experience and the inclusion of more 3D animated icons,  Flat Icons could undoubtedly cement its position as a go-to solution for creative professionals across various industries.

comments.title: Dope QUICK Banner Maker Tool. It Does What It Says -- Nothing More, Nothing Less:)
comments.comment:
This is a really dope little tool. Initially, I was a bit skeptical because it DOES NOT offer a refund. I believe the people behind Killer Player (something I bought a few yrs back, and it works well for what it does) are behind this. It DOES what it says—nothing more, nothing less. I have almost ALL design tools imaginable (some are 'fancy scroll-stoppers' and some are simplistic), but I've been waiting for something simple like this to create STATIC banners QUICKLY. NO, you won't be able to create GIF banners, but if you do affiliate marketing or have your product and want people to promote it, you'll find churning out these different (most used sizes quickly) to be a JEWEL.

So, suppose you're looking to generate banners QUICKLY that are NOT flashy, BUT stylish (they don't look like the old school banners we used to be able to generate in banner makers. These look professional). In that case, this is worth it (one thing they got right is they go off the style of some of the major players you might see in your Internet travels). I've been searching for a while for something like this. I accidentally stumbled upon it and said, 'FINALLY!' I wouldn't get this if you're looking for something animated (because it won't happen). Also, download ALL files before you leave your design because from what I see with this deal, it DOES NOT save it in the cloud. I've found quite a few programs doing this lately. I would rather this than the company going out of business because they could not afford their server space. BUT, I think it should be MADE SUPER TRANSPARENT about this at the BEGINNING and THROUGHOUT the editing process. Anyway, I'm grateful for this tool so far. If you want to add an animation, you could take it over to Crello or Canva, overlay the shop now button or something, and animate it there to give it some flare (but that sounds like work to me -- IMO). I hope this review helps a few ppl who may be on the fence.

• Cons: Some bugs and challenges (export quality, working with 'text' in 'text box') 
-------
Verdict: When I need to get something done minimalist and quickly -> Drawtify is my go-to app. 

Canva has more modern templates but their UI/UX is so complex now and they keep moving things around every few months or so, I am overwhelmed. I just want to complete my simple task in 5 minute, not 5 hours. 

I like Drawtify's simplicity and consistent intuitive UI/UX. 

When I need more advanced stuff like altering image quickly (remove/add/change colour of objects, face swap, etc.) I go to Higgsfield AI. I don't expect Drawtify to have AI features because they're a very simple LTD deal at a very affordable price. 

This is the workflow that works for my needs.

Caveats: I was unable to read or import ".ai" and  ".eps" files. Those are the standard formats for acquired images (such as Stockphoto). Not a big issue, I convert them with Inkscape, but it is one extra step.

A nuisance finally. I tried to open it on my tablet, but I got a message saying "mobile not supported - use a tablet or desktop instead." But why? Probably because the TCL tablet (that can hold a SIM) identifies itself as a phone. So what? What is the problem if I want to use it on my phone? If it is not adequate (for the low resolution) I can desist, but why prevent it? The device I will be used shall finally be a decision of mine.

I had problems at the start, but figured it out after watching YouTube videos and playing around with the software.

I hope Drawify stays in business for many years, as I don't need the tool right now, but could see myself using it in the future. I love Bézier curves, the file sizes can be printed the size of a strawberry seed to a massive billboard with such a small file size.

I have programs that can take pictures and convert them into vectors, I'm hoping I can paste them into Drawify.  I'd like to see a feature like Canva has where you can take a finalized image and get the HTML iframe code to paste in a website or blog. (1) There should be more resources for images, icons and fonts.
(2) Make the background feature more advanced. The user should have the ability to restore or erase the parts, which are left by the AI Background remover of Draftify.
(3) This is a must and urgently required. There is a feature in the Draftify Animator module, where the Icon or shape can move along a motion path. At present there is no option to adjust the "ANCHOR POINT" of the shape which moves along the path. So, at present, the end animation look off. So, my request to the developer, to give an option to the user, so that the anchor point can be adjusted, so that the "MOVE ALONG PATH" can work as intended.

comments.title: All your client's brand assets on one place
comments.comment:
I like to have all the clients logo format files, palettes and correct/incorrect uses of their logo on a digital interactive medium, rather than a simple pdf or mail message.

Pros:
- 10GB per brand is very generous.
- Colors can be copied with just one click.
- You just need to add the hex colors and Brandy converts them to other formats (Hex8, RGB HSL).
- You can upload the different font files and Brandy displays a preview.
- It shows file info (type of document, size, last updated) for the images, fonts, and other files you uploaded.
- By default, you have 4 panels (collections) on the left (logos, colors, fonts, and images), but you can add more and name them as you like. You can also change the name of the default panels.

Cons
- No onboarding, assistant or product tour to learn how to quickly use it, i took me some minutes to find how to add a new brand.
- The whole UI looks too white and simple, it needs to be polished to make it more attractive and modern, specially for clients. There is no other colors beside the orange button. This should be customized to the colors of our brand, but it's not a big issue right now.
- Maximum file size allowed to upload is 500Mb, it should be 1 gb or let us connect Dropbox or other cloud services.
- Every time i add an asset (colors, files, video, text), the asset is added on the top, instead of the bottom, so i had to drag it and move it to the bottom. -Update: i just found out that if you mouse over any line that divides the assets, you can insert assets (onboarding point). 
- Text formatting: there is no WYSIWYG editor whatsoever! you need to use an old markdown to make the text bold, italic, h1, h2, etc. There is no option to add html or css, so the text will be always black. They really need to work on this, it should not be that difficult.
- Layout: there is only one row so the assets you add will be always one below the other one, you cannot have 2 images in one line for example. This could be an issue because the logos look too big, but if you have at least 2 rows, the logos would not look that big, a lightbox could be added when clicking on the image to see it bigger.

Recommendations
- You can make you product better by adding more design to the interface, for instance you can add small icons in the file type, look at this example https://tinyurl.com/yev2k3yr
- To be able to make templates (with the custom panels and names we modified), so we can apply them when creating a new brand, then we just need to change the images, fonts, colors...
- Let us change some other texts like download button, search assets, click to copy, etc
- Let us change the color of the download button
- Integration with cloud sites: Dropbox, Pcloud, GDrive, Onedrive, etc
- the "More" option only give you "Move asset" and "Delete asset", please add "Duplicate asset" or "Copy/paste asset", so i can copy an asset from the top and paste it in the middle or the end
- Bigger or Wider Dividers to clearly separate sections.

comments.comment:
It’s true that we have Canva and many other much more complete tools, although they tend to be significantly more complex and time-consuming to achieve the results we get here so effortlessly. 

For quick editing jobs and screenshots, nothing beats this tool. It also includes a whole range of spectacular AI tools, from logo design, creating Pinterest pins, rapid infographics generation, and much more. 

It is absolutely a no-brainer tool to add to the tech stack, especially at the low price it currently offers, with unlimited AI usage (for now, until the quota runs out — which is fair and honest). Plus, the BYOK system is fair and flexible.

However, I have some suggestions:

- If using OUR API KEY, I believe you should include other AI models, particularly Google’s image models, even if the more advanced ones like “Nano Banana Pro” are more expensive. Sometimes I need to include Latin characters in infographics, and “Nano Banana Pro” is currently the only model that manages to render long texts with Latin characters perfectly — or nearly perfectly. I think having more LLM options could be very helpful and that should be brought in , not by STRAICO (which is limited) but simply implementing "OpenRouter", which includes all of them. It contains all possible image models and is always updated with the most recent/best image/text/video models.

- One essential missing feature that needs fixing is an extension that allows me to instantly capture and crop just a section of the screen. I know I can do this in two steps with Picbolt itself: first capturing the screen with the inline HTML5 web capture, then using the crop tool. But this is very rudimentary and disrupts the fast workflow you want. comments.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A Powerful Branding Platform with Exceptional Support
comments.comment:
Brandolia is much more than a logo generator. It is a practical, all-in-one branding platform that can help freelancers, consultants, entrepreneurs, agencies, and small businesses create a professional brand identity and website in a remarkably short time.

The platform can generate a complete brand package, including logos, color palettes, typography, brand stories, mission and vision statements, moodboards, websites, PDFs, and social media assets. The results may still require professional review and refinement, but Brandolia provides an excellent foundation and can save a significant amount of time compared with starting from scratch.

What impressed me most is not only the range of features, but also the attitude of the team led by Ayoub. They do not merely listen to user feedback; they actively discuss customer suggestions, implement requested improvements, introduce new features continuously, and refine existing tools with the goal of bringing them closer to a polished and professional experience.

I personally requested several improvements, and the response was outstanding. In a very short time, the team:

- Added or improved support for creating multilingual websites.
- Advanced the development of multi-page websites.
- Worked on connecting corresponding pages between different languages.
- Added Arabic support alongside English and French, showing that Brandolia is committed to serving users from different regions and language backgrounds.
- Addressed Arabic-related issues involving right-to-left layout, typography, character rendering, spacing, and PDF formatting.
- Reviewed the token cost of creating a brand from existing assets and changed it from two tokens to one token.
- Considered improvements to the Website Wizard, including social media links, chatbot integration, contact pages, reference websites, and more flexible website creation.
- Continued working on better content editing, SVG generation, prompt handling, and website customization.

What makes this especially valuable is the speed and seriousness with which the team handled these requests. They did not dismiss difficult technical feedback or make empty promises. Ayoub personally followed up, discussed the suggestions with the team, and provided clear updates about what had already been completed and what remained in development.

New users should understand that Brandolia is not intended to eliminate human judgment completely. Its greatest value is as a professional branding assistant that accelerates research, ideation, content creation, visual development, and website production. With some thoughtful refinement, the generated assets can become highly useful and client-ready.

If you are considering Brandolia, my advice is simple: subscribe—you will not regret it. Brandolia is worth every dollar spent, without hesitation, especially for anyone who needs to build consistent brand assets quickly while benefiting from a responsive team that genuinely cares about continuous improvement.

Highly recommended. Five stars.

comments.title: Pretty Decent for the Price
comments.comment:
I mean, it's $30 for 500 image credits a month, where each image costs about a credit.
What more could you want? OK, OK - fine. You wanna know about the image output, right? For the most part, I'd say it's "mostly decent". Mostly. Yeah, yeah - not much to go on. I know. Just keep with me for a bit...

There are some hits and some misses in what it generates, but overall, it's not a bad tool for the money. The upscaler is... neh.. I mean, it does what it says on the tin and doubles the image *resolution*, but the quality didn't seem to. The other tools, again, are hit-or-miss. 
I'm not saying it's a *BAD* tool; far from it. Again, for the price you're paying? If this company can stay viable and keep current with all the AI image generators on the market - or at least, keep parity - then I'd say they've got something worthwhile.
 
In sum: I wouldn't give them a straight-up 5-star review, but it's also not a straight 3-star review either. 
Put it this way: For what you're getting and what you're paying and the amount of credits provided, it's not bad at all. How's that for weasel words?

I've had worse purchases on AS, and I've bought tons of tools, so in my estimation, the fact that I'm writing a review at all should say something.

There are some interface issues (no bulk delete, no folder/hierarchy structures) that would be nice to have, but are they necessary? Nah. 
For the most part, it's clean, straightforward, and extremely easy to navigate.
Just wish the output of some of the AI-gen tools were a bit better, as some of the photos created were... significantly off to say the least.

Also wish I could generate higher rez imagery without having to feed the same imagery back into the tool.
In short, moving imagery from generation to editing to saving could use some help.

Outside all that, for $30 bucks or so? What's not to love!
Definitely worth the price.
I hope the developers keep pushing the tool/boundaries forward, and I look forward to what they come up with next.

Bottom line: if you drop $30 for tier one, you shouldn't be disappointed.

comments.title: Great Little Tool

comments.title: Interesting - but needs a lot of polish
comments.comment:
AirBrush offers an easy way to access multiple different image generation models. The fact that you can access a wide variety of models is the reason I give it 4 tacos. 

Otherwise, as the product currently work, I'd give it 3. Although straigthforward: you enter a prompt, you select a mode, you get an image. In practice, it's very clunky. The prompt rarely gives a satisfying result the first time, and like most image generation tool, you have to wait a bit for the image. It would be useful if variations of the images could be offered from the get go - maybe even across multiple models so that we can have a feel for which model gets the prompt more. That would also save time. And then maybe a fast way to iterate over the images and prompts. 

Other examples of the lack of polish: not all models support all the size. It's frustrating to request a large landscape and get back a squared image. 

There are other tools like the prompt enhancer and the image variation tools. Great, but why do I have to go a separate page to use them, and lose my workflow? Having the prompt suggestions right when I'm entering them would make sense. 

And to use the image variation tool, we have to upload a JPG. But what if I want variation of images just generated? Feels like I'm jumping through hoopses.

But if you want to be able to play with multiple models and don't mind a lot of waiting and iterations - it's great.

comments.title: Good AI tool
comments.comment:
I'm pleased with Airbrush and expect to use it a lot. While some of the pictures are not suitable, I think that is down to me still learning what to write in the description. The good pictures are so specific to my need that I couldn't have got them through a stock photo website. 

Airbrush has developed a lot since I first joined on a free account several weeks ago. I used to get the occasional completely black images which hasn't happened recently, plus there are now more AI engines to choose from. I hope this level of development continues. 

Improvements I'd like to see are:
* option for different dimensions, I want landscape images I can use in blog posts (this is why I've dropped it a taco)
* ability to tweak an image. On a few occasions, it has created an ideal picture except for one thing such as the background colour
* on the history screen it would be great to be able to see the engine used to create the image so I can learn which is my preferred choice
* the option to save or copy a description. I'm likely to use similar styles e.g. colours for consistency and it would be great if I didn't have to remember these

comments.title: Very easy to use
comments.comment: Airbrush is definitely easy to use. The UI is clean and straightforward, with no bugs that I've seen so far. I'm a full noob when it comes to writing prompts for AI image generation, but I'm also a coder and I've seen what others are doing. My results? Sometimes they are quite useable, so much so that I can't tell if it's fully a stock photo or not. That's a good thing, except for the maximum 1024 x 1024 pixel size, which really isn't good for anything besides web work. Plan to use the site's own Upscaler function or an app like Topaz Labs Photo AI to kick that up a little. So far, though, most of my prompts result in really bad 8-bit, abstract 'art', that isn't worth anything. At least you can reject it and get credit back. Will the engines get better? Probably. Will I get better writing 'conjures'? Probably. All in all, for the price, this is a decent way to dip your toes into the AI image pool. This will be VERY interesting in a few more years.

comments.title: Good Tool for Easy AI

I've been using AI imaging software for a while, so when I saw the Airbrush software available here on AppSumo, I jumped at the opportunity. Overall, I think the software is pretty good. However, I will say that there were a few notable issues as I was testing the software.

I'm going to say good because some of the images were not as good as I would have expected. My primary area of concern was with the MidJourney v.4 renders. As someone who actively uses MidJourney, I was surprised that the images really lack the detail and sophistication I'm actively seeing with MidJourney v.4. I'm not sure what's going on, but the render engine is clearly not as sophisticated as the actual MidJourney v.4. The other ones seem to be pretty good. I also didn't get as good of renders with their version of photogen. I'm wondering if they haven't uploaded the final build yet on this one. For me, the biggest problem is that the images are only able to be rendered in square form. I was hoping they'd have built in some aspect ratio into the platform, but as of right now, all images are square. 

Overall, I definitely plan on using Airbrush. I really think it's a great idea and I look forward to seeing where the development team takes the product as it seeks to improve based on the latest in AI image models.

comments.title: Airbrush is Promising and Entertaining
comments.comment:
I think the simplicity of the UI for Airbrush is pleasant - not to say it cannot be improved, but it makes finding what you're looking for easy and straightforward.

The tool itself is solid, offering 7 AI generation options (albeit Dall-E takes many more credits than the other 6, and sizes beyond the default take more credits for each engine), several sizing options, history and gallery of generated images, an image upscaler and general account dashboard.

While I believe the tool is going to become much more in the near future - the image generation quality hasn't met my expectations in 8/10 generations of imagery. I fault that potentially to not knowing how to properly prompt for what I want and what I don't, but I also think the engines offered on Airbrush can be improved.

All-in-all though, for the price, offered limits, and variety of engines - it's not bad - but I am hoping it becomes a superstar tool that generates amazing imagery that I can use for blogs and articles at some point on a consistent basis.

comments.title: Excellent. This product genuinely surprised me.
comments.comment:
I have tried many AI image generators, both cheap ones as well as expensive ones. However, I only purchased this out of curiosity because of the volume of reviews. I was genuinely cynical, thinking at this price point, it's going to be terrible. 

It created some excellent images for me. However, I realised through testing that if I gave it a general prompt, it would create your standard, what I call plasticky, perfect teeth, perfect hair type of images. But if I gave it a good prompt, it created the styling that I needed that complemented my brand. I'm not going to claim it's perfect, but it's very close to the other platform I used, which was what I'd say perfect. The other platform was also a lot more expensive. So, given the price point, it was excellent. And even if I say so myself, I really expect high standards.

However, what I found was genuinely very surprising. It created some outstanding images, and the most important thing I noticed was the platform was very reasonable about the number of credits it took off you. Apart from a few AI models, in general, it took 2 credits from me per image, which I felt was fair. As as they don't get greedy and change the amount of credits they take from customers - then I feel this is definitely a keeper. 

I'll keep an eye during the rest of the 60-day period if things change, but so far, it has been a genuine surprise. 

One last thing I would say is I hope they have a sustainable business model planned, because if we are all honest with each other, lifetime deals are great for market awareness and getting feedback for your product at the initial stage. However, if you have to keep doing lifetime deals to get revenue, eventually things will catch up and the business won't be sustainable. So that's my only minor concern. But I'm sure the people behind the platform are smart and they know what they're doing.

Thank you.

comments.title: Here is why you need this background removal tool
comments.comment:
I saw some of these background removal tools come around, and I wondered why I would need such a dedicated tool when background removal is a feature of one of my favorite Mac apps, Pixelmator Pro. Also, it is a feature of some other LTD products that are mainly for assembling graphics for social media, and similar uses.

So, I used Pixelmator Pro to remove backgrounds, and it works pretty well. Yet, it only works fast on a new M1 Mac. I am finding that I now prefer much less expensive computers that have touch screens, such as a Lenovo Flex. I am getting to the point where most of my software is online and accessible from any computer that can run the desktop version of Chrome. So, a Chromebook works, but not an iPad.

The other day, I was using the Lenovo, and I thought, "wouldn't it be nice to have a SaaS tool for background removal?" I tried one of the social media graphics tools I already have that does background removal as a side feature. It was ok, but there was additional editing to do with some artifacts, and it took a long time to process. Also, I disovered that that particular tool limits how many removals I can do per month. Even if I only do it occasionally, I hate to see an artificial limiting quota, telling me that I can only do 30 removals per month, or whatever. I'm not going to do thousands, or probably even tens, but I don't like those kinds of limits.

When I came here to look for a dedicated background removal tool, I tried this one first, because it included unlimited usage for one code. I was super impressed with the quality. There was no artifact, hair was well done, and processing was very fast.

I'm not going to obsess over the API and bulk upload features. If these were not part of the deal and never mentioned, I would still think this was a good deal for a good product that works fast, effectively, and offers unlimited use for a single code.

comments.title: Strong Topaz alternative that is almost there
comments.comment:
I picked this up a while ago and have been putting it through its paces, so here is my honest take.

The upscaling itself is excellent. When it runs properly, the output quality sits right up there with Topaz and the other premium upscalers I have tried. Clean, sharp, no weird artifacts.

 Getting results like that at this price feels like a steal, and I think paying hundreds for the big-name upscalers is money down the drain when something like this exists.

There are a few things holding it back from five stars though. The sizing options are limited to 200% and 400%. I get it, this is still an MVP and upscaling is heavy on GPU resources, so I understand why more options are not there yet. But a couple of extra steps in between would make a real difference.

Then there is stability. When I upscale a single image (I have not tried batch upscaling yet), it sometimes takes a very long time, and every now and then it just stalls at zero and does nothing at all, which forces me to restart. Tightening up the reliability and processing speed would take this tool to another level.

The amount of ads is also a bit much. I understand the developer needs to fund the project, so I will not make a big deal of it for now, but somewhere down the line it could become a sticking point. The interface has room to grow too, and I am sure that will come with time.

Overall this is a really good tool and I can see it becoming something special. I am giving it four stars purely because of the long processing times I've experienced. Fix those things and you have a five-star product on your hands. I am rooting for it and hope the developer takes this feedback on board.

comments.title: Good value, but with some flaws
comments.comment:
This is no doubt a good value if you can use it. Unfortunately, for anyone doing portraits or even candids or any photos of people, it will fail to impress. People end up looking like wax figures (eyes are especially dead and skin and features too smooth to be human). This is the same issue with some textures in landscapes, but this program will serve sufficiently for many landscapes. 
If the program ditched the Digital Noise Reduction and allowed for preserving "grain" it would vastly improve both skin and nature textures. However, it would still prove a problem for eyes. It feels like the issue is that it upscales too broadly rather than pixel-by-pixel such that it saves on cost but trades fidelity.

comments.title: 5 Tacos for sure!
comments.comment:
Firstly, I'm still a novice where AI upscalers are concerned. But I've done enough research to see the value in this one.

Secondly, I did reach out to the owner using the support email he provided in his responses to comments here but never heard back. I did that about a month before I purchased it. I wanted to make sure this upscales large enough for my needs. I do want to add that about 20% of the emails I send go to spam. So maybe he never saw it. But I like to be transparent in all things.

Lastly, in spite of not hearing back I went ahead with the purchase about 2 weeks ago anyway. Why? Because it's an amazing value to have lifetime access to a true AI upscaler and it works the way they say.

I've used it a bit since purchasing and it's worked exactly as it should. It can upscale to double your original or 4X your original. You choose the radial button. I need a very specific output size in my work so I start with an image a quarter that size and upscale 400%.

Some notes:
The maximum this will go to is 16,000px on either side.  Just an FYI. Many folks don't need to go that big. That's 53.33" x 53.33" in 300DPI if you're printing. PRETTY BIG.  I only need a 10,800 long side but I did test larger files and they are definitely capped at 16,000px

Your starting image cannot exceed 10MB. Mine do not. But when I was playing with the larger images it stopped me on one that was 10.2MB

The maximum batch size you can do at one time is currently 8.  I'm Okay with that. I sometimes have 10 and just split them. 

The output image shows 72DPI when I inspect it (in case that matters to anyone) but from the research I've done this is just semantics as long as the pixels are correct? Again, I'm still learning and providing all my notes in case it helps anyone looking to buy this. The pixels are definitely correct and the image works perfectly for my needs. I do run it through a python script in an automation process I have which changes the actual DPI to 300 since all the required pixels ARE there. Maybe this is how all upscalers work? 

I'd like to repeat that this is an AMAZING value. If you need to regularly upscale images and have them upscale correctly there are other options out there. But they all cost a heck of a lot more and are subscription based. This product provides exactly what I need for my daily work and will pay for itself in just 6 months. At that point The subscription based product would leave me with an ongoing monthly bill.  Consider me a very happy customer!

comments.title: Excellent photo companion
comments.comment:
I've used this upscaler recently to increase the size of some AI art, and wow, was I impressed with the result!

Here's where the tool shines:
• Bulk processing (up to 5 images right now, but hopefully that will increase with updates). 
• Photo deletion within 12/24 hours for privacy
• Great output for digital painting, art, or photos*
• Of most other similar products in this category, this one upscales to the highest/largest maximum output size of 16,000 x 16,000. 

Here's where it can improve:
• After logging in, the page where you process your upscales features a lot of content like photos, samples, videos, testimonials. For those who have paid or pay monthly, it would be great if this processing page was simplified and all the extra content was removed or moved to another section (such as a sample gallery, knowledge base, etc.) for a cleaner user experience.
• Don't know if this is possible, but it would be great to see a preview of the image either before processing, or immediately after processing so that users can see the before/after themselves on the screen.

I'm not a photographer, but having worked in the creative space for 20 years, I want to help set the expectation of what this tool can and can't do. 

This tool is best used for images that have lots of intricate patterns or details that a person likely won't be looking at through a magnifying glass or up-close. It is not ideal for highly detailed real-life photography that is being viewed closely. Let me clarify: If you are upscaling a very low-res image, the image you upload is already compressed in some sort of lossy format. So when the upscaler increases the size of this image, it is adding space that has to be filled with pixels. It will do its very best to fill in the blank pixels with colors and textures that match the surrounding area. It does a VERY good job of this. But if you have a very small image with barely legible text in the background, the upscaler won't magically make that text more legible. It simply can't because the data doesn't exist in order to do that. What it will do is make the text LOOK like text when you are zoomed out or viewing from afar. But when you zoom into the text, it will just be scribbles. If you are upscaling an image that will be viewed from a distance (such as posters, murals, signage, etc), this is a great tool to use. But if you are using this tool to upscale an image that will be going into a fine art gallery (or other instances where people can get real close to the art), then this tool (or any other tool) likely isn't for you.

This is not a criticism of the tool, but just a reality of the limitations of technology and lossy, compressed image formats. 

P.S. The tool was previously free with monthly limits, but the team recently introduced a paid subscription model to ensure the future viability of the tool. Jump on this deal before it's too late!

The interface was clean and easy to navigate, dark mode was a useful addition, and the tester reported very few usability problems outside an SVG resizing issue where images could overflow their containers. 

The bigger limitations were around product depth and presentation: the template library was extremely limited during testing, automatic text resizing for variable-length content still needed improvement, and clearer tutorials, broader format handling, preset variables, and more templates would make recurring bulk workflows more practical. 

Overall, the core workflow worked well and showed a solid foundation, but during our testing it still felt more like a focused bulk-image tool that needed additional product depth and polish than a replacement for broader design platforms.

comments.title: Awesome all-in-one tool that keeps getting better!
comments.comment:
I’ve been using FlexClip for quite a while now, and I’m honestly really happy with the direction the platform is heading.

What I love most is how fast the team updates everything. They’re constantly rolling out improvements, and whenever a new AI model drops, they’re usually super quick to integrate it. My absolute favorite feature has to be the workflow: being able to generate an AI video and then jump straight into the main editor to clean it up is a game-changer. It saves so much time since you don't have to switch between a dozen different tabs for video, images, voiceovers, and audio. It’s a true all-in-one setup.

That said, there are a couple of things that hold me back a bit in my daily use:

First, the "Long Video to Shorts" tool has some trouble with Arabic content. Whenever the source video is longer than 20 minutes or so, the generated subtitles start getting unreliable and pack a lot of errors. Second, the credit system is a bit heavy. Some of the AI features—especially the video generation—burn through credits way too fast, which makes frequent use pretty expensive.

If I could suggest two things to the team:

1. It would be amazing to see a dedicated AI filmmaking workflow. Imagine being able to create short films or animated series while keeping consistent characters and visual style from scene to scene. That would really set FlexClip apart from everyone else.

2. Please consider lowering the credit cost for the more demanding AI tools. It would make the platform a lot more accessible for creators who use it daily.

Overall, it’s a solid 4/5 for me right now. It’s already an excellent tool, and with a few tweaks, it’ll easily be a 5/5 product!

comments.title: Powerful tool with a lot of potential
comments.comment:
I had been waiting for this product for a long time, and overall FlexClip is a very useful video creation tool. The interface is clean, beginner-friendly and it makes it easy to create professional-looking videos quickly. For content creators, marketers and small businesses, it can save a lot of time.

However, there are a few areas that still need improvement.

The Text-to-Video feature is a great idea but sometimes it fails to generate scenes properly. Occasionally the process stops or produces incomplete results, which can interrupt the workflow. Improving the stability of this feature would make it much more reliable.

Another helpful addition would be a video length control option in the Text-to-Video tool. Being able to set the desired video duration would give creators better control over the final output.

The footage replacement workflow could also be improved. It would be great to have an easy “replace footage” option that automatically matches the current clip’s duration and position. Right now, replacing clips sometimes requires splitting or adjusting the timeline manually, which slows down editing.

Lastly, an audio/video layer lock option would be very useful. When editing complex timelines, it’s easy to accidentally move clips. A lock feature would prevent this and make editing much smoother.

Overall, FlexClip is a promising and powerful tool with a lot of potential. With a few improvements to stability and editing controls, it could become one of the best online video editors available.

I only wish there were a default “click to play” option for autoplay videos, something that could be enabled by default and turned off if not needed. Having that small feature would make a big difference in usability and viewer experience.

comments.title: Pretty decent tool..
comments.comment:
👋To provide some context to my opinions and what I'm comparing this too, I've been using Camtasia, Snagit and Techsmith tools for years and totally love their stability, intuitiveness and robustness. The only downside Techsmith has is the cost (but of course, you get what you pay for right) and they take a little too long to roll out new features. I also use Filmora a reasonable amount.
I've done  some  initial tests with ScreenToVideo and here are my thoughts..
➕ What I like:
Pretty good tool on the onset with a lightweight (loads fast) and polished feel.
Felt the robustness with this tool as recordings were done pretty fast with a fast render time and no glitches and productions were great.
Love the cursor effects, 'remove silence' feature, video effects and 'zoom and pan'.
Generally a nice set of features.
➖ Areas of improvement (and do forgive if something mentioned below is there but i haven't discovered it yet..still exploring):
To me, all the features or at least the way they're presnted..the UI could feel less 'cluttery' and a bit more intuitive, for instance: 1. I found myself trying to figure out what some of the symbols mean in the left and even in the right menu at the top when something is selected. And then, sometimes I see the same symbol on the right and on the left so it gets a bit confusing. It would be great to expand out the left menu to read what some of those symbols mean instead of having to move the cursor to hover over them every time (probably a toggle to keep the left menu expanded with the name of the symbol or contracted with just the symbol, would be nice). 
2. I'm still figuring out animations.
3. Think i recently found the 'undo' button but didn't yet see the 'redo' button though in the 'Edit' menu, and it wasn't noticeable as one of those quick action buttons.
4. Though i could split a recording, I couldn't figure out how to 'group' media or stitch back recordings together. As an extension to this, when media is split, it's hard to add cursor effects 'afterwards' since it adds only to the section that the playhead is on.
5. I couldn't figure out how to add a 'fade in;fade-out' effect for some of the video effects like a 'spotlight' so they could smoothly fade in and out instead of abruptly popping up.
6. Couldn't find 'callouts' or some stickers or 'basic' media anywhere (outside of the sketch tools). The callouts are essential for recordings.
💡 Would be nice to drag and drop animation and effects on clips, and be able to see them in their...just love that level of intuitiveness.
Overall, STV is a pretty decent tool though..I like it and would recommend it. Will definitely keep it for when i need something to record Camtasia or Snagit's editors..lol.
Keep evolving!

TIP if you're having trouble with redemption:
NOTE: After installing the plugin in the Chrome browser, when I entered the license key (redemption code from Appsumo) into Blurweb.ap, I kept getting an error message saying the license code was incorrect. The license key consists of four alphanumeric fields (Example: 1F78PQ16-2154550B-AJSDHJE5-15MHKD54). Unusually, a series of ,,,,  (Example: -15MHKD54,,,,) was appended to the end of the last license code block, which apparently does not belong there for activation.
 
I deleted these ,,,, from the key, and then the activation worked without any problems!! 
So: Copy the key from Appsumo, enter it in the app’s license field, and then delete the ,,,, at the end of the code!
Hope this works for future users as well. 
Five ***** so people will read this, not because of the complicated activation process.

comments.title: Animation works fine but a lot of developpment is need
comments.comment:
Animazer is emerging as a noteworthy video SaaS tool that has the potential to carve out a significant niche in the market. However, to truly realize its promise, several enhancements must be made, particularly the incorporation of artificial intelligence to provide users with more advanced features. The current offerings show potential, but they also highlight a few key areas where improvement is necessary.
One of the most pressing enhancements would be the ability to upload and modify fonts, including the option to integrate popular Google Fonts. This flexibility would allow users to personalize their videos more effectively, catering to diverse branding needs and aesthetic preferences. Unfortunately, the platform currently lacks this crucial feature, which limits creative expression.
Additionally, the animation tool faces significant limitations in its editing capabilities. The inability to adjust timeline frames restricts users from fine-tuning their projects, making the editing process cumbersome. The current editor is far too basic, leaving users with a sense of frustration regarding its functionality.
Several core limitations stand out:
1. Text cannot be added to all slides or images, reducing the ability to convey messages effectively throughout the video.
2. Users cannot move text and images up, down, or sideways, which hampers the ability to create visually appealing layouts.
3. The platform does not allow for the addition of more images or text beyond the animation, intro, or outro sections, which constrains content richness.
4. All animations are limited to just 15 seconds in length. It is too short
nevertheless ther is no really progress since last year. I rated 4 Tacos because the quality of the animation itself is fine
