comments.title: Nice, Simple Template-Based Video Tool
comments.comment:
At $25 for lifetime access to 10 HD downloads a month, this is a handy arrow to have in your quiver.
So, anyone expecting to make Oscar-worthy videos is looking in the wrong place - this is a collection of relatively basic editable templates into which you can upload your logo, different images, even a short audio track, depending on the template you choose. You can choose from a relatively small collection of fonts, although some templates don't allow this, and then change the colour of the text to match your brand. The system then uses the media and font/colour tweaks to modify the template to your specifications. Most of the templates are 5-20 seconds long.
There are plenty of templates to choose from - some just animate your logo, others make a slideshow of images, for when you add a new product to your e-commerce store, for example. Many of the templates are available in horizontal AND vertical mode, so you can be consistent over several platforms. The videos are simple but eye-catching, and they look quite professionally-made.
Considering the price, there's not much you can really complain about. The only annoyance I've found so far is that some of the vertical + horizontal templates have different levels of customization. For example, I liked a template called something like "Hand-drawn Logo Reveal" - thought it would be nice to add at the end of a longer YouTube/Instagram/TikTok video, so I customized the vertical version and spent 2 of my 20 monthly credits downloading it in HD only to find that the font can't be customized in the horizontal version of the same template, meaning that there will be inconsistency in the font if I choose to use it in the future. Annoying for a perfectionist, but not a fatal flaw.
So, overall, a nice little product. If you want to make a quick, low-effort Facebook Reel or an Instagram Story, you'll probably find a template you can use and get a ready-to-upload, respectable-looking short video in a few minutes that will look like you put a few hours' effort into it. And for $25 for 10 such videos a month, I recommend that absolutely anyone needing to do even just basic marketing consider signing up for this deal.

comments.title: Animated videos without starting from scratch
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Wideo has been around for a while, and you can feel that in the parts of the product that work well. If you want to make a simple animated explainer, promo video, onboarding video, or social video from a template, Wideo is great for the job.

It works very well as a template based animation tool. You pick a video structure, replace the text and visuals, add voiceover, and turn it into an explainer, promo, onboarding clip, or social post without animating every scene from scratch.

Some of the newer AI pages needed clearer wording. During my retest, the blog to video tool only captured part of the article I tested. The team explained that the tool summarizes a post and creates a short promotional video meant to send people back to the original article. So I would describe it as a blog promo tool rather than a full article to video converter.

The AI Avatars page could have been clearer during my test. The team clarified that AI Avatars are a custom solution, not a regular dashboard feature users can create on their own. Since it still appears on the landing page, buyers may not immediately understand that difference.

The Text to Speech page also slightly confused me. It was branded as Wideo, but the main Try Now button sent me to Speechify through an affiliate link. The team clarified that Wideo does offer text to speech inside the editor, so buyers should look at the editor itself for the actual Wideo feature.

The team also said a new version of the app is close and that the current legacy dashboard dependencies will be replaced as part of that migration. They also confirmed the missing license notices in the bundled JavaScript file have been addressed.

Overall, I would look at Wideo for what it already does well: template based animated videos, simple explainers, promo videos, and branded social content. The main thing is to understand the difference between the regular editor, the AI features inside the app, and custom services like AI Avatars. For explainers, promos, onboarding clips, and social posts, the editor and template library are strong reasons to consider it.

comments.title: BuzzHooks Review: Ok Results, but Expensive Credits and Questions About Future Model Access
comments.comment:
Update: 10/16/26

upgraded from 3 stars to 4 stars as they have added image gen models that can do 4K.

Old Review:

BuzzHooks offers AI image and video generation, but its pricing is higher than some competing platforms I use. The video results are okay, but I feel the platform is only halfway there in terms of functionality.

1. Image Generation Limitations

Video generation lets you select individual models, resolutions, and durations. Image generation allows styles like Cinematic, but I couldn't find options to select individual image models or resolutions.

I'd like to see image models with 4K resolution options. These are important for character sheets, preserving details, and maintaining character consistency in AI videos. You absolutely don’t need 4K video, although it would be nice to have. However, 4K images are essential because they capture the pore-level skin detail and realism needed for high-quality character sheets, which can then be used to generate videos in 720p or 1080p. When using 1080p source images, too much fine skin texture and detail can be lost during video generation, especially in scenes where the character is farther from the camera. This is why 4K image resolution is so important, even when the final video is generated at a lower resolution.


2. Included Models vs. BYOK

Models like seedance 2.5 will not use your ltd credits. Other ltd deals outside this platform do not have this issue. I have ltds that give me access to use my ai credits with any model.

Models accepting included LTD credits:
WAN 3.0 Standard, WAN 3.0 Prime, Seedance 2.0, and Minimax H3. All support up to 1080p.

Models requiring BYOK:
Seedance 2.5, Seedance 2.0 Fast, and Seedance 2.0 Mini.

BYOK means Bring Your Own Key. You connect and pay an external API provider separately.

What the founder confirmed:

The founder explained that regular AI credits and BYOK credits are separate allowances. BYOK still uses BuzzHooks credits because of processing and workflow costs.

Tier 4 offers unlimited BYOK credits, but external API generation costs still apply.

He also stated that future supported models would remain accessible through BYOK. However, I haven't found confirmation that newer models will continue accepting regular included LTD credits.

**3. Future Models, API, and MCP**

My concern is that newer models could eventually require BYOK while regular LTD credits remain limited to older models.

The deal terms also indicate that future AI models may require additional purchases or discounted add-ons.

My questions are:

- Will newer image, video, and LLM models accept regular Tier 4 credits?
- Will future model upgrades require BYOK or add-ons?
- Will included credits work through API/MCP?
- What happened to MCP, which was estimated for release two weeks back in September?
- Is a public API still planned?

4. Video Generation Credit Pricing

I had trouble finding detailed pricing before purchasing. I manually went through the model dropdowns, durations, and resolutions to document the costs. I'm sharing them because I couldn't find another review with this information, and I don't want others to have to do the same work.

These models use regular included LTD credits, NOT BYOK.

WAN 3.0 STANDARD

10s 480p: 160 credits | 12s 480p: 190 credits | 15s 480p: 240 credits | 30s 480p: 470 credits

10s 720p: 290 credits | 12s 720p: 350 credits | 15s 720p: 440 credits | 30s 720p: 870 credits

10s 1080p: 520 credits | 12s 1080p: 630 credits | 15s 1080p: 780 credits | 30s 1080p: 1,560 credits

WAN 3.0 PRIME

10s 480p: 220 credits | 12s 480p: 260 credits | 15s 480p: 320 credits | 30s 480p: 640 credits

10s 720p: 410 credits | 12s 720p: 490 credits | 15s 720p: 610 credits | 30s 720p: 1,220 credits

10s 1080p: 730 credits | 12s 1080p: 870 credits | 15s 1080p: 1,090 credits | 30s 1080p: 2,180 credits

MINIMAX H3 (10s | 12s | 15s)

10s 480p: 120 credits | 12s 480p: 150 credits | 15s 480p: 180 credits

10s 720p: 180 credits | 12s 720p: 210 credits | 15s 720p: 270 credits

10s 1080p: 320 credits | 12s 1080p: 380 credits | 15s 1080p: 470 credits

Prices are from my account and may change.

5. Tier 4 and Final Thoughts

Because of the high credit costs, I'd consider Tier 4 for regular video generation, but even 10,000 monthly credits disappear quickly. One 30-second WAN Prime 1080p video costs 2,180 credits, allowing only four complete generations at those settings.

My 3-star rating mainly reflects the missing image model and resolution controls. Video generation offers more flexibility, but image generation needs improvement. I'd also like clarity about future models, included credits, API, and MCP. Hopefully, this detailed pricing helps other buyers make an informed decision.

BuzzHooks is an AI video tool for people who need short product videos, ad ideas, UGC style clips, and quick promo content.

BuzzHooks works best when you start from hooks and guided formats. You can use a hook, a preset, a product video app, or Cinema Studio to shape the video before generating. You are not staring at an empty prompt box trying to invent the whole video from nothing. You get a starting structure, generate the clip, then adjust from there.

A few small bugs came up during review which the team addressed very fast, including a Google sign in which is already live.

Buyers should understand the credit system. Product Studio videos use credits, but BuzzHooks gives you several settings to control how much you spend on each generation. You can make tradeoffs between quality, speed, model choice, and output type depending on what you are trying to create. This is genuinely helpful because sometimes you want the best possible version, and sometimes you just want to test a rough idea before spending more credits.

Overall, BuzzHooks is worth considering if you want a faster way to create high quality short marketing videos and product ads from proven hooks, presets, and guided video apps. comments.title: A complete localization workflow for multi-speaker videos
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What I like about Voicina is that I can take one video through the whole localization process without moving it between several different tools.

I uploaded a video and got a full transcript with speaker labels and timestamps. From there I generated subtitles, translated them into Spanish and Arabic, and Arabic was displayed correctly from right to left. I then created a French dub with a different voice for each speaker.

That multi-speaker workflow is especially useful for interviews, podcasts and other videos where more than one person is talking. Localization is not just about translating the words. You also need to keep the speakers separate and make the dubbed version easy to follow. Voicina handled that within the same project.

The editing tools worked well too. I could correct terms with find and replace, generate a summary, and export the results as SRT, TXT and JSON. I also exported a video with the subtitles burned in, and that worked as expected.

When I first tested Voicina, there was no developer access. The team has since added an API and webhooks, which makes it more useful if you want to automate transcription or localization workflows instead of uploading everything manually.

One thing to watch is credit usage. Transcription and subtitles use relatively few credits, but dubbing and voice generation consume considerably more, especially if you're translating long videos into several languages. I would choose a tier based on how many minutes you actually expect to dub each month rather than just the amount of video you plan to transcribe.

Also, the dubbing does not alter the speaker's mouth movements to match the translated language. It keeps the original video and adjusts the dubbed speech to fit the timing instead.

Overall, Voicina solves a bigger problem for me than simply generating subtitles. I can take one video, transcribe it, translate it, create subtitles and produce a multi-speaker dub without rebuilding the project in several different applications. For anyone regularly publishing the same content in multiple languages, that is the main reason I would get it.

comments.title: Does what it says it does -- with a few rendering quirks
comments.comment:
First the good news, it does what it says it does!   I did a screen recording with voice and then had VideoMule transcribe it and then add an AI avatar narrator.  Really there was nothing to "edit", because it came thru the first time.  The video timeline editor looks a lot like others I have seen, so anyone can pick it up easily enough.
Now the problems I had
1.  Local Render fails with a brief popup error for a 2.5 minute video no matter which computer I use.  I guess it's Cloud Render for me
2.  It took a lot of processing time to do the 2.5 minute video, I think a lot of that was with the avatar generation.  I probably won't use that feature again.
3.   I was disappointed that it was not a true Screen Recorder.  It did not record what I was doing in Microsoft Access desktop application.  Was this not part of the description? Maybe I misunderstood.  As such there are very long pauses where nothing seems to be happening on the video because I was switching between the desktop app (which was not recorded)

comments.title: Great voiceovers from a silent screen recording, editor needs polish
comments.comment:
I used VideoMule to turn a silent screen recording of my SaaS (WP Foreman) into a voiced 3-minute comparison video for YouTube. The end result is good: the voiceover sounds natural, it lines up with what's happening on screen, and it saved me from recording and editing narration myself. That alone is worth it for product and help videos.

What could be better is the script editor. Edits to a line didn't always save when I pressed Return or clicked away, so I had to double-check each change. Deleting a line is permanent with no undo, and when I deleted the intro line it relabeled the next line as the intro, which caught me out. With a little more polish on editing it would be an easy 5 stars.

Overall: great output, editing needs work. I'd use it again for the next video.

comments.title: Finally! The Faceless Software Review Creator I've Been Searching For!
comments.comment:
I've been searching for software like VideoMule for years, and I believe I may have finally found what I've been looking for!

As a content creator building Creators Academy IO, I've always wanted to produce professional software reviews, product demonstrations, and educational tutorials without having to appear on camera or record my own narration.

I've purchased other software, including Dale and Layerpath, hoping to accomplish this, but neither ultimately met my requirements.

**What makes VideoMule different?**

It's not simply another screen recorder. VideoMule is designed to handle much of the work that happens AFTER recording.

You can demonstrate software on your screen, have AI analyze the recording, generate a script explaining what's happening, synchronize AI narration, and edit everything into a professional video.

That's exactly the workflow I've been searching for!

After purchasing Tier 3, I spent time exploring the platform and studying its tutorials to better understand its capabilities.

**Here's what impresses me most:**

**1. AI-generated scripts:** Rather than trying to explain everything while demonstrating software, I can concentrate on showing the features and let AI help create the explanation afterward.

**2. Synchronized AI voiceovers:** VideoMule can align narration with what's happening on screen. The lifetime plan also advertises unlimited standard AI voiceovers.

**3. Custom script templates:** This is one of my favorite discoveries! I can create reusable templates for software reviews, product demonstrations, and educational lessons, with custom introductions, instructions, and conclusions.

**4. Script editing:** I can refine the AI-generated explanations and incorporate my own opinions, observations, pros, cons, and recommendations. That's essential because I want to create genuine reviews, not just generic tutorials.

**5. Video editing:** The timeline editor includes zoom effects, callouts, captions, graphics, branding, and other tools that help viewers follow along.

**6. Unlimited local rendering:** I appreciate being able to render videos locally without consuming monthly cloud-render credits.

**7. AI avatars and multilingual capabilities:** These offer additional opportunities to create educational content for different audiences without constantly appearing on camera.

**What I'd like to see improved:**

First, I'd love additional integrations with JoggAI and Unmixr AI.

Some longtime AppSumo customers purchased HeyGen when it was available as a lifetime deal. Many of us missed that opportunity and later purchased JoggAI as an alternative.

Likewise, many AppSumo customers already own Unmixr AI instead of subscribing to ElevenLabs.

Allowing customers to connect these alternatives, where API access permits, would make VideoMule even more valuable.

Second, I'd appreciate greater clarity around the one-time video-analysis minutes.

My Tier 3 license includes 60 monthly upload minutes but only 120 lifetime analysis minutes. Understanding exactly what happens when those analysis minutes are exhausted is important for creators planning to produce videos long-term.

I'd also love to see an official software-review template that helps structure feature demonstrations, pros and cons, and final assessments.

**My overall impression:**

VideoMule has one of the most promising approaches I've encountered for creating faceless software reviews.

What excites me most is the potential to transform a simple screen recording into a narrated, edited educational video without the traditional production process.

I've activated my Tier 3 license, explored the interface, and researched the available tutorials. I haven't completed my first full video yet, so this is an initial assessment rather than a final judgment of production quality.

However, I'm genuinely excited about what I've discovered.

If the finished videos deliver on the capabilities demonstrated in the tutorials, VideoMule could become one of the most important tools in my Creators Academy IO production workflow.

I'm looking forward to putting it through real-world testing and seeing how the platform continues to develop!

comments.title: gkrev
comments.comment:
Pros
- Neat and tidy interface
- Smart and very user-friendly design to have the whole plan broken down into different stages and steps, making the entire process more approachable and the content more readable - unlike many similar apps which are basically a word processor with some template headings and sections 
- Pricing-wise, I appreciate the discounted price offered by taking out fancy functions like collaborators which I don't need. It'd be a great deal if they continue to develop the app and make the business planning a living and evolving document/process (the current design is more for one-off use)

Cons:
- only 1 idea slot; minimum 3 idea slots would be really useful, not so much for working on multiple ideas for different clients like professional writers/planners do, but for comparing different scenarios of the same idea or similar ideas (eg. different budgets projections, market/customers focus, marketing/partnership priorities)
- whiteboard is not included, contrary to what was promised (but I already knew before purchase). It'd be nice to at least offer a lite version of whiteboard for non-premium plan users
- no roadmap, no idea what/if the development team is working on improvement and new features

To step up their game, 
- offer minimum 3 idea slots
- provide a roadmap of what they are and will be working on
- more professionally-looking cover pages and more sophisticated layouts for the business plan export
- option to use free stock image/icon available online (instead of having to upload images for each)
- undo button/version history
- "discard or save" pop-up when we close with unsaved changes
- more colours and a collapse/expand function for sticky notes
- include a branding section and a marketing campaign section, as well as an overall milestones section (a business also plans for those, not just the financial setup and projections, which are nicely structured and included)
- Direct Costs and Other Overheads needs to add the option to combine items of the same category/group in graphs (i.e. like how it is in Startup Costs) 
- for all the financial entries, allow a selection of the exact time period, instead of just the options of onetime/monthly average/quarterly/yearly (which is not helpful for seasonal business)

Overall, I think ideabuddy has started out pretty well with unique design and strength of their app. Hope that the company will put in continuous efforts to develop and offer more great features (as pointed out above), to give more value to the app - an app that goes beyond one-off use and remains useful as a business grows.

comments.title: Idea Buddy is Secretly Amazing!
comments.comment:
I purchased IdeaBuddy because I needed a central location to log and structure my business and service ideas. While I could have used a Word document or a Notion database, IdeaBuddy’s appeal lies in being purpose-built for this task with the bonus of some AI bells and whistles.

After thoroughly exploring the platform, I quickly realized it doesn’t just have AI bells and whistles… it has a full AI symphony orchestra built in! The AI implementation is truly impressive.

One standout feature is the AI-generated template. However, calling it a "template" undersells its true value.

When starting a new idea, you describe your business or service in one clear sentence explaining what it is, what it offers, and who it’s for. You can also specify the business location and current stage: Idea, Launch, or Growth.

Next, it asks, "Would you like to use a template? Use an AI-generated template tailored to your business idea, or start from scratch if you prefer full control."

Initially, I was skeptical because templates often feel generic and require a lot of tweaking, often making more work. But since my idea was just a fun test concept, I decided to try it. Although generating the AI template costs 20 AI requests, in the end it was worth it.

IdeaBuddy did NOT generate a template. It crafted an incredibly accurate, personalized business plan from ONE sentence! It felt like it tapped directly into my brain and pulled the details right outta my noggin! There’s nothing generic about it.

That said, quality input is key. A well-thought-out, clear initial sentence describing your idea, offer, and audience is essential. With that, the AI delivers a plan that’s over 90% spot on, requiring only minimal tweaks.

Here are my recommendations for new users and the dev team:

New Users

1) Start with the Guide. There’s little initial guidance, but after testing, the Guide is the best starting point.

2) Definitely choose the AI-generated "template"—it’s NOT a template, and you’ll thank me later.

Suggestions for the Dev Team

1) I would move away from describing the AI assisted guide content as an AI Generated “Template.” It’s so much more than a “template.” It’s an AI Assisted Business Plan generated from one sentence. 🤯

2) When using the option to generate business name ideas with AI, also offer the option for AI-generated slogan ideas. I had to use Copilot separately for this.

3) Integrate AI-powered market research tools within the platform, such as growth rate analysis for your product/service in your market. This keeps users engaged without switching apps.

4) Similarly, add AI options for defining Total Addressable Market and other key metrics. More in-platform AI research means easier workflows for us and more revenue for you from AI request top-ups after we run out from all the research requests. 😄

5) Enhance the Validation feature so that it automatically pulls answers from the Guide or Plan minimizing our data entry for answers it can gather itself using AI. In addition, how about an AI agent that evaluates the Guide/Plan content and walks users through Validation steps explaining insights, uncertainties, and what needs clarification, until it can ultimately determine the validity of the idea. And hey, don’t forget to put my name somewhere on the website to thank me for these awesome ideas! 😉

comments.title: Good job
comments.comment: I've been using Headway for just over a week and it's been a great experience so far. Although there are specific books and authors I would like to see, I have been able to find good alternatives. I like being able to switch between reading and audio modes. The voices vary and I don't think they're as robotic as some have written  If you enjoy reading for pleasure and listening to long-version audiobooks, this is not for you. If you want to get the point, take a trial run at a book, while maybe digesting all you needed anyway, Headway is it. I would just like to see an expansion of titles;  those written in native Spanish in my case. I'll be using this app often.

comments.title: Get me 'reading' again!
comments.comment: I used to be an avid reader but somehow life always gets in the way these days. I don't enjoy longform audio books because I only ever have 20-30 minute snippets of time and you lose the sense of flow jumping in and out in such short bursts. I love that with Headway I can put something on whilst i'm driving somewhere for 20 minutes and get an entire book summary in that time, so I feel like I've both learned and achieved something. The summaries could be a little bit clearer/better at times, but overall, I think the concept and delivery is brilliant and I am using it loads.

comments.title: Good app room for improvement
comments.comment:
Good app to 'learn' some important books. Missing some major languages in voice and text (Portuguese language - pt-PT - hopefully is coming). It already has the top 3/5 languages. Portuguese is no. 6.

Sometimes it feels like some important things from the book are missing. The app should have a button to choose between a 20-minute mode and a 40-minute mode. The 40-minute option would cover much more and leave room for examples too. If content is king, it fell a bit short in that regard. I know the app’s purpose is 15-minute reads, but users would get more value if we like a book and want to know more about it.

comments.title: Great idea, not that great result.
comments.comment:
Headway is a great idea that turn out to be a good app.
Being able to tap into ideas in 15min is great. I've been using it a lot.
In my opinion the problems are:
- AI voice, very good, but one is able to understand that a machine is speaking.
- Probably AI written, from Sapiens: “Roughly 300,000 years later, matter and energy evolved into atoms and molecules, revealing the secrets of chemistry. Biology first appeared 3.8 billion years ago with the emergence of the first organisms.” So biology appeared 3.5 billion years earlier than atoms and molecules. This is an example of something that doesn't make sense, there are others.
- Regardless of the scope and dimension of the book, the number of key points and length is the same. There are books that should have a more in depth summary, like Thinking fast and slow, or Behave, or others alike.
Having said this, for the price this is great, even if only as a way to check if a particular book is worth reading.

PROS:
- Read or Listen
- 15 min audio summaries 
- Popular titles

CON:

- Are they AI voices? Some of them sound very disconnected. Especially the US guy who insists on dredging the bottom of his range.

comments.title: Great summaries

It offers a wide choice of books but I'd love more of scientific or history books. Would like, when I do a search, to have a sign in the result list that shows if I already have put the book in my library (or even finished reading it) & maybe possibility to have different categories/shelves in the library; also to do a search in my library (instead of in the whole of the app). Don't understand what the Download option does as the application doesn't seem to work when offline (when I did a search, it didn't show the one book I had downloaded, said "No summary found"; showed only Finished ones; maybe I must get more familiar with the app). I had one Short were it didn't pick up my choice (between self-confidence, self-awareness & self-discipline), it always showed self-awareness. I also don't know how to navigate the shorts. The section showing latest summaries is a bit short, can I sort books by date added to check only those added since I last had a look? I don't know how to change the "Categories you're interested in" (I have selected the max 3 goals). But, as I've said, I need more time to explore. I think the summaries are well-written & the app encourages you to discover more & improve yourself.

Andrew is passionate about his work. He is a genuine and sincere person who loves adding value to his customers and always finding new ways to improve Better Sheets and support for his work. comments.title: Promising Product - 2 Key Features Needed for 5 Tacos
comments.comment:
The software is working well. The creation of videos is fairly easy and it has more/different features than other tools e.g. MapDirector (Freeware). From the tools I tried to create animated travel maps, AvoMap was the best so far. To make it really awesome (and for me to give 5 tacos) two important features are still missing:
1) Reordering of route segments.
2) Upload of GPX data to each route segment so that you truly can create completely custom travel videos or videos of sports activities like triathlon. Or hiking up a mountain and paragliding down. This feature would open up so many more possibilities and really make AvoMap stand out. It was wished for by users in the feature forum multiple times in different requests but so far rejected or ignored. :( I hope this changes!

Another thing that would be nice to have, is the upload of videos or images like in MapDirector, but I do not really need that feature for now.

comments.title: Impressive tool, but even more impressive UI/UX!
comments.comment:
I was super impressed with AvoMap. This isn't just another map generator; it's a storytelling mapping product.

What I love is how clean and easy to use the product was. For Tobias being a "one man band," I am deeply impressed with the UI/UX.  The waypoints and markers are elegant and don't clutter up the screen, so the focus stays on the journey itself. Plus, the creative freedom is fantastic. I can change the colors, add my own logo, and even drop in custom icons for little landmarks along the way, all without needing to be a developer. It's almost like editing a video.

My only tiny wish is that there was a way to have more control over the speed of the animated bubble as it travels along the path. Sometimes I want to slow it down to really show off a particular part of the journey.....that's the only thing I feel is missing.

Honestly, for the value on AppSumo, this is a complete no-brainer. If you create any kind of content that involves travel or visualizing a route, you need this. Currently I don't really have that need, but I still purchased it and I'm keeping it! Five stars, without a doubt.

comments.title: A uniquely multimodal speaking practice platform
comments.comment:
I tried Tough Tongue AI for English speaking practice, specifically for IELTS preparation. I ran two pre-built scenarios and also built my own custom one. Here's what I found.

The good:

The interactive, voice-first experience is different from anything else I've used. Every session feels like an experience, not just a chatbot with a mic button. The voices are natural and conversational, and that the agent can display slides, cue cards, MCQs, and timers on screen while talking is something I haven't seen in any other speaking-practice tool. For guided speaking practice, this multimodal display during a conversation is a real differentiator.

The issues:

I noticed lag on some responses, and in my custom scenario the agent was reading emotion tags aloud ("enthusiastic," "curious") along with the actual dialogue, which broke the immersion. I haven't dug into the settings and customizations enough yet.

Feature requests:

1. Pronunciation practice mode with audio playback comparison. Drills where the agent says a target sentence, the learner repeats, the platform compares and scores, highlights which words or phonemes were off, and lets the learner try again would be amazing. 

2. Better onboarding for educators. Right now, the landing page, library, and templates are all sales/coaching/hiring oriented. A dedicated "For Educators" section with more education-related scenarios  would be great. Also, a class roster view with all users, their session history, time-on-task, score trends over time etc to share with them. 

I truly hope that this product survives and thrives, because it is unique. The multimodal awareness, voice-first approach with live visual artifacts during conversation has real potential for language education. This could become the go-to platform for AI-assisted speaking practice. Keep an eye on this one.

comments.title: Powerful AI Voice Agent With Real Business Potential
comments.comment:
2026-09-29 Update: Here is a video with an updated demo of a couple of our Tough Tongue agents where you can hear the system audio: https://youtu.be/FC4446Mh5YY
============================
Tough Tongue AI stands out because it goes beyond a typical chatbot or AI Agent. It functions as an AI agent with voice capabilities that can connect to phone lines, participate in meetings, respond in real time, and be trained on specific information or frameworks. I completely agree with jonah58w - this has real business operations implications. 

Here is a video where I share our experience using Tough Tongue:
https://youtu.be/IXP3jEw_1fs

What impressed me most is the potential for customization and the wide range of use cases. Tough Tongue AI can be shaped around an organization’s language, processes, and expertise. That makes it especially interesting for sales teams, consultants, service providers, and organizations that need to extend the capacity and effectiveness of existing team members (even if the team is you).

The ability to train an agent like “Connie” on a particular framework is a compelling feature. With the right setup, an AI agent could help qualify leads, answer routine questions, support meetings, provide information, and create a more consistent experience for clients or customers.

Pros:
🙋🏽‍♀️ Voice-based interaction feels more natural than text-only chatbots and other phone/voice agents
🙋🏽‍♀️ Can connect with phone lines and participate in meetings
🙋🏽‍♀️ Trainable on specific business knowledge and frameworks
🙋🏽‍♀️ Potential to support sales, customer service, lead qualification, team admin/coordination
🙋🏽‍♀️ Could significantly expand capacity for small teams and solo entrepreneurs
🙋🏽‍♀️ Broad range of possible applications across industries

Cons
🤷🏽‍♀️ The setup process for a scenario is very complicated - with the TT AI MCP 
🤷🏽‍♀️ As with all AI, requires thoughtful setup and training to perform well
🤷🏽‍♀️ The quality of the experience depends heavily on the information provided to the agent
🤷🏽‍♀️ Organizations should test accuracy, tone, privacy, and escalation processes before deploying it widely
🤷🏽‍♀️ Some use cases may require additional integrations or technical configuration

Tough Tongue AI is not a “set it and forget it” tool. Like any AI agent, it needs clear instructions, reliable source material, and ongoing review. However, for anyone looking to explore voice-based automation and create a more capable digital representative, it offers an impressive range of possibilities.

I see the greatest value for businesses and organizations that receive recurring questions, manage a steady flow of leads, or need to make their expertise available beyond normal working hours. With the right implementation, Tough Tongue AI could become more than a virtual assistant; it could serve as an extension of the team.

Also, the team is very responsive - we had an issue on Friday night, it was addressed by Saturday. This is one of those tools that has the potential of tools like Teable - you will regret missing this deal...if they stay on their current trajectory, it will only get better.

comments.title: From AI Roleplay to a Real Multilingual Business Voice Agent
comments.comment:
Great potential for multilingual AI voice agents, with a very responsive team

I purchased Tier 3 and have been testing Tough Tongue AI as the voice layer for our Stella business-development system, starting with a multilingual AI receptionist for our PCB business.

What impressed me most is the flexibility. We can build custom scenarios, use BYOK, integrate through API, embed the agent by iframe without the Tough Tongue branding, connect our own Twilio/Telnyx SIP numbers, extract structured data after calls, and support cold transfer to a human phone number or SIP extension.

Multilingual support is particularly important for us. After some testing and model adjustment, Galaxy Medium was able to handle Chinese conversations and respond naturally. We are also planning to test English, Chinese, and Japanese language switching within the same call.

The founder team has been very responsive and transparent when I asked detailed technical questions about white-labeling, SIP, transfers, BYOK pricing, language switching, barge-in, and business-hours handling. That level of support gives me much more confidence in building this into a real business workflow.

There are still areas I would like to see improved, especially native warm transfer, built-in business-hours routing, easier multilingual voice configuration, and CNAME/subdomain support. Accurate recognition of PCB part numbers, revisions, and other alphanumeric data is also something we are continuing to test and optimize.

Overall, Tough Tongue AI is much more than a role-play or speaking-practice tool. It has the foundation to become a practical voice and meeting-agent platform for real business operations. For our use case, the Tier 3 lifetime deal offers very good value, especially with BYOK and white-label embedding.

Looking forward to seeing the platform continue to develop.

My experience with Tough Tongue AI is mixed.

At first, I was actually quite positive. If you set up a conversation and use the standard voice functionality, it works well. The voice interaction feels good and I really like the idea behind the product.

The problems start when I add a **video avatar**. Once I enable the video avatar, it simply does not work properly anymore. I have checked my microphone and camera settings several times, so the issue does not appear to be on my side. I also tried using the support bot to fix the problem, but unfortunately it was not able to resolve it.

When I upload and use **my own custom avatar**, I also notice that the whole conversation becomes noticeably slower. For a tool that is supposed to simulate realistic conversations, this delay has a big impact on the experience.

Another issue is that my **AppSumo points/credits suddenly disappeared**, which I find quite concerning.

I also think the way the minutes and plans are structured is confusing. I purchased **500 minutes for Personal Use**, but if you want to use the product for an Organization, you apparently need to purchase minutes separately again. This was not clear to me when purchasing and I think this should be explained much more transparently.

Overall, I think Tough Tongue is a very good idea and it has a lot of potential. When the basic voice functionality works, I can really see the value of the product.

However, **this is my personal experience and opinion at this moment, not my final review**. Before writing my final AppSumo review, I would first like these issues to be investigated and resolved.

How these problems are handled and whether they can actually be fixed will also influence my final review. I genuinely want to give the product a fair chance, because I like the concept, but at the moment these issues need to be resolved first.

UPDATE: 5/5 Tacos 🌮🌮🌮🌮🌮

I want to update my previous feedback because my experience with the support team completely changed my impression.

Within less than an hour, I received help and basically all of my questions and issues were resolved. I’m genuinely impressed by how quickly they responded and how clearly they explained everything.

In the end, a large part of the confusion came from information I simply didn’t know yet, especially around the Personal vs Organization setup, the AppSumo minutes, and how the balance is allocated.

Once this was explained properly, everything made much more sense.

The support was fast, personal and helpful, and they took my concerns seriously instead of just giving me a standard answer.

So I definitely want to correct my earlier impression:

Great concept, very responsive support, and they helped me get everything sorted very quickly.

For me, that deserves 5 out of 5 tacos.

I’m now much more confident about continuing to use Tough Tongue AI and testing it further for realistic interview and conversation simulations.

comments.title: Bridges a huge gap in the market
comments.comment:
What stands out to me about Tough Tongue is that it addresses a gap I think exists in AI right now. AI keeps getting more powerful for advanced users. We can spin up agents, automate workflows, build software, conduct research, and connect tools together. Meanwhile, a lot of businesses are using basic chatbots nobody wants to use or AI systems employees have to learn. Tough Tongue feels like a bridge between those two worlds.

Instead of requiring someone to become an “AI power user,” it packages agentic capabilities around real business interactions—phone calls, meetings, sales conversations, demos, training, coaching, and customer interactions. 

That’s where I think the next stage of AI adoption is headed. It’s not just about more powerful models; it’s about making that power usable by normal businesses in the environments where work and human interactions actually happen.

Tough Tongue is one of the first products I’ve used that seems to really address that. With features like calling into a web call and live lip synced avatar. Heads up though the lip sync has three choices that range in quality and add extra usage from .5x to 2x.

It’s definitely not fully polished yet, and if you want to do more advanced things there can still be a learning curve, especially if you’re new to agentic systems. That said, the customer support has been excellent. They’ve already jumped in, explained what was happening, and fixed the issues I ran into a couple of times.

comments.title: One of the more impressive AI tools we’ve tested in months
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

First time in months a tool genuinely blew our testing team away. Tough Tongue AI lets you spin up AI conversation scenarios for sales practice, interviews, coaching, lead-qualification calls, and more in seconds, and the range of features and use cases is huge. It also includes team workspaces, course creation, meeting workflows, and customizable AI agents. The UI and UX are excellent and easy to navigate even without heavy in-app guides, and during our testing the overall experience felt polished, powerful, and surprisingly easy to use.

On first test, we hit only minor issues. Voice cloning wouldn't save for us, and the Partner confirmed it is reviewing the save flow and validation requirements. The assistant captions also scroll by quickly, making them difficult to review during fast conversations, and the Partner is already working on improving caption readability. Custom avatars, which initially appeared to be missing, are actually already supported through uploaded images or video. 

None of these were deal-breakers during the testing stage, and some may have changed since the version we tested. If you and your team lean heavily on AI, you'll probably burn through the monthly minutes quickly, but based on our experience, Tough Tongue AI is an amazing, powerful product and one we highly recommend.

comments.title: Strong Planning Depth with Room for Improvement
comments.comment:
I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Our testing team found PrometAI easy to navigate overall, with a good loading experience, helpful guided walkthrough, and no functional bugs during the testing stage. Its strongest value is the combination of AI-assisted business planning, financial projections, valuation, scenario analysis, and pitch deck creation in one workflow. Classic Mode was noticeably clearer than the more crowded Journey experience.

During testing, our biggest concern was that generation happened with limited upfront control, which could produce a first draft that felt too generic for the intended audience. The Partner has since built an optional pre-generation step for details such as business stage, purpose, tone, differentiation, target customer, funding, and custom instructions, while deliberately keeping the faster generate-first workflow as the default based on its user research.

The version we tested also produced AI imagery that sometimes felt generic for investor-facing material and did not provide the depth of brand-system controls some professional users may want, so we would still recommend reviewing and tailoring generated output before using it externally. 

The Partner allows images to be regenerated or replaced, has deeper brand controls on its roadmap, and reported that a more standardized 14-section lender/SBA-style template was in final QA following the test.

comments.title: Powerful Strategy Tool, but the Financial Model Needs Better Synchronization
comments.comment:
PrometAI is one of those tools that made me more impressed the deeper I got into it, but also more cautious.

I tested it using a fictional multi-location convenience-store company called Survival Stop. My goal was not to build a pretty startup pitch deck. I wanted to see whether PrometAI could handle realistic operating economics, multi-location P&Ls, margin pressure, labor, shrink, foodservice, CAPEX, valuation, and scenario planning.

There is a lot to like.

The strategic framework is excellent. PrometAI generated useful material around mission, vision, stakeholders, SWOT, PESTEL, VRIO, Porter’s Five Forces, risks, roadmaps, responsibilities, and task ownership. The assignment of responsibilities across CFO, COO, CIO, CPO, etc. was especially interesting because I can see this becoming useful for management training or even AI-agent training.

The tool also became much more relevant once I corrected the assumptions. I was able to build a much more realistic convenience-store model with roughly $18M in annual revenue, thin margins, operating expense pressure, and a $300K CAPEX baseline.

Where PrometAI lost points was financial consistency.

I found situations where updated assumptions were correctly saved in one part of the model but older assumptions remained in other parts of the generated presentation. For example, the recalibrated model reflected the corrected revenue and cost assumptions in some screens, while the downloaded PDF still contained older revenue projections and prior revenue-mix assumptions on several financial pages. That means you really need to audit the finished output instead of assuming that every section has refreshed correctly.

That is a serious limitation for a tool positioned around financial planning and valuation.
I also found that the AI regeneration feature can overwrite carefully entered assumptions with its own defaults. Once I learned that, manual editing worked better, but there is definitely a learning curve.

What I like:
•	Very strong strategic-analysis framework 
•	Excellent depth compared with a typical AI business-plan generator 
•	Good risk, task, responsibility, and roadmap structure 
•	Useful scenario and financial modeling concepts 
•	Potentially excellent for consulting, training, and management development 
•	Surprisingly adaptable to an industry it was clearly not built specifically for 

What needs improvement:
•	Financial recalibration needs to propagate consistently throughout the entire model 
•	Regeneration should not overwrite custom assumptions without warning 
•	Final presentations need stronger synchronization with saved financial inputs 
•	Some startup-oriented assumptions need manual correction for established businesses 
•	Users should not have to hunt for which version of a number is actually authoritative 

I’m giving PrometAI 4 tacos because there is a lot of depth and genuine value here. However, the financial synchronization issues keep me from giving it 5. If PrometAI can ensure that recalibrated assumptions flow consistently through every financial statement, valuation, and generated presentation, this could easily become a 5-taco product.

Ik ben TidyCal gaan gebruiken om mijn afspraken makkelijker te laten inplannen en daar ben ik heel blij mee.

Wat voor mij direct werkt, is de eenvoud. Ik heb mijn agenda gekoppeld en binnen korte tijd stond de basis. Klanten kunnen nu zelf een moment kiezen, wat mij veel heen en weer mailen scheelt. Dat geeft rust en overzicht.

Wat ik ook prettig vind, is dat ik verschillende soorten afspraken kan aanmaken, zoals een kennismakingsgesprek, loopbaanspreekuur en vervolggesprekken. Zo kan ik mijn aanbod duidelijk neerzetten en zelf de regie houden over mijn planning.

Er zijn ook een paar punten die voor mij nog beter zouden mogen.

Zo zou ik het fijn vinden om afspraken een eigen kleur te kunnen geven in mijn agenda, zodat ik in één oogopslag zie wat voor soort afspraak het is.

Daarnaast zou ik graag meer flexibiliteit zien in de e-mailflows. Op dit moment kun je alleen mails versturen na het plannen van een afspraak, terwijl ik juist ook een reminder vooraf handig zou vinden.

Ook de taalinstellingen mogen wat mij betreft consistenter. Mijn pagina staat in het Nederlands, maar termen zoals ‘hours’ en ‘minutes’ blijven in het Engels zichtbaar. Dat zou ik graag volledig in het Nederlands willen kunnen instellen.

Al met al ben ik heel tevreden over TidyCal. Het helpt mij om mijn afspraken professioneel en overzichtelijk te organiseren, en het geeft mijn klanten een laagdrempelige manier om met mij in contact te komen.

comments.title: The booking tool that replaced Calendly for me
comments.comment:
I picked up TidyCal when I got tired of paying monthly for what should be a solved problem: letting people book time with me without the back-and-forth email dance. If all you need is scheduling not invoicing, not payment collection this is one of the easiest lifetime deals to justify on AppSumo. I only say that because I only use it for scheduling so cannot comment on payment features.

Setup took maybe ten minutes. You connect your calendar, define your availability windows, create your booking types (30-min call, 60-min consultation, whatever you need), and you get a clean booking page link to share. That's it. The calendar sync works both ways, bookings show up on my calendar instantly, and busy blocks I've already got are respected so there's no double-booking. Buffer times between meetings, daily booking limits, and minimum notice periods are all configurable, which matters more than you'd think once people actually start booking.

What I appreciate most is the simplicity of the booking page itself. It loads fast, looks professional without any design work on my end, and visitors can pick a slot in two clicks. Custom intake questions let me collect context before a call so I'm not walking in blind. Automatic confirmation and reminder emails go out without me touching anything, and the timezone detection handles the conversion for the person booking a small thing that eliminates the single most common scheduling screwup.

A couple of honest notes: the interface is functional rather than flashy, so if you want heavy branding customization you'll hit limits. And group/team scheduling features are more basic than the big enterprise tools. But for a solo operator or small operation that just needs reliable, unlimited booking pages, none of that matters.
The real comparison is the math: Calendly's paid plan runs around $10-12/month forever. TidyCal is a one-time payment that paid for itself in the first few months, and I've had zero reliability issues since. Five tacos if you book calls, meetings, or appointments of any kind, just buy it.

comments.title: Great product but needs improvement
comments.comment:
I really like how convenient and easy ResumeUp.ai is to use. I work at an employment agency and handle a lot of resumes every day, so I can see the value this tool could bring. What would make it much more powerful is if it could properly cater to different industries. For example, if someone is applying for an electrician role, the resume should highlight the right trade skills and experience instead of just producing a general resume. That kind of tailoring would be a huge improvement and something I’d really love to see.

That being said, I’ve run into quite a few issues. Sometimes the app freezes when I change the resume theme, and certain sections like “References” get left out even though they’re in the upload. Screenshots of resumes aren’t recognised either, which could be solved by adding OCR to read text from images. The job tracker feels a bit limited and could use more flexibility. Uploading existing resumes doesn’t always work well either, and I’ve had to re-enter job history and skills manually. On top of that, the analysis tool sometimes criticises its own AI-generated text or even invents achievements that don’t exist. I’ve also seen problems with the order of work experience where the tool sets it up one way, then tells me it’s wrong, and when I tried fixing it the system duplicated or deleted entries. Exporting as docx sometimes leaves messy markup, and switching between docx and PDF downloads doesn’t always work as expected.

The positives are that the templates look really nice, and the initial feedback does give a good starting point. But overall, it feels like a work in progress. If the developers can fix these bugs, add proper industry-specific tailoring, improve uploads, and polish the analysis tool, then ResumeUp.ai could become a must-have. From my side, I’d be more than happy to pitch it to my company and act as the middleman, because I honestly believe some specific agencies would roll this out at scale and buy hundreds of licenses once it’s ready.

comments.title: Great tool with Room for More Customization
comments.comment:
Overall, the ResumeUp.AI is a solid tool for creating clean, professional resumes with minimal effort. It's especially useful for users who want quick results without diving into complex design software.

What Works Well:

+ The app offers a good variety of resume templates that are modern and professional (hoping for more templates) with AI rewrites.

+ It's easy to use, even for those who aren’t tech-savvy.

+ Exporting to PDF is fast and straightforward, and the resume formatting generally holds up well.

Areas for Improvement:

+ AI writes functionality for some other sections where description is written.

+ It would be great to have the ability to change font size in individual sections. Right now, formatting feels a bit rigid if you want to highlight certain parts differently.

+ The app should allow users to add hyperlinks with custom text (e.g., “My Portfolio” instead of displaying the full URL). This would make resumes cleaner and more readable, especially in creative or digital fields.

Final Thoughts:

This app is a strong choice for most resume needs, but a few added customization options would make it even better. If you're looking for something quick and effective, it does the job well — and with a few tweaks, it could easily become one of the best in its category.

comments.title: A Practical Resume and Job Search Platform for Modern Professionals
comments.comment:
I’m genuinely impressed with how easy and practical this platform is. It does not just help you create a resume, it helps you create a better, smarter, and more competitive resume. The ATS-friendly templates are clean, professional, and customizable, which makes it easy to build something that looks polished while still matching your personal brand.

What I really like is the AI assistant. It saves a lot of time by helping tailor resumes, write cover letters, and add the right keywords to highlight skills and experience. The resume analysis and ATS score checker are also very useful because they instantly show what is missing, what needs improvement, and how to fix it before submitting applications.

Another strong feature is the LinkedIn optimization. Instead of starting from zero, you can use your LinkedIn profile as a base and improve your headline, summary, experience, and skills using best practices. That alone is a big advantage for job seekers who want to move faster.

The job tracker and Chrome extension make the whole process even more efficient. Saving job opportunities, tracking interview schedules, monitoring application status, and accessing follow-up templates in one place makes job hunting much less stressful and more organized.

Overall, this is an all-in-one tool that gives real value, especially for professionals, job seekers, and even those helping clients build resumes and cover letters. With the 60-day money-back guarantee from AppSumo, it also feels like a low-risk investment. For me, this is a solid and practical solution for anyone serious about improving their resume, LinkedIn profile, and entire job search process.

comments.title: Overall a snag I'm glad I got!
comments.comment:
I work in a pretty unique industry compared to most on here—we use XInterview for student employment at a local college/university. Even though we only have a few positions available, we get tons of applications. XInterview has been a lifesaver, cutting down on the hassle of scheduling individual interviews. It lets students pick a time that works for them, which frees up my team from days and days of interviews. Plus, it helps us avoid the headache of no-shows and wasted time. Everyone gets asked the same questions, and the experience is consistent for all students, which is great for fairness—especially in a small college town where everyone knows each other.

One thing I’d love to see improved: the base plan could use a bit more flexibility with user access. Most hiring decisions aren’t made by just one person, so having 2-3 users on the platform would be awesome. But overall, the interface is super easy to use for both admins and students. We asked some students about their experience, and while it was new to them, they found it quick, easy to navigate, and pretty much no learning curve at all.

The AI has also helped us rephrase some questions, which makes more sense and gave clarity for a video response instead of a real-time response, so it helped clean up the questions and overall quality of questions.

Initially I bought this to keep in my back pocket for something of a different case.  But I figured after getting it, I would test with my staff and next thing I know they're rolling it out for their students to setup interviews.  So far it's been a great experience, a neat little game-changer app for us!

comments.title: Streamlining Volunteer Screening for Non-Profits
comments.comment:
As a non-profit, we rely heavily on volunteers, and like many organizations, we use VolunteerMatch to list our open positions.  However, we quickly discovered that managing the influx of applicants was a huge challenge.  We were often flooded with candidates, and sifting through them to find the right fit felt like a full-time job.  Our biggest pain points?  Candidates applying on VolunteerMatch but then ghosting us when we requested resumes or tried to schedule interviews.  Even worse, some candidates would actually schedule interviews and then simply not show up.  This was a massive waste of our limited time and resources.

We knew we needed a better system, and we decided to explore video interviewing platforms.  Our goal was to add a screening layer that would help us identify genuinely interested and committed volunteers, prioritizing quality over sheer quantity.  XInterview has been a game-changer for us.

The platform's video interview feature has immediately proven its worth.  It requires candidates to put in a little effort, which naturally filters out those who aren't truly serious.  We've found that applicants who complete the video interview are significantly more engaged and responsive throughout the rest of the process.

XInterview's features have significantly improved our workflow.  We love the ability to send bulk reminders to candidates who haven't completed their video interviews.  If they still don't respond, we can quickly and efficiently move them to the "rejected" pile and send automated status updates.  This alone has saved us countless hours of administrative work.  The bulk upload feature for inviting candidates is another huge time-saver.

For non-profits looking to maintain a professional image, XInterview's white-labeling and custom URL options are fantastic.  We can brand the candidate-facing pages with our logo, ensuring a consistent and professional experience for everyone involved.

Pros:
- Significantly reduces candidate ghosting: Video interviews act as a natural filter, attracting more committed volunteers.
- Streamlines candidate management: Bulk actions for reminders and rejections save significant time.
- Easy candidate uploads: Simplifies the process of inviting applicants.
- White-labeling and custom URLs: Maintains a professional and consistent brand identity.
- Improved quality of volunteer applicants: Focuses efforts on candidates who are genuinely interested and willing to put in the effort.

Cons:
- Only one thing one noted at this time - while the platform has met our needs effectively, it could use a notification feature. Right now we find ourselves having to check frequently to see if we have any new interview submissions. This is a little inefficient.

Overall:
XInterview has been an invaluable tool for our non-profit. It has transformed our volunteer screening process, allowing us to efficiently identify and onboard high-quality candidates.  If you're a non-profit struggling with volunteer recruitment and candidate ghosting, we highly recommend giving XInterview a try.  It's a worthwhile investment that will save you time, energy, and ultimately, help you find the passionate volunteers you need to fulfill your mission.

comments.title: Great start with a few bugs to work out---one is critical
comments.comment:
I've loved the idea of having a Lifetime product for contracts & invoices!  Breeze Doc is simple to use and has so much potential to be a stellar, no-brainer-everyone-should-just-buy-it product.  
What I Love:
-One time fee for lifetime access
-Easy to upload my contract templates  + new auto discover feature is pretty good at detecting where the document needs to be completed.  
-Easy to adjust signature requirements (text boxes, dates, signatures, etc)
-User-friendly interface---clients have also said its easy
-Invoices!  I love that I can send invoices from this platform now, too.

Two things that have me a bit hesitant:
-THE MAJOR ONE:  When "signing" a contract that requires adding text to a text box, you cannot see how the text will load in the final version. Unfortunately, the default makes the text spacing big and that results in the words overriding the allocated space & sometimes going over very important other information in the contract.  I've had to do practice rounds & send them to myself to make sure everything is OK and usually have to go back to adjust several areas of figure out if the wording can be shortened to fit the space (even when I allocated a big space).  3 solutions that could help: 1) As the signer types, see the text in the same format it eventually saves in, 2) Make the default spacing smaller, 3-Have the autoformat shrink text to fit the box the template allocated--this would be ideal for me as the client because it eliminates extra steps.

2) Option for partial payment on invoices.  I charge a convenience fee if clients pay by credit card, so I'd love an option on BreezeDoc invoices to have clients able to pay different amounts if they use CC vs. ACH.  I can create a line item for the CC fee, but the client can't "opt out" of it if using ACH. 

Alternatively, I can also create a payment link in Stripe that makes that fee optional, so if there was a way to have the invoice link directly to that payment link vs. my general Stripe account, that could work.  

Overall its a great product, especially at this price point.  The #1 concern above is a big one that ends up taking more of my time in editing contracts, so could be a dealbreaker if not fixed.

comments.title: Beta software with a lot of space to improve
comments.comment:
I’ve been using Breezedoc for a couple of days now. As a freelancer I was looking for a way to have some documents better managed and more easily signed ("can you put a signature on this PDF and send it back?").

BreezeDoc is well-priced here on AppSumo and the proces is quite straightforward, making it a good option for basic signing needs. However, after some testing it’s clear that the platform is still in its early stages, with some limitations that make it less flexible than I’d like.

One of the first things I noticed is the heavy branding. Every email, activity PDF, and thank-you page includes Breezedoc’s branding. The thank you-page has a "Sign your own documents with BreezeDoc!"-space set up on a page that's empty beside a thank you message.
Even the signed document has a centered footer logo that can’t be removed, which forced me to adjust my document design. There’s no option to turn off or reduce branding, which makes it feel more like a promotional tool for Breezedoc rather than a white-label solution.

The lack of customization is also a drawback. While I can edit the initial email to clients, every other email—reminders, completed document notifications, and thank-you pages—can’t be customized or translated. I also can’t rename a template after saving it, which makes organizing documents harder than it should be. In multi-sign templates, text fields can’t be renamed or given placeholders, so they all just show “Text” without context for the client.
An option to categorize the documents or put them in folders would be a great addition.

I also find the reminder system too rigid. The only available option is to send reminders every three days. I would prefer more flexibility, as I like to give my clients more time before reminding them again.

The signing process itself needs some improvements. Some text fields appear smaller when signing than they do in the editor, which makes the final document look inconsistent. There’s no custom date formatting, so I’m stuck with month-day-year, which isn’t ideal. If a required field is left blank, the user can’t press the "finalize" button, but the system doesn’t indicate which field is missing user input. This creates unnecessary friction in the signing process. There’s also no option to upload a signature image, only to draw or type a signature.

In general I think Breezedoc is a convenient and affordable solution for basic document signing, but like I said before I feel it still has a long way to go. For now I'm not planning to use it for my clients just yet. I would love for a roadmap to become available to see what's on the planning and when. But for now, I haven't seen a roadmap or clear indication of what features are planned, which makes it hard to know whether any of these limitations will be addressed.

comments.title: Great alternative to the other expensive document request apps.
comments.comment:
I am the president and co-founder of a small car club with about 30 members and 8 sponsors. Unlike most car clubs, we are structured. We have Rules and Regulations for our members and Sponsorship Agreements that must be signed. Even though I only need to renew these once a year with occasional new members or sponsors joining throughout the year, having to go to each person one at a time to get these done was a hassle so I wanted to go digital signatures.

I was previously using DocuSign with the help of a member who had a business account. However, when they choose to jack their prices yet again, he decided to drop the service completely. Luckily another member found BreezeDoc.

After reading the reviews, I still had some questions. Especially on the plan size I needed. The largest plan was for 40 documents. I was counting 40+ so I was concerned this was not enough. I sent a message to the creator asking about the details who responded very quickly. Turns out I only needed the 15-document plan. One of the documents I sent out to all members was the exact same document. Just signed by each one. I was able to upload this document as a "Template" which counts as just one document. When I need to use it, I simply choose the address to send it to and I'm done. All the fields are pre-set for myself and the members.

In the end, I went ahead and got the 40-document plan just in case. Although I doubt I will ever need that many to send in a month, at the price for the plan, I just couldn't pass it up.

PROS:
1. Easy to upload documents.
2. Easy to drag and drop fields that need to be filled out by all parties.
3. Fairly simple to use.

CONS:
1. I wish it allowed you to set the date field type you wish to use. I just want month/day/year. It includes a time stamp with the date. Not something I want and it makes it too big for my documents. I am having to bypass this by using the "Text" field instead of the "Date" field.

2. It would be nice to have a "Name" field. When you add parties to the document, you have the option to input the name instead of it just saying "1st, 2nd or 3rd party". Being able to drag and drop a "Name" field could just pull that party name and pre-fill it out. Currently I am using the "Text" field which has to be filled in later by the party.

3. I wish it would allow me to save my signature to my account for use anytime I need it. This is something that DocuSign has. Made it much easier to quickly sign my part as I do not want to use the "generated" one. I want my personal signature which requires a capture device. Therefore, I am having to copy/paste my saved signature to the documents before I upload them. Really didn't want to go that route.

4. It would be nice if it allowed you to sign your part of a document immediately after creating it. Something else DocuSign does. With BreezeDoc, I have to wait for the email, click on the link and THEN I can sign it. 

5. I do not see an "App" available for it yet to use on iPhone or Android. Another plus DocuSign has available for mobile use.

6. As others have mentioned, the ability to copy/paste a field would be helpful in keeping similar fields the same size. Especially if you have to do a bunch of them.

7. I do wish it had an option to "archive" completed documents to another folder. I have a feeling over time the "Document" folder will be getting cluttered.

8. When using the "Checkbox" field, it can be difficult to check if you make the box too small. I was not able to simply click on it with my mouse when trying to complete it. I had to select a previous field and press tab to highlight the checkbox field and then press the space bar to add the check. Not something I feel most would be able to figure out.

9. As others have also mentioned, the ability to remove the "BreezeDoc" logo from the document when needing to print. It's fine for when you are sending to review and sign, but if you are printing for legal needs, it does look a little unprofessional.

In all, I am happy with this program. Sure, it will take some time to adjust to something new. I feel a lot of the issues I have would be simple to correct and perhaps they will be added in the future. I would highly recommend BreezeDoc to anyone with a small business who needs occasional documents signed electronically.

comments.title: Super esignature software
comments.comment:
BunnyDoc Review

I'm the founder of a naturopathy educational institute in Quebec, Canada. We needed an e-signature solution to collect consent forms from students and clients before appointments — roughly 100 documents per month. After researching DocuSign, eZsign, and BreezeDoc, I purchased the BunnyDoc Lifetime Plan 3 on AppSumo.

What works well:

• Public Form Links are the standout feature. We generate a unique URL for each consent document and embed it in our appointment reminder emails (via Acuity Scheduling). The client clicks, enters their name and email, receives the signing request, signs, and we're done. Zero manual work on our end. This alone justified the purchase.

• The signing request email arrived instantly and landed in the inbox (not spam) on our first tests with Gmail. This was our biggest concern going in, given reports from other users about deliverability issues.

• The client-facing form is clean and professional. Our logo appears at the top, the title is clear, the interface is in French (a pleasant surprise for our Quebec clientele), and the reCAPTCHA adds a layer of security.

• The field editor is intuitive. Placing signature fields, text fields, auto-fill name, and signed date on our PDF took minutes. Once you understand the drag-and-drop system, it's fast.

• Entrust digital certificates (AATL) embedded in the signed PDFs give real legal weight — important for us.

• The plan includes 1,500 web signatures/month, 10 public form links, and 10 team members — more than enough for a small company.

• Google Drive integration for automatic backup of signed documents is a smart safety net.

What could be improved:

• The confirmation page after the client submits the public form link is in English only ("Action Required - Follow Instructions in the Email"). For a bilingual or French-speaking clientele, this is jarring. A language option or customizable confirmation message would help.

• Templates and Links are separate workflows. You'd expect to create a template once and generate a public link from it, but instead you upload the same PDF twice — once for the template, once for the link. Minor inconvenience, but it feels redundant.

• No custom email domain (sending from @yourdomain.com instead of @bunnydoc.com). This would significantly improve deliverability and brand trust. I hope this feature is on the roadmap.

• The "Powered by BunnyDoc" footer on the client-facing form can't be removed on the Lifetime plan. Not a dealbreaker, but white-labeling would be appreciated.


Bottom line:

For the price of a one-time lifetime deal, BunnyDoc delivers serious value. The Public Form Links + appointment reminder workflow is exactly what small clinics and educational institutes need. The digital certificates give it an edge over simpler alternatives like BreezeDoc. If email deliverability holds up across a broader range of recipients and the team addresses the language/localization gaps, this could be a long-term solution. Hope the company will stay alive. We never know with startup. Still, very promising.

Thank you.

I started out with two codes just to test it, even though I only sign about 10-15 documents a month, definitely more than enough. Today I went ahead and purchased another code to support the product and lock in a great deal, thanks to a responsive and active team.

What I Like:
1. Responsive Support: I’ve reached out several times and usually get a reply within 3-12 hours.
2. Quick Feature Implementation: I needed a specific date format in the "signed date" field, and they added it in less than 24 hours.
3. Helpful Troubleshooting: I contacted them today about an email delivery issue, and they showed me an effective workaround using links.

What Could Be Improved:
1. Email Delivery Issues: A few envelopes didn’t reach clients. Once an email is flagged as spam, Bunnydoc stops sending further emails to that address.
2. Lack of Replace Function: It would be great to have a feature that lets you update a document while keeping all the fields intact, rather than setting everything up again. (Of course only replace when document is unsigned)
3. Delayed Document Sending: The document sometimes isn’t sent immediately after it’s signed and locked. For comparison, DocuSign is almost instantaneous.

Is it the perfect DocuSign replacement? No. Is it close? Maybe. Does it do what I need? Absolutely. I’m excited to see how it improves over time, but for now, it reliably gets the job done when it comes to signing documents.

Solid Editing Tools: From editing text and images to annotating and rearranging pages, everything works smoothly. It feels fast and reliable, without the lag I’ve experienced in some other editors.

Performance: Opening large files, searching through them, and applying changes is quick and responsive. It’s a “solid PDF” solution in every sense.

Extras That Add Value: Features like OCR (text recognition in scanned documents), batch processing, and password protection make it much more than just a basic editor. I haven't used these yet but I will be.

UPDF has exceeded my expectations. It’s professional, dependable, and affordable compared to many other PDF solutions out there. If you’re looking for a solid, all-in-one PDF editor, I highly recommend giving UPDF a try.
