comments.title: A thoughtful API-first document workflow tool with strong governance ideas
comments.comment:
We use PlutusDoc as a lightweight, document-first execution option alongside our broader client-operations platform.
What stands out is not simply e-signature. There are plenty of tools that can send a document for signature. The interesting part of PlutusDoc is the control model around the document lifecycle: scoped access, API/MCP support, idempotent writes, lifecycle states, audit/readback, and the ability to preserve a human approval boundary before consequential send/sign actions.
That architecture is a strong fit for how we work. We want automation to be able to prepare, inspect, correlate, and track a document, while keeping the actual external commitment under deliberate human control. PlutusDoc is clearly designed with agent/API operation in mind rather than having automation bolted on afterward.
We also like that it has a distinct role from a full CRM/client portal. PlutusDoc is attractive when we want a lighter, document-centric execution layer with deterministic IDs, readback, and integration behavior.
Our testing did uncover areas that could be better. The largest is least-privilege MCP/OAuth interoperability. We saw clients request broader scopes than the very narrow document-read scope we intended, even though PlutusDoc can issue API keys with exact read scopes. I would like the MCP path to make the same least-privilege behavior straightforward and consistent across clients.
We also encountered a UI-state edge case around a voided document where a signing control could remain visible. Lifecycle state should be absolutely unambiguous in a document/signing product, so I would like invalid actions to disappear or become clearly disabled immediately when the underlying state changes.
Overall, I like the product direction a lot. It is focused, developer/agent friendly, and takes idempotency, scopes, auditability, and lifecycle state more seriously than many document tools. We kept our Tier 1 license because that combination gives it a useful place in our stack even though there is still integration hardening I would like to see.

comments.title: Great signals, easy to implement with their recommendations
comments.comment:
Update as of December 7, 2024:
I have to set things straight. I kept using the signals after my review and there was one day I lost 10% of my allotted capital for this.

There were several losing signals on the same day. I know this is risky, so I was expecting that something like this could happen.

I tried to recoup some losses and was able to do it. In the end, I was happy with the learning experience and decided to invest less in these signals. 

Why?

The app shows their winning and losing signals, revealing their overall record. They use a take profit strategy with 5 levels which is very useful to handle risk and reduce losses.

I dislike that they report signals reaching Take Profit 5 when, in reality, many only achieve Take Profit 1 or 2. This happens because of the up and downs of the price, and sometimes they go to the stop loss take profit level, and the position gets closed.

Many times it recovers and goes higher up, but your position is already closed. This means that the winning signal is misleading at least on how they report it within the app. 

On the contrary, with the losing signals they go down to -5% lost. To recover a lost signal, you need about three or more winning signals that reach Take Profit Level 2. 

They should be more transparent and inform new users that this can happen. It took me some weeks to figure it out.

I recommend considering crypto trading as an opportunity, but be aware of the risks and plan accordingly.

My comments from November, 2024:
I decided to test the signals and give it a good try.

I already had a Binance account so I just had to activate the Futures option.

For making it easier to open positions (Long or Shorts), they recommend using Altrady which has a 14 day trial. It's not necessary but makes it easier.

The signals work. Most of them will come in the morning and close at the end of the day. So even if you don't have a huge amount of capital, you can invest in most signals in a day.

Pros:
- The signals work.
- Easy to start, specially if you have traded before (I'm in Mexico).
- The Telegram group and support is good.
- You can start with a small amount and recover your investment in this tool fast.

Cons:
- Even though you can start positions directly on the Binance exchange, Altrady make it easier but it comes with a monthly cost.
- You have to wait for the signals as they come and lose some of them if you're not on your phone all the time.

Thanks for a great service and your support.

comments.title: Finally, a simple WordPress payment solution
comments.comment:
I picked up WPSmartPay because I wanted a simple way to accept payments on WordPress without having to install and maintain a full WooCommerce setup.

So far, I’m really impressed with how straightforward it is. The form builder is easy to work with, and setting up payment forms doesn’t feel unnecessarily complicated. I also like that it supports both one-time payments and subscriptions, which makes it useful for selling services, digital products, memberships, or even collecting donations.

comments.title: A Fast, User-Friendly Platform with Accounting Gaps
comments.comment:
Invoiless positions itself as a streamlined invoicing solution, and in many aspects, it absolutely delivers on that promise. However, its approach to financial reporting might not suit every business.

Pros: Invoiless is incredibly fast and easy to use, with a snappy, responsive interface that makes invoicing a breeze. The white-labeling, customer portal, and multi-language support are excellent features for a professional, international-facing business.

Cons: The reporting is basic, and the biggest drawback is its cash-basis accounting. Unpaid invoices don't count as income, which is problematic for anyone needing to use accrual accounting. This limits its usefulness as a complete financial tool. 
The tax report has two main issues:
    - It shows a combined total for all taxes, with no breakdown between provincial and federal amounts.
    - It groups total sales and expenses, instead of listing each individual line item and its corresponding tax."

I'm eager to adopt and recommend this platform, but its current reporting shortcomings are a significant barrier. To be viable, the reports must provide the comprehensive data and flexibility our accountant needs to prepare accurate business tax returns.

What really makes Personeo valuable is the training framework around the AI, not just the AI conversation itself. The platform includes:
	•	scenario templates
	•	defined roles
	•	performance feedback
	•	scoring and evaluation
	•	structured training modules
	•	team training possibilities

This turns it into something closer to a conversation training simulator, rather than just another AI chat tool.

Many other AppSumo AI products are:
	•	chatbot builders
	•	prompt tools
	•	automation assistants

Those can sometimes role-play if you push them with prompts, but they usually lack structure, analytics, scoring, and training design.

Personeo fills that gap really well.

Compared to enterprise platforms that do AI sales or negotiation simulations (which often cost hundreds or thousands per year), this LTD is actually very affordable for what it offers.

I also see interesting possibilities beyond just sales training. For example, it could be used for:
	•	customer service training
	•	ethical sales practice simulations
	•	consumer education
	•	product transparency conversations
	•	coaching and counseling scenarios

Overall, if you are looking for a structured AI role-play training platform rather than just another AI chatbot, Personeo is one of the more unique and useful tools I’ve seen on AppSumo.

Definitely worth trying if you want to practice realistic conversations, training simulations, or customer interaction ("customer coaching") scenarios. That's very impressive. 

I just hope they come out with an iOS app and allow this to speak in Japanese by 2027 if not sooner ( ^.^)(^.^ )/.

*****Warning: This tool is primarily intended for training, experimentation, and conceptual work, and should not be treated as a strict fact-checking proof-of-concept type of work. If insufficient data is provided, the AI may attempt to fill in gaps by generating very convincing examples or illustrations that may appear factual but are actually inferred or hypothetical.  Still, exceptional in flow.

Despite this limitation, I still find the platform very useful and plan to continue using it. In the future, it would be great to see an option or toggle that allows users to restrict or override fictional assumptions, characters, or unsupported claims when factual accuracy is required.

comments.title: AI assisted automation for systematic traders
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

TradeSgnl is built for traders who want to connect trading signals, strategy testing, risk rules, and execution into one automation workflow.

I’ll be honest, this one had a learning curve for me because I was not already familiar with some of the MT5 concepts. Once I understood how the pieces fit together, the product became much clearer.

The interesting part is how it helps move a trading idea from signal to execution with more structure. You can bring in alerts, use AI to interpret trading messages, apply risk rules, map symbols, test ideas in Strategy Lab, and choose whether to run execution locally or through the cloud option. The benefit is that you are not just reacting to alerts manually. You can build a more automated and controlled workflow around how trades are interpreted, tested, and executed.

The biggest value is for traders who already have a strategy, follow Telegram providers, or use TradingView alerts and want a more automated way to execute. Instead of manually watching alerts and copying trades, TradeSgnl gives you a way to turn those inputs into rules, execution, and monitoring.

A few things buyers should be aware of. This is not a casual trading app. You need to be comfortable with MT5, broker setup, risk rules, and trade automation. If you want to trade from the cloud, you connect your MT5 account during onboarding. If you want to run it locally, you have to install the TradeSgnl EA on MT5, which is Windows only.

I also asked about MT5 credential handling because MT5 does not offer an OAuth style connection. The team confirmed that credentials are sent over encrypted HTTPS, are not stored on their end, are not accessible to staff or third parties, and are wiped when the terminal is deleted.

Overall, TradeSgnl is worth considering if you are already an MT5 trader and want AI assisted automation around TradingView alerts, Telegram messages, strategy testing, and risk controlled execution. It is probably not the best first trading tool for a beginner, but in the hands of someone who wants to get better or someone who understands MT5 and automated trading, there is a lot here to work with.

comments.title: TradeSgnl (Tier 3)
comments.comment:
I picked up Tier 3 to test the TradingView integration and the strategy development side, and overall I'm pretty happy so far. The documentation is comprehensive, Market Analyst gives a fast, useful read on structure across timeframes, and Strategy Lab is a real time-saver for turning a plain-language idea into working Pine Script.

A few suggested improvements / comments:

1. I think there is a bug in Market Analyst. ASX tickers like CBA and WOW show up in the search, but running them just returns "The analyst is experiencing high demand right now." I waited and retried a few times before realising it does it every time, so I don't think it's actually load-related.

2. Market Analyst itself is good but a bit narrow. It's mostly EMA, MACD, RSI and ATR, and you pick one trading style per run. I'd love to see day, swing and scalp together in one go, and export would be handy too. Kavout offers more in this regard, with near-term and swing setups, entry, stop and target levels, plus a confidence read. That said, that's one of Kavout's main features, whereas TradeSgnl offers a much wider range of trading tools and automation.

3. The model behind Strategy Lab handles simple strategies well, but it starts to struggle once you're combining several indicators or stacking conditions. I have experienced it stalling partway or producing a Pine Script that encounters some errors when you upload it in TradingView. 

4. There's also no backtesting built into Strategy Lab, so there's no real build-test-refine loop. You can generate a strategy in one place and test it somewhere else, but you can't iterate in a single flow. Even a rough, clearly-labelled quick test inside the Lab would make a big difference.

5. It would be great to have access to a TradeSgnl API or MCP server, so we could use our own AI to build, test and save strategies into the application, then use TradeSgnl to deploy them.

For completeness, I haven't yet tried the MT5 integration or the Telegram copier, which are arguably the main features of the app, so I can't comment on those.

Overall, a good tool that has potential.

comments.title: Automates execution of TradingView strategies and Telegram signals
comments.comment:
TradeSgnl turns TradingView alerts into live MT5 orders without having to rewrite the system in MQL5. That's a genuine gap and it would be worth the money if it only did that. TradingView is the better place to design and test; most FX, CFD, and prop accounts still live on MetaTrader. TradeSgnl is the layer that connects them.

The workflow is simple. Build or attach a strategy on TradingView, send a webhook, and the EA executes on your broker. Symbol mapping handles the usual broker-name mess. The EA adds the trade management Pine is weak at live: sizing, stops, trailing, breakeven, partials. CloudConnect keeps the terminal running when your laptop is off, which is the difference between a weekend idea and actual unattended trading.

Telegram parsing, a visual strategy builder, and a single dashboard for connections and logs make the stack usable for people who want automation without running their own webhook server. If your account is on MT5 and your thinking happens on TradingView, this is a practical way to put those two worlds on the same trade.

Beyond live signal execution, TradeSgnl also includes a bunch of features for building TradingView strategies visuially, plus an integrated AI strategy builder. It also includes a full backtesting module, so you can evaluate your strategies before going live.

public_name: Equitest Elite - AI-Powered Business Valuation Platform

comments.title: CPA
comments.comment: Pretty good app!  Of course, Business Valuations do take a bit of knowledge of valuation techniques and metrics so if you are not experienced, please don't think that an app will make you a qualified expert...  No app will!  Follow your professional standards, get some education and this app will help you with your presentation report.  Again, overall good tool.  Developer is highly responsive with support and seems to be open to feedback, enhancing the experience and improving the app as needed.

comments.title: Solid software filling a major need
comments.comment: I have been very impressed by Equitest and its staff.  The platform is extremely useful to me as an attorney periodically tasked with negotiating resolutions where one party is entrenched in their nonsense business "valuation" based on nothing but their opinion.  I use Equitest to provide a real value based on metrics that are verifiable.  When the amount at issue doesn't really warrant a business appraiser, this is my go to solution.  It is very useful and valuable software for my needs. Thanks Dev!!!

comments.title: Equitest rocks - very supportive
comments.comment: Equitest is a great product and has all important valuation methods. CEO is very supportive ans had an hour long videocall with us to give detailled explanation.

comments.title: Very helpful in financing deals.
comments.comment: We needed a tool to quickly and efficiently help us get company valuations for financing deals.  And this fits the bill perfectly.

comments.title: Valuable tool!
comments.comment:
I purchased Equitest with an immediate need, to work on a valuation for a proposed business purchase and expansion. I had already modelled it using spreadsheets which was helpful for financial data input. However, I needed to somehow translate those figures into an equity valuation and Equitest did that and more. A third party assisted valuation gives a lot more credibility, and in the case of Equitest it saves a lot of time and headache! I was able to input, adjust and successfully complete the valuation.

I did need help from support on four occasions and EACH time the response was received very quickly (by email), on two occasions I setup a video call and on two other occasions they sent me video instructions. The support alone was worth 5 stars let alone getting the product-result I needed from this. Buy and stash for when you need this in your business, especially if you are likely to need a couple of them over time.

comments.title: More Value Than Expected
comments.comment:
I recently used Equitest to generate a business valuation report for my company. The process was incredibly easy and user-friendly. With the help of their AI-driven algorithm, I was able to accurately assess the net worth of my business. The report was accurate and gave me valuable insights into the financial performance of my company. The industry experts behind the software are highly knowledgeable.

I highly recommend Equitest for anyone looking to get a quick and accurate assessment of their business. It saved me so much time and effort in creating an investor-ready financial model and plan for my startup.

comments.title: Good transcriptions and reports, but with considerable room for improvement.
comments.comment: The application strikes me as very good and functional. I truly value being able to record my meetings on both my phone and computer and receive useful transcripts and reports. I'm giving it four stars because the constant work and daily improvement behind the project are evident. However, I believe there's still much room for development. When comparing it to other tools like Plaud, I consider Plaud to be superior, as it has pre-designed templates for different reports and a more robust platform. Personally, I hope this app incorporates more editing options in the future and improves transcription accuracy, especially on the mobile version and for the Spanish language, where I still detect some significant errors. Despite these details, I continue to use the application to get accustomed to its operation, as I see great potential in it and my goal is for it to become my primary tool over time.

comments.title: Better than expected, but terrible at differentiating voices
comments.comment:
Using for business meetings on Zoom and Meet. My first frustration was that it was giving me terrible suggestions, but even so I could tell that it was just lacking the context of previous conversations. I forgave that. My biggest problem is that it cannot tell who is talking if they're the same assumed gender. It's telling me to follow up on things that I just assigned to someone else, it's suggesting I ask a follow up question on something I just presented, it's a mess. 

Told it that a particular meeting was going to be contentious and that I needed help knowing when we were going around in circles, how to better communicate when someone else just doesn't have the knowledge and skills I do and it frustrates me, and most importantly to tell me when to shut up and move on. It did with flying colors. "Try explaining it this way" and then "It's time to table this and move on." WHEW!

I used it for a doctor appointment. It got the medical jargon wrong, but it captured my task options perfectly. 

Used it while I was setting up some software, so as I had ideas I could simply say out loud "I need to remember that when X happens, we will need to do Y" so I could capture those action items and port them into my project tasks. Amazing. It also have me a couple suggestions for other follow ups that were useful. 

Where it really shines is in my parenting conversations. I've had a couple chats with my 9 year old and I was able to both stay present rather than trying to remember the decisions we made, but it also gave me follow up questions that ended up being insightful and leading to productive discussions. 

All in all, just the ability to grab action items and list them all in a logical order is worth every penny I paid. With continued context I think its suggestions in meetings will get better. I just need it to have the ability to read who is actually speaking, much better than it does.

Please consider adding support for these languages. In India any meeting or lecture is usually in mixed language of English+Hindi or any regional language. Hence it makes sense to add these. I hope hedy evolve as my daily use app.

comments.title: Great resource
comments.comment: The product delivers as presented in Appsumo. I'm very pleased with how Hedy summarizes the meeting and correctly identifies the speakers and aligns the action items to each speaker. The only component that would improve the app is for it to run on a computer, independent of the phone, which I understand is currently in the works.

comments.title: Robust but can do better
comments.comment: wanted to provide some feedback on my one month extensive use of HedyAI.. The app is robus there is no doubt however there are some features that can get better, particularly regarding its meeting and cross meeting management features. While the app excels in recording and minuting meetings, I find that the search functionality is somewhat lacking. This makes it challenging to quickly locate specific meetings or gather comprehensive summaries across multiple meetings.As someone who conducts 15-20 meetings per day, I rely heavily on the ability to search and retrieve information efficiently. Currently, I need to manually search or remember which meeting contains the information I need, which is time-consuming and inefficient. A more robust search capability would significantly enhance my ability to manage and recall meeting details effectively.I would like to suggest the implementation of a feature that allows users to ask the app about events during a specific week, month, or even for a particular event while selecting multiple meetings. This feature should be able to search through meeting scripts and provide relevant information to user..

comments.title: Top notch support...

Very few product support teams really care about resolving a problem started by someone who should have known better but didn't at the time.  I truly appreciate the help and patience they showed in helping me get back on track.

comments.title: I use this all the time

The software is easy to use, regularly updated, and continues to improve over time. I also love that it works seamlessly across both desktop and mobile, making it convenient to use wherever I am. comments.comment:
Long overdue review!

Hedy AI has become one of my favorite and most-used AppSumo purchases. The platform is highly effective at helping me get more from meetings and conversations while reducing the burden of note-taking and tracking key discussion points.

Excellent product, active development team, and outstanding long-term value. Easily one of my best AppSumo purchases. The team consistently releases updates and meaningful new features, demonstrating a genuine commitment to product innovation and user success.

It's rare to find a tool that not only delivers on its original promise but keeps improving months after purchase. Hedy AI has done exactly that.

Highly recommended.

comments.title: Reliable AI Meeting Assistant – Very Satisfied!
comments.comment:
After using Hedy AI intensively across several meetings, I was convinced by the product and decided to purchase the lifetime deal.

I’ve been using Hedy on Windows, iOS, and Android, and everything has worked smoothly and reliably across all three platforms.

The transcription is accurate, the real-time AI assistance during meetings works very well, and the post-meeting summaries are clear and useful.

Overall, I’m very satisfied with Hedy AI. It’s a well-designed and reliable product that genuinely adds value to my daily workflow.

I hope Hedy AI continues to grow, improve, and establish itself as a strong player in this highly competitive market. Looking forward to seeing how the product develops!

comments.title: Support that actually builds what you ask for
comments.comment:
I run a small UK e-commerce business and take customer calls through a softphone on my PC. I use Hedy to record and summarise those calls, and its webhooks send the transcript and recap straight into our own customer system, so every caller's history is there next time they ring.

The one gap was starting and stopping sessions automatically, since meeting detection only covers Zoom, Teams and Webex. I asked support. They gave me a clear, honest answer about what was and wasn't possible, then came back to say they'd built it for the next release: links to start and stop a session, so my phone system can control Hedy itself. They even made it off by default for safety.

The recap plus full transcript is what makes it useful day to day, and the webhook data is clean and easy to work with. For a lifetime deal, being listened to and having a feature request picked up this quickly is rare.

Highly recommended if you want call or meeting notes that plug into your own tools.

Writing this after having bought it a while back to say thank you to the founder. The best part is EU residency which is a great idea and he helped transition my account when that was introduced. 

The professionalism and support is exemplary. 

I might be picking up a new code soon!

comments.comment: Installed it with no glitches or drama ( and I hate computers).     I also hate typing  and listening to meetings ..             Have it running in the background of anything you are attending to get used to it.       It will serve you well after the meetings are over too. You will come to realise it is a Godsend! When I have it on spiritual counselling  sometimes the things I require takes quite some time to be completed by the host who talks slower and longer.  I made the error of asking it to do the same request in business meeting mode and it admitted it was better for me to switch to spiritual... ( i didn't know it noticed the difference ).      It is reliable with its transcribing too and if I wanted I could get it to identifiy speakers.......................   Unsure if it can translate but that would be another gem.

comments.comment: it does what it says on the tin. it takes a while to get used to its interface, but it is good software.

comments.title: Exceeds Granola!!!
comments.comment:
I bought this product less than a week ago. I have been a heavy Granola.AI user with a monthly bill and I approached this with skepticism. I have been running both bots for a week and only found one insufficiency in my use.  I reached out through the customer support channel, got engaged with Julian via chat and very shortly got a committment that they would not ony add that feature but he committed to making it far better than the Granola feature.  The feature is being able to share your session notes - transcripts with others without them having to create an account, which other bots require and is a non-starter for me and my use.  I am impressed with this developer and I encourage everyone to get this before the lifetime option goes away.   Phenomenal software with tremendous responsive support.  Good job team.  I will reccomend this to everyone I know.

Update:  Less than three days later the update with the fix is live.  Great response by the Hedy team.....Don't wait, get this tool, it is fantastic and just getting better.

comments.title: Impressive Founder and Product
comments.comment:
I run a UK coaching practice and needed to know whether Hedy could transcribe confidential client messages safely. So I read everything and sent a detailed written enquiry with further questions. 
Hedy passed: a proper DPA covers UK GDPR, and new accounts can have EU data residency, and transcription can be done locally. If you have strict confidentiality needs, Hedy can be configured to be private.
Support answered every question fully and promptly, and even corrected their documentation when my questions uncovered errors. My lifetime licence also transferred between accounts without fuss. Highly recommended.

comments.title: Constant evolution replaces early doubt
comments.comment:
I am pleased with Hedy evolving regularly. First sessions were really much lower than Granola + lack of integration. 
More and more, new features show up and quality evolves. 
I have hope that this becomes the strongest tool in his category.
thanks for the developer

comments.title: Wow, awesome product – and it works great in German too! 🤩
comments.comment:
I’ve been using Hedy in a couple of meetings now (both in English and in German), and I’m honestly impressed. 🤓✨

The transcript works really well, the suggestions are super helpful, and it does a great job identifying action items and summarizing everything. One key thing: you really need to define the meeting context clearly beforehand – whether it’s a workshop, status update, or planning session – so Hedy knows what it’s dealing with.

I’m using the Windows client together with the mobile app sync, and so far everything has been running smoothly.

5 tacos from me! 🌮🌮🌮🌮🌮

comments.title: It Just Works. Every Time.
comments.comment:
I’ve purchased a lot of software on AppSumo, and Hedy AI is easily in my top three purchases.

What I appreciate most is that it does exactly what it promises. Whether I’m in a client meeting, a leadership session, brainstorming ideas, or on a conference call, Hedy just works. I don’t have to think about it. It quietly captures the conversation so I can stay focused instead of worrying about taking notes.

The team also deserves credit for how they build the product. The updates are thoughtful, practical, and genuinely improve the experience. They aren’t adding features just for the sake of adding features. Each release makes the product more intuitive and more valuable.

I believe in Hedy enough that I purchased multiple lifetime licenses and gave them to members of my team. That’s not something I do often. It reflects the confidence I have in both the product and the people behind it.

If you’re looking for an AI meeting assistant that is reliable, easy to use, and continues to get better over time, I highly recommend Hedy AI.

One of the best AppSumo purchases I’ve ever made.

comments.title: This is the one!  Browser and desktop automation, tons of integrations, and great support. Plus ongoing development!
comments.comment:
I have tried more than a dozen RPA tools from API integrations like Make, ActivePieces, Boost, and n8n to the browser/desktop automations like UIPath, ZeroWork, Power Automate, RTILA, and Taskmagic.  I have refunded other AppSumo automation deals and let some mothball, but the one I go back to again and again is Robomotion.  If you want to automate browser actions and desktop programs, it is simply head and shoulders above the others. 

Robomotion has let me build so many cool automations for myself and my colleagues.  We have RM handling file conversions and transfers, uploads and downloads to/from password-protected sites, reading and modifying Excel and Word files (even triggering Excel macros), sending API calls to all kinds of services (including LLMs/AI), and much more--things no other platform could do (or if they could they required a much steeper learning curve).  

I was on RM T2 for a year and then upgraded to T4 because I was using it so much and needed to implement queues.  Best investment of the decade.  I tell anyone who asks me about desktop automation to buy this and ignore the rest.  And I have learned a ton from the folks on their Discord, going from being decent at RPA to blowing people's minds. I recommend at least T2 for triggers. 

Now, nothing is perfect, so a few caveats about RM just so you can buy it fully informed (but you should definitely buy it!):

1. RM cloud run hours are expensive.  I love RM and want to support them, but if you're going to use a lot of cloud run hours, it's cheaper to spin up your own VPS and host a robot there to run your cloud hours. Ubuntu is the preferred OS for that.  Or do what I did and repurpose an old PC as a 24/7 server in your home/office and let it run RM in addition to whatever else you need.  I did that and then bought just a few cloud run hours "a la carte" as a backup in case my home server is offline.

2. RM runs best on Windows in my opinion.  People will differ on this, as the Ubuntu install is good and runs really nicely, but you get better automation of desktop actions and Excel with RM running on Windows than any other OS. The reason for that is no fault of RM's -- it's just that Microsoft has baked a bunch of desktop automation tools right into their OS and others have not.  That just makes a lot more possible in Windows than on other platforms, regardless of which RPA tool you use.

3. There is a learning curve.  Spend some time with the Robomotion Academy videos and reading the documentation, then play around with it and learn by doing.  If you run into trouble, ask on the Discord.  Support there is awesome but there is a very reasonable expectation that you have spent a little effort to learn the platform and tried to build it yourself before asking for help.  If you are doing browser automation, learn Xpath selectors.  I have no idea why people use CSS selectors anymore, as Xpath is quite easy once you get the hang of it and is incredibly powerful with boolean operators, truncators, etc.  Tons of sites/videos on this and you can learn it in under an hour. Xpath will up your browser automation game 1,000%.

4. JavaScript helps but isn't essential -- and Sonnet 3.5 or 3.7 (or some other LLMs) can write 99% of the JavaScript you might use.  Once you start integrating some basic JS (even if it's 100% written by AI), you will find you can do so much more with RM.  

5. Other tools are for other needs.  RM isn't a replacement for Make/Boost, n8n, Activepieces, etc.. Those are just API integrations with some basic automation functions, not RPA platforms.  They aren't designed to handle local files (or really handle any files well) and they can't interact very effectively with Excel (though some do ok with Google Sheets).  They also are not going to do any kind of desktop automation and probably not any browser automation either.  BUT, they are really good and connecting together APIs with some logic and maybe custom JS, then running in the cloud 24/7.  I use ActivePieces a lot for API to API interactions that are triggered by webhook, form, or date/time.  It's just a different tool for a different purpose.

Zerowork is also good if you only need browser automation.  I really like ZW and their development has been great, but it's designed to do one thing well: browser automation. It scrapes really nicely and plays well with most APIs, but it lags far behind RM in file handling and can't do desktop automation. But, ZW is still a tool I love and use when I am strictly working in the browser and APIs. 

Past that, it's hard for me to recommend any of the other options. UIPath and Power Automate are too hard to learn for most.  RTILA made no sense to me, I could not get it to do what I need.  Taskmagic I poured hours into learning and found completely unusable and non-functional (and the lead dev terribly rude and condescending).

In the end, Robomotion wins.  There's simply nothing else I can recommend as highly in this space.

comments.title: Best and most flexible automation tool ever - the best tool I have ever bought.
comments.comment:
I've already bought a lot of really good tools from Appsumo, especially because I try not to simply collect tools, but only buy what I'll actually use productively afterwards. Among all my purchases, Robomotion is an absolute exception.

I have been using Robomotion since 2022 and have had enough time to form my opinion about the tool.
Honest statement... I would rather give up all my other tools than give up my Robomotion accounts.

Robomotion is an absolute DYNAMITE!!!
The possibilities, efficiency and scalability that the tool opens up are completely unrivaled.
I use Make, Activepieces, ZeroWork, Power Automate and Robomotion. But nothing really comes close to this tool. 

In 2022, I still had an army of freelancers who were tasked with implementing my own projects. I'm now on my own again, saving myself the money for freelancers and implementing many times more of what I used to do by automating my processes. At the same time, however, I am much less tied to the day-to-day project tasks. This would be unthinkable without Robomotion. Robomotion has massively changed my way of working and my success in what I do for the better.

Robomotion gets better the more intensively you use it and the more advanced the use cases become. 
In my opinion, this is where the tool can make the most of its many advantages.
In addition, I personally really enjoy working in the drag and drop canvas and it is a deeply satisfying feeling to see the bot working after completing a flow - much faster and better than a human ever could.

Sure, RM has a bit of a learning curve and I personally took the time in the beginning to really get to grips with the tool before automating my processes with it, but it was more than worth it. When I started out, I didn't have much to do with RPA tools. Robomotion made it as easy as possible for me to get started. Especially in comparison with other RPA tools, it becomes clear how low RM has set the entry barrier here. 
I also think the approach of a low-code tool instead of a no-code tool is perfect. It is this fact that makes the automation of really complex use cases possible at all. And without having to be a developer! In retrospect, this was probably also the key to me being able to transfer my extensive and complex use cases to a tool in the first place. A pure coding solution would have lacked the knowledge and a no-code solution would have lacked the necessary options.

Support is mainly provided via Discord. I have always received personal and problem-oriented support here over the past few years. Even late at night or at the weekend. In any case, it should also be emphasized that Faik personally takes care of the support and that you have an absolute expert as a contact person here. I have never experienced that he was unable to answer a question - and I read every single message on the Discord server. The response times are also abnormally good.

In addition, the RM team is very user-oriented. I have yet to experience another provider that is so responsive to user feedback and requests and incorporates them so actively into the tool. This is quite a unique selling point.

Since I started with RM, the tool has been continuously developed and improved. 
Much of this is not even listed in the deal description. There is a web recorder that enables the recording of web actions and outputs a functioning flow. There are subflow libraries that make it possible to create reusable workflows that can be used across flows and managed and customized centrally. The entire UI has been updated and now looks much more modern. Many packages (integrations) have been added. And much more. 

The Appsumo deal is really VERY generous in terms of its limits. If you take a look at the pricing page, you will quickly realize that even the largest plan (Growth) includes just 2 Production Robots - in Tier 4 you get 10!
One robot is already so efficient that you can't really bring it to its knees.
And for those who haven't noticed - there is NO limit to the number of steps you can perform, as is the case with Make, Activepieces or most other tools. You have UNLIMITED steps and finishes at your disposal. Unlike most other deals, there is no unnecessary restriction or limitation of your processes. 
If you don't go for it, you will definitely regret it!!!

A big compliment to the entire Robomotion team in any case. The tool is an absolute beast and the team is absolutely outstanding. Robomotion isn't a 5 taco tool - it's a 10!!!

comments.title: Still A Long Way To Go
comments.comment:
Starting off, it’s important to note that this application certainly offers value for your money. However, it is still in its nascent stage with some key features missing. A significant omission is extraction via XPATH for most parameters, which could make data scraping more organized.

When multiple parameters were selected to be scraped under my dataset, it only pulled specific ones when I had deactivated others. This issue might be due to the lack of an XPATH selection for extracting results. An XPATH provides precise data extraction as it points directly to a location of data.

Adding a feature that scrapes “Relative Xpath” and allows extracting multiple parameters in one dataset using a “Relative Xpath” would be beneficial.

Additionally, RTILA could do with more documentation, but considering its early stages, there is substantial room for improvement over time.

Another potential enhancement includes suggested scraping; where the program predicts what parameters you want from the page upon starting a new project. Effectively, it could scan the page and propose certain data to scrape while also providing a flow for data extraction without manual creation.

In its present state, RTILA does have limitations - including the need for multiple scrapers to extract data when ideally one should suffice. Nevertheless, priced at just $100 USD and packed with numerous features, it does offer excellent value compared to competition.

To sum up, despite some shortcomings and areas for improvement, RTILA delivers bang for your buck.

comments.title: 4 days in...Pros & Cons...
comments.comment:
I am a huge fan of RTILA and have been using it for the past four days, both as a scraper and a frontend bot. Let me provide a summary of my experience, including the pros and cons.

Here are the issues I have encountered:

1. The app occasionally crashes when left open for an extended period (on MacOS).
2. The spinning wheel remains on the page even after saving project configurations.
3. Headings are not exported in Google Sheets.
4. I faced problems with the inspector and dataset functionality. Sometimes, selecting something as simple as an H1 tag wouldn't yield any results. I had to delete the dataset and start over to get things working.
5. The exported data appears correct in the preview, but the resulting CSV file is missing crucial information.
6. The documentation and videos are outdated.
7. It takes approximately 24 hours to receive a response, which is acceptable. However, it can be frustrating when you're in the middle of a project and need prompt assistance because of bugs / missing documentation.
8. You cannot run a project from the automation/inspection window, which would be a helpful tool when troubleshooting
9. Many commands have unintuitive names, requiring extra digging to find what you're looking for

On the positive side, here are the advantages I have experienced:

1. RTILA enables me to perform tasks that other automation tools cannot handle, such as cPanel account procurement, cPanel customer ID scraping, and cPanel account storage space scraping.
2. The documentation has been helpful at times
3. New videos are being released, indicating ongoing support and development (love the new chatGPT potential)
4. Mohamed, the developer, has been very responsive and helpful. He resolved one of my issues and even offered to log into my site if needed.
5. When the software functions correctly, it is truly a game changer

Initially, I purchased RTILA but had to refund it due to the issues I encountered. However, I decided to give it another chance and recently repurchased it. I am grateful that I did, as I believe it has potential. I look forward to seeing it evolve into a solid 5 taco tool in the near future.

I would like to express my gratitude to Mohamed for creating this wonderful software. If there is any way I can assist you, please don't hesitate to let me know. :) - Scott

comments.title: An Automation Factory for Serious Builders
comments.comment:
If you’re serious about leveraging automation—(or combining it with AI)—RTILA is the tool to get. It’s not for everyone, but for those who see its potential, it’s a game-changer.

I picked up RTILA through AppSumo about six months ago: 6 codes (100 machines) for $594, unlocking standalone bot compilation—a massive feature. Later, RTILA offered backend upgrades for Sumolings, so I upgraded to unlimited machines for $396 directly through their team. Total: $990 for what’s listed at $4,999 on their website. Lifetime licenses, no recurring fees.

RTILA isn’t Zapier. It’s closer to Puppeteer, Selenium, or Playwright—but with a simple UI and a fraction of the learning curve. 

If you don’t know those tools, here’s the gist: RTILA can do almost anything a human can do with a mouse and keyboard.

If you can map out the steps, RTILA can automate them. But it’s more than just a tool—it’s a factory. It lets you build bots, chain them into workflows, and even compile them into standalone software you own and can rebrand and sell (insane).

RTILA is versatile, but these are some of its strongest use cases:

Data Scraping: Extract public data—like pricing, reviews, or contact info—and organize it into CSVs, Google Sheets, or databases.

Lead Generation: Automate scraping leads, verifying emails, initiating outreach, and importing cleaned data into a CRM.

Chaining Automations: Stack bots by feeding the output of one into another or have them collaborate on a single project (e.g., updating a shared Google Sheet). 
Example:
Bot 1 scrapes leads.
Bot 2 verifies emails.
Bot 3 sends the data to your CRM.
Bot 4 triggers an outreach campaign.

Building SaaS Tools: While not fully ready yet, you’ll eventually be able to host RTILA Studio on a VPS and integrate it with GPU-powered PCs for local AI models.

AI-Powered Automations: Pair RTILA with AI to unlock exponential potential. Think sentiment analysis on scraped reviews, AI-enriched lead insights, or bots that dynamically adapt to changing web content.


RTILA isn’t “set it and forget it.” To use it effectively, you’ll need to learn:

1. CSS Selectors: RTILA interacts with webpage elements (like buttons, forms, or text) using CSS selectors. It’s straightforward to learn with a bit of practice.

2. BPMNs (Business Process Model and Notation): These flowchart-like visuals help you map out workflows and create reliable automations.

3. The Blank Canvas Problem: The hardest part? Deciding what to automate. RTILA gives you the entire internet as your playground, and that sheer freedom can feel overwhelming. But for those who know how to use it, it’s an incredibly powerful tool.


The tool is fantastic, but the team makes it exceptional.

Mohamed, RTILA’s CEO, is one of the most thoughtful, hardworking founders I’ve come across. He (& the team) have bootstrapped RTILA, delivers regular updates, and directly engages with users. Got a question? He’ll answer it. Stuck? He’ll hop on a call to help.

Mohamed isn’t just building a company—he’s building a community. The team actively involves users in shaping RTILA’s direction, and their dedication to delivering value is unmatched.


If you’re dabbling in automation, RTILA might be overkill. But for serious builders, it’s a no-brainer.

The Price: Through the AppSumo deal and backend upgrades, I got a lifetime license for unlimited machines and standalone bot compilation for under $1,000. That’s insane.

The Potential: RTILA is a factory for automations. You can build bots, stack them into workflows, and sell them as standalone products—or use them to enhance your current offer.

The Future: RTILA’s roadmap includes AI-generated bots, It’s not here yet, because they need enough templates (think pre-built automation blocks) to train it on, but it’s coming.


The Bottom Line

RTILA is a tool for serious builders. It’s powerful, flexible, and built for those ready to automate and scale. If you’re willing to learn, it can save you hundreds of hours, unlock new revenue streams, and help you create products to sell.

For some, it’ll sit on a shelf. But for those who see the opportunity, RTILA is a no-brainer.
And at this price—lifetime licenses, unlimited machines—you’re either in, or you’re missing out.

comments.title: Solid Features for the Price, but Needs Usability Improvements
comments.comment:
While the core idea—email aliasing—isn’t new, it does work quite well in practice. Especially for the price, the features are solid: the ability to set a prefix and “catch-all” for that prefix (like prefix.*@domain.com) is very handy. This means I can segment my emails for different uses (newsletters, accounts, etc.) without enabling a real, global catch-all address that would flood me with spam. It’s a smart way to manage categories without overwhelming your inbox.

Another strong point is the option to bring your own custom domain, which is much appreciated for those who want more control and a personal touch.

However, there are downsides. The UI and UX feel clunky and unpolished; sometimes creating new aliases or even refreshing the mail list can be slow. The workflow isn't as seamless as it could be. A major letdown is the lack of a proper browser extension: there’s no Firefox extension at all, and the Chrome extension seems broken at the moment. For a service like this, having a reliable, easy-to-use browser extension would make a world of difference.

Overall, ProxiedMail gets the big things right and is a good value for the price—but I hope the team focuses on performance, usability, and browser integration in future updates.

comments.title: A practical and very useful tool for teaching and academic research
comments.comment:
As a lecturer and someone interested in education and academic research, I have found Kortex to be a practical and very useful tool for organizing both teaching and research work. I use it to collect important conversations from AI tools, save articles, webpages, and sources related to a specific topic, and then organize everything inside NotebookLM in a clearer and more manageable way.

I find this especially useful when preparing lectures, reviewing sources, or creating educational materials for students. Instead of having ideas scattered across the browser, AI conversations, and different files, I can bring them together in one place and return to them whenever needed. The option to export sources and notes in different formats is also helpful for keeping academic materials and preparing summaries, study guides, and learning activities.

One aspect I particularly appreciate is that Kortex is not limited to saving notes. It helps create a more organized workflow around NotebookLM. I believe it can be useful for teachers and researchers who work with a large number of sources or use several languages, such as Arabic, German, and English.

That said, I have a few suggestions that could make the tool even stronger for academic use. More specialized research features would be valuable, such as comparing studies, extracting key ideas, and organizing literature reviews. Shared workspaces, comments, and version tracking would also be very useful for researchers working in teams.

I also like the feature that saves webpages as PDF, but I would appreciate an additional option to save pages in HTML format. This could preserve a version that is closer to the original appearance of an article or source.

Overall, I see Kortex as a promising and useful tool for teachers, lecturers, and researchers. It reduces the time spent copying and organizing information and provides a practical way to collect knowledge and turn it into material that can be used for teaching and research. I would recommend it especially to anyone who uses NotebookLM regularly and wants to manage academic sources and AI conversations more effectively.

That said, it hasn’t been perfect. Looking through user feedback, the main complaints were reliability issues early on, especially around notebooks not loading properly or things feeling buggy. 

A few people also called out PDF export formatting and the extra Kortex branding in exports as frustrating. So it’s definitely not a flawless product.

Still, what gives me confidence is that the founder has been very active in responding, fixing issues, and shipping updates. That matters a lot with a tool like this. 

If you use NotebookLM seriously and want a faster way to collect AI chats, notes, and sources in one place, Kortex is genuinely promising and already very useful — just with a few rough edges that seem to be improving over time.

comments.title: Decent utility - shame about the UX (and all the different UIs).
comments.comment:
The top 3 reasons to get this toolbox are:
1. Global Search
2. Tag-based search
3. Chat management

Top reason not to get this toolbox:
* Fragmentation

It feels like this was 4 different vibe-coded projects.  The clunky UI is completely different for each AI platform.  There is global search, but there are no global folders, no global tags, etc.  You have to recreate each one on every platform.

Not a lot of thought seems to have been put into how the user interacts with the features. Smart tags in chatgpt show up as a single line of tags in the sidebar.  
* Want to see your tags? You have to side scroll until you get to the right tag - wait - you scrolled too far - remember you can only see 1 or two tags at a time.  Scroll slower! ;)
* Want to search for your tag? Can't do it from the sidebar.

If you want smart-tag search, you have to click on the icon and then click on the smart-tags menu.  Then you get to a useful smart-tags interface.  But the order in which the ui components are presented is baffling.  Why are the statistics (Conversations, categories, tags) the first thing you see "above the fold" so to speak? Who cares about that stuff when you just want to interact with your tags?  It's noise. Put it at the bottom or as a tooltip.

If you select a chat or chats, there's no way to manually assign tags. You have to rely on the "smart" search system.

To be honest, all tag and folder functionality should just be rolled into the global search.  You should be able to manage every aspect from the search menu.  Adding different interfaces for each is very non-DRY and messes up the ux.  search for your chats, multi-select them, drag onto a tag, or hit a button to move them to a folder.

Not only does it feel like each AI platform has been vibe-coded separately, it feels like each and every _feature_ has been vibe-coded completely separately. 

It's one thing if you are vibe coding stuff for yourself, but when you go to sell the "system" for 60 dollars? That's a more challenging proposition and requires more engineering and UX discipline.

... all that said - the utilties are GENUINELY USEFUL.  Sure, you could get 2 or 3 free utilities on  the webstore and it would make a similar toolbox. But this toolbox puts many of the important ones in one place.

AI Toolbox has a ton of potential. The ideas are great. The utilities are good. It's just the user experience  that needs work. If I were the developer, I would stop chasing features.  Curtail the technical debt and code rot.  Instead,  work on cleaning house.  Minimize the number of clicks and scrolling. Minimize distracting noise on the screen. Don't force the user to move their eyes and mouse all over the screen. Bring similar functionality into one interface panel. Unify the code.  Unify the interface. 

TBH, it might almost be worth rewriting instead of refactoring. 

YAGNI + DRY -> Clean.

comments.title: A very useful and promising tool

I’ve been testing AI Toolbox for a few weeks now. After a lukewarm first impression—mainly because it wasn't immediately clear what it could do or how to launch it—I started finding it genuinely useful once I located the floating button.

My main use case so far is the cross-platform search across multiple AI tools, which currently feels like its most valuable feature. However, I plan to dive deeper into the rest of its capabilities, as I see a lot of untapped potential that I’m not fully exploiting yet.

On the downside, there are a few limitations that hold it back at the moment:

1. Indexing issues: Some platforms never finish indexing (ChatGPT in my case), making them unusable for cross-searching.

2. Web-only integration: It only integrates with the web versions of AI platforms, not their installed native apps. This is a bit of an annoyance—while it can be partially bypassed by saving Claude and ChatGPT as PWAs/web apps (Gemini already is), it's still far from ideal.

3. Lack of Perplexity integration: Perplexity is currently not supported.

I hope these limitations will be addressed in future updates. Overall, though, it’s a promising and great productivity tool.

comments.title: One Program Simultaneously Searches All Your ChatGPT, Grok, Claude, and Gemini threads.
comments.comment:
Important Things First: You can search for a term not only in, say ChatGPT, but simultaneously at Grok, Claude, and Gemini. You can export to a file or click to visit chat. Super useful.

AI Toolbox solves a fundamental structural flaw in native AI platforms: the inability to effectively search, organize, and secure high-volume chat histories, both within a LLM, and between the various AI options. 

For those managing thousands of threads across multiple engines, the ability to bulk export entire projects and folders into localized formats (TXT, Markdown, JSON, PDF) provides a necessary barrier against data loss. It transforms a scattered digital footprint into a manageable, searchable architecture.

When dealing with the inevitable syncing challenges of an extensive chat database, their support desk provided immediate, precise technical instructions to rebuild the index without resorting to scripted deflection. 

If your workflow requires rigid control, rapid retrieval, and the security of offline backups for your AI interactions, this tool is required infrastructure.

UPDATE 08/23/2026: An example of competent customer service...  I asked for a 'nudge.'

THE QUERY
I was wandering through this
https://www.ai-toolbox.co/ai-toolbox-chatgpt-features/chatgpt-toolbox-prompt-library
Do you have a YouTube video on this?

And I am debating the best way I could use this; how about a little 'nudge'?  

THE RESPONSE

Yes, there is a playlist covering the features, here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLNM6c3LPnAQcJvlZD6J9x1lCRSVoxTo9J

And yes, I will happily nudge, because I think the obvious way in is the wrong one for you.

The page you were reading is about the curated library, hundreds of prompts you can browse by category. That is worth a look, but it is not where I would start in your case. You have thousands of conversations and you name your threads deliberately, in a scheme, with roman numerals and a stated principle in the title. 

People who do that are not short of good prompts. They are short of a way to stop retyping the ones they already trust.

So the nudge is this: mine yourself first, borrow second.

Search your own history for a phrase you know you have typed more than five times. The framing you always use to open an analysis, the way you ask for a critique, the format you always request output in. Pull up two or three of those. That is your real prompt library, and it is already written, just scattered across five thousand chats.

Then save each one with the parts that change turned into fill-in-the-blanks. Type two forward slashes in the message box, and it appears; you pick it, it drops in, and it asks you for the pieces that vary. The point is that the reasoning stays fixed and only the subject moves.

Where I think you will get the most out of it, though, is chains. A title like "Effective Before Efficient" is not a prompt; it is a sequence, and my guess is you already run it manually across many messages. A chain is that sequence saved as one thing, up to ten steps, and it fills in all the blanks once at the start and then runs. If you have a routine you repeat across projects, build that first. Two dots in the message box brings your chains up.

Use the curated library as a parts bin, not a catalog. When one is close to what you need, save it, then edit it into your own words. A borrowed prompt in someone else's voice will annoy you within a week.

comments.title: Four issues, but I'll keep the app.
comments.comment:
After using this for a while, I came to a conclusion and I'm writing my review. The first thing that I don't like is that the prompt can only be called at the start of the chat. You cannot add a prompt in the middle of the chat or even at the end; you need to be at the start. This is something I would not expect from this app.

Second, the smart tags have a mind of their own. They include a few default tags that most of us won't even need, and they are extra in the workflow. If you add your own custom tags, the system might find a post that is two months old but will not find a post you have just written a few seconds ago. This is a second main hurdle.The way the search is organized, you don't know which chat is the earlier one or the later one. It would be advisable to add a date with that particular chat name to give a view of what date we are actually dealing with. 

The third issue is that when you make folders and refresh your page more often, the folders are not completely loaded and they miss their content. To get that working you need to refresh the page until you see all. This again is something that needs to be solved.

The fourth thing is that it needs a stronger PC. For example, my desktop PC is an i9, so it takes about 4 to 5 seconds to load. When I am on a slower laptop like an i3 or i5, it takes about 12 seconds to load. Imagine the pain when you have to spend 12 seconds just to browse in between.

The most important question, even besides all of this, is: will I keep this app? Yes, I will. Great things take time to build, and we have to support the developers for this purpose. That's why I'll keep this, and I hope these issues will be resolved and this will become one of the best apps. That's what I pray for it. I request the developers to please solve these issues.

Domain Monitor has proven to be an effective tool for keeping track of domain status. It does exactly what it claims, providing reliable monitoring and timely alerts. This reliability is crucial for maintaining the health of my domains and ensuring that any issues are addressed promptly.

However, there are a few areas where the product could use some improvement. The user interface (UI) is not as polished or intuitive as some of the other competing products on the market. It's functional but a bit clunky, and it could benefit from a more modern and user-friendly design.

One feature I find lacking is the ability to configure alerts to trigger only if the monitor is down for a defined period. This would help avoid unnecessary notifications for short-lived issues and allow for more precise control over alerting.

In summary, Domain Monitor is a solid product that performs its core functions well. The alerting is reliable, which is the most critical aspect. However, the user interface and lack of certain alert configurations are areas that need improvement. Despite these drawbacks, it's still a worthwhile investment, and I hope to see continued enhancements from the development team in future updates.

On the downside, the number of integrations is still quite limited. I’d strongly recommend the developer to focus on the apps that are actively used here on AppSumo. No more scrolling through a long automation screen wondering where it went wrong.  I really like that!  Also it's really great that I can set the intervals easily and the credits that I've used are really clear to see in both the logs and at the top right of the screen so I always know how much I have left.

I would like to see a native ThriveCart integration since they have Kajabi.  Guessing a Shopify would be great for them to have too.  Finally a Stackby integration would be great as well since many of us have used that to replace Airtable. Finally, I would like to see a "Re-run this Automation" button in the log somewhere so that I can quickly re-test changes made to an automation.

I really like that they have a Webhooks integration already in it since that is usually what is needed when you are using some of the newer tools.

I highly recommend APIXDrive for anyone who is looking to run automations between separate softwares and needs a tool to do that!  They have definitely earned a great rating and this 5 out of 5 tacos is well deserved!  Thanks for a great product!

comments.title: Plug-and-play automations — just wish it looked newer
comments.comment:
Bought Tier 3 on AppSumo (May 2025) to replace a patchwork of Zapier + Make tasks. 
Wizard had my first flow (Hedy → Gmail → Notion) live in under 5 min—no docs needed. 

Why I’m keeping my code
	•	Zero learning curve: step-by-step builder makes even non-tech teammates look like automation pros. 
	•	Instant triggers—webhooks push data in seconds, not 15-min polls
	•	AI actions (ChatGPT, Claude) now let me enrich leads or draft replies mid-flow without extra tools.

Room for improvement
	•	Old-school UI: tiny dropdowns, no dark mode, and activity log feels 2016.

Verdict
ApiX-Drive nails the “set-it-and-forget-it” promise for real-time automations, earning 5 tacos. If you can live with a retro UI and a growing (but not yet exhaustive) connector list, snag a code before pricing climbs—your future self will thank you when Zapier invoices shrink.

comments.title: A real proposal agent running in one evening
comments.comment:
I started on Tier 3 and moved up to Tier 5 after a few tests. In one evening I built an MVP: a custom skill with Python scripts that generates sales proposals as PowerPoint files. You request it via Telegram, the agent asks for missing data, builds the deck, sends it back to the chat, and emails me a control copy with the file attached. It worked better than I expected.

Things worth knowing:

Skill uploads have a size limit (a 7 MB ZIP was rejected, 2.7 MB was fine), so keep large files compressed.
In my tests, Telegram didn’t pass files I sent to the agent, so I forward them to the agent’s Gmail instead. Sending files from the agent works using the Bot API.
Secrets must be declared in the skill’s Credentials, or the scripts won’t receive them.

No servers, no Docker, and support answers fast. Excited to see what comes next.

comments.title: Self Hosted Hermes Killer? It just might be!
comments.comment:
OK, I will say that I'm a bit late to the game when it comes to the world of "OpenClaw and Hermes", but the past 6 months have been a full time masterclass in digging into this world, and I'm always looking for tools to make this easier / faster / cheaper / more efficient.

Thanks to another AppSumo LTD, and three other tools that I use for social media content creation and management - and have cut my workflow by orders of magnitude.  Bottom line my self hosted Hermes / OpenClaw / PaperClip are crushing it - that is until there are failed updates, server "burps", weird coding issues, and overall time spend being the coding mechanic to fix things that went wrong with those platforms.

Then I saw BetterClaw - and I said for $400 (T4) the approximate price of a "good deal" on a lower end mac mini - I had a cleaner interface and user experience than I had with my self hosted system.  

I will admit, that this is a work in progress, and that Naveen and the team have been VERY responsive with fixing things, adding things, answering my dumb questions :-) and making it easier to add MCP connections, things like FreeLLMAPI model system, and other goodies that just felt "easier" to work with.  In fact migrating the skills / knowledge zip file from Hermes to BC was a breeze and only needed a couple of tweaks to set up.

Today I tested the workflow / skill my personal business - and after a couple of minor clarifications BC did exactly the same work that my Hermes did - but in some respects a lot faster - and the fact that things like connections / agents / workflows / browser integration etc are SO much easier to work with and find - INCLUDING ADDING MODELS - just made the work feel like less "work".   I also like that Composio is built and and somewhat easier to use (although not everything from there is IN BetterClaw - but again this is a work in progress).

So ... if I am happy with Hermes and already spent about $400 why did I spend another $400 (well I had a 10% coupon HA) for something that does a lot of the same things?  Simple.

Simplicity. comments.title: Promising AI Platform, but Significant Limitations for Digital Marketing Agencies
comments.comment:
I purchased BetterClaw's Tier 3 lifetime deal with the intention of using it as a standalone AI operating platform for our digital marketing agency.

The good news is that the AI capabilities are promising. I've successfully tested the Research Analyst on SEO/GEO research and client-specific industry intelligence. The reports were detailed, well-structured, properly sourced and commercially relevant. Setting up recurring research tasks is also straightforward.

However, after spending time configuring the platform and speaking with support, I've identified some significant limitations for agencies managing multiple clients.

1. No client folders or projects

BetterClaw currently recommends creating one agent per client because memory, conversations and tasks are organised around individual agents.

We manage a number of clients, and our Tier 3 plan includes eight agents. Following this recommendation would immediately consume our entire agent allowance just to organise our clients.

2. Agent scalability is a concern

Each client requires multiple specialist functions, including SEO, technical audits, content writing, research, GEO/AEO, reporting and advertising analysis.

If these functions require dedicated specialist agents for each client, an multi-client agency could potentially need 50–70 agents, based on what support have told us.

It's not yet clear whether one multi-skilled agent per client can deliver the same capabilities through separate workflows and instructions.

A much better structure would be client projects containing their own knowledge, credentials, tasks and deliverables, with specialist agents shared across those projects.

3. No support for custom MCP servers

This is another significant limitation for us.

We already use MCP integrations for SEO Crawl, Semrush and You.com etc. BetterClaw currently doesn't allow users to connect their own MCP servers.

Support suggested using built-in Connectors or custom Skills, but these aren't necessarily equivalent replacements and could require additional configuration, charges and maintenance.

4. Client work organisation needs improvement

For an agency, being able to quickly find completed research, content, audits and reports by client is essential.

Using agents as client containers may work for simpler setups, but it's not the flexible project-based organisation we'd expect from a standalone agency platform.

Overall

BetterClaw has genuine potential. The research quality impressed me, and the scheduled automation functionality is useful.

However, the current architecture feels better suited to individual businesses or narrower automation use cases than agencies needing multiple specialist capabilities across several clients.

I'd particularly like to see:

- Client projects or folders independent of agents
- Shared specialist agents with isolated client knowledge and credentials
- Native support for custom MCP servers
- Better organisation of client deliverables and task history

For now, I'm holding off on rolling it out across our remaining clients until I can establish whether it can realistically meet our requirements.

A promising product, but the multi-client architecture and integration limitations are significant enough that I'm reconsidering whether to keep it or request a refund.

What it is
SheetXAI is an AI-powered add-on for Google Sheets and Excel that helps you build dashboards, fix formulas, and automate logic using natural language prompts. You describe what you want; it writes and adjusts the formulas and structure for you.

Pros

Strong for non-technical users
You can ask in plain English for changes (e.g., “only show high-priority tasks due today”) and SheetXAI updates filters, formulas, and logic without you digging into complex functions.

Great for building real workflows
In testing, it handled:

A task management dashboard
A client revenue tracker
Both were built and debugged almost entirely through chat.
Low AI credit usage (BYOK model)
Uses a BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) setup via OpenRouter or similar. Building two fairly complex sheets cost under $1 in AI credits. Total project cost was about $16 in credits plus the $39 Tier 1 purchase.

Fast iteration when used correctly
If you keep prompts short and periodically clear the chat history, you minimize context size and keep your AI spend tiny.

Cons / Watchouts

Lifetime deal risk
As with most LTDs, there’s always the chance the company pivots or shuts down. Don’t treat it as guaranteed forever infrastructure.

Prompt precision matters
You need to be fairly clear and specific in your instructions. Vague prompts can lead to odd changes or require extra back-and-forth.

Best with one sheet open
Works more reliably when you focus on a single spreadsheet at a time. Having multiple sheets open can cause confusion about what the AI should modify.

Ideal For
Freelancers, consultants, and small businesses who live in Sheets/Excel but don’t want to learn complex formulas.
People building dashboards, trackers, or lightweight “apps” inside spreadsheets.
Power users who like to prototype quickly and then refine with AI help.

Bottom Line
SheetXAI is a surprisingly capable AI copilot for spreadsheets. If you’re already comfortable working in Sheets/Excel and want to speed up building dashboards or logic-heavy trackers, the Tier 1 deal offers solid value—especially given how little AI credit it consumes when used efficiently.

comments.title: Meeting notes without the bot
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Prismical got my attention for a very convenient reason: it can take meeting notes without putting another bot in the call.

It records the audio already playing on your computer, along with your mic, so it can work with calls, lectures, demos, interviews, and voice notes. Prismical does not join the call as a visible meeting participant, so the other people do not see a bot, get a bot notification, or have the call feel like it is being monitored by another attendee.

In my test, Prismical gave me a live transcript with speaker labels, then turned the recording into a summary, decisions, and action items accurately. This is what makes it unique for me: useful notes after the meeting without making the meeting itself awkward.

The local first setup is another big reason I like it. Prismical can transcribe locally with Whisper, supports local models and BYOK, and lets you choose when to use cloud providers. For client calls, internal discussions, interviews, or anything sensitive, I like having that control.

It is also built for people who already use AI in their workflow. MCP, API, webhooks, and integrations are part of the product, so your notes can connect to tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Obsidian, Notion, Zapier, n8n, Make, Activepieces, or custom workflows.

During my early test, I ran into a few issues around integrations, model availability, and app version confusion. The team pointed me to the newer build, and I retested using a newer version from the correct download page. The MCP OAuth redirect worked properly with Notion, Gemini had been added, the previously coming soon model options were cleaned up, and Zapier, n8n, Activepieces, Make, and Notion integrations were available. Slack, Linear, HubSpot, and Attio were still listed as coming soon.

Overall, Prismical is worth considering if you spend a lot of time in meetings and want notes without inviting a bot to every call. Its best fit is someone who cares about privacy, local transcription, and AI workflow hooks, and is comfortable with a product that is moving quickly.
