comments.title: A Promising Tool for Turning Lectures and Academic Discussions into Structured Knowledge
comments.comment:
As a university lecturer and school teacher, I see real potential in Prismical beyond its usual role as a meeting-notes tool. It can become valuable for students, teachers, and researchers, particularly for recording lectures, academic discussions, and seminars, then turning them into structured text that can be reviewed and used later.

What I appreciate about Prismical is its privacy-oriented approach and technical flexibility. The option to transcribe locally with Whisper, rather than relying entirely on the cloud, is especially valuable in a university context. Recordings may contain research discussions, student data, or sensitive information that should not leave the institution. The ability to work without a bot joining the meeting is also a practical and professional advantage, especially in lectures and academic meetings where participants may not want external tools to appear in the session.

I also see clear value in live transcription, speaker identification, and summaries that extract key points, decisions, and action items, as well as MCP support and integration with AI tools. These functions can help a faculty member quickly return to an earlier discussion, prepare an initial meeting summary, or organize voice-recorded research ideas. For students, a recording can become a useful starting point for revision instead of relying on scattered notes or replaying an entire long lecture.

From an educational perspective, however, the current summary templates appear closer to the business-meeting model: decisions, action items, and next steps. This is useful, but it is not enough for lectures. I would love to see dedicated academic and educational templates, including learning objectives, new concepts and terminology, key definitions, examples, questions raised during the lecture, revision questions, suggested references, and points that require clarification. It would also be extremely helpful to generate flashcards, short questions, or a quick quiz directly from a lecture summary.

My most important observation concerns Arabic-language support. It is good that Arabic is available as a transcription language, and I will test this more deeply in real use. However, simply selecting Arabic for transcription is not sufficient to create an appropriate experience for Arabic-speaking users. The application needs native and complete RTL support across the interface, transcripts, summaries, editor, and exports: correct right-aligned Arabic text, a natural reading direction, punctuation appearing in the correct position, proper display when Arabic is mixed with English or German, and clear, comfortable fonts for Arabic text. These are not merely visual refinements; they directly affect whether text can be read, reviewed, and used effectively in education.

I would also encourage the team to test Arabic transcription across a range of dialects, especially Modern Standard Arabic used in lectures, as well as foreign names and academic terminology. It would be very useful if users could select the summary language independently from the recording language. A lecture may be delivered in Arabic while the student or researcher needs a summary in German or English, or the other way around.

Compared with Voicenotes, Prismical appears stronger in privacy, local transcription, and its no-bot approach to meetings—advantages that matter greatly in universities. However, Voicenotes offers quick PDF export. I therefore hope Prismical will develop professional Word and PDF export in print-ready formats, because teachers often need to turn lecture content into worksheets, summaries, or materials that can be shared with students.

One positive point that deserves mention is that the Prismical developer is very open to feedback and professional and easy to communicate with. In my communication with the team, I found a genuine willingness to listen to users’ needs—especially educational and academic needs—and to engage seriously with suggestions. The team does not merely receive feedback; it shows a clear interest in considering it and working on it as part of the product’s development. For me, as an educator, this is very important, because successful educational tools are not built only on strong technical features, but also on a team that understands real-life use cases and responds to them continuously.

My first impression is very positive: Prismical is not just another voice recorder, but a promising project that could become an excellent tool for education and academic research if the team invests in genuinely educational templates, practical academic export options, and native right-to-left Arabic support. I will continue testing it in real teaching contexts, especially in Arabic and German, and I look forward to sharing more detailed feedback with the team.

comments.title: Cool Stuff!
comments.comment:
Ok, first of all, it's good! :-)

What I like. It works as promised, which is something you sometimes miss with other products. Although it doesn't - purely by feel - push your own projects quite as quickly as you might have hoped, it increases productivity even more. 

Who is it suitable for? Anyone who is used to choosing their words and formulating a prompt coherently - to some extent - should use it. Of course you can also make manual changes to the text generated by the audio file, but this is actually something you want to avoid. 

However, there is a solution here if you simply add a corresponding instruction to the prompt in your own actions (e.g.: Correct my speech input, i.e. turn keywords into complete sentences etc......). then the transcript can be formed accordingly with the actual prompt to a good result.

All in all, very nice!

What I don't like. First of all, the login. Yes, it works well and securely and probably has advantages for the manufacturer, but for me personally it has disadvantages. Firstly, to be able to use the extension (sidebar), this has to be done in Chrome or Edge. So I can't use Firefox here in a meaningful way. However, since a link is sent by email during login, which is then used to access the standard browser, I also had to switch this to Chrome. Secondly, if I want to log in on an iPad where Safari normally opens, am I now also forced to switch to Chrome, if this is even possible without any problems? Thirdly, the actions are good, but a slightly more productive, possibly alternative display, i.e. instead of always jumping from page to page, would be a solution. Perhaps a directory tree with its own folders, hidden behind a button and thus fitting into the design? Thirdly, it is a bit sluggish on my system. However, this may be due to my connection to the Internet, as the audio file must first be transferred to Wiz in order to generate the transcript and then - with the respective action / prompt - the result. This could be faster, but it may be an individual problem.

Now a question. I've watched the YouTube videos that talk about the actual engine. I don't really care what's under the hood, but if I already have my own API key with OpenAI or another engine, why can't I use it? I have unlimited inputs, but surely one or two additional users would be added who would like to secure a cheaper rate - outside of appsumao. As I have an interest in the success of the tool, I would like to receive future updates, of course I support the continued existence of the company. 

Suggestion. And to finish, as pretty as it is, it should be pre-installed on every MAC.

OK, nice work and productive solution. Good Luck!

comments.title: More Than Another AI Chatbot — A Promising AI Workspace for Business Owners
comments.comment:
What initially attracted me to WorkLLM was the idea of having more than just another AI chatbot. As a business owner building Creators Academy, I'm always looking for practical ways to bring AI research, content creation, business knowledge, and automation together without constantly switching between different platforms.

WorkLLM caught my attention because it approaches AI as a complete business workspace rather than simply offering access to different language models.

**What I Like**

One of the biggest strengths is the five-layer memory system. Having organizational, personal, project, folder, and conversation memory creates a foundation for keeping business knowledge organized and accessible. This is especially valuable when managing multiple projects that need consistent context.

Access to 200+ AI models is another major advantage. The ability to choose and compare models for different tasks offers flexibility without being tied to one AI provider.

I also appreciate the support for BYOK, MCP, and integrations with popular business applications. These capabilities give WorkLLM the potential to work alongside existing software rather than requiring businesses to replace everything they already use.

The workspace setup was straightforward. I was able to establish my business identity, upload branding, configure my administrator profile, and access the workspace without unnecessary complications. The interface is organized, with dedicated areas for AI chat, memory, integrations, agents, administration, and usage reporting.

Another feature I appreciate is the visibility into credit consumption. Having reports that break down usage by model, provider, and task is important for managing AI expenses.

**What Really Stands Out**

What impressed me most was the founder's communication.

I asked a detailed question about whether WorkLLM could eventually replace platforms such as Genspark AI for digital-product research, multi-agent workflows, browser automation, and product creation.

Rather than giving a generic marketing response, Dhimant addressed each capability individually, clearly explaining what WorkLLM supports and where its limitations are.

He also shared details about Agent 2.0, including multi-agent orchestration, reusable workflows, scheduling, event-based triggers, and approval checkpoints.

I particularly appreciate that he was transparent about browser automation and full application deployment not being supported. That kind of clarity helps customers make informed decisions.

**Where I'd Like to See WorkLLM Grow**

I'd love to see WorkLLM continue developing toward more complete, end-to-end business automation.

Browser interaction, deeper connections with third-party tools, and more advanced product-development workflows would make the platform even more valuable for entrepreneurs and creators.

I also hope the team continues improving credit transparency, workflow efficiency, and documentation as the platform grows.

**Final Thoughts**

WorkLLM has an ambitious vision, and I like the direction the team is taking.

For small businesses, entrepreneurs, and creators, having AI models, organizational knowledge, research capabilities, integrations, and agents in one environment could make a meaningful difference in productivity.

My experience with the initial setup has been positive, and the founder's responsiveness has given me additional confidence in the product's direction.

I'm looking forward to putting WorkLLM through more real-world business workflows and seeing how the platform develops.

This is a promising product with a strong foundation and a lot of potential.

comments.title: A Multi-Model AI Workspace With Real Value for Education
comments.comment:
As a teacher and university lecturer in language education , I purchased WorkLLM and have used it daily for lesson preparation, worksheets, and research. Here is my assessment from an educational perspective.

Key strengths:

- Model comparison: over 200 models in one place, with the option to send the same prompt to four models at once.

- Chatting with files: I uploaded lengthy PDFs (including a roughly 90-page curriculum document) and extracted summaries, exam questions, and differentiated worksheets with high accuracy. Here WorkLLM clearly outperforms WritingMate, whose "chat with files" feature is very poor — it struggles with large files and loses track of details.

- The five-tier organization memory and shared threads: I stored my templates and curriculum standards, so outputs now stay consistent with my style, and colleagues can build on each other's work.

For Arabic-speaking users: the experience is positive overall. The app fully supports right-to-left writing, and the developer is extremely cooperative on this topic and listens to feedback remarkably well. Arabic quality depends on the model chosen, and the comparison feature helped me identify which model writes the most polished Modern Standard Arabic. The only remaining flaw is export: it does not yet work well, and the font in exported PDFs is unfortunately poor — but given the developer's responsiveness, I expect this to improve.

My suggestions: improve export to Word and PDF (top priority), ready-made educational agents (lesson plans, quizzes with answer keys), LMS integration. I also hope an iPhone and Android app is released soon — that would greatly enrich the user experience and make it possible to keep working on the go.

Conclusion: WorkLLM is a fully fledged collaborative workspace, not just another AI chat app. worth every penny you pay for it!

comments.title: This is the one. I’ve tried a LOT of AI tools — and WorkLLM is the first one that actually feels built for getting work done.
comments.comment:
I bought WorkLLM on AppSumo after trying countless AI platforms, wrappers, agents, and automation tools. Honestly, I was getting frustrated.

Some were buggy. Others had amazing feature lists but were so complicated that you needed terminals, workflows, mind maps, prompts, or tutorials just to accomplish one simple thing.

Then I tried WorkLLM.

This is it.

The UI is amazing. No technical setup, no terminal, and no support call needed just to figure out how it works. You open it and can start working immediately.

For someone who isn't an AI expert, that's huge.

Chat with AI without thinking about the AI

You get 200 models, including GPT, Claude, Gemini and others, and can switch models while keeping the conversation and context.

The shared memory is a major advantage. Your context can carry across LLMs, chat projects, and organization-wide memory instead of starting from zero every time.

I've tried different AI platforms, and honestly, I now prefer WorkLLM for much of my work over going directly to ChatGPT or Claude.

Instead of asking, "Which AI tool do I need?" you just chat and get the work done.

⭐ Amazing for a small team

This may be one of the most underrated parts of WorkLLM.

If you have a small team or work with freelancers, you can have a shared workspace where everyone can work with AI together.

Instead of every employee having separate AI accounts and knowledge being scattered everywhere, your team can actually use AI as part of the business.

And because the interface is so easy, you don't need to train everyone for hours before they can start.

A small-business owner can hand this to a team and say: "Go use it."

Getting the work done is incredibly easy.

I love how easy it is to turn AI output into something useful.

With essentially one click, you can export/send to:

Word
PDF
CSV
Excel
Email

You're not stuck figuring out how to get the AI's work into your actual business. Click → export → done.

That's what makes WorkLLM feel like a real work tool rather than another AI demo.

Is everything perfect? No.

There are things I'd still like: better clarity about credit usage and what gets saved where, BYOK, API/MCP access, dedicated desktop/mobile apps, offline access, and improved RTL support.

I'd also love higher-tier plans for heavier users. At the same time, I appreciate that they're thinking about sustainability instead of simply giving away unlimited usage to win customers.

Many of these features are already on the roadmap, and after seeing the heart and soul of the founder in every support response, I’m completely comfortable waiting. It’s clear that he genuinely cares about the product and the users, and that gives me confidence that these features will be done right.

The support is on another level

This is where WorkLLM really surprised me.

I sent a long list of feedback, questions, bugs, and feature requests. I expected the usual "Thanks, we'll pass it along."

Instead, I got real answers within hours, even on Sundays.

But what impressed me even more is that they didn't just tell me they were working on things.

They actually shipped updates and fixes.

I've seen issues I reported get fixed within a day or two, along with improvements being released based on customer feedback.

They also explain what they're doing, why they made certain decisions, and when something doesn't fit their vision. That's the kind of transparency I really appreciate.

I've rarely seen a SaaS team respond to customers this quickly and then actually deliver the changes.

Why 5 tacos? 🌮🌮🌮🌮🌮

I've tried a ridiculous number of AI tools looking for something that actually saves me time.

I've seen buggy platforms, complicated automation systems, endless-feature tools with terrible UX, and wrappers that don't add enough value.

WorkLLM is different.

The product gets out of your way.

You can open it and start chatting. Use different models in the same conversation. Keep your context and memory. Work with your team. Export to Word, PDF, CSV or Excel. Email the results. And you don't need to be technical to understand what you're doing.

I'm not giving it 5 stars because every feature is finished.

I'm giving it 5 stars because the core product is already genuinely useful today, the UI is excellent, the team listens, and — most importantly — they actually act on the feedback they receive.

If you're a small-business owner, especially with a small team, and you want something you can open and start using immediately, this is one of the best AI tools I've come across.

I've tried a LOT of them.

This is the one I'm sticking with.

Disclaimer: I used the help of multiple AI models available in WorkLLM to improve and refine the writing.

George (the founder) reached out personally and addressed all our issues at lightning speed. He took our feedback seriously, and delivered quick fixes to 99% of our problems, and shipped most of the features we wanted in just a couple of days.

The roadmap also looks VERY promising: at the current pace of development, I think it's reasonable to say that ApproveThis will mature into a full approval & feedback management platform within a few months at most.

With that being said, the tool is already super useful for us to manage approvals/feedback from our clients, regarding deliverables. It also helps internal decision making, although that's not our primary use case.

To summarize: amazing tool, promising roadmap, and an incredible founder – don't miss this gem!

comments.title: Just what we needed
comments.comment:
With our e-commerce team ApproveThis solved a very specific pain fast. Setting up the mailbox took a few minutes. I created a forwarding address to the ApproveThis mailbox, and new requests started showing up immediately. 

The easy part is how approvals works, all our managers are in email all day, so thats perfect. They get an email, click Approve or Decline, add a short note if needed, and they are done. That single feature removed a lot of “did you see this?” messages. We also like the simple status view and the automatic record of who approved and when, which keeps audits straightforward. Custom fields are there if we want them, but the default flow already fits 90% of our use cases. If you want a lightweight way to collect and track approvals without creating more logins, this hits the mark.

comments.title: Fast, No-Login Approvals
comments.comment:
We recently started using ApproveThis to streamline approvals in our startup, and it’s been a big win for our team. 

Setting up a mailbox to receive requests took less than five minutes, and now we can route any approval, whether for budgets, marketing materials, or contracts, straight to the right people. The best part is that approvers don’t need to log in or create an account. They just click “approve” or “reject” right from the email notification. 

This has cut down on delays and back-and-forth messages, since decisions get made on the spot. 

For a small team where everyone is juggling multiple roles, that speed and simplicity make a huge difference. Thank you for building this!

comments.title: Custom forms made our approval process actually work
comments.comment:
Setting up custom approval forms in ApproveThis was surprisingly straightforward. I created different forms for purchase orders, time-off requests, and project approvals with specific fields for each type. The form editor let me add dropdown menus, required fields, and validation so we don't get incomplete requests anymore.
The best part? Once someone submits a form, it automatically emails the right approvers who can just hit approve or reject directly from the notification without logging into anything. Our department heads went from taking days to respond to approving requests the same day.
No more digging through messy email chains or chasing people down for decisions.

So much better than just using email since it introduces an unmistakable yes/no approval for the request and keeps everything in one place for record keeping. comments.title: AI that follows you wherever you type
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What stood out in Acti is that the AI is built into the keyboard itself. I don't have to leave the app I'm using, open a chatbot, ask for something, copy the answer, and then come back.

I tested it on iOS in Gmail, Notes and Messenger, and it worked as advertised. I could use the main action from the space bar, and I also assigned a specific action to a letter key and triggered it directly from the keyboard.

This is what differentiates Acti from a normal AI keyboard. It can help with writing, dictation and translation, but the bigger idea is turning any text field into a place where you can ask a question or run an action without leaving the app you're already in. Just imagine how much time this could save.

I'm finding that there are a surprising number of little app switches throughout the day that add up. You're chatting with someone and need to look up an address. Someone makes a claim and you want to check it before replying. You need a quick answer or a bit of research while writing an email. Normally that means leaving the conversation, opening another app or AI tool, finding the answer, and coming back. Being able to do those things from the keyboard saves more time than I expected.

You can also create your own Acts by describing what you want in plain language. Act Builder Agent can turn that into a reusable workflow, and you can refine it through conversation until it does what you want. There are also thousands of existing Acts you can add and personalize instead of making everything yourself.

Acti can connect those Acts to apps and APIs too, so they can do more than manipulate the text in front of you. The current deal includes connections across 300+ apps and APIs, with integrations such as Gmail, Slack, Notion and custom APIs.

One thing to understand about the credits is that normal voice dictation does not use them. AI actions and workflows do, with basic workflows currently using one credit per execution. The monthly credits reset rather than rolling over, and BYOK is not currently available.

For me, the biggest advantage is still where Acti is located. The keyboard is already there in almost every app I use on my phone, so the AI comes to me instead of making me change apps every time I need it.

One drawback I've run into is that the keyboard can occasionally feel less responsive, especially when I'm typing quickly. It isn't constant, and it hasn't stopped me from using Acti, but there are moments when it feels a little sluggish compared with the standard iPhone keyboard.

I've actually kept Acti on my iPhone since the original test and I still use it. The more I use it, the more I notice how much time is normally wasted jumping between apps for small questions and tasks that can now happen right where I'm already typing.

comments.title: Very cool keyboard with ai integrated.
comments.comment:
I set it up on my Android and tested it. This is very innovative, and phones should come with this keyboard by default. I'm concerned that when big Google sees this, they will implement it immediately for Android. This keyboard gives you the power of AI at your fingertips. I'm frustrated that a lot of tools that come to appsumo lately don't support Windows, which blows my mind considering windows/nvidia is leading that race and can handle larger LLMs for AI infrastructure. 

I would like to see access to the Windows app within the next 60 days so I can determine if it's a keeper or not. 

The layout is different from the default Android keyboard, so it will take a little bit of muscle memory unless they could examine the Samsung keyboard and make layout options to switch to. The question key comes on the Samsung KB by default as a standalone button; it doesn't in Acti, so it's one extra step to use a very common question mark. All of the common symbol keys you would use, such as @, %, $, ', ", #, and! etc are all inside a button that you hold down, whereas on the Samsung KB, they are all visible on your main keyboard to hold down and click as a secondary key. 

I communicate in GIFs and emojis; I was glad to see the AI skill for being able to analyze our text and pick a relevant GIF. The problem is you can't see the GIF until you send it. That's a big trust to an AI that might misread a typo and send your girlfriend a GIF of a big sausage by accident, and nobody wants to see that. It makes me wonder what GIF it would choose if I used a bad word in my text. So I'd like to see some sort of preview for GIFs, as well as other GIF options if I don't like the one it picked- maybe a retry button or a GIF gallery. 

The Acti keyboard on my Samsung Galaxy S26 could use some improvement in visuals. The keys don't have much effect on them to look like real buttons. This is partly due to the background behind the keys being too light. Samsung uses a grey color as the background with white keys so they stand out a bit more. 

Looking forward to the Windows app so I can see what this tool is really made of, but even without it currently, it seems like I'll get good use out of it. 

I took off one star so far in testing for no Windows application and no GIF preview.

Update: there is a high-contrast theme mode in the settings that makes the keys stand out more. Also, I'm very impressed with the voice transcribing and emoji mode! This thing has a lot of great AI skills. It would be awesome if the Acti app had an AI chat convo mode where I could talk to the AI and use these skills, since they are valuable beyond just texting someone. The more I use this, the more it's becoming a must-buy, and I haven't even scratched the surface because I don't have access to the Windows app.

comments.title: The “Goldilocks” of Data Viz: Powerful, Fast, and UI-Focused
comments.comment:
If you’ve ever felt like Excel is too basic but Power BI is a full-time job just to learn, InstaCharts is your new best friend. It occupies that perfect middle ground where professional design meets extreme ease of use.

The Sharing Controls are “Fab” This is a huge standout for me. When you share a chart via a public link or iFrame embed, you aren't just dumping data. You have granular control:

Privacy & Scope: You choose if the end-user sees just the chart or the underlying data table too.

Look & Feel: You can lock down the aesthetic so it matches your brand perfectly, keeping your reports looking cohesive and high-end.

UI/UX & Founder Support The interface is a breath of fresh air—clean, snappy, and zero clutter. But what really seals the deal is the human element. The founder, Bart, is incredibly active and actually listens. It’s rare to buy a tool where you feel like your feedback could literally shape the next update.

The "BI Tool" Reality Check Is this a replacement for a £100/mo enterprise BI tool? Not yet. It’s missing a few "big league" components like:
- API-driven data collection (for pulling live app data automatically).
- Advanced Dashboards with multi-chart drill-down capabilities.
- Complex Team Permissions for large-scale orgs.

But here’s the kicker: If it had those features, would it be on a Lifetime Deal for this price? Absolutely not. You’d be paying a monthly subscription that would make your eyes water.

The Verdict: For 90% of business owners, marketers, and researchers, InstaCharts does exactly what you need it to do: it makes data look beautiful, instantly. It’s a "speed-to-insight" tool that pays for itself in saved time within the first day!

comments.title: Hello Aria App Review
comments.comment:
Hello Aria App Review

I tested Hello Aria once by using WhatsApp to record a task and view my daily schedule. The app is designed to connect with Google Calendar, allowing users to add reminders and appointments through WhatsApp instead of opening the calendar manually.

The daily message displayed my reminders, calendar events, times, and links in a fairly clear format. This could be useful for people who want a quick overview of their schedule or prefer sending voice messages rather than typing directly into Google Calendar.

However, this review is based on only one test, so I cannot yet comment on its reliability, accuracy, or performance over a longer period. It would be useful to test how well the app handles unclear voice messages, changes to appointments, recurring reminders, and missed notifications.

What I noticed
- Tasks and reminders can be recorded through WhatsApp.
- The app provides a daily summary of calendar events.
- Appointment times and links are shown in the message.
- It may reduce the need to check Google Calendar manually.

Overall
Hello Aria appears to be a convenient calendar assistant, but I have only tested it once. The initial experience was straightforward, although more testing would be needed to assess how dependable it is for regular use.

comments.title: Good productivity tool but needs lot of improvement.
comments.comment:
The application is excellent, particularly because of its broad integration capabilities. However, I believe a few enhancements could significantly improve the user experience and help position Aria as a stronger productivity, task management, and note-taking platform.

Suggestions for Improvement

1. Richer Task Management

Tasks should support a dedicated description field with full Markdown support.
Support for nested tasks, subtasks, and checklists would make it easier to manage larger projects and action plans.
The ability to add structured notes directly within tasks would help consolidate task context in one place.

2. Better Calendar Integration

The calendar integration does not appear to be functioning as expected.
After connecting Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar, Aria should display and synchronize existing calendar events seamlessly.
Changes made in either platform should be reflected consistently within Aria.

3. Custom System Instructions

Users should be able to define custom system instructions or preferences for different modules, such as:
Tasks
Reminders
Notes
Calendar
This would allow Aria to adapt its behavior to each user's preferred workflow and organizational style.

4. Stronger Memory and Skill Learning

Aria should develop a persistent memory layer that learns from user behavior and gradually builds personalized workflows, preferences, and skills.
Currently, task creation often requires users to provide every detail upfront.
Instead, Aria should support an Inbox-style capture workflow, allowing users to quickly capture ideas, tasks, or action items with minimal information and process or refine them later.
The experience should feel more proactive and adaptive over time rather than repeatedly collecting the same information.

5. Smarter Multi-Action Processing

Aria should be capable of understanding and processing multiple requests from a single message.
Users should not have to repeatedly separate tasks or provide information in a rigid format.
The current approach introduces unnecessary friction and slows down the quick-capture experience that Aria's integration-focused design is intended to provide.
More intelligent extraction and processing of multiple actions would make interactions much more natural and efficient.

6. Full-Fledged Notes Experience

Notes should support Markdown formatting and rich content rendering.
Images, attachments, and files shared with Aria should automatically be stored in connected cloud storage such as Google Drive or OneDrive and referenced within the note.
Notes should support embedded images, attachments, links, checklists, code blocks, and other Markdown elements.
A modern note-taking experience similar to tools such as Obsidian would make Aria significantly more valuable as a knowledge management platform rather than just a capture tool.
Overall Recommendation

Aria already has a strong foundation with its conversational interface and extensive integrations. The next stage of evolution should focus on reducing user friction through better memory, richer task management, improved note-taking capabilities, seamless calendar synchronization, and more intelligent processing of user inputs.

With these improvements, Aria could become not only an excellent integration platform but also a highly capable task management and note-taking solution that users can rely on as their primary productivity workspace.

comments.title: Turn your expertise into AI tools you can sell
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

What interests me about Formwise is that it goes beyond making an AI form or chatbot. You can take the way you already work, your methods, documents and knowledge, and turn that into something another person can actually use.

You can create a Flow for something that should follow the same process each time, or an Agent for work that needs a more open conversation. For example, a consultant could turn their assessment process into a guided tool that asks the client the right questions and produces the same type of deliverable they would normally create manually.

You can also give Agents your own knowledge and instructions, and even combine several Agents under a supervisor that sends each request to the appropriate specialist. That opens up more interesting uses than a single chatbot answering questions from a PDF.

The part I find particularly useful is what happens after you make one. Formwise lets you share or embed what you've created, or put it inside a portal where clients can log in. You can even charge for access through built-in checkout. For coaches, consultants and agencies, I can see that turning a process you normally deliver one client at a time into something clients can use on their own.

BYOK is another important addition. On Tier 2 and above you can connect your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini key, so once the included credits are gone, your AI usage can go directly through your own provider instead. That's especially relevant if you're planning to give clients ongoing access rather than just experimenting with a few internal tools.

There are also API, webhook and MCP options if you want to take things further. The MCP is particularly interesting because you can manage Formwise Agents, Flows and knowledge bases from assistants like ChatGPT or Claude rather than doing everything from the dashboard.

Overall, I think Formwise is most interesting when you already have knowledge or a repeatable process that other people pay you for. Instead of simply using AI to help you do that work faster, you can turn some of that process into an AI tool and give or sell access to it. For me, that's a much more interesting use of Formwise than simply making another chatbot.

comments.title: Built a working branching audit tool in one session — this is the real deal
comments.comment:
I came in skeptical of a zero-review Launchpad product, but I used it to build something concrete: a Shift Change Culture Audit for my convenience store training platform. Three yes/no questions, an AI Prompt node scoring the answers into structured JSON, a Classify node routing to three different outcomes, and each branch producing a fully formatted, signable PDF report — compliance summary, findings, recommended actions, signature lines, the works.

What impressed me most: the Classify node’s branching worked reliably across every test, including the worst-case scenario (all three answers failing), which produced the most detailed output of the three — a two-page audit document with a risk assessment table I could hand to a store manager today. The document artifact capability turning a scored conversation into a professional PDF, on command, was the feature that sold me.

Support was excellent and fast — the founder answered detailed technical questions about knowledge base architecture, memory scoping, and integration options same-day, which told me a lot about where this product is headed.

One thing worth knowing going in: branching isn’t called “If/Else” — it’s done through a Classify node that uses example-based categorization rather than exact logic matching. Once I understood that, it worked exactly as I needed.

If you’re sitting on structured expertise — checklists, audits, frameworks, SOPs — and want to turn them into interactive tools instead of static PDFs, this does exactly that. I’m already planning dozens of these across my training platform.

Worklenz proves itself to be a commendable project management software, striking a balance between usability and functionality. The platform offers a clear and concise design that caters to both technical and non-technical users, empowering business owners to manage projects with ease. However, the software's ongoing development leaves room for improvement, earning it four out of five tacos.

Pros:

Usability: Worklenz excels in providing a user-friendly interface, making it accessible to individuals with varying technical backgrounds. The intuitive design ensures that even non-technical business owners can efficiently navigate and utilize its features.

Functionality: The software covers the essential project management features, allowing users to perform tasks effectively. From task management to project tracking, Worklenz delivers on its promise to meet the basic needs of project teams.

Clear and Concise Design: The interface is well-organized, promoting clarity and simplicity in project management. This is a significant advantage for users who prefer straightforward tools without unnecessary complexity.

Cons:

Work in Progress: While Worklenz fulfills its core functions, it's apparent that the software is still a work in progress. Users may encounter limitations as the platform continues to evolve, affecting the overall experience.


Suggestions for Improvement:

Unlimited User/Team Feature: Considering the needs of agencies, an ideal enhancement would be the inclusion of an Unlimited User/Team feature in the Appsumo plan. To balance this, introducing a Client/Guest Preview or observer feature could provide a workaround for accommodating various stakeholders without compromising the subscription model.

FAQ Center Implementation: To enhance user experience and address potential confusion surrounding certain features, the addition of a comprehensive FAQ center is recommended. This resource can serve as a valuable knowledge base, providing users with clear explanations and step-by-step guides for functionalities that may not be immediately self-explanatory.

Client Bios Customization: Offering more flexibility in client management by allowing the creation of custom fields for client bios would be a valuable addition. This feature would empower users, especially agencies, to tailor client profiles according to their specific needs. Customizable fields can include additional details, preferences, or project-specific information, providing a more personalized approach to client management.

Mobile App Development: Exploring the development of a mobile app could significantly enhance the software's accessibility and flexibility. This addition would enable users to manage their projects on the go, contributing to a seamless project management experience.

I created my first mind maps with AmyMind and I am absolutely thrilled! Whether I created new mind maps completely frm scratch with AI or automatically from a Word document or PDF – AmyMind delivers! Usually, the mind maps are more than good on the first try, but if needed, I can also have the AI generate additional subpoints after creation or, of course, add them myself.

The handling of the tool is really well-developed, so that it can be used very well as a standalone mind map program, independent of the AI functions. The mind maps also look very appealing. In my case, I had the mind maps created in German, which worked flawlessly.

What I would still wish for:
- You can move the mind map back and forth by holding down the spacebar and left-clicking. This works very awkwardly on a (at east my) laptop. It would be nice if you could just hold down the mouse button to move it back and forth.
- Expanding and collapsing is done via a small menu directly on the entry. In my opinion, a dedicated symbol would be better (as long as clarity does not suffer).
- Although there is a presentation mode (which is great), it would be amazing if it showed the mind map overview and then zoomed in and out of the individual branches, so you always know where you are in the mind map. Currently, the view is text-based.

Apart from that, AmyMind is one of my favorite tools here on AppSumo and gets an absolute recommendation from me!

comments.title: A mind‑mapping game‑changer that finally “gets” power users!

A mind‑mapping game‑changer that finally “gets” power users!
What I love

Full Korean UI – huge thanks for localizing the menus. It makes onboarding lightning‑fast for my team.

True mind‑map file export ( *.mm , *.opml , etc.). Most AI tools only spit out images, which are useless for further editing. AmyMind lets me keep an open workflow.

Blazing‑fast product iteration. I suggested tweaks last week and already saw them live. The devs clearly listen.

What would make it perfect

Pitch Mode – a dynamic, Prezi‑style presentation view so a single map can become a wow‑factor slide deck in seconds.

Native mobile apps (iOS & Android). PWA works, but an installable app with offline caching and biometric login would be next‑level.

“Lock layout” toggle. After finishing a map, automatic zoom/resize can ruin the composition. Give us per‑branch pinning and fixed canvas size so our design stays exactly as crafted.

Bottom line
AmyMind is already the fastest‑improving AI mind‑map tool I’ve tested, and the only one that outputs real map files instead of flat images. Add Pitch Mode + mobile apps + layout lock and it will be the gold standard. Grab the deal while you can—you’ll thank yourself later!

comments.title: Loving this App
comments.comment:
I've been using this app for over a year now, and it's the best tool I have found to help keep me organized and not forget things. I have ADHD and always forget things that are not right in front of me. 

I had tried many tools previously, but none of them worked very well and were abandoned within a few weeks. With browser-based tools, you need to have a browser open and a connection to the internet in order to use them. I would pin the tab so I would always see it, but often I would close the wrong browser window first and lose all my tabs and would forget about the tool, and end up missing important deadlines or appointments. Or sometimes I might not be connected to the internet or have the browser open and would then not get the notifications. Some other apps could only installed on one device; they wouldn't sync, or you would need an active internet or cell phone connection, which I don't always have, or they just didn't have the features I needed. 

Physical planners rarely worked unless I made a point of always carrying them around, but would often then lose them or just forget to open them to look. Often the way they were set up didn't work for me either, and I would abandon them after a couple of weeks of use.

Chaos Control was fairly easy-to-use right from the start, but it took a little trial and error to figure out exactly how to use all the features in a way that worked for me. I have installed it on my home desktop system, my laptop, my tablet and my phone, so no matter where I am, one of these devices has it right there, and the notifications alert me so I don't forget appointments and deadlines very often now. Also having the app set to start as soon as your device starts up is a big win for me, so I don't forget to start it.

You can set tasks with repetitions, so they pop up daily, weekly or however often you set them to. 

You can create projects with different tasks for them and set start dates and deadlines up for each task so it will appear in your daily task to do list only when applicable, and you can create a checklist inside each task in case you want to break them down into smaller steps. You even have a folder structure so you can put different projects and tasks into different categories and organize them in a way that makes sense to you.

I love the timer that tracks the time you spent on each specific task so you can check back later to see the total time it took and time spent for each individual session. There are also options for tagging your tasks by priority, color, or other means. The app has different themes you can use to customize it. You can also bookmark certain tasks or projects in order to find them more easily. 

I really like that you can store files and images right in the app and have it synced with your other devices.

The most important things for me are that it can still be used when you are offline or out of cell service (which is often for me), and will sync as soon as you get back online, and I can install it on as many devices as I want and they will all sync, so I rarely forget important tasks and appointments now.

Since I've been using the app, there have been several upgrades, and each one keeps getting better. There is now the ability to use AI right in the app and to record voice, although I haven't used them yet, so I can't comment on how it works.

The only thing I would like to see added is something like a habit tracker that you can click each time you do something that might be something you do several times a day or a couple times a week but not at any specific times, so you can see how often you are doing the desired task (or bad habit). For instance, I ate healthy 4 times this week, and ate junk food 3 times this week, or drank 7 glasses of water today. 

Overall, if you've tried other ways to organize your life and they haven't worked, then give Chaos Control a try to see if it's right for you.

The Time Tracking option is also a game-changer. I’ve recently started logging all my daily activities following the book Buy Back Your Time by Dan Martell, and Chaos Control provides the perfect solution for this.

I also appreciate how intuitive it is to set up repeating tasks. It’s much more flexible and visually appealing than similar apps I’ve used. For example, I even track my daily water intake with it!

I use both the desktop version and the iOS app. While the desktop version has some minor issues, they’re not deal-breakers, and I’m confident future updates will improve them.

I’m really happy I found this app—it’s a great tool for anyone looking for a structured yet flexible way to manage their tasks and time.

comments.title: Super Intuitive to Use!
comments.comment:
I've tried lots of different organizing/to-do apps, but this one is the most intuitive for how my brain works. Most apps are just basic to-do reminders, which is great, but doesn't help with organizing big projects. Notion is really robust, but it's not intuitive for me at all, and I don't have time to take a class to learn how to use it.

Chaos Control was intuitive for me "out of the box". It uses a file folder-type structure to keep bigger projects organized, but it also has a Chaos Box for the "don't want to forget this" details (just like a normal to-do list) that could be organized later if needed.

Also, the program gives you many ways to *see* what you can work on, even without cluttering your daily plan with deadline tasks, such as priority levels, contexts, etc. For example, I set up a "15 minutes or less" context to flag little things like "Work on organizing desk pile" or "Make appt with eye doctor", so I can find something productive to do anytime I'm not sure what to work on next.

I already feel more organized and motivated to get work done, and that alone makes this worthwhile!

comments.title: Persistence is valuable, expecting tacos to increase
comments.comment:
I originally purchased FuseBase (1 year ago) for an online education use case: onboarding students, creating portal rooms for individual learners and groups, sharing session documents, and supporting collaborative project work. The vision was compelling—a flexible client and student portal that could bring learning materials, communication, recordings, and project collaboration into one place.

My experience has been mixed, largely because I joined during a major period of product transition. FuseBase was moving from more basic AI features toward a much more agent-driven product direction. During that shift, there was a noticeable drop in communication and continuity for early users like me. It sometimes felt like we were caught between the former platform and the future version still being built.

That said, I chose to stay engaged. I joined the community spaces, followed product updates, watched videos, and learned from power users willing to share how they were using the platform. That has helped me see both the current limitations and the longer-term opportunity.

One feature that did not work reliably for me was the webinar recording extension. It failed to record an important consulting call that was under an hour long. I later tested it with a much shorter call, under five minutes, and it worked correctly—but that was not a meaningful test for the type of client meetings I need to capture. Reliable recordings are central to my intended use of FuseBase within a client portal, so this was a significant disappointment.

I do not see this as a permanent product flaw so much as a maturity and documentation issue. The platform is evolving quickly, but the training materials and documentation do not always appear to keep pace with what is actively being built and changed. There is a large amount of educational material available, yet it can be impractical when it does not reflect the current product experience.

Despite these frustrations, I am giving FuseBase four tacos because I believe in Pavel and the team. They have invested heavily in the platform’s transition, and their development experience is visible. I expect the current turnaround to produce meaningful benefits for the broader user base—not only customers who receive high-touch, white-glove support.

I also had a one-on-one conversation with Pavel when I first decided to onboard (April). His advice was candid: unless I needed an immediate solution, I should give the product a few months to develop and, in the meantime, become more comfortable with VS Code for general AI upskilling. That was some of the best advice I have received in this space. It increased my ability to work with tools that are less dependent on a simple user interface and more capable under the hood.

In some ways, that captures FuseBase’s current challenge. Highly technical users may find parts of the platform insufficient and wonky while it continues to add deeper capability. At the same time, non-technical users may feel that the product is becoming more complex faster than its documentation and training can support.

Still, the progress so far is impressive. The transition is not finished, but it is already showing real promise. The user community is generally helpful and supportive, and I remain optimistic that FuseBase can become a powerful solution for client portals, education programs, collaborative workspaces, and knowledge-driven businesses.

Bottom line: FuseBase is not yet a fully polished, plug-and-play platform for every use case. But for users who can tolerate some change, stay engaged with the community, and grow with the product, it has substantial potential that is being realized in real-time.

comments.title: FuseBase for Palliative Care Coordination: What the LTD Delivers
comments.comment:
We evaluated FuseBase as a coordination layer for care plans, medication schedules, goals-of-care notes, and advance directives for a small palliative care team. The white-labeled portals are clean and family-friendly—families get one place to find what they need, and it carries our name rather than a generic dashboard. Setup took an afternoon.

The newer AI Apps with backend support—introduced earlier this year—let non-developers describe a symptom tracker in plain language and get a working app with a Postgres database and role-based permissions. Pain, dyspnea, anxiety, and alertness scores logged into structured fields, and the app flagged trajectory shifts that would otherwise require manual chart review. Permissions were more useful than we expected: nursing got full write access, family members stayed read-only on selected pages, and admin controls stayed with our lead. The database held up as entries accumulated, and we never had to touch a schema. Onboarding was smoother than we feared, support answered within a day on portal permissions, and reliability stayed steady across months of daily use—no lost entries, no sync surprises. It's not a full EHR, but for palliative care's messy, human-scale workflows, it's close.

On the AppSumo side, the coupon mechanics are unusually generous. Codes stack without a hard limit, the founder has confirmed that every code counts as "+1," activating 20 coupons gives you a doubled Tier 10 plus a bonus, and codes can be distributed across multiple organizations. That's genuinely useful if your program spans several sites, and the math scales cleanly if you're deciding how many to buy.

Two factual notes worth confirming directly with the vendor before committing to clinical use, since contract terms sit outside the lifetime deal: a BAA is issued only on Enterprise plans, with a DPA as the default agreement for LTD buyers, and the Nimbus iOS app is dated compared to the browser version—the browser is where the AI Apps and automations live, so treat mobile as a companion for now.

Overall: for the price of the LTD, the portals, AI Apps builder, permissions, and stacking flexibility add up to real value. We'd buy it again.

comments.title: Ambitious all‑in‑one notes platform that still needs to fix the basics
comments.comment:
I run a small consulting advisory and have been using Nimbus Note (now called FuseBase) since 2020 when I moved my whole knowledge base out of Evernote. 5 years into a Business Plan lifetime deal I feel in a good position to give a frank, practitioner's opinion for Sumolings who care about productivity tools that actually work in the day-to-day pressure. 

FuseBase has become a feature-rich product. The ambition of the team to be more than just a notebook (integrating task management, web clipping, collaborative docs and now increasingly AI-powered features) is apparent in the product and marketing. Product updates and the company site talk about expanded integrations and a push into more automated workflows. That ambition is good: as a consultant I want a one-stop shop for capturing meeting notes, clipping research, annotating files and doing quick analyses without switching tools. Where FuseBase does well is in how the product has blended multiple use cases. The UI supports both structured notes and freeform capture, it can store attachments and web clips, and customer support has been responsive when I have needed help. 

But the rebrand from Nimbus to FuseBase is still not finished: domain redirects are inconsistent, some pages and links point to nimbusweb.com and important desktop continuity has been forgotten. My Mac desktop client is stuck in limbo: it has not received the polished modern refresh I expected and for years now the behavior and performance is behind the web app. One concrete casualty has been extensions: The Nimbus Clipper was removed from my workflow and not replaced with a clear, direct alternative. For consultants who live in the browser and clip research all the time that is a real workflow regression. Performance is my biggest recurring complaint. 

FuseBase is functional but often slow. Search queries and note opens can impose multi-second waits, sometimes I have seen one-to-three second delays that feel trivial in writing but add up to real friction across a day of client work. The public messaging of the platform has not addressed this. Other modern note platforms – historically Evernote – set a baseline expectation for near-instant search and navigation. The feature proliferation of FuseBase is promising, but not if the core experience of capturing and retrieving information is still sluggish. 

I am also watching the company's strategic focus with cautious optimism. The recent moves to promote AI features and "agents" are in line with industry trends and will attract new users but risk shifting development and product attention away from core note capture, clip reliability, desktop parity and speed. Personally, I don't need fancy AI assistants embedded everywhere, I need fast, reliable input, editing and search, plus robust clipping and sync behavior. If FuseBase puts more engineering effort into shiny AI demos than into the nuts and bolts of syncing, indexing and client stability, long-time users like me will feel neglected. 

For potential buyers on AppSumo: FuseBase is worth a look if you want a single platform that tries to replace a constellation of apps (note taking, web clipping, lightweight tasks and collaborative docs) and you care about responsive support. The lifetime deal I bought made the financial decision easy years ago. If you are deciding now ask specific questions about Mac desktop parity, the status of browser extensions and performance benchmarks for search on data volumes similar to yours. Test the web clipping and search on a free account with real workload before you commit. If your priority is blinding speed, frictionless search and an absolutely solid desktop client, proceed with caution. FuseBase can be slower than competing tools and the rebrand inconsistencies suggest some execution risk. If the team prioritizes polishing the fundamentals (restoring and improving the clipper, accelerating search indexing and shipping a reliable Mac desktop experience) FuseBase could be a best-in-class consolidated workspace. Until then it's a powerful evolving product with moments of brilliance and still many rough edges.

I have checked out many alternatives, but so far Nimbus Notes is the best. The Chrome web clipper is the best I've tried and note updates are quick. The template gallery seems pretty good.

The recognition is ok. But you just get a seperate window with text. No searchable PDF output (where you can select and copy parts of text) + no OCR for PDFs and other documents in general - just for pictures it seems.

comments.title: Great Tool with a couple caveats
comments.comment:
First off, I've been a Notejoy user for the last few years.  I never was able to jump all in with Evernote and their limits turned me off when I tried.  Notejoy has been good but there were limitations.  Other reviewers mentioned Notion which is one I have no experience with.

Enter Nimbus Note.  I had not heard of it previously but decided to give it a try after taking a look at the software.

Right off the bat I was impressed with the range of options with formatting, outlining, working in visual media, etc.  I quickly saw that though much of the basic functionality I had elsewhere was sufficient, the experience in Nimbus would be much nicer and appealing to use.  So far that expectation has been the case - in the web portal version - which leads to a few concerns.

I've accessed the software in three ways.  One via a web browser, one through the desktop software (Windows 10), and one on my android phone.  The web browser is great and I've had zero issues or lag.  With my desktop installation I have some nested folders that still don't show up.  The notes are there if I search for them, but it does not show the folder.  Not a huge deal, but odd.  The phone app is okay - not great.  I do not like how I have to sometimes manually hit the sync or exit/reopen the app to get everything up to date.  It just isn't a great user experience.

Other than the issues with a couple of the access points I've really liked the software and plan to use it.  I'm expecting it to increase in value over time.

comments.title: Fixed Data Storage :(
comments.comment:
I had been using the free tier for a few months and that is the only reason I bought this app.

If I wasn't a free user, I wouldn't get the deal because I am not very happy about the hard limits on how much content I can store.

I get that data has cost (low and going lower by the day), but a fixed data limit doesn't feel very "lifetime" to me.

We need to have better data storage limits. This isn't really a lifetime deal with storage that is capped. It doesn't matter how limited your usage is, you are going to hit the ceiling on the 50GB one day and be forced to choose a different app or spend money to get more storage.

Also the deal isn't very clear about what happens after 50 GB is used because eventually everyone is going to run out of storage... especially when the app is so versatile! (catch 22?) 

So what happens after I am over the 50 GB? I tried to find an answer in the questions but I couldn't. Do I have to pay monthly? Can I buy storage upgrades as 1 time cost upgrades? Can I connect to external storage? 

In this day and age data storage is super cheap so this restriction has me very annoyed.

With that major gripe about fixed storage data limits out of the way I am very happy that AppSumo brought Nimbus to their platform. I missed out on this when it was offered on another website and have been secretly wishing it would come back.

The main draw for me is clipping text and screenshots into a rough working draft that I can then quickly transform into awesome, well researched content.

I also bought markuphero but that is only for quick screenshot capture and sharing. Nimbus enhances my workflow by letting me collect all the thoughts and then build on stuff that I have clipped from across the web.

My only other suggestions would be to have the ability to edit saved images like you can with markup hero.

P.S. I get a notion vibe from the app and can't wait for it to evolve further.
