comments.title: A comprehensive, modern platform that stays on the cutting edge of tech
comments.comment:
FuseBase has successfully evolved from a simple workspace into a versatile operational platform built to drive value across the entire organization. Its greatest asset is how fast it adopts cutting-edge technology—integrating white-labeled client portals, databases, and autonomous AI agents to automate workflows and consolidate tools into a single dashboard.
Because the platform advances so quickly, there is an unavoidable learning curve, and the official documentation occasionally lags behind new releases. However, the product's forward-looking direction and active development more than compensate for it. For any team looking for an all-in-one ecosystem that scales alongside modern tech innovations, FuseBase is an outstanding long-term asset.

comments.title: Wasn't sure before, but now i am: this rocks!
comments.comment:
As another user pointed out, I got this to replace Notion/Evernote. But a month after fully stacking the app, it took a different direction. I was kind of bummed, to be honest, so I just let it rest for a few months.

Now they’ve released so many new features that I initially thought wouldn’t work for me, until I started putting them to use. I just rebuilt an app I had on Frontly using client portals in the latest format (Astro), without using Google Sheets. I think this will be better in the long run. I used MCP and Codex; it took about six hours of going back and forth, but it’s much more powerful now.

Also, since I have 10 codes, I get to use their Paperclip implementation (Fusebase Work). I’m already looking into creating agents to ingest data and process tasks.

I’ll likely stack more codes now. :)

comments.title: From scattered information to one organised client workspace
comments.comment:
FuseBase has changed how we manage client work. Before, documents, drafts, feedback and approvals were spread across emails, chats and shared drives. Now everything sits in one white-labelled workspace under our own brand, and clients always know where to find what they need.

The team keeps shipping useful updates, and support has been quick and helpful whenever we needed it.

Next, we're setting up the AI agents to help with drafting, summaries and client onboarding, and we're looking forward to seeing how much time they save.

The result so far is a more organized operation and a more professional experience for every client, from the first login onwards.

Looking ahead to 2027, we're excited to grow our use of FuseBase's AI and app-building features, especially to create tailored client solutions for the fintech industry.

comments.title: BEST in APPSUMO
comments.comment: started buying with 3 codes, until I keep on stacking up to 10, and planning to add more soon.. fusebase definitely one of the best app here in appsumo, and they constantly updating their products. this is for sure not a fly by night app that we mostly see in lifetime deals.

comments.title: One space for everything, and I do not regret taking the chance
comments.comment:
I almost did not get FuseBase. I only took the chance after reading someone else's review, and I honestly do not regret it.

My biggest problem was organising my work. I was jumping between so many apps that things got lost and I spent more time managing tools than actually creating. Now everything lives in one space.

I am building a Prompt Bible with a full frontend and database, all managed on FuseBase. The part that still surprises me is that I did not build it from scratch. I connected Claude, tell it what I need, agree to the plan, and it goes ahead and creates it. When I want to change or update something, I just ask Claude again. No starting over, no stress.

For someone with a busy brain who runs multiple projects, having one place to create, store and update everything has made a real difference. I am getting more done with less mental clutter.

comments.title: Solid product, and it keeps getting better.
comments.comment:
I've used FuseBase since September 2025. It was a solid product then, and it has improved steadily since without breaking what already worked.

The addition that matters most to me is Apps. You describe a feature in plain English, an AI agent builds it on top of your FuseBase databases, and you test it locally and deploy it. Access is set per feature (public, members only or managers only), so the permissions I'd already set up carry over.

That means I can build tools I would otherwise have paid a developer for. I'm using it for a planner and professional development tracker for healthcare professionals, with many features, all running off the same databases.

A few things to know:

- They're web only, with no offline mode or native mobile app.
- A feature usually needs a few rounds of fixes before it's right (not new in vibe coding).
- Setup takes some figuring out: the right plan, your organisation role, the CLI and an IDE. But worth the effort. 

If you've outgrown templates and don't want to hire a developer, it's very much worth a look.

comments.title: From Tier 1 to Tier 7 - Worth Every Step
comments.comment:
I started with Tier 1 and upgraded to Tier 7. FuseBase has quickly become the center of my client workflow. It replaces scattered emails, messy folders, and multiple apps with one organized, branded space that makes everything run more smoothly and professionally. The client portals look great, the AI tools save time, and having everything in a single dashboard has greatly improved how I manage projects.  

What’s even more impressive is how much FuseBase offers that I haven’t even fully explored yet. Entire sections of the platform, from advanced automation to deeper customization options, that I know will unlock even more value as I grow into them. It’s reassuring to use a tool that lets me expand without feeling overwhelmed.

The FuseBase team continually improves the platform and listens to user feedback. Their customer service is consistently fast and helpful. Overall, it’s a strong, modern tool that keeps you organized and polished, especially if you’re juggling multiple clients or projects.

comments.title: Flexible client portal and internal workspace for agencies with fast development
comments.comment:
FuseBase is a great fit for anyone in the consulting or agency business like ourselves as it's becoming more and more integral part of our internal operations while presenting a polished on brand experience to our clients.  The white-labeled client portals has significantly elevated our delivery, giving clients a single, professional destination to view deliverables, roadmaps, and campaign assets under our own brand identity.

The team consistently pushes meaningful updates rather than letting the product stagnate. The built-in AI agents and automations have eliminated several repetitive administrative tasks, and the recent introduction of Apps and Sites is especially exciting. Whenever I ran into any issue configuring specific features, the support was responsive and genuinely helpful.

The platform is not without a learning curve. Because it brings together document collaboration, database structures, and portal architecture, getting fully up to speed takes some time and effort. The official documentation doesn't always keep pace with the feature releases, which means configuring newer features sometimes requires trial and error or reaching out to support for clarification.

Overall, you can't go wrong with taking a phased approach, gradually integrating specific parts of Fusebase into daily operations as the tool expands.

comments.title: A game-changer for client collaboration—solid, powerful, and evolving
comments.comment:
I’ve been putting FuseBase through its paces, and it has quickly become the central nervous system for my client workflows. If you’re looking to move away from scattered emails, messy Google Drive folders, and fragmented project management tools, this is the environment you’ve been looking for. 4.75 tacos.

What I love:

The "Portal" Experience: Being able to provide clients with a branded, professional, and secure space to access files, feedback, and project statuses is a massive upgrade in perceived value.

AI Integration: The AI-powered agents are surprisingly handy for handling routine queries and summarizing documentation, which saves me a significant amount of back-and-forth time.

Consolidation: It successfully replaces several disconnected SaaS subscriptions by merging documentation, project management, and client portals into one cohesive dashboard.

The reality check:
Because this platform is so feature-rich, there is naturally a bit of a learning curve to get everything configured exactly how you want it. It isn't a "set it and forget it" tool; you need to spend some time building out your workspaces to get the most efficiency out of the automation features.

Why it’s a keeper:
The team is clearly dedicated to the platform's long-term growth. They are consistently rolling out improvements, and the responsiveness to the community’s feature requests is evident. It’s a robust, professional-grade tool that makes a massive difference in how clients perceive your operations.

Highly recommended for anyone juggling multiple projects who wants to look as organized and high-tech as possible.

comments.title: One of the most outstanding products that I have ever purchased.
comments.comment: Well, where do I start. I bought this last time FuseBase was on AppSumo and went full stack. First the cons: a) there is a little bit of a learning curve - that is to be expected because honestly there is so much on offer. b) The documentation links are not always reliable. That being said, I diligently started building my internal workspace (on my custom domain) and have started building one portal that is linked to the workspace (again on a custom domain). There are loads of customisation options and if you are any good at coding or knowledge of CSS (or a friendly LLM to hand) you can get the portals looking exactly the way you like! FuseBase integrates perfectly with Claude and I actually use my internal workspace as memory for Claude and have set up 'session triggers' ensuring Claude fetches the appropriate knowledge docs from my Workspace before we work on different projects. As someone who loves Open Source, Docker and Vibe Coding the new app creation feature is simply remarkable! The fact that with tier 10 you can build 100 frontend SPA and 10 full stack apps with a Hono backend - just wow! If you are an starting up as an Agency, or even an established one, willing to migrate, and can handle a little bit of a learning curve and enjoy Vibe coding, I cannot recommend this purchase enough. Really, since I've gotten into FuseBase, I literally have hours of fun! I have developed/developing a FuseBase skill to streamline the process, I actually deployed a Full Stack application (prepared briefly on AI Studio to get the general look and scaffold) on FuseBase with CoWork, with very minimal input from me (developing the skill as I go along) - honestly I am so impressed...I'd be lying if I said I didn't have issues with the app this morning, so I contacted support and literally within minutes I got a reply and then another from a really helpful (though anonymous) assistant. It is one of the few (if any) apps I would ever consider going Full Stack again. I think FuseBase/Nimbus really do lifetime deals well - just make them so fantastic that you will want them and you will want them for your clients, and I love that you are able to stack beyond 10. I am pleased that FuseBase (formerly Nimbus as Gemini keeps telling me!) return fairly regularly to AppSumo and maybe next time round, I'll go full stack again. Really FuseBase, thank you for being a solid company that value your LTD owners - in this day and age that really stands out (especially for me having been burned by many AS deals in the past). I wish you the very best for your continued growth.

comments.title: Fast Support - Great Product
comments.comment:
I had a couple of questions and an issue (my fault!) and suppoort were very quick to react.

Fusebase is more than just a a tool, way more!

There are so many different things you can do with this, the mind boggles, and it keeps ploughing forward and improving

I can't imagine you'll ever get this at this price again, it's insane value. If you are on the fence, I'd suggest jump off and get on board.

comments.title: Keeps Getting Better
comments.comment:
After buying enough software on AppSumo to single-handedly fund their entire marketing department, my digital closet was looking like a graveyard of abandoned tech. But out of that massive pile of SaaS, Fusebase, Taskade and a few others became the chosen ones—the only apps that didn't end up in my "why the hell did I buy this" folder.

Honestly, listing everything Fusebase has been cooking up over the years would result in a TL;DR longer than a CVS receipt. Fortunately, after boatloads of updates, Fusebase has really shifted into high gear, pulling double duty to inject serious AI juice into its DNA. From autonomous AI Agents that do everything short of brewing your morning coffee, to shiny new AI CRM functionalities being integrated weekly, this tool is executing its roadmap faster than a getaway driver. If you're looking for a sign to stop hoarding lifetime deals and actually build your business backend, this may be  it. You’ll be pleasantly surprised by just how much heavy lifting this App can do!

comments.title: Great deal
comments.comment:
Fusebase is a great value overall. It gives you access to vibe coding, AI tools, the ability to create portals, and encrypted storage all in one place. I could also see this being a strong alternative to paying for a separate Google Drive subscription, since it may work well for storage too.

The best part is they are constantly improving the platform.

comments.title: Great Note Taking Tool
comments.comment:
I ditched Evernote for Nimbus back in the day, now renamed Fusebase. Whenever they have been back I picked up a code or two to add to my stack. So far great experience, and I loved ditching a subscription tool.

I haven't even started using portals or any of the advanced features, I just like my notes.

comments.title: Best solution ever !
comments.comment:
I bought fusebase when it was Nimbus and since then i am using it daily.
this is mostly for note taking but now after having a call with Pavel i discovered the use of database and code within the system. This makes it the most complete marketing or digital solution i ever worked with.
totally recommend  it.

comments.title: Great App
comments.comment: Absolutely love this app, def helps you focus when you have to set a time to meet and "docks" you for being late.

comments.title: I saw this when it first came on AppSumo and thought, 'Next!' And now,...
comments.comment:
I've completed my first session. I get it! 

I'm going to use this to finally tackle all the tasks that I've been putting off--like cleaning out the freezer, organizing the garage, the pantry, my closet, and the drawers in my desk. There's a never-ending list of things to do. I'm hoping this comes back as an unlimited lifetime deal! I'm sold!

comments.title: Late review, LOVE THIS!
comments.comment: This is incredible, the kind of accountability I needed. Just having someone there helps me focus on the task at hand. If this comes back, buy it. If not, join on their site. One of the best products I've gotten, thanks AppSumo!

comments.title: Surprises Me!
comments.comment: I signed up and had my first session last week. I was surprised about how productive I was during that brief period. Time periods are 25, 50 or 75 minutes. Next time I'll make it 75 minutes. I found having a set time period encourages me to go, go, go on a task. I'm fairly self motivated, but we all have those yucky jobs we have to push ourselves to do, so for me, this tool is excellent to get those ones done. I think I'll end up paying the subscription fee...I have plenty of yucky jobs :)

comments.title: Excellent
comments.comment:
Focusmate allows you to quickly and easily setup a one-on-one work session, to get things done.

It's easy to use, and effective. I spend a lot of time working by myself, and am always able to find sessions, even at very early, and late hours of the day, due to the global reach of the platform.

The interface is well thought out, as are the various options.

Very much recommended.

comments.title: So far...hmmm.
comments.comment:
I fully enjoy this tool.  I literally had this idea myself with others from a groups I was meeting with briefly.  (Problem there was there was no way to know when anyone else was free and would be "working" or "meeting up" in the group area of the tool.)  So this is great.

In fact, ny very first focusmate try stood me up.  A timer came on and offered to hook me up with someone else if I didn't want to wait for my current focusmate.  I took the offer and had a really productive time.

There is a minus--but not so much with the Tool. I like the "introduction" to the tool, but prefer to have a real AppSumo deal!

As other sumolings question here, I would prefer some type of UNLIMITED access., especially, since I enjoyed it and I found out that my focusmate only pays $5 month for unlimited access.

Suggestion for the tool:  Allow a "break," a time that each person agrees to have the GONG or GONGs go off.  I think breaking up longer times to share progress is more ideal.  ALSO: If there was an ability to share similar work items and be matched that way!  

Still, 5 tacos.  It is a great tool.

comments.title: Zoom for Your Productivity!
comments.comment:
I just had my first session with Focusmate, and it worked great! I was paired up with a random person who had over 1,500 sessions and had been using it for years as a paid member. We started by stating our goals to each other. Mine was to get through 29 emails. His was to write a cover letter with the help of ChatGPT. We had 25 minutes for the session. Then we started. I was able to focus on my emails and finish the task in 22 minutes, when I had been sitting on those emails all day long up to that point. Now I'm at Inbox zero! So, it works!

I asked him why he liked Focusmate so much, and he said that it helps people who have ADHD or other issues with focus remain singularly focused on the task they want to achieve. It also helps them be accountable when someone else is there with them. I don't have those issues, but do have an issue with getting started on things instead of watching videos online as a form of procrastination, so I figured I'd give it a shot since it's here on AppSumo for Plus members. In the end, I got my work done, and that's what matters. 

Yes, it's a little gimmicky, and you could just set a timer and do the work alone, but the price is right, and it's effective, so who cares? I could see this becoming a regular part of my day, or using it whenever I need to buckle down and stop letting myself be distracted. And it was fun to meet someone new who is also focused on getting things done.

comments.title: This tool is revolutionizing my professional life.
comments.comment:
It's incredibly easy to use. You simply log in to the platform and book a coworking session of 25, 50, or 75 minutes. The sessions start every quarter of an hour. People are working all around the world at any time of day or night, on weekdays and weekends.

The impact on productivity is incredible.

You set your objective before the session.
Before the session, you briefly communicate your goals to your coworker, just one minute is enough.
During the session, you work on your objective with your camera on and sound muted.
After the session, you share your achieved results with your coworker, again just one minute is sufficient.
The result: my productivity has doubled.
After just two days of trying it out, I have fallen in love with this coworking tool, and I'm going to use it for the rest of my professional life!
Thank you, AppSumo, for introducing me to this fantastic tool.

comments.title: It works, though could be improved
comments.comment:
This is a simple tool that provides a few polling methods that benefit me as a trainer. When I cannot use Zoom's polling features or if I'm doing an in-person session, I like to use Feedbeo. I haven't been able to use it many times, though it gets the job done. I prefer Zoom's advanced polling because it helps me keep most of my client data in the same place, though it's easy enough to export the results with this tool, too. There are things I can do with Feedbeo, like word clouds, that I can't do with Zoom.

It's four tacos because while the UX and UI have improved since I first purchased this long ago, 1) the Feedbeo logo and company name take up too much real estate - especially in the TV view. 2) You can't have your logo on the TV view. 3) There are minimal customization options. 4) When loading your logo and selecting a background, it's unclear that these will be on separate live views. 5) You cannot edit the user's experience in which they vote, write, etc., except to upload your logo, and Feedbeo's logo still shows. 6) There are no universal or event-specific settings, such as hiding the live view of results for polls by default.

It's a great tool for the price, though I would love to see more features and development.

comments.title: Simple & Clean
comments.comment: Excellent polling tool - simple, clean, intuitive, with responsive support. Few limitations: does not show all data and graphs on printout, and can't open all questions at once like in a survey, etc. If you need a basic, intuitive polling tool - Feedbeo is a top choice.

comments.title: Awesome.
comments.comment: Great solution for capturing feedback

comments.title: Simple and effective !
comments.comment:
I always find that built in polls and quizzes look boring in meeting apps (except for one platform that is sadly shutting down by the end of february).

Feedbeo does exactly what it says it does. Without knowing the platform, I have been able to setup multiple word clouds, polls and Q&A elements in a matter of minutes.

Participants really enjoyed the idea of interacting with their phones while watching the workshop. Showing the results was super easy as well.

For live webinars on streaming platform like youtube, this is a genius way of having LIVE interaction even if you can't have participants with audio/video in the event.

Could there be even more kinds of interactive elements ? Sure ! But for the price, it's hard to beat.

The look is minimalist, and it just works. Amazing !

comments.title: Impressed with the ease and usefullness
comments.comment: I faced a challenge today with a webinar of 450 participants, and we wanted to run a few polls. As always, my first stop was AppSumo. I'm very happy with my purchase, Feedbeo did the job perfectly. I look forward to using and incorporating it more in future sessions. It's a great deal at this price.

comments.title: 5 Tacos and then some!
comments.comment:
Feedbeo makes meetings more interactive and engaging. It’s simple, smooth, and easy to use, and people actually enjoy participating. Worth every penny! I'm a speaker and the ROI for a lifetime deal is hard to beat. 

Highly recommend!

comments.title: It works as seem. Its a good Alternative for Mentimeter
comments.comment: I haven't used it extensively but I used a free version once in a real training with about 30 people before I bought this. And it worked pretty well. In between there was glitch, where I opened the poll but participants were not seeing it. I want to assume that it was one of those scenario. But except that it worked really well for what it is. I feel the UI and speed could be better. But a great option if you are into training.

comments.title: Just works
comments.comment: Feedbeo works fine for my usage. I tested some question forms and it works. For me a good solution.

comments.title: Really impressive!
comments.comment: I've always liked the idea of a Kahoot during my online English lessons, but always found it overwhelming and really awkward to setup. So I'm happy to say that this app has really pleasantly surprised me. It is very intuitive to use and set up, and provides a brilliant experience for my students, in fact I use it every week now and they love it too! Great job team!

comments.title: Hidden gem
comments.comment: Great product. Responsive team. Just what I was looking for. It offers moderation features that cost a bundle with the main competitor.

comments.title: Ground floor bargain!
comments.comment:
This is a bargain deal for unlimited participants.

I don't want a bunch of quickly-launched bells and whistles to make it seem more feature-packed. I'm happy to see a focus on core features and simplicity; Q&A, and some poll/feedback responses for a live event.

Simple is good!

I can change the background colors, and add a branded logo, which is all I need to make it fit the event.

My only minor complaint is that the "enter your code" page should be on a dedicated domain, not the app sales page. I'm using a domain redirect as a work-around.

I'm going to get a lot of use out of Feedbeo!

comments.title: Does the job very well and is easy to use
comments.comment:
This is a fantastic tool if you conduct a lot of discussions, workshops or sessions.

It takes a minute to configure and you can immediately go live with it. The configuration is so simple that you can even put up a question or a poll quickly in a live event.

The admin console offers three views, Admin, User and TV (Live) view. So you don't have any confusion on how the questions appear for the participants and how is the result displayed. You can see it as you configure it.

As you switch from one question to another participants do not have to refresh their screens, which is a huge plus.

The QR code is automatically generated, so you don't have to use another tool to get the QR code.

No hesitation in giving 5 tacos.

comments.title: This is nice
comments.comment: I feel like this product is a gem in the rough - I feel the potential is enormous for anyone doing presentations, and I see the value grow exponentially as the product develops

comments.title: Great app at a great price... some features still missing but they will be available.

comments.title: great product with corncern
comments.comment: Stackby is a great product that comes with a lot of feature with some future concern for lifetime using for larger business. To see the picture clearer let’s say if we stack 9 codes, we get 10 users and 40 stacks in this workspace. After that your business gets larger with the need to get more users to collaborate but your stack nearly user up, I would recommend shifting to other platform instead. Let compare stackby Business plan (18$/user) with alternative platform like airtable(team plan 20$/user around 10% pricier), you get the same row limit ber base(stack) the same upload limit, more integration with some feature difference but  the main deal breaker is that airtable allow unlimited base (stack) so each user can use same workspace to collaborate with each user get unlimited of base, but in contrast if you add more user in stackby business plan you still get stack limit of 50, so in my opinion likely as they suggest get some stack this for personal use or to startup your business and move to other platform you’re your company get larger. No offense but not that I hate this product I also buy 10 code with both powerup and marketplace add-ons to use in my business. it a great product that I think it would work for my first 5-10 years of my current business but in my opinion they need to revise their plan in the future if they want to compete with other platform in lower deal (business plan) than enterprise plan that offer unlimited workspace.

comments.title: Updated Review
comments.comment:
I happened to see a mention of Stackby while I was searching for an online database service. Stackby is this weird love child of a database and a spreadsheet. It's neither of them, but somehow it's better than either of them. It's a great place to rapid prototyping, and with the API, it's actually a good solution for storing and manipulating data for apps.
There's some quirkiness in how Stackby works that takes some getting used to. They have mostly adopted the language of spreadsheets, so it feels very familiar, but there are things here and there that they decided to do differently, so you have to figure out their version of those formulas/commands.
REVISION: I am revising this part at the request of Rachit. As was pointed out, there have indeed been updates to the product, but as an example of the sort of "different" ways that Stackby does things, the updates page has the most recent updates at the BOTTOM of the page. So, unless you scroll all the way down, you don't see the recent updates, like I didn't.

comments.title: Updated Review
comments.comment:
My official rating is 3.5 tacos but am giving them benefit of the doubt.

My initial review was for 2 tacos updating it because support did reach out to me on an urgent basis and did resolve the doubts if not the issue. I still feel that the product is unpolished, slightly buggy with improvements needed in UX. That being said the platform does have potential. Hoping it brings the improvements required to become one of the better buys.

comments.title: Good alternative to Airtable
comments.comment:
I have a paid Airtable account and have worked extensively with it. It is a great tool with lots of flexibility, but I had some concerns: the lack of API connections, and the price range ($20/month per user for the Pro plan). Stackby does almost everthing Airtable does, adds API integration, and this deal includes several users from the start, which is great. 
My main concern with this deal is the limitation in rows per stack. Stacking a max. of 5 codes gives you 30.000 rows per stack, which can be a problem with data - intensive projects. In comparison, the Pro plan in Airtable gives 50.000 rows. I am surprised that Stackby has not matched their competitor with this number in this deal, and I would love them to go up to 50.000 rows in this offer.
Otherwise, it seems like a very promising tool, no regrets so far. Keep up the good work!

comments.title: Great.... But...... Missing features
comments.comment:
I've been wishing to find something like this here on AS.
seems like a great product, but still needs a ton of improvement.

First thing i did was to paste a few entries into a few different tables.
and then i set up a new column in the "product" table to link to the "client" table.
and suddenly all my data was gone.
not a big deal since i just started to play around with it and could do it again.
but if that would happen on a more complex table i would be quite devastated.
feels like beta

ux is not polished.
settings are mostly for US it seems (date etc)
still lacking most common integrations.
It's quite slow to load and do stuff. not smooth enough.

And most important (for me)... where are the dashboards?
I want to be able to create charts and dashboards with my data.

I hope this product will improve as i really want this product in my life :)

comments.title: Glorified Spreadsheet and more...
comments.comment:
Yes, I call this a glorified spreadsheet! I use FREE Airtable and I don't have any other alternatives to it. 
What do you use it for? Please take a look at their templates here: https://stackby.com/templates

So why 4 star?
Pros
- You can do more with a glorified spreadsheet. Signup for a FREE account or try Airtable
- Best for sharing spreadsheets with an external partner
- Almost everyone understands a spreadsheet!
- Integrations are existing

Cons
- A lot of other systems like PM, CRM, ATS, etc. do the same thing as using spreadsheets.
- You can do almost the same as Google Sheets or MS Excel Online
- Integrations are not as plenty (wish it has more like Appsumo launched tools)
- No mobile app (yet)

This is worth getting at least a code, depending on how big your tracking / monitoring / data will be. Personally, I would use this to collaborate with an external partner who I am doing work with. It has a lot more rows than the FREE tier of Airtable. Both Airtable and Stackby has some "limitations" or I have not yet discovered, how to restrict a certain column to be UNIQUE (i.e. no duplicates). 

I also have not yet tried if you can use a Stackby Stack like a database table in a regular DBMS like MySQL, MSSQL, etc. I have yet to discover it :D

Hope this review helps you!

Cheers

Mike
designpreneurs.com

comments.title: Solid, but Could be Better
comments.comment:
I have been looking at options to manage company data for a while now. I've recently tried Airtable, so this deal couldn't have come at a better time. 

These seems similar to Airtable for what I am looking to do. The templates that I use are the same, the 1 workspace and users are roughly the same. I think Airtable's UI is better, easier to navigate and cleaner.

Here are the things I wish Stackby would improve:
1) Users. I work with a lot of freelancers and consultants, the data I want to share/collaborate with these people will be sensitive to my company. So only having the "creator", which allows these users to copy or download my data is not an option for me. As an educational resources developer, I'm always searching for tools to streamline my workflow. SlideFill has been a revelation, completely transforming how I create lesson plans.

SlideFill's genius lies in its ability to seamlessly integrate Google Slides with data from Google Sheets. By simply setting up a spreadsheet with the relevant information and creating a template in Google Slides with placeholder tags, SlideFill automatically generates polished, data-driven slides. Each row in the spreadsheet becomes a new slide deck, populated with the corresponding data.

While SlideFill may have been initially designed for businesses to create presentations at scale, I've found it to be incredibly versatile. Leveraging my existing expertise with Sheets & Slides, I've been able to adapt the platform to effortlessly produce visually appealing A4 PDF lesson plans in bulk.

The interface could benefit from some refinements, such as improved file and project organisation but the core functionality is exceptional. I'm incredibly excited about the potential of SlideFill and eagerly anticipate future developments.

Overall rating: 5 tacos!!!

All the best to the SlideFill team, and thanks for this wonderful tool :)

I write technical documentation frequently and had been using another app for a long time to create screenshots (one at a time) which was very time consuming.

The other tool that has been around for a long time couldn't even capture inside of the WordPress page builder I use, but in Stepsy it all works great, especially since support was able to add compatibility to make it even better. 

I'm blown away by the great support Stepsy offers. They have really gone out of the way to make sure I'm a happy user, and have already made the app better based on my feedback. 

I'm looking forward to seeing where this tool goes, but it has already saved me a TON of time. 

Here are the top things I like about Stepsy: 
1) Takes step by step screenshots as I go through the steps.
2) It creates the text for each screenshot
3) Each screenshot is editable after you take it, or come back at the end before saving/exporting to make edits. Currently you can highlight things, draw lines, and boxes around things so the person viewing can see and focus on those areas. 
4) You can edit the text on each step now (it's a new feature that just came out if I'm not mistaken). 
5) There is a blur feature that you can use BEFORE you even start recording where you can choose what parts of your screen you do not want to have captured.
6) Export to Google Docs - This puts all the steps in a Google Doc that you can edit and share (if you want).
7) You can export as an HTML document which also includes a folder that contains all the full size images - this is what I like to use since I have to write and publish articles separately.

There are a few things I would like to see in future updates, which they already confirmed to me that they'll look into.
1) Cropping - either automatically when the screenshot is taken or give the ability to crop the image in the image editor after all images are captured.
2) Arrows - I have to have arrows to point to the steps. I do like the boxes that are automatically created, but an arrow would be awesome as that is what I need to use.
3) More export options, such as HTML export to Dropbox or other cloud services (instead of sending it to my computer where I then have to upload to dropbox). 
4) Integration with WordPress where it can export to WordPress as a draft post using the default WordPress block editor - this would be super amazing since that is where I publish guides.

As I mentioned, I'm looking forward to seeing what Stepsy does in the future. So far I'm impressed.

For the price of this deal, it's a no-brainer to get this. 

5 Tacos :-)

comments.title: Solid Platform with Great Potential but Needs Improvements!
comments.comment:
I wanted to give this product a full 5 tacos, but after thoroughly exploring 99% of the Tier 3 features, I found a few limitations and shortcomings. My primary goal for purchasing this LTD was to sell digital products and subscriptions, and it shows promise in those areas. It’s also a great addition to my portfolio of cart platforms like WooCommerce, ThriveCart, and SamCart. I truly hope the team delivers on their roadmap and remains around for the long haul.

PROS ("The Good")
*Digital Products & License Keys: The standout feature for me is the ability to sell digital products and generate license keys for activation. While manual activation may be required on my end, I'd appreciate clarity on tracking and managing license keys—especially for refunds and deactivations.

*Customizable Landing Pages & Checkout Features: Offers a variety of options for customization, including the ability to add images, videos, and custom code.

*CNAME/Custom Domain Setup: Straightforward setup with clear instructions.

*Coupon Functionality: Ability to create fixed or percentage-based discounts is a nice touch.

CONS ("The Bad & The Ugly")
*White Label Limitations: The CNAME feature falls short when Zylvie branding is still visible in headers and footers. Charging extra to remove branding, especially for top-tier LTD buyers, is a poor practice.

*Outdated Design: The landing page design options feel stuck in the 90s, with limited flexibility.

*Brand Management Restrictions: There’s no option to delete and replace brands while preserving the inventory limit.

*Domain Linking Issues: After setting up a custom domain, the "view my store" link in the admin dashboard still points to the Zylvie site, leading to an error page.

*Cart Abandonment Disclosure: This valuable feature is locked behind Tier 5, which isn’t made clear in the AppSumo listing.

*Affiliate/Referral Limitations: Affiliate links can only be created manually via email invitations. The absence of a self-service affiliate registration (like Partnero) is a missed opportunity.  Please refer to these screenshots: Refer to these screenshots: https://prnt.sc/yV4P7Wfbiii9, https://prnt.sc/KP_seoF5uvnq

*Coupon Date Errors: Coupons with specific start and end dates arbitrarily change when revisited for editing.

*In the cart, when customer selects the bump offer, the cart total does not add up correctly.  There's also no option to "continue shopping" or go back to the home page if customer wants to select more products.  

*Sales Volume Uncertainty: It's unclear what happens after reaching the stated $1 million sales cap for Tier 3 users.

Final Thoughts
This platform is a strong and cost-effective alternative to other cart platforms, but there’s room for significant improvement. Addressing the issues outlined above could make this a 5-taco contender.

comments.comment:
I’ve really enjoyed using Zylvie so far. I’d been hunting for a simple way to deliver lead magnets without routing every download through my ESP, and Zylvie nails that workflow. Setup is quick, the UI is clean, and the built-in upsells, affiliate tracking, abandoned-cart recovery, and flexible subscription options make it feel like an all-in-one growth engine—no extra plugins required.

I’m on Tier 5 and have explored every feature. Yes, the stock templates look a bit dated, but a few lines of custom CSS let me make the storefront feel fully on-brand. Jay (the founder) has answered every email personally; his responsiveness and genuine drive to improve the platform are huge pluses. I’m especially excited about the roadmap items like gated member areas, expanded download management, and course-creation tools.

That said, a few pain points keep Zylvie from being my complete storefront:

- Physical products – Selling them works, but it’s clunky: no SKU fields, no real inventory management, and each item in a shipment fires its own tracking email.

- Multiple digital files – If a cart contains two digital products, only one “prepared” email template goes out and the second file is tacked on in an odd spot, with cryptic file names that could confuse customers.

- Catalog size & editing – Zylvie is clearly optimized for creators with one or two flagship offers. My shop includes dozens of items, and I’d love to see more support for bulk or multi-product editing—it gets tedious making changes one product at a time.

Wishlist: smoother multi-item fulfillment flows, more intuitive delivery for multiple digital files, better support for physical product sellers, and native print-on-demand integrations—something many digital-first creators could really use. I’d also love to see improvements like better multi-product editing and the ability to connect related products for upselling directly on product pages.

Zylvie gives me a lot of what I need to grow—easy lead capture, digital delivery, upsells, subscriptions, and a clean interface that doesn’t overwhelm. It’s not quite there yet for managing physical products or larger catalogs. Still, the foundation is solid. I’m glad I invested early and I’m looking forward to watching the platform grow. 5 Tacos!

However, I’ve encountered a peculiar behavior with Stripe, my primary payment gateway. When users proceed to the checkout page, Zylvie creates an ‘incomplete’ transaction in Stripe before any payment is processed. This anomaly has led to confusion among my clients, cluttering the Stripe transaction console and raising concerns about unintended charges. While these ‘incomplete’ transactions can be filtered out, they still pose an inconvenience. In one instance, I had to generate manual payment links to mitigate the confusion.

Despite this hiccup, I remain optimistic about Zylvie’s potential. The cart software industry is challenging, and I’ve previously invested in platforms that were later abandoned by developers. Zylvie’s commitment to continuous improvement gives me hope that this issue will be addressed promptly.

comments.title: Flowlance is a great way to sell products and services
comments.comment:
We purchased Flowlance a few months ago and we have nothing but positive things to say about the product. The features and functionality available in Flowlance are amazing, and when you consider the price point, it is an easy recommendation!

The features included on the Teir 3 option we purchased include:
--- Flowie - AI product, store and ad content creation
--- Sales Dashboard
--- Orders - Order Details
--- Helpful CRM - Track every session spent with a customer, every invoice sent, every product they purchase, and any notes you take about this customer. You have one place to manage and automate customer records. You can also import a current customer list.
--- Use your own URL - You can set up your store using your own URL. 
--- Communities - Want to provide a space where customers within the same or similar category can network, share ideas, etc.? Create a community.
--- Courses - Simple-to-use LMS that enables a business to offer training as a feature add-on or as a primary product. We may use the Communities section to promote a course following a customer purchasing a specific product. 
--- Calendar - Customers have the ability to schedule an appointment with you during the time frame you identify as available [Consultation/Coaching/etc.]
--- Email Sequencing and Broadcast Emails- this is very helpful.
--- Direct Sales - Send a customer a link for a one-off or even recurring charge
--- Funnels [BETA] - And they are adding more features. We have not created a funnel yet, but I can assure you we will check out this feature when we are ready.
--- Referral/affiliate link - If you refer one of your customers [or anyone] to Flowlance and they subscribe, Flowlance will pay you 20–30% commission monthly [based on your plan]. Seriously… automatic PayPal payouts every month. There is no minimum payout amount, no sales limit, and you can track your revenue in real time. 

In full transparency, on two occasions, support didn't respond within a day… one request took two days, and the other took three. And I still have nothing but positive things to say about Patrik Kruntorad, his team, and the product they have brought to market. Both times the issues were resolved. Only after the fact did it occur to me that we were probably prioritized lower than customers who were already live with products. I am also hoping my fellow entrepreneurs residing in the U.S. remember that 9:00 AM in Prague is 3:00 AM in New York and midnight in Los Angeles. Likewise, 2:00 PM in LA is 8:00 PM in Prague… you get the idea. 

Patrik and his team may want to consider adding a KnowledgeBase and a ticketed support system/workflow that doesn’t begin with “send an email to support”. An automated acknowledgment when a support request is submitted could include a link to the KnowledgeBase, especially if Flowlance is experiencing a higher-than-usual support request volume. This helped us a lot almost three years ago when a promotion/ad campaign produced a lot of inquiries and sales and also significantly increased support requests. It was a great problem to have; however, we could not keep up with support. We hired two freelancers to categorize support requests, build a basic Knowledgebase, and automate an acknowledgment email that inserted links based on keywords in the "issue description" and/or selections from a category drop-down menu. When the next advertising push launched, purchases and support requests spiked again; however, this time over half of the support requests were closed by the customer that submitted the request. A surprisingly high percentage of customers visited one or more of the Knowledgebase links included in the support request acknowledgment email. Anyhooooo…. I am sure there are solutions being considered and Flowlance will land on the right solution.

The key takeaway here is that without hesitation, everyone on our team would recommend Flowlance. Flowlance, like the other products we have purchased on AppSumo, was conceived, created, and coded by a founder/business owner [and if they were lucky... a small team] genuinely trying to help other business owners navigate the sticking points we crawl over every day. So everybody, keep crawling until we can zoom and glide!

Thank you!
Jan J.

comments.title: Project management with gamification and WhatsApp built in
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product evaluator for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Most project management tools are good at telling people what they need to do. Syncupp tries to give them another reason to actually do it.

The gamification is a big part of that. Completing work can earn coins and XP, build streaks and move people up a leaderboard. Those coins can then be tied to rewards you define yourself, so the reward system becomes part of the everyday work instead of something a manager has to run separately.

I tested creating and completing tasks and awarding coins, and that worked well. I can especially see this working for agencies, sales groups or other environments where a little friendly competition can make routine work more engaging.

Syncupp also brings a lot of the day-to-day work into the same place. There are project boards, tasks, chat, meetings, time tracking, attendance, roles and permissions, along with the leaderboard and rewards. You can work in kanban, list or calendar views and break tasks down with subtasks, dependencies and recurring schedules.

The other big advantage for me is the native WhatsApp integration. Task assignments, deadline reminders and daily summaries can go directly to WhatsApp, and some approvals can be handled just by replying without opening Syncupp. For groups that already rely heavily on WhatsApp, that could make the product much easier to adopt because people can see what needs attention where they are already communicating.

I also like that WhatsApp and the gamification are included across the AppSumo tiers rather than being reserved for the higher plans. The tiers mainly change how many people and workspaces you can have, along with the amount of AI usage included.

During my test, the leaderboard did not update immediately after coins were awarded. The team reproduced the issue and said they were adding real-time updates. The current AppSumo listing now describes it as a live XP leaderboard with real-time rankings, so that appears to have been resolved.

I also found a visitor-tracking script running inside the logged-in application during the original test. The team removed it completely after I reported it, which I appreciated.

There are also integrations with Slack, Zapier, Make and Pabbly, plus Claude MCP if you want to bring Syncupp into an AI workflow.

Overall, I think the reason to choose Syncupp over another task manager is the combination of gamification and WhatsApp. The project management side is familiar, but coins, streaks, rewards and native WhatsApp updates give people more reason to stay engaged with the work and less reason to miss what needs to get done.

comments.title: Amazing Lead Generation for the Price
comments.comment:
For the price, the amount of leads is a crazy good deal. I recently learned of AppSumo, and honestly without this we would've had a hard time affording tools for our lead generation strategy. 

LeadShark, one platform that I was recommended, for example, charges $0.4 per lead, which when multiplied by the number of leads of this deal (I got the plus exclusive that gives 7500 leads per month) would cost $3,000/mo. Instead, you get it for a lifetime for merely $69!!!! Granted, the platform is still maturing, but it shows plenty of progress and potential.

Pros:
-Unbeatable price.
-Large contact database, with contacts in every industry and country.
-Easy-to-use platform.
-Email validation, CSV export, list creation, LinkedIn Extension

Cons (more like a list of suggestions):

-Add keyword search for industry: currently, LeadRocks only lets you search for specific industries under a dropdown list (which is moderately large), however searching outside of this is rather hard, especially for niche audiences.

-More accurate and tailored data: currently, the emails returned by LeadRocks are messy and can require filtering (some contacts can have upwards of over 8 emails). It would be nice if there were an option to just export a single email (the one associated with its industry/current job associated with the industry/job in the search fields). Same thing with phone numbers.

-Improve the Email validation process: currently, you click "validate" and it will update your CSV file export with an extra column for the email status. However, you still need to filter out these emails from the CSV manually. It would be nice if contacts with invalid emails are updated or removed automatically.

-Domain search should return emails ONLY associated with that domain (or at least have the domain email in the first column). I was trying to get contacts from a specific university, and even the though all contacts had an email associated with that university, a big portion of them had a primary email in another domain, or otherwise had the domain search email in a second or third column, which was really tedious to fix manually.

-Duplicate check: Search results should not show contacts that have been "opened"/saved to a list.

They're also working on a cold emailing tool, which looks impressive, however, I am a bit worried they're trying to grow their offerings to quickly without refining what they already do well. My advice for the LeadRocks team would be to focus on making the best lead generation / prospecting tool, and then expand into cold emailing and outreach.

Bottom line: has a few quirks that can easily be overlooked by the price. I hope this tool grows and becomes very successful!

- I also get the idea that the internal Wallet balance convert the 'real money' you charged the account with into virtual, tokenised money only. What I mean by this is that after you've 'charged' your wallet in order to verify your mobile number and validate your payment card ($25 and $5 transactions) you can earn a $25 bonus just by clicking on a banner .... ok, nice, but where does that money come from? When I pointed out that I paid a fee to do a Wallet transfer on a $50 transaction + 0.5% fee, I got a $30 bonus ... just like that? Where does all this 'money' come from?
- MCP onboarding  - the downloadable skills and prompt copy - was not obvious i.e. you can connect your AI without knowing these skills exist. Spent a few unecessary tokens before I inadvertently bumped into the MCP webpage with the skills.md files etc.
- Support is almost too friendly. I understand customer satisfaction is important, but sending me a huge throbbing heart sticker .... LOL. And the 'mate',  'howzit' surfer dude tone can be toned down for my liking :-).
- I need quick accurate answers from Support (which seems to be out of :-(  my timzone often) that show me an understanding of what I am asking and that support actually knows and understands more than I do ... which is not the impression I got all the time.

Final thoughts: Platform dependence is already an issue poking its ugly head out. Yes, all-in-one is great and 'no plugins', but that leaves us at the mercy of Selldone ... and they are VERY gracious. But i.e. with Logistics/Shipping services the lack of flexibility and options are close to dealbreaker for me especially if they do not open up endpoints for own development ... soon.

Still a four Taco review even though it seems I'm in total more negative?!
Yes, because Selldone, if done right (and it's still early days?), is a done deal for me. That's why im sold on it .... for now.

I originally tried Selldone back in 2022 and refunded the LTD because it wasn't quite ready for my needs. Fast forward to now and I am amazed at the progress! Overall, it has almost everything I need. 

Here are a few notes I think are important:

Order Management: You currently can't edit existing orders directly to add or remove products post-purchase. Adjusting customer orders requires a few roundabout workarounds.

Product Bundles: There is no native product bundle feature to combine multiple items into a single kit with individual product inventory tracking. If customers could create a bundle from certain products, get a bundle discount, and have a customized shopping experience, that would be great to have. 

Backend UI: The dashboard can feel crowded given how much is packed into it. Take the time to explore the navigation—there are tons of powerful, hidden capabilities once you get familiar with the layout. So many cool things to find!

Selldone Genesis & Apps: Genesis makes front-end customization and store management smooth, and having dedicated mobile/desktop apps makes managing shop operations on the go seamless.

I didn't refund Selldone this time around. Selldone is a keeper! I think it is a solid platform with wonderful support and developers that will keep on bringing us great features. I look forward to using Selldone for many years!

comments.title: Ecommerce Masterpiece well worth exploring
comments.comment:
Short version: it does what it says, and then some.

It's been a few years since I've bothered writing a review here — that alone should tell you something.

What stands out with this deal:

- Marketplace builder, POS, CMS + blog, subscriptions, digital file delivery, affiliates and discounts — all native. No add-ons, no plugins.
- Let me say that again: no add-ons, no plugins.
- 143 currencies and a long list of payment gateways built in
- Higher tiers give you multiple stores on one Enterprise licence, unlimited admins, and generous per-store storage
- Client isolation is built into the permission system — a client only ever sees the store you put them on
- PWA and Android apps included
- And the list keeps going. Have a look for yourself.

Support:

Stellar, especially Mark on the Selldone website chat, who always seems to be on hand no matter the hour.

Worth knowing:

It's a deep platform. The opportunity is there, but you need to put the time in to understand Selldone and their Business OS philosophy. Once it clicks, the sky's the limit.

Why I'm in:

- They ship fast — Stripe Tax, EU withdrawal compliance, CJdropshipping, Lulu, Bookvault, and now Genesis AI. And they listen, attentively.
- The Claude integration is the one I use daily — asking about a store beats clicking through dashboards.

At this rate I wouldn't be surprised to see Selldone finish up as one of the highest-rated deals Sumo's had. Well done to the Selldone team on this masterpiece.

comments.title: Amazing Lead Generation for the Price
comments.comment:
For the price, the amount of leads is a crazy good deal. I recently learned of AppSumo, and honestly without this we would've had a hard time affording tools for our lead generation strategy. 

LeadShark, one platform that I was recommended, for example, charges $0.4 per lead, which when multiplied by the number of leads of this deal (I got the plus exclusive that gives 7500 leads per month) would cost $3,000/mo. Instead, you get it for a lifetime for merely $69!!!! Granted, the platform is still maturing, but it shows plenty of progress and potential.

Pros:
-Unbeatable price.
-Large contact database, with contacts in every industry and country.
-Easy-to-use platform.
-Email validation, CSV export, list creation, LinkedIn Extension

Cons (more like a list of suggestions):

-Add keyword search for industry: currently, LeadRocks only lets you search for specific industries under a dropdown list (which is moderately large), however searching outside of this is rather hard, especially for niche audiences.

-More accurate and tailored data: currently, the emails returned by LeadRocks are messy and can require filtering (some contacts can have upwards of over 8 emails). It would be nice if there were an option to just export a single email (the one associated with its industry/current job associated with the industry/job in the search fields). Same thing with phone numbers.

-Improve the Email validation process: currently, you click "validate" and it will update your CSV file export with an extra column for the email status. However, you still need to filter out these emails from the CSV manually. It would be nice if contacts with invalid emails are updated or removed automatically.

-Domain search should return emails ONLY associated with that domain (or at least have the domain email in the first column). I was trying to get contacts from a specific university, and even the though all contacts had an email associated with that university, a big portion of them had a primary email in another domain, or otherwise had the domain search email in a second or third column, which was really tedious to fix manually.

-Duplicate check: Search results should not show contacts that have been "opened"/saved to a list.

They're also working on a cold emailing tool, which looks impressive, however, I am a bit worried they're trying to grow their offerings to quickly without refining what they already do well. My advice for the LeadRocks team would be to focus on making the best lead generation / prospecting tool, and then expand into cold emailing and outreach.

Bottom line: has a few quirks that can easily be overlooked by the price. I hope this tool grows and becomes very successful!

I also appreciate the built-in lead database, the ability to target prospects based on specific criteria, and the flexibility to manage multiple accounts and campaigns.

As someone who has spent years working with CRMs, marketing automation, and lead generation, I'm always looking for tools that can do more than just automate repetitive tasks. I want flexibility, integrations, and the ability to build workflows around how I actually run my business.

Flow is moving in that direction.

Definitely worth checking out, especially if you're already using AI assistants in your business.

comments.comment:
I see ChooseFlow.ai as a practical option for anyone who relies heavily on LinkedIn for finding clients or booking sales meetings. What I like most is that it brings lead search, outreach campaigns, follow-ups, inbox management, and AI-assisted replies into one place. That can save a lot of time compared with using several separate tools.

In my view, it is best suited to consultants, agencies, and sales teams that run consistent outreach campaigns. The unified inbox and campaign tools make it easier to stay organized, especially when handling several prospects at once.

The main downside is the price. Starting around $79 per month, it may feel expensive for someone who only sends occasional LinkedIn messages. I would also recommend testing account connections and lead-search quality during a trial before fully committing.

Overall, I think ChooseFlow.ai is a strong choice for serious LinkedIn outreach. It is not the cheapest tool, but its all-in-one approach can be worth it if it helps you run campaigns more efficiently and keep conversations from slipping through the cracks.

comments.title: Flow helps you get quality leads
comments.comment:
I've been using Flow AI for LinkedIn prospecting, and the biggest difference compared with other tools I've tried is the quality of the leads, not just the quantity.
Flow doesn't simply blast out connection requests. It behaves more like a real person: visiting a prospect's profile, engaging naturally with their page, and then sending a connection request. The timing isn't rigid or predictable either. It adapts based on your own profile activity and on how each prospect responds, which makes the outreach feel much more authentic. From the prospect's perspective, it looks like normal profile activity rather than an obvious bot sequence.
That has led to better conversations for me. The people who accept tend to be relevant decision-makers, and the replies feel warmer because the first interaction doesn't come across as forced. 
For anyone doing B2B outreach in Indonesia or elsewhere, Flow is worth trying if you're aiming for a steady pipeline of quality opportunities, not just volume for the sake of numbers.

comments.title: Absolutelly Brilliant! Our journey
comments.comment:
Absolutely Brilliant!

I have heard many great testimonials on how giveaways can help growing brand awareness, grow email lists and get even more visitors to your website.

Quick insight in our journey (no experience in running giveaways whatsoever):

Initial numbers were +-
* Email list: 0 (starting with fresh and round "0")
* Facebook Likes: 27
* Twitter followers: 120
* YouTube subs: 19

// Tasks //

1) Grow brand awareness
2) Grow email list

Side tasks, with keeping in mind our customer avatar (people who look for best deals at lowest prices):
* Grow Twitter following - social proof is important when you reach out other brands
* Grow Facebook Likes - I plan to do Facebook live videos with cool online companies (first guest was already today - Adrian from tawk.to)
* Grow YouTube following - I plan to stream live videos into YouTube as well

// What else was needed? //
After buying KingSumo, also took 1 code of SendFox (decided to use software that are built to interact with each other).

Bought both on October 1st.

// What we did //
preparations stage) watched following KingSumo setup video at YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fm4IGZGfqRQ
1) Set up KindSumo deal: https://kingsumo.com/g/dbiivj/100-amazon-gift-card-hostmaria-october-giveaway
2) Set up SendFox account
3) Made an announcement on our website: https://www.hostmaria.com/index.php?rp=/announcements/25/100-Amazon-Gift-Card---October-2020---HostMaria-Giveaway-is-LIVE.html
4) Published the link to the giveaway at KingSumo.com (not our site) at several Facebook giveaway groups (7 or 8 of them)
5) Published the link to the giveaway on my FB profile (around 700  followers) and Latvian online business community page @ibf.lv of more than 5000 followers
6) Posted the link at r/Giveaways subreddit (62.2k members)

Less than 1 day later had 124 Contestants with 3217 Entries // scr: https://i.imgur.com/DiE4a2r.png
.. and a look into first contestants (emails blurred, of course): https://i.imgur.com/nFT8dg6.png

.. my setup? .. here you go: https://i.imgur.com/sR7DB3t.gif

// ---- slight problem ------ //

Originally I wanted to embed the giveaway in our Announcement and did so, but our CMS system (WHMCS) isn't configured yet that Facebook pulls in an image from post and posts it with the shared link. So, decided this month to stick with KingSumo link and just move on.
-----------

Started promoting a custom page on our website: https://www.hostmaria.com/giveaway.php

6 days later:
Contestants: 407
Entries: 14,903
scr: https://i.imgur.com/5gPDM95.png

Sendfox subscribers (active): 339 // scr: https://i.imgur.com/iYCFWX5.png
* Facebook Likes: 106
* Facebook follower: 114
* Twitter followers: 140
* YouTube subs: 46

New clients who can be linked to the giveaway? None. But, I am very optimistic about the future.

----

Verdict > Are you building a brand, awareness, reach or just an email list? Go for it!!

A+++++

Best of success to everybody,
Helmuts
founder of HostMaria

comments.title: A Capable Marketing Platform with Solid Foundations
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

During our testing, MailMunch delivered a clean, intuitive experience with a drag-and-drop builder, AI-assisted content tools, landing pages, forms, email automation, analytics, and email validation, and our tester rated usability and stability highly. 

We did identify several testing-stage gaps, including inconsistent save behavior with no version history or rollback, AI text regeneration that did not preserve formatting, and the lack of a tablet/device preview in the editor. comments.title: We thought we had a demo problem. It turned out to be a positioning problem.
comments.comment:
We are the developers of NibWP, a WordPress plugin that lets AI agents work on a real site through typed, permissioned tools. It ships with builder Skills that produce proper on-system output, and workflows that make the same result repeatable across every client site.

Explaining it is where we keep failing. Connect your site to your AI agent, choose the integrations and Pro Skills for the plugins and builder you use, then pick or build a workflow that produces the output a developer would have written by hand, or better. That's accurate, and it's aimed squarely at developers. Everyone else falls off. Agency owners care about what happens across a portfolio and what their client sees when they log in. Designers care about getting a Figma frame into their builder without rebuilding it. Site owners and content editors want to ask for a change and trust that nothing breaks. One product, four or five genuinely different conversations. Every demo we give picks one of them and loses the rest.

Nizamudheen took us through Dale today, and the answer was obvious inside ten minutes. In a branched demo, you ask as many qualifying questions as you need (role, builder, what they're trying to solve) and each combination of answers routes to its own path, all from a single link. The developer would get tokens, validation and the audit trail. The agency owner would get portfolio control and what their client sees. The designer would get Figma-to-builder. Nobody has to sit through someone else's version of the product.

Then it keeps going after the demo ends. Viewers land in segments based on what they told you and what they actually did: which topics they marked as mattering, what they went back to, where they lost interest. You can then mail each segment something relevant from your own domain, rather than sending everyone the same follow-up. We've been guessing at all of that in calls, one prospect at a time.

Which is why this stopped being a demo tool in my head before the call ended. It's the layer where the product explains itself to four different markets at once, tells us which one is actually listening, and then follows up accordingly.

The thing that made me stop worrying about the setup effort is Dale Studio. Rather than facing a blank canvas, it walks you through your product, your segments and their pain points, then lays out the skeleton: topics, pages, walkthroughs and priorities, already mapped and ready to fill. You still record and write everything that goes inside it, of course, but structuring this for five audiences was exactly the job I'd been avoiding, and it turns out that's the part Dale takes off your hands first.

To be straight about where we are: we bought last week, and after today's call we upgraded to Tier 4. So this is a review of the thinking and setting up, rather than the results. I'll know more in a month.

First time in years I'm actually looking forward to making demos.

comments.title: WarmySender - I’ll up-tier and keep !
comments.comment:
I’m not a fan of cold outreach, but it’s inevitable on some occasions, clients who hold an event or a roadshow in a new location, stale lists, domains trashed by email newsletter services sent from a shared server with a suddenly blacklisted IP, etc.

I was initially reluctant to give WarmySender a tryout given that my experience of other similar services has proved disappointing or worse-than-useless.  The open-and-honest responses to questions by the dev. tipped the balance for me.

The dashboard is easy to navigate, and the info.  is simple to understand, detailed and well presented.  

I bought a new domain, added managed spf, dkim and dmarc via DMARC Report and set up a mailbox via private email at Namecheap.  WarmySender connected immediately, displayed the DNS info., triggered an email, and gave an estimated conservative total warm-up time of 4-8 weeks, which is realistic.  

The campaign email builder has all the basics and can integrate custom fields from an uploaded .csv file, something I’ve found was sometimes missing from similar services.

The B2B database is unfortunately a weak spot given it’s extremely limited outside of the USA, which the dev. did warn about in the Questions section.  The State-Region only lists a very few areas in the UK and there’s no sector search.  The City-Town search returned just 56 prospects rather than the almost 1,000 from another B2B list service.  It was also annoying there was no way to select all of these at one go, you have to select each prospect or a whole individual page separately, and the save is limited to 33-a-day on Tier 1, divided up rather than being able to use up the available 1,000 monthly allowance.  The same rules apply to the email verifier, limited to 37-a-day, which again makes using this a chore.  These limits on B2B prospects and email verification can be bypassed by purchasing additional credits.

I haven’t checked out the AI integration facility as WarmySender currently doesn’t support OpenRouter.

If you do utilise cold outreach or want to have the facility in case disaster strikes, then I can recommend WarmySender, it’s one I intend to up-tier and the only such service I’ve tried so far that I would feel comfortable recommending to clients.

UPDATE RE: OPENROUTER

I’ve had some genuinely insightful helpful comms. with the dev.  

OpenRouter is supported if you drive WarmySender via an agent, using Zed (or Cline, or LibreChat), just set OpenRouter as the provider, and whatever model it serves does the campaign work. 

WarmySender are also happy to now look at integrating OpenRouter in copy generation, enabling a dropdown for the selection and ability to compare various AI models in that area.

A great response from them !

A lot of outbound tools help you write and send campaigns, but WarmySender is clearly paying attention to the parts that usually decide whether those emails have a chance to work: warmup, sender reputation, spam score checks, email verification, mailbox rotation, and pacing.

The warmup approach is the most interesting part. The team says their warmup uses multi turn email conversations, up to 5 replies deep, instead of just simple send and open activity. That is closer to the kind of engagement inbox providers expect to see, and it makes the deliverability more reliable.

I also like that the tool is built for people who want to run outbound without stitching together too many separate products. You can build lead lists, verify emails, warm up mailboxes, create sequences, and manage replies from the same place. For founders, agencies, consultants, and sales people, that can remove a lot of the usual cold email setup work.

One thing buyers should know upfront is how mailbox connection works. Gmail and Google Workspace use app passwords, while Microsoft and Outlook use OAuth. So if you are connecting Google mailboxes, have the app password setup ready instead of expecting the same OAuth flow you get with Microsoft.

I would also look at WarmySender mainly for the AppSumo core deal: cold email, warmup, leads, verification, and sequences. Other channels like LinkedIn, Instagram, and WhatsApp are separate add ons, so I would not assume they are included in the lifetime deal.

Overall, WarmySender is worth considering if you run cold email and want deliverability handled inside the same workflow as your campaigns. Its best fit is someone who wants to send outbound with the basic best practices already built in, instead of treating warmup and sender reputation as an afterthought.

comments.title: Find relevant LinkedIn posts and automate your comments
comments.comment:
Disclaimer: I'm a paid product tester for AppSumo and received this tool for free to provide a detailed review. My opinions are entirely my own, and my compensation is not tied to the rating or taco score I give.

Posting on LinkedIn is one thing. Finding the conversations where your potential customers are already active, and making time to contribute to them, is another. ConnectSafely helps with that by finding relevant posts and preparing comments you can publish from your own account.

You can target posts using keywords, job titles and specific creators. For example, if you sell software to agency owners, you can look for conversations around the problems your product solves rather than spending time scrolling through your feed hoping to find the right people.

You can also give ConnectSafely a persona with your background, tone and writing style. I like that you can test it against an actual LinkedIn post before letting it comment on your behalf. There's an approval option too, so you can read, edit or reject comments before they go live. I'd use that while getting the persona right, especially because a generic AI comment under someone else's post can do more harm than good.

The commenting and engagement features ran during my test once I had them set up. I haven't used it long enough to judge whether that activity turns into leads, but I can see the appeal of spending less time searching for relevant posts and more time reviewing what I want to say.

One of the options to connect your account is through a Chrome extension that works with your authenticated LinkedIn session in your own browser, on your own computer and IP. I highly recommend using this method over others. The team also uses randomized activity intervals, variable session lengths, activity scheduled during your working hours, conservative daily limits and a gradual warm-up for newly connected accounts. 

These safeguards are designed to reduce account risk, although no automation can guarantee that an account won't be flagged. I'd start with comment approval enabled so I can control what gets published.

Overall, I'd look at ConnectSafely if you already know who you want to reach on LinkedIn but struggle to consistently find and participate in the right conversations. The targeting and comment approval options are the features I'd spend time with first.
